# Citadel — Minefort Citadel developer documentation (llms-full.txt)

> Minefort Citadel is Minefort's Luau scripting engine for Minecraft
> servers: a *pack* — a folder of `.luau` files — runs server-side on a
> vanilla server and drives the whole game through globals such as `world`,
> `players`, `ui`, `game`, `commands`, `stores`, `network`, `http` and `hub`.
> Unmodified Java clients from 1.8 to 26.x join and play. This file is the
> complete, restructured developer reference: 61 wiki documents
> (concepts, guides, cookbook, appendices) plus the full API reference —
> 171 global and type pages, 682 documented members.
>
> Generated 2026-10-29 from the Citadel Developer Wiki (an Astro Starlight
> project). Regenerate with
> `python3 scripts/gen_starlight.py && python3 scripts/gen_llms_full.py`.

How to use this file:

- Every document is one `## <title>` section, opened by an HTML anchor
  (`<a id="...">`) and a `<!-- /route/ -->` comment with the page's path on
  the live site.
- Internal links resolve inside this file: `#ref-world-spawn` is the
  `world.spawn` section. The same string without the `#` —
  `/ref/World/spawn/` — is the live-site route.
- All code is Luau (Lua with types); `--` starts a comment. Tables are
  GitHub-flavoured markdown.
- A lean index of the same documentation set lives in `llms.txt`.

<a id="index"></a>

## Citadel Developer Wiki

> **In short:**
> Citadel is Minefort's Luau scripting engine for Minecraft
> servers. This wiki is a restructured, developer-facing reference of the
> whole platform — the concepts, every API call, and working guides —
> rebuilt from the official documentation into scannable, linkable,
> table-first pages.


Citadel runs a Luau script on a vanilla Minecraft server and gives it the
whole game: blocks, terrain, entities, players, inventories, UI, storage,
networking and the shop. The same script runs on Java clients from 1.8 to
26.x. This wiki covers the full surface, from your first pack to the
limits the engine enforces.

## Start here

- [What is Citadel](#getting-started-what-is-citadel) — the platform, the lite, full
  and plugin modes, and what a pack is.
- [Quick start](#getting-started-quick-start) — your first pack, from empty folder to
  a running server.
- [Luau primer](#getting-started-luau-primer) — strict mode, types and the task
  library, for developers new to Luau.
- [The event model](#concepts-events) — the one programming pattern every
  Citadel pack is built on.

## How the wiki is organized

| Section | What you find there |
| --- | --- |
| [Getting started](#getting-started-what-is-citadel) | The platform, your first pack, tooling, the Luau primer. |
| [Core concepts](#concepts-architecture) | Architecture, pack anatomy, runtime, events, conventions, rooms and dimensions. |
| [World & building](#world-terrain-generation) | Terrain generation, block reference, building, custom blocks, game data, world state. |
| [Entities](#entities-custom-entities) | Custom entities, entity handles, mobs and drops, NPCs. |
| [Players](#players-player-lifecycle) | Lifecycle, movement and cameras, inventory, visibility, health, permissions. |
| [Interface & media](#ui-ui-basics) | Messages, titles and bars, screens, canvases, menus, dialogs, displays, fx, sound. |
| [Server systems](#systems-commands) | Commands, storage, shared stores, network, HTTP, shop, hub, server settings, limits. |
| [Guides](#guides-guide-build-a-cottage) | Five complete, step-by-step builds — cottage, coin rush, parkour, a dungeon dimension, a scoreboard. |
| [Cookbook](#cookbook-cookbook-cooldowns) | Drop-in patterns: cooldowns, leaderboards, teleport pads, kits, teams, a minigame loop, save/load. |
| [Appendix](#appendix-event-catalog) | The event catalog, client version matrix, the limits table, and the FAQ. |

## API reference

Every global, type and call — 29 globals in five domains, 141 types, 674
documented members, each with its signature, parameters, returns and the
guides that use it — lives in the [API reference](#ref).

  options-table rules, before you read anything else.

<!-- /getting-started/what-is-citadel/ -->

<a id="getting-started-what-is-citadel"></a>

## What is Citadel

# What is Citadel?

> **In short:**
> Citadel is a scripting engine for Minecraft servers, built by
> Minefort. You write **packs** — folders of Luau (Lua) files plus a
> `citadel.yml` manifest — and the engine runs them as a game server that every
> Java client from 1.8 to 26.x can join. A pack either **is** the whole game
> (`mode: lite`) or **adds to** vanilla survival (`mode: full`).


## The one-paragraph model

Citadel replaces the plugin/mod ecosystem with a single scripting API. There is
no Java to compile, no per-version builds, no Spigot/Paper fork to track. Your
pack calls globals — `world`, `players`, `ui`, `game`, `commands`, `fx`,
`sound`, `http`, `stores` and about twenty more — and Citadel translates those
calls into the right packets for each client version. The same pack serves a
1.8.9 client and a 26.x client from one server. Where a client cannot show a
feature, the API degrades on its own: a call that cannot render is simply not
sent, and you can query support per player with `player:supports`.

## Three ways a pack can run

The `mode` key in a pack's manifest says **who owns the game**:

| Mode | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `mode: lite` | Your scripts are the game. No survival: no natural mob spawning, no block drops, no health rules — unless you switch each on with `world.rules` or per-kind fields. Terrain comes from your `world.on_generate` (or a world folder). |
| `mode: full` | **Citadel plays survival** — terrain, health, hunger, mining, inventory, mobs, world rules — and your pack *adds* to it: a shop, a scoreboard, a custom drop. |
| no `mode` key | The pack runs on either kind of server, like a plugin. Useful for packs that work everywhere. |

The server decides its mode in this order: a `--lite`/`--full` flag, then the
server's own `citadel.yml`, then what the packs' manifests agree on, and
finally survival when there are no packs. A `--lite` server with no packs runs
an empty world and no game.

## Where Citadel runs

- **Locally**: a `citadel` binary on your machine. `citadel --lite --pack ./first`
  starts a server on `localhost:25565` you join from Minecraft Java Edition.
- **On Minefort**: a *development workload* builds an **experience**; its
  instances are the published copies players join. `citadel.env` tells a script
  which copy it is on (`"development"`, `"unlisted"`, `"published"`).
- On Minefort, a development workload and all instances of its experience share
  one data store (see [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores)).

## Game versions

The engine emulates the game version you pick, not just the newest one:

- `game: "1.8.9"` (the default) and `game: "a0.1.0"` (Alpha) are the named
  versions a server file may choose. Blocks, items and entity kinds come from
  that version's own registry — `game.block(name)` returns `nil` for a block
  the game lacks.
- Every Java client from **1.8 to 26.x** can join the same server. The script
  never sees a client version; it asks `player:supports("display")` and the
  like (see [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions)).
- What a version lacks is **absent, not zero**: on Alpha, `player.food` is
  `nil` because there is no food rule there.

## What is in the API

The API surface, all documented in this wiki's [API reference](#ref):

- **World** — terrain generation (`world.on_generate`), block reads/writes,
  builds and schematics, zones, raycasts, pathfinding, lighting.
- **Players** — lifecycle events, movement, inventory, visibility, health,
  per-player UI.
- **Entities** — custom entities with think loops and physics, mob spawning
  rules, NPCs.
- **UI** — titles, chat, boss bars, screens, canvases, menus, dialogs,
  layouts, displays, particles, sound.
- **Systems** — commands with tab-completion, permissions, per-pack storage,
  experience-wide stores with leases, HTTP, WebSockets, Gem shop, hub
  discovery, rooms and dimensions.

## See also

- [Quick start](#getting-started-quick-start) — a working pack in five minutes.
- [Architecture](#concepts-architecture) — how the engine runs your script.
- [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy) — every `citadel.yml` key.
- [Tooling](#getting-started-tooling) — strict types with `citadel.d.luau` and `luau-lsp`.
- [Conventions](#concepts-conventions) — the rules every API call follows.
- [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions) — the per-feature version matrix.

<!-- /getting-started/quick-start/ -->

<a id="getting-started-quick-start"></a>

## Quick start

> **In short:**
> a Citadel pack is two files — a `citadel.yml` manifest and one
> Luau entry script. This page builds a small lobby pack: generated ground, a
> welcome title, and a `/spawn` command. Then it changes one line while the
> server is running and watches the hot reload. About five minutes, end to end.


## 1. Create the pack folder

Make a folder named `first` and put this `citadel.yml` inside it:

```yaml
# citadel.yml
name: first
entry: main.luau
motd: My first Citadel pack
spawn_point: [0.5, 65.0, 0.5]
gamemode: 2
mode: lite
world: script
```

What each key did:

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `entry` | The script to run: `main.luau`, beside this file. |
| `world: script` | Your script supplies the terrain through `world.on_generate`. A chunk the script does not fill is air. |
| `mode: lite` | The pack is the game — no survival underneath. |
| `gamemode: 2` | Adventure mode: players explore without breaking the floor. |
| `spawn_point` | Where players arrive: `[0.5, 65.0, 0.5]` puts their feet one block above the floor, centred on the gold marker you create next. |
| `motd` | The message of the day shown in the server list. |

## 2. Add the script

Create `main.luau` beside `citadel.yml`:

```luau
--!strict
-- A small lobby: solid ground, a welcome, and a way back to spawn.

world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(
        vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z),
        vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z),
        "stone"
    )
    chunk:set(vec3(0, 64, 0), "gold_block")
end)

players.on_join(function(player)
    player.ui.title{
        title = "Welcome",
        subtitle = player.name,
        color = "aqua",
    }
    player:message("Walk around, then type /spawn to return to the gold block.", "aqua")
end)

commands.add("spawn", function(player)
    player:teleport(world.spawn_point)
    player:message("You are back at spawn.", "green")
end, { help = "Return to the lobby spawn" })
```

Read the three callbacks in order — they are the three ideas a pack is built
from:

- **`world.on_generate`** fills each chunk with a stone floor at y = 64, then
  marks `(0, 64, 0)` with gold. `chunk:set` ignores positions outside its own
  chunk. `vec3(x, y, z)` describes a position; y is height. A chunk is 16 by
  16 blocks, and the callback must make the **same blocks every time** it runs
  for a position (see [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation)).
- **`players.on_join`** receives the player who joined. The title and the
  message go to that player alone. You register the callback once; Citadel
  calls it when the event happens.
- **`commands.add`** registers `spawn` — the name without the slash. When a
  player types `/spawn`, `player:teleport(world.spawn_point)` returns them to
  the point from the manifest, so the coordinates live in one place.

## 3. Run it

With `citadel` on your `PATH`, run this from the directory containing `first`:

```sh
citadel --lite --pack ./first
```

Join `localhost:25565` from Minecraft Java Edition (any version from 1.8 up).
You should see the welcome title and stand on the gold block. Walk away, type
`/spawn`, and check that you return to it with a confirmation in chat.

If nothing works, read the server log first — a script error in a callback
names the file and line, and a load failure explains which budget was exceeded
(see [The tick budget](#concepts-runtime--the-tick-budget)).

## 4. Edit it while it runs

Change `title = "Welcome"` to `title = "My lobby"` and save the file. Citadel
reloads `.luau` files while players stay connected, and runs the join callback
for those players again — the new title should appear immediately.

Two rules about reloading, from [Runtime](#concepts-runtime):

- **Reload keeps existing chunks.** Edits to `world.on_generate` affect newly
  generated terrain only. For a fresh map, delete the world folder (a lite
  server keeps it in `<pack>/data/world`).
- **Restart after editing `citadel.yml`.** The manifest is read once at boot.

As a next exercise, add a `/hello` command that sends a message to the player
who uses it, then a second argument with a type — the pattern is in
[Commands](#systems-commands).

## Where to go next

Each of these takes one idea from this page and goes deep:

- [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation) — chunks, deterministic
  generation, heightmaps, `on_populate`.
- [Commands](#systems-commands) — typed arguments, tab-completion, permissions.
- [The event model](#concepts-events) — every `on_*` subscription, cancellation,
  and the ask handlers.
- [Guides](#guides-guide-build-a-cottage) — full builds and games, step by step.

## See also

- [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy) — every manifest key, assets, dimensions.
- [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) — reload semantics, tasks, budgets.
- [Cookbook](#cookbook-cookbook-teleport-pads) — small, complete patterns to copy.

<!-- /getting-started/tooling/ -->

<a id="getting-started-tooling"></a>

## Tooling

> **In short:**
> Citadel ships a full type-definitions file, `packs/citadel.d.luau`.
> Point Luau's language server at it and you get autocomplete, signatures and
> strict type checking across the whole API. The `citadel` CLI runs the server,
> analyzes packs, generates world folders and renders builds to images.


## The type definitions file

`packs/citadel.d.luau` types this whole API. Start every script with
`--!strict` and point a language server at that file: misspelt fields, wrong
argument types and unknown options become squiggles before you run anything.

> **Gotcha:**
> use the standard platform and Luau's **new type solver**
> (luau-lsp 1.70.1 or later). The old solver misresolves several of the API's
> table types.


## Command-line type check

```sh
luau-lsp analyze --platform=standard --flag:LuauSolverV2=true \
  --definitions=packs/citadel.d.luau main.luau
```

Run this in CI or before you ship; it catches the same errors the editor does.

## VS Code setup

With the `luau-lsp` extension installed, set in `.vscode/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "luau-lsp.platform.type": "standard",
  "luau-lsp.types.definitionFiles": ["packs/citadel.d.luau"],
  "luau-lsp.fflags.override": { "LuauSolverV2": "true" }
}
```

## The `citadel` CLI

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `citadel --lite --pack ./first` | Run a lite server with one pack. `--full` (or no flag) runs survival. |
| `citadel --packs-dir ./packs` | Run with every pack in a folder. |
| `luau-lsp analyze ...` (above) | Type-check a pack's scripts. |
| `citadel check <pack>` | Frame-check a build: says which named part an edit touched. |
| `citadel render` | Render a build (or one named part) to an image. |
| `citadel generate <pack> --from -4096,-6144 --to 4095,6143` | Pre-generate a world folder from the pack's `world.on_generate`, one script per core; a stopped run continues where it left off. `--threads n` caps cores. |
| `citadel generate <pack> --part tower-3` | Run one named part's generator into the world folder. |
| `citadel parts <pack>` | List every named part: clean, modified, kept or orphaned, and who edited it. |
| `citadel import builds/lobby.schem <pack>/hub --at -186,48,-236 --spawn 0.5,65,0.5` | Import a `.schem` (Sponge or MCEdit) or a vanilla world as a pack's world folder. |

Details on world folders, named parts and build mode are in
[Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy) and [Building](#world-building).

## Build mode

`/build` and `/part` exist on `citadel.env == "development"` only — the
Minefort workload where an experience is built. They edit a pack's world folder
by hand and mark named parts as modified. See
[Named parts](#world-building--named-parts).

## Knowing where your script runs

```luau
print(citadel.version)  -- the engine build, e.g. "0.1.0"
print(citadel.game)     -- the game version from citadel.yml, e.g. "1.8.9"
print(citadel.env)      -- "development", "unlisted" or "published"
```

`citadel.env` is:

- `"development"` on the Minefort workload where an experience is built.
- `"unlisted"` or `"published"` on an experience's instances, by visibility.
- `"published"` on a Minefort server that is not an experience.
- `"development"` anywhere else (including local runs).

Gate debug tools on it:

```luau
if citadel.env == "development" then
    -- builder-only commands, verbose logs, ...
end
```

## Logging

`citadel.log(...)` writes its arguments to the server log under this pack's
name — the one logging call a script has. Errors in callbacks are logged with
file and line automatically.

## See also

- [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy) — the manifest and the folders around it.
- [Luau primer](#getting-started-luau-primer) — the language, if Lua is new to you.
- [Limits](#systems-limits) — what `citadel.budget()` reports and what happens
  when a pack runs long.

<!-- /getting-started/luau-primer/ -->

<a id="getting-started-luau-primer"></a>

## Luau primer

> **In short:**
> Citadel packs are written in **Luau**, Roblox's typed dialect of
> Lua 5.1. If you know JavaScript the shape will look familiar: first-class
> functions, tables used as objects and arrays, closures everywhere. This page
> covers the syntax you will meet in every Citadel example, plus the standard
> library that is and is not there.


## Values and syntax essentials

```luau
-- Comments start with --. Block comments: --[[ ... ]]

local n = 42                  -- numbers: doubles
local s = "double or 'single' quotes"
local b = true                -- true / false / nil (nil is "absent")
local pos = vec3(1, 2, 3)     -- engine values are plain calls

-- ~= is "not equal"; .. concatenates strings
if n ~= 0 and s ~= "" then print("no") end

-- Blocks close with keywords, not braces:
for i = 1, 10 do end          -- inclusive range
for i = 10, 1, -1 do end      -- with a step
while b do break end          -- break exists; continue exists in Luau
repeat local x = 1 until x == 1
```

The `if` **expression** — Luau's ternary:

```luau
local block = if mix(x, 0, z) < 0.3 then "mossy_cobblestone" else "cobblestone"
```

## Tables are the one data structure

There are no classes and no arrays — tables do both jobs:

```luau
local list = { "red", "green", "blue" }   -- 1-indexed arrays
list[1] == "red"                           -- arrays start at ONE

local opts = {                             -- dictionaries (string keys)
    count = 40,
    spread = 2,
    color = colors.red,                    -- trailing comma allowed
}

local nested = {                           -- nested tables build any shape
    from = vec3(0, 64, 0),
    to = vec3(8, 70, 8),
    on_enter = function(player) end,
}
```

Table keys with dots, array indexes with brackets. Functions are values:
stored in tables, passed as arguments — that is how every `on_*` callback in
the API works.

```luau
local function greet(name) return "hi " .. name end
world.on_generate(function(chunk)          -- anonymous function argument
    chunk:fill(chunk.min, chunk.max, "stone")
end)
```

The colon `chunk:fill(...)` is method-call syntax — it passes `chunk` itself as
a hidden first argument. That is why the API reads `player:teleport(pos)` for
methods but `players.list()` for plain functions.

## Types and `--!strict`

Luau has an optional type system. Put `--!strict` at the top of every file —
with Citadel's definitions file it type-checks the entire API (see
[Tooling](#getting-started-tooling)):

```luau
--!strict

local count: number = 0
local function total(prices: { number }): number
    local sum = 0
    for _, p in prices do sum += p end     -- += exists in Luau
    return sum
end

-- Optional values carry ?: a nil is allowed
local function find(id: string): Player?
    return nil
end

-- String unions read like the docs write them
local face: "north" | "south" | "east" | "west" = "north"

-- Table types, as the API's options tables are typed
local opts: { count: number?, spread: number? } = { count = 3 }
```

Compound assignments (`+=`, `-=`, `..=`), string interpolation with backticks
(`` `hi {name}` `), and generalized iteration (`for _, v in table do` without
`pairs`/`ipairs`) are Luau additions you will see throughout the samples.

## What is *not* there

Citadel's Luau is sandboxed to the pack, and a few Lua/Roblox staples are
deliberately absent:

- `loadstring` is not there — a pack cannot run text as code. `require` reads
  only files **inside the pack**.
- `getfenv` and `setfenv` are not there.
- There is no `os` / `io` access: files, time and network all go through the
  engine's own globals (`storage`, `stores`, `http`, `time`).

`require` resolves from the pack root, caches by canonical file path, rejects
cycles, and rejects symlinks that lead outside the pack. A module returning
`nil` is cached as `true`. Details in [Runtime](#concepts-runtime).

## Patterns you will see in every pack

Event subscription with cancellation:

```luau
local conn = players.on_click(function(player, hit) end)
conn:cancel()          -- stop the subscription
```

Options tables instead of long argument lists (calls with more than three
inputs take an options table, and **an unknown field is an error**):

```luau
fx.particle("dust", pos, { count = 40, spread = 2, color = colors.lime })
```

`nil` vs `false` for optional overrides — a distinction the whole API uses
(see [Conventions](#concepts-conventions--nil-false-and-true)):

```luau
player.visible = false    -- hidden from everyone
player.visible = nil      -- back to the default (visible)
```

## See also

- [Conventions](#concepts-conventions) — the API's rules for options, colours,
  positions and text.
- [Tooling](#getting-started-tooling) — `luau-lsp` and the definitions file.
- [The event model](#concepts-events) — callbacks, connections, asks.

<!-- /concepts/architecture/ -->

<a id="concepts-architecture"></a>

## Architecture

> **In short:**
> one Citadel server hosts a **main room** (and any rooms you
> create), runs each loaded pack's entry script in its own VM, and drives
> everything from a 50 ms world tick plus a script scheduler. This page lays
> out the machine model the rest of the docs assume: which table belongs to
> which room, when callbacks run, how chunks come and go, and what reload
> actually replaces.


## The server, rooms and per-room tables

A server has one **main room** at boot, and a pack can make more with
`rooms.create{}`. Each room owns its own copy of the six room tables:

| Room table | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `world` | the room's blocks, entities, displays, screens and time |
| `players` | who is in that room, and their room-scoped events |
| `ui` | UI broadcast to everyone in the room |
| `game` | that room's registries and spawn settings |
| `rooms` | making and destroying rooms |
| `sound` | sound heard in the room |

The lowercase globals you use at the top of a script belong to the **main
room**; `rooms.create{}` returns a room handle whose fields (`room.world`,
`room.players`, ...) are that room's own tables. Everything else — `fx`,
`commands`, `time`, `task`, `http`, `storage`, `stores`, `shop`, `hub` — is
server-wide. A player is in exactly one room at a time; `player.room` is
`nil` while they are between rooms.

## Ticks, tasks and the scheduler

The world advances in 50 ms ticks. Two clocks drive pack code:

- **`time.on_tick(fn)`** — runs `fn(tick)` once per world tick for work tied
  to the simulation. Missed ticks coalesce: remaining listeners resume with
  the latest tick number.
- **`task.wait` / `task.delay` / `task.spawn`** — the script scheduler.
  `task.wait` uses elapsed **real time**, resumed once the requested time has
  passed and the scheduler can run, without rounding to Minecraft's ticks.

`spawn`, `delay` and `defer` accept a function or a suspended coroutine,
forward all arguments, and return the coroutine. `time.every` is a repeating
timer that returns a connection and may cancel itself inside its callback.
The full task semantics — including the initialization exception — are in
[Runtime](#concepts-runtime).

## The pack lifecycle

A pack is a folder: a `citadel.yml` manifest, an entry script, and whatever
else it `require`s or ships (assets, world folders, layouts). At boot:

1. The server reads its own `citadel.yml` (mode, game version, bind ports).
2. Packs load; each manifest's keys are checked — an unknown key stops the
   server with the field named.
3. Each pack's entry script runs in its own VM. The entry has **5 seconds**
   of work between two waits and **30 seconds** in all; past that the load
   fails and the log says why. Big scenery is built once at load and pasted
   per chunk, never block-by-block at load.
4. Initialization commits: recipes, assets, layouts, block/entity
   registrations, commands, model registrations, asks and spawn settings all
   register at once. Tasks spawned during load start only after this commit.
5. The port opens; players join. The chunks around the spawn are generated
   before the port opens.

A failed entry script discards its drafts and the previous script keeps
running (see [Reload](#concepts-architecture--reload) below).

## Chunks: loading, unloading, determinism

**Chunks nobody is near are unloaded.** Every ten seconds the server drops
chunks beyond the view distance of all players and entities. When someone
returns, a stored world loads the chunk from disk; a `script` world calls
`on_generate` again.

> **Gotcha:**
> `world.on_generate` must therefore make the **same blocks every
> time** for the same chunk. Draw from a hash of the position, never
> `math.random`. A script-world chunk changed live (`world.set_block`,
> `world.fill`) stays in memory and is not regenerated.


Where the world lives on disk: a full server keeps it in `world/` beside the
server's `citadel.yml` (the world is the server's — removing a pack does not
take the map). A lite server keeps it in the first pack, `<pack>/data/world`.
A dimension is a folder beside the main world (`world_dungeon`). The
`world` manifest key decides where chunks come from — `script`, `overworld`,
a world folder, or "ask the scripts first" when the key is absent. All of it
is in [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy--the-world-key) and
[Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions).

## Events and asks

Pack code reacts through `on_*` subscriptions that return a connection
(`connection:cancel()` unsubscribes), with one deliberate exception:
`world.on_generate` and `world.on_populate` are single-handler **setters** —
a later call replaces the previous handler and returns nothing.

Most events are notifications. Three are **asks** — cancellable questions the
engine asks a few milliseconds before acting: `players.on_break`,
`players.on_place` and `players.on_damage`. No answer in time denies the
action; a listener that returns `nil` still allows it. Miss too many and the
engine stops asking that kind. The whole model is in
[The event model](#concepts-events).

<a id="concepts-architecture--reload"></a>

## Reload

Saving any `.luau` file in the pack, at any depth, restarts the pack's script
while the server keeps running:

- Players stay connected, and the join callbacks run for them again.
- Initialization re-registers everything atomically; a failed entry discards
  the drafts and resumes the old script.
- Local storage is flushed before the replacement loads; the old VM finishes
  cleanup first.
- Existing chunks are **not** regenerated — `on_generate` edits apply to new
  terrain only. Restart (or delete the world folder) for a fresh map.
- `citadel.yml` is read at boot only: manifest changes need a restart.

The tick budget and every other limit around reload are collected in
[Limits](#systems-limits).

## Identity and connections

A player's identity comes from one of three places: a proxy signing it
(`MODERN_FORWARDING_SECRET`), Mojang verification (`online_mode: true`, the
default), or nobody (`online_mode: false`, where anyone can join with any
name). Bedrock clients connect over RakNet/UDP or NetherNet, driven by the
server file's `bind` keys. Every Java client 1.8–26.x joins the same server;
feature differences are per-player facts (`player:supports`), never script
branches on a version number.

## See also

- [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy) — the manifest, files and assets.
- [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) — tasks, modules and budgets in depth.
- [The event model](#concepts-events) — subscriptions, cancellation, asks.
- [Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions) — more rooms, more worlds.
- [Server settings](#systems-server-settings) — the server's own `citadel.yml`.

---

<!-- /concepts/pack-anatomy/ -->

<a id="concepts-pack-anatomy"></a>

## Pack anatomy

> **In short:**
> a pack is a folder: a `citadel.yml` manifest at its root, one
> entry script, whatever modules it `require`s, and optional folders for
> assets, layouts, world data and dimensions. This page is the complete
> manifest reference and the folder map around it.


## The manifest, key by key

```yaml
# citadel.yml — a pack manifest
name: first                  # the pack's id; "castle:dungeon" ids are prefixed by it
entry: main.luau             # the script that runs
motd: My first Citadel pack  # shown in the server list
spawn_point: [0.5, 65.0, 0.5]
gamemode: 2                  # 0 survival, 1 creative, 2 adventure
mode: lite                   # lite | full | absent (runs on either)
world: script                # script | overworld | a world folder name
budget_ms: 2                 # this pack's slice of each tick (default 2 ms)
```

### `mode` — who owns the game

| Mode | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `mode: lite` | Your scripts are the game. Terrain from `world.on_generate`; no survival rules unless switched on. |
| `mode: full` | Citadel plays survival; the pack adds to it (a shop, a scoreboard, a custom drop). A pack cannot ship survival — it *adds* to it. |
| no `mode` key | Runs on either kind of server, like a plugin. |

Packs that name different modes, or that all name none, stop the server with a
message saying how to set one. A flag or the server file overrules a pack that
names the other mode — the log names that pack.

<a id="concepts-pack-anatomy--the-world-key"></a>

### The `world` key

`world` says where a chunk comes from:

| Value | Chunks come from |
| --- | --- |
| `"script"` | `world.on_generate` makes them. A chunk it does not fill is air. |
| `"overworld"` | Citadel's terrain: biomes, hills, caves, ores, trees, sea level 63. `seed` pins the map. Scripts only add (`world.on_populate`). |
| a name, e.g. `"hub"` | A world folder in the pack, `<pack>/hub`, made once from a build or a vanilla world. The server reads it chunk by chunk and saves player changes into it. A chunk the folder lacks comes from `world.on_generate`, or is air. |
| no `world` key | The scripts are asked first. A chunk no script filled is overworld terrain on a full server, air on a lite server. |

Making a world folder ahead of time (a map too big to make live):

```sh
citadel import builds/lobby.schem <pack>/hub --at -186,48,-236 --spawn 0.5,65,0.5
citadel generate <pack> --from -4096,-6144 --to 4095,6143   # --threads n caps cores
```

`citadel generate` runs one script per core, any map size fits in memory, and
chunks already in the folder are kept — a stopped run continues.

### `dimensions`

A pack adds worlds under `dimensions:`. The name is its id inside the pack
(`castle:dungeon`):

```yaml
dimensions:
  dungeon:
    type: { has_skylight: false, has_ceiling: true, weather: false }
    world: script        # or "void" to leave chunks empty
```

Every `type` field is optional and starts from the main world's:
`has_skylight`, `has_ceiling`, `weather`, `ultrawarm`, `bed_works`,
`respawn_anchor_works`, `coordinate_scale`, `fixed_time`, `effects`. A world
with a roof looks like the Nether to a client, one with no sky and no roof
like the End; `effects` picks one of the three yourself. A dimension ticks
after the main world and saves to `world_dungeon` beside it. Full guide:
[A dungeon dimension](#guides-guide-a-dungeon-dimension).

### `permissions`

The manifest defines permission groups; every player starts in `default`:

```yaml
permissions:
  default: { nodes: [casino.play] }
  vip:     { inherits: [default], nodes: [casino.vip] }
  staff:   { inherits: [vip], nodes: [minecraft.command.gamemode, "casino.*", "-casino.debug"] }
```

Same-name groups in two packs merge; a group that inherits an undefined group,
or one named `operator`, stops the server. The full node syntax is in
[Permissions](#players-permissions).

### Other keys

- `spawn_point: [x, y, z]` — where players arrive in the main room. With no
  spawn point, an overworld pack takes the first grass block above sea level,
  ring by ring out from (0, 0); the search runs once and is stored in
  `level.json`.
- `min_client` — refuse clients older than this (e.g. `"1.14"`), instead of
  guarding each feature with `player:supports`.
- `store_dir` — moves where `stores` keeps its files (two servers on one
  machine need two directories). Default `data/store`.
- `terrain` — sets the overworld's step list; only `game: a0.1.0` has one
  (the full step table is in [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation--the-a010-terrain-steps)).

## The folder map

```
first/
  citadel.yml          the manifest
  main.luau            the entry script
  *.luau               anything the entry requires (pack-root resolution)
  assets/
    sounds/...         "<pack>.<file>" sound names
    (other folders)    go into the resource pack unchanged
                        (assets/<pack>/textures/...)
  hub/                 a world folder, if world: hub
  data/
    world/             a lite server keeps the world here
    store/             stores' files when no platform store was named
  dimension folders    beside the world on the server, not in the pack
```

## Textures of your own

On Java 1.21.4 and later, a pack's own items and blocks can have textures: set
`texture` in `game.items.define` and `game.blocks.define`. The engine adds
them to its resource pack; older clients see the vanilla item or block, and a
client that turned the resource pack down sees them too from then on
(`player:supports("resource_pack")` is `false`). A pack that needs its
textures says so with `min_client`.

## The load budget

The entry script has **5 seconds** of work between two waits (`task.wait`)
and **30 seconds** in all; past that the load fails and the log says why.
Build big scenery once at load and copy it (one tree variant pasted per
chunk); do not loop over every block of every level at load.

## Where the world and its data live

- Full server: `world/` beside the server's `citadel.yml` — the world is the
  server's; removing a pack does not take the map.
- Lite server: `<pack>/data/world`.
- Dimension: a folder beside the main world (`world_dungeon`).
- `level.json` in the world keeps the seed, spawn, time and weather of the
  first run. Changing `seed` later does nothing to an existing world; delete
  the world folder for a new map.

## See also

- [Server settings](#systems-server-settings) — the *server's* `citadel.yml`:
  bind ports, game version, operators, online mode.
- [Architecture](#concepts-architecture) — how the manifest is consumed at boot.
- [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) — the load budget in context, reload semantics.
- [Storage](#systems-storage) and [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) — the
  two persistence APIs and their on-disk layout.

---

<!-- /concepts/runtime/ -->

<a id="concepts-runtime"></a>

## Runtime

> **In short:**
> each pack runs as one Luau VM with a cooperative scheduler.
> This page covers the task library's exact semantics, how `require` resolves
> modules, the per-pack tick budget and what happens when it runs out, and the
> precise rules of a hot reload.


## Tasks: `spawn`, `delay`, `defer`, `wait`

`task.spawn`, `task.delay` and `task.defer` accept either a function or a
suspended coroutine, forward all arguments (including nils), and return that
coroutine:

| Call | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| `task.spawn(fn, ...)` | Immediately, until the task yields or returns. |
| `task.delay(sec, fn, ...)` | After `sec` seconds of elapsed real time. |
| `task.defer(fn, ...)` | On the next scheduler turn. |
| `task.wait(sec)` | Yields the calling thread until `sec` real seconds have passed. |

- `task.wait` and `task.delay` measure **elapsed real time**, in full and lite
  mode alike. Unlike Roblox's heartbeat scheduling they resume once the time
  has passed and the scheduler can run them — not rounded to Minecraft's 50 ms
  ticks. Use `time.on_tick` for work tied to world ticks.
- Zero or negative seconds yield until the next scheduler turn.
- The actual wait may be longer under load. Durations must be finite and
  within the supported clock range; invalid values raise catchable errors.
- `time.every(sec, fn)` is a repeating timer that returns a connection and may
  cancel itself inside its callback.
- `task.cancel` works on a suspended task, also after `task.wait`; cancelling
  a **running** thread is an error. Cancelling stops the task's code but
  cannot undo I/O it already submitted.

## The initialization exception

Tasks spawned, deferred or delayed **while `main.luau` loads** start only
after initialization commits — the pack's startup is atomic:

- The top level of `main.luau` may `task.wait`, but it cannot wait for one of
  those child tasks to finish before startup completes.
- If the entry script fails, the drafts are discarded and the previous script
  (if any) resumes.

## Modules and `require`

`require` splits a pack into files:

- Resolves from the **pack root** (`require("util/math")` is
  `<pack>/util/math.luau`).
- Caches by canonical file path; a module returning `nil` is cached as `true`.
- Rejects cycles, and rejects symlinks that lead outside the pack.
- `loadstring`, `getfenv` and `setfenv` are not there — a pack cannot run text
  as code or reach another environment.

> **Gotcha:**
> a module's top level may not call `task.wait`, and synchronous
> ask handlers may not either. Ordinary event callbacks, `main.luau` and task


  threads may.

<a id="concepts-runtime--the-tick-budget"></a>

## The tick budget

A pack's tick and event callbacks share part of each tick, set with
`budget_ms` in the pack's `citadel.yml`. The default is **2 ms**.

| Covered by the budget | Not covered (100 ms runaway limit instead) |
| --- | --- |
| `time.on_tick`, `time.every`, survival events (`world.on_block_break` and the rest) | `players.on_join`, input events (`on_click`, `on_chat`, commands), task threads |
| | Chunk callbacks keep their separate **2 s** limit |

It counts work, not time spent waiting. When the budget runs out mid-batch:

- Ordinary events retain their arguments and remaining listeners until the
  next budget window; cancelling a subscription also removes its pending
  delivery.
- `time.on_tick` coalesces missed ticks — listeners resume with the latest
  tick number, no replay.
- Socket messages stay queued until their callback can run; a `time.every`
  timer that does not fit keeps its place among due timers.
- **Nothing is killed.** A started callback always finishes. Going over is not
  an error — do less per tick, or raise `budget_ms`.

Each pack retains at most **4096 ordinary events**; overflow drops the oldest
and logs the pack. Joins, leaves, deaths and respawns are retained in order
and never evicted — they carry the original player session, so a delayed
leave still has its `player.data` after a reconnect. This is in-process
delivery, not a durable journal across a crash: keep lifecycle callbacks
short.

## Reading the numbers

```luau
local b = citadel.budget()
print(b.of)        -- 2, the ms this pack gets per tick
print(b.used)      -- what the last tick spent
print(b.peak)      -- the most any tick has spent
print(b.skipped)   -- callbacks not run for want of budget, since the script started
print(b.dropped)   -- events this pack never saw (overflowed the 4096 queue)
print(b.slowest)   -- { hook = "on_tick", ms = 4.1 }, or nil
print(b.asks)      -- what the engine's questions cost this pack; see "asks"

citadel.on_slow(function(slow)
    print(slow.hook, slow.used, slow.of, slow.skipped)   -- "on_tick" 2.4 2 3
end)
```

`citadel.on_slow` runs at most once a second; hook names are `"on_tick"`,
`"every"`, or the event's name (`"block_break"`, `"pickup"`). The server log
shows the pack, hook and time at most once every five seconds.

<a id="concepts-runtime--reload-exactly"></a>

## Reload, exactly

Saving any `.luau` file in the pack, at any depth, restarts the pack's script.
The server keeps running:

- Players stay connected; `players.on_join` runs again for every online
  player — **make it safe to run twice**.
- Initialization stages recipes, assets, layouts, block/entity registrations,
  commands, model registrations, asks, spawn settings and queued world
  actions. A failed entry discards these drafts and resumes the old script.
- The entry must finish within 30 seconds, including any `task.wait` or read
  requests. `task.spawn` work starts after successful initialization.
- Local storage is flushed before the replacement loads; the old VM finishes
  cleanup before the replacement starts callbacks.
- Writes to shared stores, purchase prompts/acks and `storage.flush` belong
  in `task.spawn` or callbacks — external writes cannot be rolled back, so
  existing-world/player side effects belong in callbacks too.
- On success, the old script's timers and connections end.
- **The world stays.** Every existing chunk stays, in script and terrain
  worlds. A changed `world.on_generate`, `seed` or `terrain` applies only to
  chunks generated from here on. To regenerate the whole map: stop the
  server, delete the world folder (the log names it), start again.
- A script reload removes a spawn/drops/attacks value that the new script
  does not set again (see [Game data](#world-game-data)).
- A mob a pack spawned stays when the script reloads; an NPC does not.

## See also

- [Architecture](#concepts-architecture) — the machine around this runtime.
- [The event model](#concepts-events) — subscriptions, asks, queue semantics.
- [Limits](#systems-limits) — every numeric limit in one table.
- [Modules and tasks recipes](#cookbook-cookbook-save-load) — using tasks for
  I/O patterns.

<!-- /concepts/events/ -->

<a id="concepts-events"></a>

## The event model

> **In short:**
> pack code reacts to the game through `on_*` subscriptions that
> return a connection; `connection:cancel()` unsubscribes. Most events are
> notifications that arrive after the fact. Three — `players.on_break`,
> `on_place` and `on_damage` — are **asks**: the engine pauses the action for
> two milliseconds and `false` vetoes it. This page is the model; the full
> per-event catalog is in the [event catalog](#appendix-event-catalog).


## Subscriptions and connections

```luau
local conn = players.on_click(function(player, hit) end)
-- ...later:
conn:cancel()      -- the subscription stops; pending deliveries are removed too
```

- Subscriptions live in the pack that made them. On reload, the old script's
  timers and connections end.
- `world.on_generate` and `world.on_populate` are **not** subscriptions: they
  are single-handler setters. A later call replaces the previous handler, and
  they return nothing.
- The engine's own `/help` lists every command a player may run — commands are
  registered, not events (see [Commands](#systems-commands)).

## Notification events

Notifications arrive after the fact. The load-bearing ones on the world and
its entities:

```luau
world.on_block_break(function(player, pos, block) end)   -- block: what was there
world.on_block_place(function(player, pos, block) end)   -- block: what was put down
world.on_entity_spawn(function(entity, name) end)        -- a mob appeared; entity is the handle
world.on_entity_death(function(id, name) end)            -- it is gone: id and name is all there is
players.on_pickup(function(player, item, count) end)
players.on_drop(function(player, item, count) end)
```

`block` is the canonical name in both. `player` is `nil` when the world
dropped the stack (a leaf decays, a mob dies, an explosion) or the player has
already left the room — always check before using it:

```luau
world.on_block_break(function(player, pos, block)
    if block == "diamond_ore" and player then
        message(player.name .. " struck diamond", colors.cyan)
    end
end)
```

Player lifecycle — `players.on_join` fires on connect in the main room, and a
room's own `room.players.on_join` fires on each `player:move_to(room)`;
`players.on_leave` matches. Joins, leaves, deaths and respawns are retained in
order and never dropped by budget pressure (see
[Runtime](#concepts-runtime--the-tick-budget)).

<a id="concepts-events--asks-the-cancellable-events"></a>

## Asks: the cancellable events

Three events are questions the engine asks **before** acting, waiting a few
milliseconds for the answer:

```luau
players.on_break(function(player, pos, block) return false end)
players.on_place(function(player, pos, block) return false end)
players.on_damage(function(player, hit) return false end)
```

`players.on_damage` receives a `hit` table:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `hit.amount` | The damage, in half hearts, before armour. |
| `hit.cause` | `"fall"`, `"drown"`, `"suffocate"`, `"void"`, `"lava"`, `"fire"`, `"cactus"`, `"starve"`, `"attack"`, `"shot"`, `"blast"` or `"magic"`. |
| `hit.by` | The player who hit, or who shot the arrow; `nil` for anything else. |
| `hit.kind` | The kind's name (`"Skeleton"`) when a mob did it; else `nil`. |

The veto rules:

- **Only `false` is a veto.** A handler that returns nothing allows the
  action; a handler that errors is not a veto — it counts as a missed
  deadline.
- **Across packs, any `false` wins.** One `false` cancels the action.
- A refused arrow bounces off, as off a creative player.
- A pack's own `player:damage` call is not asked about, in this pack or
  another. An entity of a pack's own has the same question as a hook:
  `on_damage` in `game.entities.define`, which answers `"take"` or `"ignore"`.

```luau
-- No friendly fire, and nobody is hurt at the spawn.
players.on_damage(function(player, hit)
    if hit.by and hit.by.data.team == player.data.team then return false end
    if player.at:distance(SPAWN) < 8 then return false end
end)

-- A spawn area nobody digs in.
players.on_break(function(player, pos, block)
    if math.abs(pos.x) < 16 and math.abs(pos.z) < 16 then
        player:message("not here", colors.red)
        return false
    end
end)
```

## The deadline

The engine waits **two milliseconds** for your pack, then stops waiting.
`task.wait` and anything that blocks are errors inside an ask handler.

| Hook | A missed deadline means |
| --- | --- |
| `players.on_break` | **The break is denied.** Protection fails closed on timeout, error, overflow, or a disabled handler. |
| `players.on_place` | **The place is denied.** The same protection guarantee. |
| `players.on_damage` | **The damage is denied.** The same protection guarantee. |

The rule: **fail open only where the default is safe.** A pack block's own
`on_break` (which comes with pack blocks) fails *closed* to the drops its
definition declares.

Miss a kind too often and the engine **stops asking you** that kind: it takes
the default, logs this once, and sets `disabled`. Watch the counters:

```luau
time.every(60, function()
    for kind, count in citadel.budget().asks.kinds do
        if count.missed > count.answered then
            citadel.log(`slow at {kind}: {count.missed} of {count.asks} missed`)
        end
    end
end)
```

- Answer at once — never `task.wait` in an ask.
- Answering costs tick budget, under the hook name `"ask"`.
- A spent budget does not stop an ask from being answered.
- With no protection listener registered, the action follows the normal game
  rules; a listener that completes and returns `nil` still allows it.

## Observe-after-veto

The observe-only events come **after** the asks: a vetoed break never reaches
`world.on_block_break` or `world.on_block_place`.

## See also

- [Event catalog](#appendix-event-catalog) — every `on_*` event in one table.
- [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) — the budget, the event queue and its 4096 cap.
- [Cancelling in practice](#players-health) — damage rules and room rules.

<!-- /concepts/conventions/ -->

<a id="concepts-conventions"></a>

## Conventions

> **In short:**
> the whole API follows a handful of rules. Learn them once and
> every call behaves the way you expect: positions are `vec3`, colours are
> `color(...)` or a name string, long calls take options tables where an
> unknown field is an error, `nil`/`false` mean different things, and one
> spelling serves each idea.


## Namespaces

| Kind | Globals |
| --- | --- |
| The main room's tables | `world`, `players`, `ui`, `game`, `rooms`, `sound` — `rooms.create{}` gives another room the same six |
| Server-wide | `fx`, `commands`, `time`, `task`, `storage`, `stores`, `http`, `network`, `shop`, `hub`, `models`, `parts`, `routes`, `data`, `fields`, `message` |
| Values and helpers | `vec3`, `color`, `colors`, `noise`, `tween`, `camera`, `citadel` |

A pack is its files. `loadstring` is not there, so a pack cannot run text as
code; `require` reads only files inside the pack; `getfenv` and `setfenv` are
not there.

## Positions: `vec3`

Positions are `vec3(x, y, z)` with fields `x`, `y`, `z`. **Block positions are
floored** — `vec3(20.2, 65, -7.9)` addresses block `(20, 65, -8)` where a
block is asked for. A box's corners are `from` and `to`, in either order, both
corners inside.

## Colours

Colours are `color(r, g, b)` in `0..1`, `colors.red`, and so on, or
`color.hsv(h, s, v)` — everywhere, text included. A name string also works:

- Minecraft's sixteen: `"red"`, `"dark_aqua"`, `"light_purple"`, ...
- Six more: `"orange"`, `"lime"`, `"cyan"`, `"purple"`, `"magenta"`, `"pink"`
- `"transparent"`, or hex (`"#ff8800"`)

`colors` holds the same names. `colors.grey` is an error that lists them all —
`colors.gray` is the spelling. For more see
[Colour helpers](#ref-color) and `color.nearest(c)`, the colour a screen or
canvas really shows, since a picture snaps to the map palette.

## Text

Text is a string, or a table of coloured runs — the full run syntax is in
[Text formatting](#ui-ui-basics--text-runs). Every call that takes text
takes both forms.

## Options tables

Calls with more than three inputs take an options table. Every field has a
default, and **the tables are strict**:

> **Gotcha:**
> an unknown field is an error that names the nearest valid one.
> `world.display{ kind = "text", colour = "red" }` stops the script with
> *no option "colour"; did you mean "color"?* — and a field of the wrong type
> is also an error.


<a id="concepts-conventions--nil-false-and-true"></a>

## `nil`, `false` and `true`

For optional settings that accept both, **`nil` removes an override and
`false` switches it off**. Each field documents whether it accepts `nil`:

- `player.visible = nil` shows the player again, because a player is visible
  by default. `player.visible = false` hides them.
- Where off is the default the two do the same: `display.glow = false` and
  `display.glow = nil` both remove the glow.
- A flag is `true`, `false` or `nil`. A number or a string is an error:
  `world.rules{ fall = 0 }` does not turn the rule off.

> **Gotcha:**
> numeric settings such as `player.speed`, `player.scale` and
> `player.reach` **require a number** — `nil` does not reset them.


## One spelling per idea

| Idea | Spelling |
| --- | --- |
| A position | `at` |
| Removing a thing | `:destroy()` |
| Stopping a timer or an event | `:cancel()` |
| A box's corners | `from` and `to` |

## Block names

Block names are Minecraft's, without `minecraft:`.

- Every block of every version is real here and stored exactly. An older
  client sees the nearest block its version has; a name even the newest
  version lacks becomes the nearest block. Write `"future_block|obsidian"` to
  pick the substitute yourself.
- Properties go in brackets, in any order and any subset:
  `"oak_trapdoor[facing=east]"`,
  `"stone_button[facing=west, face=wall]"`. Missing properties come from the
  default state; the nearest state wins.
- A name that is no block of any version (`"grassblock"`, `"stone_brick"`)
  is an error that lists the nearest real names.
- Queries (`game.block(name)`, the block an entity stands on) return `nil`
  for a name the game lacks.

Full treatment, including half-block `detail = 2` and player-head skins:
[Block reference](#world-block-reference).

## Sound names

Sound names are `"<pack>.<file>"` for your assets, or vanilla names like
`"block.note_block.hat"` — see [Sound](#ui-sound).

## Time

Time is in seconds. Only the day itself is in game units where the API says
so (see [World state](#world-world-state)).

<a id="concepts-conventions--what-a-version-lacks-is-absent"></a>

## What a version lacks is absent

`player.health`, `player.max_health`, `player.food` and `player.saturation`
are `nil`, not `0`, on a game version with no rule for them. Every Alpha node
is one (a0.1.0 has no food and no damage). Across the engine, **what a version
lacks is absent, not zero** — check for `nil` before you do arithmetic.

## Event subscriptions

`on_*` subscriptions return a connection; `connection:cancel()` stops the
subscription. `world.on_generate` and `world.on_populate` are single-handler
setters — see [The event model](#concepts-events).

## See also

- [The event model](#concepts-events) — connections, asks, deadlines.
- [Luau primer](#getting-started-luau-primer) — the language these conventions live in.
- [Block reference](#world-block-reference) — names, states, version fallbacks.
- [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions) — the per-feature matrix.

---

<!-- /concepts/rooms-and-dimensions/ -->

<a id="concepts-rooms-and-dimensions"></a>

## Rooms and dimensions

> **In short:**
> a **room** is a runtime world the script makes with
> `rooms.create{}` — a player swaps to it in place, and it gets its own
> `world`/`players`/`ui`/`game` tables. A **dimension** is a manifest-declared
> world of the server's group, saved to its own folder and reached by
> `routes.add` or `player:travel`. Rooms are for instances (a minigame, a
> per-player course); dimensions are for places (a dungeon, a nether).


## Rooms

```luau
local room = rooms.create{
    spawn_point = vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5),
    generate = function(chunk) chunk:fill(chunk.min, chunk.min + vec3(15, 0, 15), "stone") end,
}
player:move_to(room)          -- the client swaps worlds in place
room.ui.title{ title = "Welcome" }
room:message("A new round starts")   -- a chat line to everyone in this room
room.players.on_join(function(p) end)  -- fires after move_to as well
print(player.room == room)    -- rooms compare by identity; nil while moving
room:destroy()                -- when the last player left; players still in it keep the world
```

The rules:

- The global `players.on_join` fires on connect, in the main room. A room's
  own fires on each move in. `players.on_leave` matches.
- A room made by `rooms.create` runs no survival rules and no natural mob
  spawning by default (as a lite world).
- Destroy a room when the last player leaves it; players still in it keep the
  world until they go.
- Per-room game settings: `room.game.entities.cow.spawn = true` is that room's
  own value.

### A world per player

The per-player-instance pattern — `/play` builds a course in a room that
belongs to one player:

```luau
local COURSE = { vec3(0, 65, 4), vec3(4, 66, 8), vec3(-3, 68, 12) }

world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z), "stone")
end)

players.on_join(function(player)
    player.ui.title{ title = "Lobby", subtitle = "type /play", color = colors.cyan }
end)

commands.add("play", function(player)
    local mine = rooms.create{
        spawn_point = vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5),
        generate = function(chunk)
            chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z), "stone")
            for _, at in COURSE do
                chunk:set(at, "gold_block")
            end
        end,
    }
    mine.players.on_join(function(p)
        p:message("Reach every gold block.", colors.yellow)
        mine.ui.title{ title = "Go", color = colors.lime }
    end)
    mine.players.on_leave(function()
        if mine.players.count() == 0 then mine:destroy() end   -- the last one out closes it
    end)
    player:move_to(mine)
end)
```

The full tutorial is [Parkour, a room each](#guides-guide-parkour-a-room-each).

## Dimensions

A pack adds a world in `citadel.yml`, under `dimensions:`. The name is its id
inside the pack, so `dungeon` under pack `castle` is `castle:dungeon`:

```yaml
dimensions:
  dungeon:
    type: { has_skylight: false, has_ceiling: true, weather: false }
    world: script            # or "void" to leave chunks empty
```

- `type` says how the world behaves. Every field is optional and starts from
  the main world's: `has_skylight`, `has_ceiling`, `weather`, `ultrawarm`,
  `bed_works`, `respawn_anchor_works`, `coordinate_scale`, `fixed_time` and
  `effects`.
- A world with a roof looks like the Nether to a client, one with no sky and
  no roof like the End. `effects` chooses one of the three yourself.
- A dimension is a world of the server's group: it ticks after the main world
  and saves to `world_dungeon` beside it.

`world.dimension(name)` is that world's own `world` table, by dimension id or
its last part (`"dungeon"`, `"minecraft:the_nether"`):

```luau
local dungeon = world.dimension("dungeon")
dungeon.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 63, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 63, chunk.max.z), "bedrock")
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 68, chunk.max.z), "mossy_cobblestone")
end)
```

## Routes between worlds

A route is how a player gets from one world to another, with a trigger:

```luau
routes.add{
    from = "overworld",
    to = "dungeon",
    trigger = { block = "light_blue_carpet" },
    placement = { x = 7.5, y = 64, z = 7.5 },
}
```

- `trigger = { block = "light_blue_carpet" }` fires on the first tick a
  player stands in the block. `ticks = 80` makes them wait, as a Nether
  portal does.
- `placement` is where they arrive; leave it out for the dimension's spawn.
- After a trip, a player must step out of the trigger block for half a second
  before it can fire again.

`player:travel(dimension, pos)` sends a player to any world of the group, at
`pos` or its spawn — the command version of a route:

```luau
commands.add("leave", function(player)
    player:travel("overworld")
end)
```

<a id="concepts-rooms-and-dimensions--spawn-points-precisely"></a>

## Spawn points, precisely

- `spawn_point` is the position where a player arrives. `spawn` is never a
  position: it is the call `world.spawn` and the switch of an entity kind.
- `citadel.yml` has `spawn_point: [x, y, z]` for the main room;
  `rooms.create { spawn_point = vec3(..) }` sets it for a new room.
- A write to `world.spawn_point` or `room.spawn_point` changes where a player
  arrives — on a join, on a respawn, and on a move to the room — and the
  clients in the room get the new compass target.
- The write is **not stored**: after a restart the room has the point of
  `citadel.yml` or of the stored world again.
- The write does not move the chunks that stay loaded, the spawn protection,
  or the area where no mob spawns by itself. Those stay at the first point.
- `player.spawn_point` is the player's own respawn point. A bed sets the same
  value where the game has beds; a point a pack sets needs no bed. The engine
  keeps the block of the position: `vec3(20.2, 65, -7.9)` reads back as
  `vec3(20.5, 65, -7.5)`. `player.spawn_point = nil` also removes a point a
  bed set.
- Manifest keys and `rooms.create` options are checked: an unknown key is an
  error naming the field and the accepted keys.

## See also

- [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy) — the manifest's `dimensions` key.
- [A dungeon dimension](#guides-guide-a-dungeon-dimension) — the full tutorial.
- [Architecture](#concepts-architecture) — rooms and per-room tables.
- [Game data](#world-game-data) — per-room registry settings.
