<!-- /players/movement/ -->

<a id="players-movement"></a>

## Movement and cameras

> **In short:**
> the pack moves a player with `player:teleport`, `player:push`,
> `player:move_to` (another room) and `player:travel` (another world of the
> group); the body has writable `speed`, `scale` and `reach`. A player can
> ride anything with an id the client sees. The camera system — `fixed`,
> `free`, `orbit`, `chase` and the easing `camera.path` — replaces what they
> look out of, for cutscenes and follow shots. Clicks and held keys arrive as
> events.


## Teleporting, and between worlds

Three calls move a player outright, at three scales.

| Call | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| [`player:teleport(pos, rotation?)`](#ref-Player-teleport) | To a position; yaw and pitch left out keep the way they face. |
| [`player:move_to(room)`](#ref-Player-move_to) | To another room; the client swaps worlds in place. |
| [`player:travel(dimension, pos?)`](#ref-Player-travel) | To another world of the group, at `pos` or its spawn. |

```luau
player:teleport(vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5))              -- rotation left out: keeps facing
player:teleport(SPAWN, { yaw = 0, pitch = 0 })   -- faces south, level
player:move_to(room)                              -- the client swaps worlds in place
```

Rotation is a `BodyRotation` in degrees: 0 yaw faces south, 90 west; positive
pitch tips down. `player.room` is nil while the player moves between rooms;
rooms compare by identity. Rooms and dimensions are covered in
[Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions).

## Pushing and the body

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| [`player.speed`](#ref-Player-speed) | Walk speed as a multiple of normal; 0 pins them. |
| [`player.scale`](#ref-Player-scale) | 1/16 to 16; 1.20.5 and later, older clients stay as they are. |
| [`player.reach`](#ref-Player-reach) | How far a block can be clicked or dug, 0 to 64 blocks (4.5 by default); 1.20.5 and later. Measured from the camera when there is one. |
| `player.can_fly` | May fly in a mode that cannot. |

[`player:push(velocity)`](#ref-Player-push) is a shove in blocks per tick, on
top of what they are doing.

> **Gotcha:**
> Numeric settings such as `player.speed`, `player.scale` and
> `player.reach` require a number; `nil` does not reset them.


The anticheat rule watches what each Java client claims. `player:push` and a
movement effect (`speed`, `jump_boost`, `levitation`, `slow_falling`,
`dolphins_grace`) exempt the player while they last, and `player:teleport` is
always allowed. A pack that moves players in any other way turns `anticheat`
off: `world.rules{ anticheat = false }` (see
[World state](#world-world-state)).

## Looking

- `player.rotation` — degrees: `yaw` sideways, `pitch` up or down; live, read
  only.
- [`player:look()`](#ref-Player-look) — the unit vector the player faces.
- [`player:look_at(pos)`](#ref-Player-look_at) — turns the player's head to a
  point, where they stand.
- `player.eye` — where the player's view is from, as a vec3: the camera they
  look out of, or their own eyes.

## Riding

| Call | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| [`player:ride(thing, opts?)`](#ref-Player-ride) | Seats the player; `opts` is `{ seat = number?, locked = boolean? }`. |
| [`player:dismount()`](#ref-Player-dismount) | Gets the player off; sneaking does the same, as off a horse. |

- Seat 1 drives a vehicle; `locked` keeps a sneak from getting them off.
- `ride` returns `false` when somebody sits in that seat; it keeps the current
  ride on failure.
- It works immediately after creating the target. Repeating the same ride
  keeps the seat; no delay or extra movement is needed.
- `player.sitting` is true while the player sits on something; live.

```luau
player:ride(c)                                -- seat 1: W and S throttle, A and D steer
friend:ride(c, { seat = 2, locked = true })   -- locked: sneaking does not get them off
```

`player:ride(thing)` seats a player on anything with an `id` the client sees —
a vehicle, a model display, a display, a hitbox, an npc. The pack moves these
things; see [Displays](#ui-displays) for seats, vehicles and ridden
displays.

### Cameras and seats

`free` and `orbit` cameras seat the player, hidden and locked, on an engine
seat — so the two systems collide:

- Assigning `free` or `orbit` while the player rides is an error. The previous
  ride and camera remain intact.
- `player:ride` while a `free`/`orbit` camera is active is an error; clear
  `player.camera` or switch to `chase` first.
- For the driver's own eyes, seat them — `player:ride(car, { locked = true })`
  and `player.camera = nil`. A chase camera and a seat go together: the body
  is in the car and the view is behind it.

## The camera system

A camera is a value you put on a player: `player.camera = cam`, or `nil` or
`false` for their own eyes. There are four kinds, and
[`camera.path`](#players-movement--camera-paths) eases from shot to shot:

| Mode | What the player sees | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fixed` | A shot from a point (`at`) or of a target (`from`), with optional `look_at`. | works in every mode |
| `free` | Mouse look from a point — not free flight. | 1.19.4 |
| `orbit` | The eyes `distance` blocks behind `follow`, `height` over its feet, opposite the look direction. | 1.19.4 |
| `chase` | The view from behind a car: behind `follow`, `height` over it, heading its way, `pitch` degrees down. | 1.19.4 |

### fixed

- `fixed` takes either `from` or `at` with optional `look_at`. Combining them
  is an error.
- `fixed{ from = target }` exposes `from`; `fixed{ at = point }` exposes `at`
  and `look_at`.
- A player or thing as `look_at` (a model too) is followed by its head.
- The player still walks and sees their own body: set `player.speed = 0` for a
  cutscene. Do not use `gamemode = 3`.

### free and orbit

Both seat the player, hidden and locked, on an engine seat, and both need
1.19.4 (`player:supports("display")`). `free` means mouse look from a point,
not free flight, and exposes `at`. `orbit` puts the eyes `distance` blocks
behind `follow` (anything with an id), `height` over its feet, opposite the
look direction, and in front of walls.

### chase

The engine keeps the eyes `distance` blocks behind `follow` (a model, a
vehicle, an npc, a player), `height` over it, looking the way it heads and
`pitch` degrees down, and in front of walls. It moves with `follow` in the
same step, so `follow` does not shake in the view. 1.19.4 and later.

> **Tip:**
> Use this to follow a thing a pack moves. Do not move a display of
> your own behind it and look out of that: the two are sent as two things and
> drift against each other. A barrier does not pull it in.


A chase camera is aimed as its `follow` is. Submit the target's current
position; the engine keeps its picture, seats and camera moving together.
Custom physics needs no future-position simulation or client timing constants.

Chase and orbit move as their `follow` moves, with its `glide` and `lead`.
Smooth movement needs Java 1.20.2 or later.

### Fields, sharing and lifetime

- Each mode exposes only its relevant fields: `orbit` and `chase` expose
  `follow`, `distance` and `height`, and `chase` adds `pitch`. `mode` and
  `from` are read-only. Ineffective fields are errors.
- Distances must be finite and nonnegative, and angles/heights finite.
- `cam.look_at = nil` removes the point or thing a camera looks at; `false`
  does the same. Reading `look_at` returns the point or target handle; reading
  `follow` returns the followed handle. A removed target reads `nil`.
- One camera can be on many players. A change (`cam.at`, `cam.distance`,
  `cam.follow = other`) shows on all of them next tick.
- Ending the camera, or leaving the room, gives back body, feet and eyes.
- Free/orbit cameras hide the body independently of potion effects. Ending
  one preserves those effects and any ride assigned after the camera's seat.
- Destroying a camera's source or follow/look-at target ends the camera
  automatically. A remote camera keeps terrain loaded around both the view
  and the player's body, including when looking out of another player.
- Creating a target and assigning its camera in the same callback needs no
  delay. The engine spawns the target before selecting it and switches to a
  replacement camera before removing the previous one.

> **Note:**
> A server cannot set the field of view, force third person or hide
> the hotbar.


<a id="players-movement--camera-paths"></a>

## Camera paths

`camera.path` is a fixed camera that eases from shot to shot. Each shot after
the first takes its own `duration`, or the path's (5 seconds by default). It
returns the camera and a handle with `cancel()`.

```luau
local cam, run = camera.path({
    { at = vec3(0, 80, 30), look_at = vec3(0, 64, 0) },
    { at = vec3(40, 70, -10), look_at = vec3(0, 64, 0), duration = 5 },
    { at = vec3(10, 66, -20), look_at = vec3(0, 65, 0), duration = 3, easing = "out" },
}, { easing = "in_out", on_done = function() player.camera = nil player.speed = 1 end })
player.speed = 0
player.camera = cam
```

A shot `{ at = player }` is the player's eyes, looking where they look. A
player or thing in a shot is read when the shot starts:

```luau
camera.path({
    { at = vec3(0, 90, 60), look_at = vec3(0, 64, 0) },     -- over the map
    { at = vec3(4, 67, 4), look_at = player, duration = 4 }, -- down to them, standing there
    { at = player, duration = 2 },                           -- into their eyes
}, { on_done = function() player.camera = nil player.speed = 1 end })
```

- End on `{ at = player }` so removing the camera does not jump.
- To hold a shot, repeat it.

A camera moves 20 times a second. From 1.20.2 the client glides between moves.

## Input: clicks and keys

- One click is one event. A held button repeats every 200 ms — that is not a
  click.
- A left click on the world carries the block under the crosshair, up to five
  blocks from the eyes.
- On a pack server, a click never changes the world.
- `player.input` reads keys on foot from 1.21.2. Before 1.21.2, a client
  reports keys only while it rides.
- The first `players.on_chat` takes over chat in its room. Each line is then
  said once as `<name> text`, unless a listener returns `false`. With several
  packs, each gets every line; it is still said once or not at all.

Clicks arrive through `players.on_click` with a `hit` table — the button, the
slot, and the player, entity, block and face the click met. The event model
and the full catalog are in [The event model](#concepts-events) and the
[Event catalog](#appendix-event-catalog).

## See also

- [Displays](#ui-displays) — vehicles, seats and ridden displays.
- [Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions) — `move_to` and `travel` in context.
- [World state](#world-world-state) — the `anticheat` rule and the rest of `world.rules`.
- [The event model](#concepts-events) — `on_click`, `on_chat` and connections.
- [Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle) — join, leave and the session.

<!-- /players/inventory/ -->

<a id="players-inventory"></a>

## Inventory and items

> **In short:**
> an item is a name (`"stone"`) or a table (`{ item = "arrow",
> count = 16 }`) carrying its meta. `player:give`, `take`, `inventory`,
> `count`, `held` and `set_held` work on inventory stacks — given items merge,
> hotbar first, and overflow is dropped, not duplicated. A pack can mint its
> own items with `id`, give heads a face with `skin`, fill the four armour
> slots with `wear`, and add crafting recipes.


## An item is a name or a table

An `ItemSpec` is a string or an `ItemTable`; every call that takes an item
takes either form.

```luau
"potion"                             -- just the item
{
    item = "potion",                 -- required in a table
    count = 2,                       -- 1 by default
    name = "Lime Laser",             -- text; never italic unless it says so
    lore = { "a laser follows you" },  -- lines under the name, grey unless they say; one text is one line
    color = colors.lime,             -- a potion's liquid
    dye = color(0.2, 0.5, 1),        -- leather armour's colour
    glint = true,                    -- the enchanted shine, with no enchantment
    canvas = c,                      -- a filled map of that canvas; then `item` may be left out
}
{ item = "player_head", skin = player.name }   -- a head with a face; see "head items"
```

With `canvas = c`, the item becomes `filled_map` unless you name another. The
table fields are the `ItemMeta`:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `count` | How many in the stack; 1 by default. |
| `name` | Text; never italic unless it says so. |
| `lore` | One line or a list of lines, grey unless they say otherwise. |
| `color` | A potion's liquid colour; 1.11 and later. |
| `dye` | Leather armour's colour. |
| `glint` | The enchanted shine, with no enchantment. |
| `canvas` | A filled map of that canvas: what the item *is*, so `item` may be left out. |
| `id` | A pack's own item (below). |
| `damage` | The wear a tool has taken; 0 is new. |
| `model` | The item model a 1.21.4+ client draws: `assets/<pack>/items/<model>.json`. |
| `skin` | The face a `"player_head"` item shows. On any other item it is an error. |

## give, take, count, inventory, held

| Call | Returns | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`player:give(item: ItemSpec)`](#ref-Player-give) | — | Puts a stack in the inventory. |
| [`player:take(item: ItemMatch, count?)`](#ref-Player-take) | number | Removes up to `count` (1 unless you say), the hand first. |
| [`player:count(item: ItemMatch)`](#ref-Player-count) | number | How many the player carries, across every slot. |
| [`player:inventory()`](#ref-Player-inventory) | `{ InventorySlot }` | One `{ item, count }` row per filled slot. |
| [`player:held()`](#ref-Player-held) | `InventorySlot?` | The stack in hand, or nil. |
| [`player:set_held(item?)`](#ref-Player-set_held) | — | Replaces the stack in hand; nil or false empties it. |
| [`player:hotbar(slots)`](#ref-Player-hotbar) | — | Replaces the nine hotbar slots; a missing index is empty. |
| [`player:set_slot(n)`](#ref-Player-set_slot) | — | Selects hotbar slot 1..9. |

The give/take contract:

- A given stack merges into existing stacks, hotbar first.
- What does not fit is dropped from the give, not duplicated.
- `take` takes up to `count` of what matches, the hand first, and answers how
  many it took.

A stack as a script reads it is an `InventorySlot` — `{ item, count }`, plus
`id` for a pack item and `damage` for a worn tool. An `ItemMatch` (what
`take`, `count`, a recipe's ingredient accept) is a name or a table matching
the fields it names; see [pack items](#players-inventory--pack-items-id) below.

## The player's own window

Clicks in the player's own window work as in the game, all seven click modes
included.

- A pack's own menu over the inventory is `player.ui.menu{}` — see
  [Menus](#ui-menus).
- A chest's stacks are [`world.container`](#ref-World-container) — `items()`
  to read them, `take`/`put` to move them.

<a id="players-inventory--pack-items-id"></a>

## Pack items: `id`

`id` makes an item the pack's own. The client draws the base item with its
`name` and `lore`. The server knows it by its `id` everywhere, across
restarts.

Where a call *finds* an item (`take`, `count`, a recipe, a container):

- A name matches the plain item only.
- A table matches by the fields it names. `{ id = "x" }` is that pack item,
  whatever its base.
- A pack item stacks only with the same pack item. Only your own recipes (see
  [recipes](#players-inventory--recipes)) take it.

`id` is a lower-case word, kept under your pack's name. Your ids read back
bare, another pack's as `"pack:word"`. Either spelling works. `model` is the
item definition that clients from 1.21.4 draw — `model = "copper_ingot"` is
`assets/<pack>/items/copper_ingot.json`; `game.items.define` sets it. Set it
by hand only for a file you shipped in `assets/`.

`damage` is a tool's wear bar. `0` is new. Past its maximum, the tool breaks.
Read it from `held()`; write it with `set_held`.

The base item sets the look and what it does in a hand. A pack pickaxe mines.
A pack block places that block, unless its `id` names a block of yours (see
[Custom blocks](#world-custom-blocks)).

## Items with their own pictures

`game.items.define` returns an item table for anywhere an item goes:

```luau
local ingot = game.texture(16, 16)       -- a picture drawn in code, or a PNG file in the pack
ingot:rect(2, 6, 12, 5, "#d9822b")
ingot:rect(3, 6, 10, 1, "#f0a860")
local COPPER = game.items.define {
    name = "copper_ingot",                -- its id; the pack's namespace is added
    texture = ingot,                      -- or "textures/copper_ingot.png"
    label = "Copper Ingot",               -- its name; left out, "Copper Ingot" from the id anyway
    lore = { "Smelted from copper ore" },
}
player:give(COPPER)                       -- { ..., count = 4 } for more: COPPER is a plain table
player:take(COPPER, 2)                    -- an item table matches by its id
game.recipes.smelt{ input = ORE, result = COPPER }
```

- `looks` is the vanilla item underneath. Clients below 1.21.4 draw it. It
  sets what the item does in a hand.
  - Default: `paper` (stacks to 64, does nothing).
  - With `stack = 1`, the default is `carrot_on_a_stick`.
  - Name a pickaxe for a tool that mines, a sword for one that hits.
- `texture` is drawn flat in a hand and in the inventory. Vanilla items are 16
  by 16.
- Define items while the pack loads.

A texture's colours are any colour the API takes; `colors.transparent` is
see-through. Where a call takes a texture, a string names a PNG file in the
pack.

## Head items

A `"player_head"` item shows a face when you give it a `skin`. It works
everywhere an item goes: a hotbar slot, a menu, a hand, a display, a chest.

```luau
player:hotbar{ [9] = { item = "player_head", skin = player.name, name = "Profile" } }
player:give{ item = "player_head", skin = player.name }
player:give{ item = "player_head", skin = { value = "ewogICJ0aW1l...", signature = "..." } }
```

- `skin` takes the same forms as a placed head: a player's name, or
  `{ value = , signature = }`.
- The name of a player in the room uses the skin they joined with. This costs
  nothing.
- Any other name is looked up from Mojang once, in the background:
  - Clients from 1.20.5 look the name up themselves and show the face.
  - Older clients show a plain head the first time. Make the item again (for
    example, set the hotbar on the next join) and they show the face.
  - A name with no account shows a plain head and logs one line.
- The face stays with the item: in the player's file, in a chest, on the
  ground.
- `skin` on any other item is an error.
- Clients from 1.7 see the face. Bedrock clients see a plain head.

## Armour: `wear`

```luau
player:wear{ head = "iron_helmet", chest = { item = "leather_chestplate", dye = colors.blue },
             legs = "chainmail_leggings", feet = "golden_boots" }
player:wear{ head = "carved_pumpkin" }   -- replaces all four: the three left out are bare
player:wear{}                            -- all off
npc:wear{ chest = "diamond_chestplate" } -- the same on an npc
```

`wear` fills the armour slots of a player or an npc. Each piece is an item
(see above), so `dye` and `glint` work. The `Worn` table has `head`, `chest`,
`legs` and `feet`, each an `ItemSpec`.

- The inventory, the body and the armour bar show the pieces. Armour does not
  reduce damage yet.
- Nearby clients draw the pieces from 1.8.
- Any item goes on the head. Other slots draw only armour made for them.
- On a pack server, only the pack takes armour off.
- On a survival server, these are the real armour slots. `wear` replaces their
  contents, and the player can take pieces off.

<a id="players-inventory--recipes"></a>

## Recipes

Add recipes at the top of `main.luau`, while the pack loads. A reload replaces
the pack's recipe list.

```luau
game.recipes.shaped{
    pattern = { "CCC", "CMC", "CCC" },    -- 1 to 3 rows of 1 to 3 letters; a space is an empty cell
    keys = { C = { id = "copper_cable" }, M = "iron_block" },
    result = macerator.item,              -- an item, with its count: { ..., count = 4 }
}
game.recipes.shapeless{ items = { "coal", "coal", { id = "iron_dust" } }, result = STEEL }
game.recipes.smelt{ input = { id = "copper_dust" }, result = COPPER }
```

- An ingredient is an item to match (see [pack items](#players-inventory--pack-items-id)): a
  name, or `{ id = ... }`.
- A shaped recipe matches anywhere it fits in the grid, and mirrored.
- The 2x2 inventory grid takes recipes that fit in it. The crafting table
  takes all.
- Vanilla recipes are checked first. A pack adds recipes and never removes
  one.
- A furnace smelts a pack item only through a `smelt` recipe. No pack item
  burns as fuel.

## How clients show the meta

The engine writes the meta in each client's format: NBT tags up to 1.20.4,
data components from 1.20.5. A field a version cannot show is left out. A
potion's colour needs 1.11. No other field has a version limit.

```luau
player:give{ item = "potion", name = "Lime Laser", color = colors.lime, lore = { "30 seconds" } }
npc:hold{ item = "potion", color = colors.lime }
world.display{ kind = "item", item = { item = "potion", color = colors.lime }, at = vec3(0.5, 66, 2.5) }
```

## See also

- [Menus](#ui-menus) — `player.ui.menu{}` over the inventory, hotbar menus.
- [Game data](#world-game-data) — `game.item(name)` and the game's own items.
- [Displays](#ui-displays) — items posed in the world (`context`, `worn`, `held`).
- [Custom blocks](#world-custom-blocks) — a pack block whose `id` names a block.
- [Kits](#cookbook-cookbook-kits) — giving sets of items in practice.

<!-- /players/visibility/ -->

<a id="players-visibility"></a>

## Visibility and teams

> **In short:**
> a player sees others in their room who are in view. Two
> settings remove a player's body from a client: `player.visible = false`
> (from everyone) and `viewer:hide(player)` (from that viewer only). The
> teams pattern pairs `hide`/`show` with `player.data.team`. Hidden is not the
> `invisibility` effect, the tab list still shows hidden players, and a new
> session resets everything.


## Who sees whom

A player sees others in their room who are in view. Two settings remove a
player's body from a client:

```luau
player.visible = false        -- from everyone; true or nil brings it back
viewer:hide(player)           -- from this viewer only; viewer:show(player) undoes it
viewer:can_see(player)        -- what the two add up to
```

| Setting | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| [`player.visible = false`](#ref-Player-visible) | No other player is sent this body. `true` or `nil` shows the body again. |
| [`viewer:hide(player)`](#ref-Player-hide) | This viewer stops seeing `player`. |
| [`viewer:show(player)`](#ref-Player-show) | This viewer sees `player` again after a `hide`. |
| [`viewer:can_see(player)`](#ref-Player-can_see) | True unless `player` is not visible or is hidden from this viewer. |

> **Note:**
> `player.visible = nil` shows the player again, because a player is
> visible by default.


## Two patterns

The source's own examples — a lobby, and teams.

A lobby where nobody sees anyone:

```luau
-- a lobby where nobody sees anyone
room.players.on_join(function(p) p.visible = false end)
room.players.on_leave(function(p) p.visible = true end)
```

Teams: each side sees only its own. The loops pair every player against every
player — [`players.list()`](#ref-Players-list) returns every player in the
room — and `data.team` decides:

```luau
-- teams: each side sees only its own
for _, a in players.list() do
    for _, b in players.list() do
        if a.data.team ~= b.data.team then a:hide(b) else a:show(b) end
    end
end
```

Run the pairing again whenever a player joins, leaves or changes team. The
cookbook walks the full pattern in [Teams](#cookbook-cookbook-teams).

## What hidden means

- A hidden player is gone from that client: no body, name, armour or hitbox.
- The `invisibility` effect differs: it shows armour and the held item.
- The tab list still shows hidden players.
- Free/orbit cameras hide the body too, independently of potion effects (see
  [Movement and cameras](#players-movement)).

> **Gotcha:**
> Hiding a player is not the `invisibility` effect. The effect
> leaves armour and the held item drawn; `hide` and `visible = false` remove
> body, name, armour and hitbox from the client entirely.


## How long it lasts

Both settings last across rooms. `hide` is by account — it survives the other
player's rejoin. Only a new session resets: nothing hidden, and `visible` is
true again.

## See also

- [Teams](#cookbook-cookbook-teams) — the full teams pattern with `player.data`.
- [Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle) — sessions, joins and leaves.
- [Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions) — a player sees others in their room.
- [Movement and cameras](#players-movement) — `free`/`orbit` cameras hide the body too.

<!-- /players/health/ -->

<a id="players-health"></a>

## Health and damage

> **In short:**
> `player.health`, `max_health`, `food` and `saturation` are
> `nil`, not `0`, on a game version with no rule for them. The maximum is 1
> to 1024, lasts for the session and every Java client draws its hearts. On a
> pack server only `damage` and `health` hurt a player; PvP is the pack's job
> through `hit.player` in `players.on_click`, and `world.rules` switches the
> engine's own damage on.


## nil, not zero

`player.health`, `player.max_health`, `player.food` and `player.saturation`
are `nil`, not `0`, on a game version with no rule for them. Every Alpha node
is one (a0.1.0 has no food and no damage). Across the engine, what a version
lacks is absent, not zero.

`health` is always the health of one individual now. `max_health` is always
the most it can be. This is the same for a player, for an entity in the world
and for a kind (a kind has `max_health` only).

## The maximum: `max_health`

| Write | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `player.max_health = n` (1 to 1024) | Sets the most health they can have. |
| `player.max_health = nil` | Gives the game's own (20) back. |
| Another type, or out of range | An error. |
| Any write, on a version with no damage rules | An error. |

- A lower maximum takes `player.health` down to it. A higher maximum does not
  heal.
- The maximum lasts for the session, also across rooms and deaths. Set it in
  `players.on_join`.
- Every Java client (1.7 to 26.3) draws the hearts of the maximum. A Bedrock
  client draws no health today.

## health, food and saturation

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `player.health` | Their health now, 0 to `max_health`; `nil` where the game version has no damage rules. |
| `player.max_health` | The most health they can have: 20 unless a pack set it. |
| `player.food` | 0..20, or nil where the game version has no food bar. |
| `player.saturation` | The food saturation, or nil where the game version has no food bar. |
| `player.dead` | True while the player is on the death screen. |

`player.health` is writable: set outright, no flash; `0` is a death; a number
above `max_health` stops there. Food, regeneration and peaceful healing stop
at the maximum. A respawn fills to it.

## Hurting a player

- On a pack server, only `damage` and `health` hurt a player. Creative and
  spectator players take no damage.
- [`player:damage(amount)`](#ref-Player-damage) is a hit in half-hearts: the
  flash, the sound, the resistance window. It returns `false` on a version
  with no damage rules.
- [`player:kill()`](#ref-Player-kill) kills the player; it returns `false` on
  a version with no damage rules.
- At zero health the player dies. `players.on_death` fires with cause
  `"other"` (a pack's own `player:damage`), and the client shows the respawn
  screen.
- On a pack server a death drops and clears nothing. The hotbar is a menu,
  not an inventory.

> **Note:**
> A pack's own `player:damage` call is not asked about —
> `players.on_damage` never sees it, in this pack or another. Damage the
> engine itself deals is asked first: `false` refuses it, `hit` carries the
> amount, cause, attacker and mob kind. The ask model, its two-millisecond
> deadline and the `hit` fields are in [The event model](#concepts-events).


## Death and respawn events

`players.on_death` receives the player (nil once they have left), the cause,
the broadcast English death line as `message`, and `by` — the player who hit
or shot them, or `nil`:

| `cause` | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `fall`, `drown`, `suffocate`, `void`, `lava`, `fire`, `cactus`, `starve` | The environment. |
| `attack` | A mob's or a player's hit. |
| `shot` | An arrow. |
| `blast`, `magic` | An explosion, magic. |
| `other` | A pack's own `player:damage`. |

`players.on_respawn` fires when they come back; a respawn fills health to the
maximum. The session facts — one player value, `data` kept ten seconds — are
in [Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle).

## Room rules: damage, fall, survival

A `mode: full` server has them all on; a pack can turn one off. The
`world.rules` facts in full are on [World state](#world-world-state) — what
matters for health:

- A rule is `true` or `false`. A rule left out keeps its value, and so does a
  rule written as `nil`. Any other value is an error:
  `world.rules{ fall = 0 }` and `world.rules{ fall = "off" }` stop the script.
- `survival` gives the room to the engine's survival, as on a `mode: full`
  server: it turns on `fall`, `damage`, `hunger`, `anticheat` and
  `day_cycle`; a death drops the inventory, and the respawn button works.
- Anticheat checks each Java client's claims: a hit on something the player
  does not look at, or faster than 20 per second, does not land; a claim to
  stand on nothing does not prevent fall damage.

Anything that is not a rule is the pack's job: `player:damage` for a hit,
`player.health` to heal, `players.on_death` and `players.on_respawn` for what
happens next, and `hit.player` in `players.on_click` for one player hitting
another:

```luau
world.rules{ fall = true }
players.on_click(function(player, hit)
    if hit.button == "left" and hit.player then
        hit.player:damage(2)
        hit.player:push(player:look() * 0.5 + vec3(0, 0.3, 0))
    end
end)
```

## See also

- [Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle) — join, leave, death and respawn delivery.
- [World state](#world-world-state) — every `world.rules` entry.
- [The event model](#concepts-events) — the `on_damage` ask and its deadline.
- [Movement and cameras](#players-movement) — `push` and the anticheat rule.
- [Inventory](#players-inventory) — what a survival death drops.

<!-- /players/permissions/ -->

<a id="players-permissions"></a>

## Permissions

> **In short:**
> a permission node is a dotted name. `casino.*` covers
> everything under `casino`, `*` covers everything, and a leading `-` takes a
> node away; the most specific node wins. Groups are defined in the pack's
> `citadel.yml` under `permissions:` — every player is in `default` — and the
> script puts players in groups with `player:add_group`, which lasts until
> they leave. Gate your own commands with `player:has`.


## Node syntax

| Node | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| `casino.play` | Exactly this node. |
| `casino.*` | Everything under `casino`. |
| `*` | Everything. |
| `-casino.debug` | Takes the node away. |

The resolution rules:

- A leading `-` takes a node away.
- The most specific node wins. Between two equally specific nodes, the `-`
  wins.

So `"casino.*"` plus `"-casino.debug"` in one group's nodes grants the whole
`casino` tree except `casino.debug`.

## Groups in citadel.yml

The pack's `citadel.yml` defines groups. Every player is in `default`, and a
group may inherit the nodes of others with `inherits`:

```yaml
permissions:
  default: { nodes: [casino.play] }
  vip:     { inherits: [default], nodes: [casino.vip] }
  staff:   { inherits: [vip], nodes: [minecraft.command.gamemode, "casino.*", "-casino.debug"] }
```

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `nodes` | The group's permission nodes. |
| `inherits` | The other groups this group inherits from. |

The `staff` group shows all three node forms at once: an exact node, a
wildcard, and a negation — and it inherits `vip`, which inherits `default`.

## Putting players in groups

| Call | Returns | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`player:add_group(group)`](#ref-Player-add_group) | — | Puts the player in a group until they leave. |
| [`player:remove_group(group)`](#ref-Player-remove_group) | — | Takes the player out of a group. |
| [`player:groups()`](#ref-Player-groups) | `{ string }` | The player's groups; `default` is not listed. |

- Groups last until the player leaves. Store them and re-add them in
  `players.on_join` — see [Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle).
- `add_group` errors on a group citadel.yml does not define.

## Operators

Server operators — the `operators:` list in the **server's** `citadel.yml`,
by uuid — have every node. Minefort writes the server owner there.

## Checking permissions

Gate your own commands with [`player:has(node)`](#ref-Player-has): true if
the player's groups give them the node (and always true for an operator).

```luau
if player:has("casino.vip") then
    -- the node the vip group grants
end
```

Commands take a `permission` option directly — without the node, a player
does not see or run the command (see [Commands](#systems-commands)). One name,
several shapes: calls with one name, such as `"tekkit"` and
`"tekkit give <item:word>"`, make one command, and each shape has its own
permission. The engine's `/help` lists every command a player may run.

## Merging and errors

- Same-name groups in two packs merge.
- The server stops on a group that inherits an undefined group, or on a group
  named `operator`.

> **Gotcha:**
> A group named `operator` — or an `inherits` pointing at a group
> that is not defined — stops the server at load. Name groups anything else.


## See also

- [Commands](#systems-commands) — the `permission` option of `commands.add`.
- [Server settings](#systems-server-settings) — the server's `citadel.yml` and the `operators` list.
- [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy) — the pack's `citadel.yml` manifest.
- [Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle) — re-adding groups in `on_join`.

<!-- /ui/ui-basics/ -->

<a id="ui-ui-basics"></a>

## UI basics

> **In short:**
> the text surfaces of a player's screen — chat, titles, the
> action bar, boss bars, the sidebar and the tab list. The `ui` global (or
> `room.ui`) addresses everyone in a room; `player.ui` holds the same calls for
> one player. Every call takes the same text: a string, a table of styled runs,
> or a function of the time. The run syntax, the colour spellings and the
> moving-text rules are documented here once and used by every other surface.


## One set of calls, everyone or one player

Titles, chat, the action bar, boss bars, the sidebar and the tab list are one
family of calls. `ui` (or `room.ui`) reaches everyone in a room; `player.ui`
holds the same calls for one player — "everyone" below is one player on
`player.ui`.

| Call | Returns | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`ui.title{ title, subtitle, color, fade_in, stay, fade_out }`](#ref-Ui-title) | — | Title and subtitle; fades and stay in seconds |
| [`ui.actionbar(text, color?)`](#ref-Ui-actionbar) | — | The line above the hotbar |
| [`ui.bossbar{ title, color, progress }`](#ref-Ui-bossbar) | `Bar` | A boss bar; progress 0..1 |
| [`ui.sidebar{ title, lines }`](#ref-Ui-sidebar) | — | The sidebar; `nil` or `false` removes it |
| [`ui.tab{ header, footer }`](#ref-Ui-tab) | — | The tab list's header and footer |
| [`message(text, color?)`](#ref-message) | — | A chat line to everyone in the main room |
| [`player:message(text, color?)`](#ref-Player-message) | — | A chat line to this player alone |

## Chat lines

Chat is not part of the screen, so it is not in `ui`. `message(text, color)`
sends a chat line to everyone in the main room; `player:message(text, color)`
sends one to a single player. In both, `color` is for the words that did not
pick a colour of their own.

## Titles and subtitles

```luau
ui.title{ title = "DROP", subtitle = "hands up", color = "red",
    fade_in = 0.1, stay = 0.7, fade_out = 0.4 }   -- fades and stay are in seconds
```

`title` and `subtitle` are text (see [Text runs](#ui-ui-basics--text-runs)); the call's
`color` colours the words with no colour of their own.

## The action bar

```luau
ui.actionbar("Round 2", "gold")                            -- everyone in the room
player.ui.actionbar("Bet 50 · Chips 1200", "light_purple") -- one player
```

The line above the hotbar; the call's `color` is for the words that did not
pick one.

## Boss bars

```luau
local bar = ui.bossbar{ title = "Race starts in 30 s", color = "purple", progress = 1 }
bar.title, bar.progress, bar.color, bar.visible   -- live; progress 0..1
bar.visible = false    -- off every screen; true or nil shows it again
bar:destroy()
local mine = player.ui.bossbar{ title = "Your horse: Lightning" }   -- one player's bar, the same handle
```

The [`Bar`](#ref-Bar) handle's live fields:

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `bar.title` | Reads back the words; takes any text |
| `bar.progress` | How full the bar is, 0 to 1 |
| `bar.color` | From the bar's own closed set; anything else is white |
| `bar.visible` | `false` takes it off every screen; `true` or `nil` shows it again |

A boss bar needs the `bossbar` feature: clients from 1.9.

> **Gotcha:**
> 1.8 has no boss bars. A 1.8 client shows the title on its action
> bar.


A bar's colour is its own closed set: `pink`, `blue`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`,
`purple`, `white`. It is not a colour value and has no hex form; anything else
is white.

> **Note:**
> a boss bar re-sends on every change. A late joiner sees it at the
> next change.


## The sidebar

```luau
ui.sidebar{ title = "INDIGO", lines = { "Chips  1200", "Bet  50", "", "Roulette" } }  -- everyone in the room
player.ui.sidebar{ title = "INDIGO", lines = { ... } }   -- one player; lines run top to bottom
ui.sidebar(false)     -- removes the sidebar, as nil does; player.ui.sidebar(false) for one player
```

> **Gotcha:**
> the sidebar sends only changed lines. Repeated lines are fine;
> long or extra lines are trimmed.


## The tab list

```luau
ui.tab{ header = "INDIGO", footer = "minefort.com" }
```

Sets the player list's header and footer. Every title, line, header and footer
on this page is text: `{ "Chips ", { "1200", color = "gold" } }`.

<a id="ui-ui-basics--text-runs"></a>

## Text runs

Every call that shows words takes text: chat, the action bar, titles, kicks,
boss bars, the sidebar, the tab header and footer, item name and lore, menu
titles, text displays, npc speech and name tags. Text is a string or a table:

```luau
"Lap 2/3"                                                   -- words, in the surface's own colour
{ "1st", color = colors.gold, bold = true }                 -- one styled run
{ "Lap ", { "2", color = "white", bold = true }, "/3", color = "gray" }
player.ui.sidebar{ title = { "KART", color = "gold", bold = true }, lines = {
    { { "1. ", color = "yellow" }, "Mario" },
    { "2. Luigi", color = color(0.4, 1, 0.4) },
} }
```

- A table's entries are its **runs**: strings or tables.
- Its named fields style all its runs: `color`, `bold`, `italic`, `underline`,
  `strike`. A run's own style wins.
- A call's own colour (`player:message(text, color)`, `ui.actionbar(text, color)`,
  a title's `color`, a text display's `color`, `npc:say(text, color)`) colours
  the words with no colour.
- A live text field (`bar.title`, a display's `text`) reads back the words.

> **Gotcha:**
> any other field is an error that names the five style fields.


## Text that moves

A text table's `effect` styles **every letter**. A whole text can also be a
**function of the time**.

- The sidebar, boss bars, the tab list and text displays recompute them ten
  times a second. Other surfaces show the frame at send time.
- Only what moves is recomputed: a sidebar's still lines are read when it is
  set. To change one, set the sidebar again.
- A moving text table shown to many players at once, such as one title table
  every player's sidebar uses, is worked out once a frame.

```luau
-- a rainbow, one cycle a second: letter, its number i of n, and t = time.now()
local rainbow = function(letter, i, n, t) return { color = color.hsv((i - 1) / n + t, 1, 1) } end
p.ui.sidebar { title = { "KART", effect = rainbow, bold = true } }

local sparkle = function(letter, i, n, t)
    if (i + math.floor(t * 8)) % 4 == 0 then
        return { color = "white", bold = true }
    end
    return { color = "gold" }                -- or nil: the letter as it was
end
world.display { kind = "text", at = vec3(0.5, 70, 0.5), text = { "WINNER", effect = sparkle } }

-- a text that is a function of the time: rebuilt every frame
ui.sidebar { title = "Lobby", lines = {
    function(t) return { "Next race in " .. math.max(0, math.ceil(race_at - t)), color = "yellow" } end,
} }
```

An effect returns a style (`color`, `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `strike`,
plus `text` to replace the letter, `""` to hide it) or `nil`. More effects,
each one line:

```luau
-- colours across the letters, flowing at `speed` cycles a second
function(_, i, n, t) return { color = color.gradient(list, (i - 1) / n - t * speed, true) } end
-- the whole text in one colour at a time, `speed` times through the list a second
function(_, _, _, t) return { color = list[math.floor(t * speed * #list) % #list + 1] } end
-- the letters appear one after another, `rate` a second from `from = time.now()`
function(_, i, _, t) if i > (t - from) * rate then return { text = "" } end end
```

> **Gotcha:**
> an effect or text function that errors keeps its last frame and
> logs why.


> **Gotcha:**
> clients from 1.16 get exact colours, older ones the nearest of the
> sixteen. Sidebar lines take hex colours from 1.20.3. A screen or canvas draws
> text as pixels, in the colour of its `text` call — see
> [Screens and layouts](#ui-screens).


## Colour names and helpers

Anywhere a colour is asked for, every spelling works: a `color` value, a name,
or hex (`"#ff8800"`). A name nobody has is an error that says the nearest.

| Set | Names |
| --- | --- |
| Minecraft's sixteen, every client since 1.7 | `black`, `dark_blue`, `dark_green`, `dark_aqua`, `dark_red`, `dark_purple`, `gold`, `gray`, `dark_gray`, `blue`, `green`, `aqua`, `red`, `light_purple`, `yellow`, `white` |
| Six more | `orange`, `lime`, `cyan`, `purple`, `magenta`, `pink` |
| Special | `transparent` |

`colors` holds the same names as values; any other name is an error naming the
nearest (`colors.grey` says `gray`).

| Helper | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `color(r, g, b)` | A colour from red, green and blue, each 0 to 1 |
| `color.hsv(h, s, v)` | From hue, saturation and value, each 0 to 1 |
| `color.gradient(list, u, loop?)` | The colour `u` (0 to 1) of the way along the list; with `loop`, `u` wraps and the last colour runs back into the first |
| `color.nearest(c)` | The colour a picture really shows, since a picture snaps to the map palette |
| `kit.mix(a, b, t)` | Mixes two `"#rrggbb"` colours (see [Dialogs](#ui-dialogs)) |

## A canvas on the player's screen

`player.ui.overlay` puts a 128×128 canvas in a corner of one player's screen.
It draws like a canvas. Only that player sees it.

```luau
local map = player.ui.overlay{ corner = "top_right", size = 96, margin = 4 }   -- nil where player:supports("overlay") is false
if map then
    map:clear()                                  -- see-through: the game shows through
    map:rect(0, 1, 128, 127, "#101820", 10)      -- rows 1..127; row 0 is the engine's and never shows
    map:text(8, 6, "MAP", colors.white, 12)
    map.open                                     -- false after destroy or when the player leaves
    map:destroy()
end
```

- `corner` is `top_left`, `top_right`, `bottom_left` or `bottom_right`. `size`
  is screen pixels a side at GUI scale 1 (16 to 511). `margin` is the gap to
  the edges (0 to 63). The client's automatic GUI scale multiplies both.
- It stays over room moves and respawns. It goes when the player leaves.
- Changed pixels go to that player once per tick.
- Only 26.3 draws it, with the engine's shader in the resource pack. A pack
  that names `player.ui.overlay` makes the pack required for 26.3; a player
  who declines it is disconnected with a how-to message.
- Several at once are fine: each is its own canvas.

> **Gotcha:**
> shader mods (Iris, OptiFine) replace the shader. There the HUD
> does not show.


## See also

- [Screens and layouts](#ui-screens) — pixel screens and client-drawn HUD layouts.
- [Canvases and pictures](#ui-canvases) — the canvas drawing calls the overlay shares, video and streams.
- [Conventions](#concepts-conventions) — colour, text and options-table rules across the API.
- [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions) — the per-feature version matrix (`bossbar` 1.9, `overlay` 26.3).
- [Leaderboards cookbook](#cookbook-cookbook-leaderboards) — a sidebar in use.

<!-- /ui/screens/ -->

<a id="ui-screens"></a>

## Screens and layouts

> **In short:**
> a screen is a wall or floor of item frames that hold maps —
> 128 pixels per frame, on every client from 1.8 — that the script draws on
> pixel by pixel, with a click hook and an optional per-player layer. A layout
> is the other direction: a HUD made of boxes, pictures and labels that the
> client itself draws from the resource pack, with live values the script
> changes while it runs. Both belong to their room and end with the script.


## Placing a screen

Put it in the air blocks in front of a wall. [`world.screen{}`](#ref-World-screen)
places it:

| Option | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `at` | The top-left frame as the viewer sees it |
| `facing` | The side the viewer stands on; `"up"` lies the screen flat |
| `up` | For `facing = "up"`: the way the top of the picture points, `"north"` by default |
| `width`, `height` | The screen's size in frames |
| `glow` | `true` makes glow frames on 1.17 and later, plain frames before |
| `on_click` | A click hook, settable here or later |

- Changes go out once per tick, as each frame's box of changed pixels.
- Colours snap to the map palette (about 250 tones). Each client gets its
  closest tone; `color.nearest(c)` does that snap in advance.
- A screen belongs to its room and ends with the script. Players who join
  later see the current picture.

<a id="ui-screens--drawing-on-a-screen"></a>

## Drawing on a screen

A screen draws with the [`Picture`](#ref-Picture) calls — the same calls a
canvas or a view takes:

```luau
local board = world.screen{ at = vec3(-2, 68, -10), facing = "south", width = 4, height = 2 }
board.width, board.height                  -- pixels: 512, 256
board:clear(colors.black)                  -- every pixel; default black
board:set(x, y, color)                     -- one pixel, (0, 0) top-left
board:fill(x, y, w, h, color)
board:rect(x, y, w, h, color, 12)          -- rounded corners of radius 12, smoothed
board:circle(x, y, r, color)
board:text(x, y, "Jackpot 2500", colors.yellow, 32)   -- 32 pixels tall, smoothed; returns the width
board:measure("Jackpot 2500", 32)          -- the width without drawing, for centring
board:line(x0, y0, x1, y1, color, 3)       -- 3 pixels wide (1 by default), round ends, smoothed
board:ring(x, y, r, color, 2)              -- a circle's outline, 2 pixels wide (1 by default)
board:polygon({ {10, 10}, {60, 10}, {35, 50} }, color)   -- filled, any number of corners, smoothed
board:gradient(x, y, w, h, colors.red, colors.blue)      -- top to bottom; a 7th value "across" runs left to right
board:sprite(x, y, { ".##.", "#..#", ".##." }, { ["#"] = colors.black }, 4)   -- pixel art, 4 pixels a dot
board:pixels(x, y, w, h, data)             -- raw RGB bytes (a buffer or a string), three a pixel, row by row
board:draw(canvas, x, y)                   -- another canvas or screen, its top-left at (x, y); its transparent pixels are skipped
board:part(col, row)                       -- one map of it, { id = .. }, for a hand or a single frame
board:play{ file = "video/intro.rgb", fps = 20, loop = true }   -- a video; see "video" in Canvases
board:destroy()
```

Text is DejaVu Sans Bold, anti-aliased, 16 pixels by default. It has every
Latin letter, digits, symbols and `♠ ♥ ♦ ♣`.

Drawing notes:

- `line`, `ring` and `polygon` take fractional positions and blend into the
  pixels under them. Draw them on a background, not on `colors.transparent`.
- A polygon point is `{x, y}` or `{ x = .., y = .. }`.
- Each `sprite` string is a row. Each character is a dot `scale` pixels square
  (1 by default). A character with no colour (the `.` above) leaves its pixels
  unchanged.

## Clicks

Set `on_click` (in `world.screen{}` or later) to get the pixel a player clicks:

```luau
board.on_click = function(player, x, y, button)   -- button "left" or "right"
    board:circle(x, y, 6, colors.red)
end
board.on_click = nil   -- no hook again; false does the same
```

- A click on a block or the air behind the picture also counts.
- `players.on_click` still gets the click, with the frame's `entity_id` and no
  handle.

## One player's own layer

`board:view(player)` is one player's own layer over the screen, with the same
drawing calls. Only that player receives it.

```luau
local mine = board:view(player)
mine:text(8, 8, "Your turn", colors.yellow, 24)   -- nobody else sees this
mine:destroy()                                     -- back to the shared picture
```

- See-through pixels show the shared picture. A new view is all see-through,
  and `view:clear()` paints see-through.
- The call returns the same view until `view:destroy()` or the player leaves
  the room.
- Canvases have views too.

## Floor screens

For a floor or a table, set `facing = "up"`, in the air blocks on top.

- `up` is the way the top of the picture points, `"north"` by default. Use
  `"south"` for a player north of the table.
- Rows run away from `up`. With `up = "south"`, x runs west and y runs north.

> **Gotcha:**
> clients before 1.13 see nothing of a floor screen (the
> `floor_frame` feature).


```luau
local felt = world.screen{ at = vec3(2, 66, 2), facing = "up", up = "south", width = 5, height = 3 }
```

## Layouts

A layout is a HUD made of boxes, pictures and labels: a health bar, a level
badge, a frame round the hotbar. Define it while the pack loads, then show it
to a player and change its values.

```luau
local STATUS = ui.define("status", { anchor = "bottom", margin = 42,
    ui.row{ gap = 6, align = "end",
        ui.column{ gap = 1,
            ui.label{ id = "hp_text", text = "20 / 20", width = 82 },
            ui.stack{
                ui.box{ width = 82, height = 9, color = "#1c1410", radius = 2 },   -- the frame
                ui.box{ id = "hp", width = 80, height = 7, color = "red", radius = 1 },
            },
        },
        ui.label{ id = "level", text = "1", color = "gold" },
    },
})

players.on_join(function(player)
    local hud = player.ui.show(STATUS)
    hud:set{ hp = 0.7, hp_text = "14 / 20", level = "22" }
    hud.hp.color = "orange"                          -- every value is a live field too
    tween(hud.hp, { fill = 0 }, { duration = 2 })
    player.data.hud = hud                            -- hud:destroy() takes it off the screen
end)
```

## The layout tree

Three things to show, three ways to place them:

| Call | What it is | Options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`ui.box{}`](#ref-Ui-box) | A plain shape | `width`, `height` (1 to 256), `color`, `radius` |
| [`ui.image{}`](#ref-Ui-image) | A picture | `image` (a `game.texture`), `color` (a tint) |
| [`ui.label{}`](#ref-Ui-label) | Words | `text`, `color`, `width`, `align` |
| [`ui.row{}`](#ref-Ui-row) | Its children side by side | `gap`, `align`, then the children |
| [`ui.column{}`](#ref-Ui-column) | Its children under each other | `gap`, `align`, then the children |
| [`ui.stack{}`](#ref-Ui-stack) | Its children over each other, the last on top | `align`, then the children |

- There are no coordinates. Rows, columns and stacks place everything. `gap` is
  the pixels between two children. `align` is `"start"`, `"center"` (the
  default) or `"end"`, across the row or column.
- A pixel is one pixel of the game's own HUD: the hotbar is 182 wide and 22
  high.
- A bar is two boxes in a stack. The one with an `id` gets a fill.
- A label is as wide as its first words. Give a label whose words change a
  `width`: its place is fixed when the pack loads.
- [`ui.define(name, { anchor, margin, child })`](#ref-Ui-define) takes one
  child. `anchor` is `"bottom"`: the layout is centred over the hotbar, its
  bottom edge `margin` pixels above the screen's bottom. The default is 40,
  over the hearts, or 25, just over the hotbar, when `hide_hud` takes the
  hearts and the food away.

## Live values

An item with an `id` is live. [`hud:set{}`](#ref-Hud-set) takes a value per id,
and `hud.<id>` has the same values as fields:

| Field | In `hud:set{}` | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fill` | a number | How much of a box or picture shows, from its left edge, 0 to 1 |
| `text` | a string | A label's words |
| `visible` | `true` or `false` | Whether it shows; `hud.<id>.visible = nil` shows it again |
| `color` | (field only) | A box's colour, a picture's tint, a label's ink |

An unknown id is an error that lists the layout's ids. The values tween, as the
`hud.hp` example above shows.

## What is fixed when the pack loads

A client gets the resource pack when it joins, and never again. So the shape,
size, picture and place of every item are fixed when the pack loads, and
`ui.define` in a callback is an error. Show different layouts to different
players; do not look for a way to change one.

## Client support

- Only Java clients from 1.21.4 with the resource pack draw a layout
  (`player:supports("layout")`). On any other client, [`player.ui.show`](#ref-PlayerUi-show)
  returns a handle that takes every call and shows nothing. Send that player
  `player.ui.actionbar` instead. A client that turns the pack down stops
  getting its layouts.
- A layout uses the action bar. While one shows, `player.ui.actionbar` text is
  replaced by it within a second.
- A label starts at most 73 pixels above the screen's bottom, and uses the
  letters from space to `~`. Any other letter shows as `?`.
- A layout holds 254 items. A live box or picture is at most 256 wide.

## The game's own HUD

`hide_hud` in `citadel.yml` takes parts of it off the screen, for the whole
server and clients from 1.21.4 — `hearts`, `food`, `armor`, `air`, `xp`,
`hotbar`, `dialog_warning`:

- `xp` hides the bar; the level's number stays.
- `hotbar` hides the frame; the items stay.
- `dialog_warning` hides the ⚠ that the client puts next to the title of every
  dialog from this server. That sign tells a player the screen is the server's,
  not the game's, so hide it only for screens no one could mistake for the
  game's own.

`resource_pack: required` makes the pack required — or a player without the
pack sees no hearts and no layout. See
[Server settings](#systems-server-settings).

## Rendering a layout with no client

`citadel ui render` draws a layout with no client:

```sh
citadel ui render ./pack                 # every layout: its size and its ids
citadel ui render ./pack status --out hud.png --set hp=0.5 --set "hp_text=10 / 20" --scale 6
```

Boxes and pictures are exact. A label is drawn as blocks as wide as its
letters, because the letters are the client's own: report a label's words as
unchecked.

## See also

- [Canvases and pictures](#ui-canvases) — canvases, the shared drawing calls in depth, video and streams.
- [UI basics](#ui-ui-basics) — the action bar a layout replaces, and the text system.
- [Dialogs](#ui-dialogs) — full-screen dialogs, also client-drawn and pack-gated.
- [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions) — the `floor_frame`, `glow_frame` and `layout` rows.
- [Server settings](#systems-server-settings) — `hide_hud` and `resource_pack: required`.

<!-- /ui/canvases/ -->

<a id="ui-canvases"></a>

## Canvases and pictures

> **In short:**
> a canvas is a picture of one or more maps (128×128 pixels each)
> with no item frame of its own. Show it on a frame display, in a player's
> hand, or on a screen; draw on it with the same calls a screen takes. This
> page covers canvas creation, frame displays (`world.display{ kind = "frame" }`),
> the map palette every canvas snaps to, and the video and live-stream playback
> a screen or canvas can carry — with sound.


## Where a canvas shows

- A frame display, by map id.
- A hand: a hotbar slot with `canvas = c`.
- A screen, after `screen:draw(c)`.

An item display shows a blank map. Several walls can show one canvas. Drawing
another canvas switches a wall's picture; only changed pixels are sent.

A canvas draws like a screen. Changes go to the whole room once per tick; later
joiners get the whole picture. A destroyed canvas keeps its last picture on
clients that saw it; its id is never reused.

## Creating a canvas

```luau
local c = world.canvas{}              -- one map; world.canvas{ width = 4, height = 2 } is 4 by 2 maps (16 at most a side)
c.id                                  -- the map id of its top-left map, for a filled_map
c.width, c.height                     -- pixels: 128, 128 (512, 256 for 4 by 2)
c:part(col, row)                      -- another of its maps, { id = .. }, from (0, 0) top-left
c:clear(color) c:set(x, y, color) c:fill(x, y, w, h, color)
c:rect(x, y, w, h, color, radius) c:circle(x, y, r, color)
c:text(x, y, "A♠", color, size) c:measure("A♠", size)
c:line(x0, y0, x1, y1, color, width) c:ring(x, y, r, color, width)
c:polygon(points, color) c:gradient(x, y, w, h, from, to, "across") c:sprite(x, y, rows, inks, scale)
c:pixels(x, y, w, h, data) c:draw(other, x, y) c:play{ file = "video/clip.rgb", fps = 20 }
c:view(player)                        -- that player's own layer over it; see screens
c:destroy()
```

The drawing calls are the [`Picture`](#ref-Picture) calls, shared with screens
and views — the full list, with per-call detail, is in
[Screens and layouts](#ui-screens--drawing-on-a-screen). A canvas in the hand
updates live: with `canvas = c`, the map shows the picture on every client from
1.8, and it updates as the script draws (see [Menus](#ui-menus)).

## The map palette

Every pixel snaps to the map palette — about 250 tones; each client gets its
closest tone. `color.nearest(c)` does that snap in advance, for choosing
colours that survive it.

A pixel painted `colors.transparent` is see-through, and
`clear(colors.transparent)` empties a canvas.

## Frame displays: pictures on walls and floors

A client draws a map picture only in an item frame. To show a canvas in the
world, use a frame display (invisible by default):

```luau
local card = world.display{ kind = "frame", at = vec3(3, 65, 7), facing = "up", canvas = deck[12], invisible = true }
card.canvas = deck[53]        -- the back
card.id; card:destroy()
```

- The frame hangs in the block `at`, on the side `facing`.
- `"up"` lies flat on a floor (1.13 and later). A wall side works from 1.8.
- The frame does not turn or move.
- Set `canvas` to change the picture. `destroy` removes the frame.

Frame displays are a `world.display` kind — the rest of the display API is in
[Displays and models](#ui-displays).

## Video

`play` shows a video on a screen or canvas, with no script per frame. The pack
file holds raw RGB frames at the picture's size. Make it with ffmpeg:

```sh
# a 4 by 2 screen is 512 x 256 pixels
ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -vf "scale=512:256,fps=20" -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgb24 mypack/video/clip.rgb
```

```luau
local tv = world.screen{ at = vec3(-2, 70, -9), facing = "south", width = 4, height = 2 }
local v = tv:play{ file = "video/clip.rgb", fps = 20, loop = true }
-- fps 0.5 .. 20, one frame a tick at most
v.playing          -- false once it ends (and does not loop) or is stopped
v:stop()
```

- Each frame snaps to the map palette. Only changed pixels are sent.
- A pixel changes at once when one of its channels moved more than 32 of 255
  from what the screen shows. A smaller move, of more than 8, waits for the
  next half second. So movement is as smooth as the video, and the noise of a
  camera is not sent in every frame.
- A fully changed frame costs 16 KB per map per player in the room. A 2 by 2
  screen at 10 fps is about 640 KB/s per player. Keep videos small or slow
  where many players watch.
- A video ends with the script. The file streams; it is never loaded whole.

> **Tip:**
> a **named pipe** in place of the file is a live picture. Another
> program writes the frames into it while the video plays, and the screen shows
> each frame at `fps`. A stream gives frames in bursts, so up to 24 frames wait
> in a queue; with more, the oldest are dropped. It has no end and does not
> loop: with no writer the picture stays, and a new writer continues it.


```sh
mkfifo mypack/video/live.rgb
ffmpeg -i https://example.org/live.flv -an -vf "fps=10,scale=512:256" -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgb24 -y mypack/video/live.rgb
```

<a id="ui-canvases--streams-and-sound"></a>

## Streams and sound

`url` plays a live FLV stream (H.264 video, AAC sound) with no other program.
On a screen, the stream's sound is heard too. `url` can also be an MP3 stream,
as a radio station sends it (Icecast, Shoutcast); it has sound only — the
screen keeps the picture the pack draws on it, so a radio's own buttons and
titles stay. The first bytes of the stream say which kind it is.

```luau
tv:play{ url = "https://example.org/live.flv", fps = 10 }            -- picture and sound, heard 48 blocks out
tv:play{ url = url, audio = { distance = 24 } }                      -- heard 24 blocks out (1 .. 128)
tv:play{ url = url, audio = { static = true } }                      -- the same volume everywhere in the room
tv:play{ url = url, audio = false }                                  -- picture only
tv:play{ url = "https://radio.example.org/live.mp3", audio = { distance = 24 } }   -- a radio: sound only
```

- Players hear the sound through Simple Voice Chat: Citadel is a voice server
  for it, as a Paper server with the mod's plugin is (UDP port 24454,
  `CITADEL_VOICE_PORT`). A player without the mod sees the picture only.
- A locational sound comes from the screen's centre and reaches the players
  within `distance`, fading out towards it. A static sound reaches everyone in
  the room, with no place and no fade.
- Sound needs a screen. A canvas has no place in the world, so
  `c:play{ url = .., audio = true }` is an error. A file of frames has no
  sound.
- The sound keeps time with the picture. If the server falls more than half a
  second behind, the sound skips to now and is not played late.
- A client older than 1.13 hears nothing.
- The sound stops with the video, or when the screen is destroyed.

A sound with no screen, from several speakers or from no place, is
[`sound.stream`](#ref-Sound-stream) — see [Sound](#ui-sound).

## See also

- [Screens and layouts](#ui-screens) — the shared drawing calls in full, clicks and per-player views.
- [Sound](#ui-sound) — `sound.play`, `sound.stop` and streaming from speakers.
- [Displays and models](#ui-displays) — frame displays and every other display kind.
- [Menus](#ui-menus) — a canvas in the hand, as a live picture.
- [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions) — the `floor_frame` row for flat frames.

<!-- /ui/menus/ -->

<a id="ui-menus"></a>

## Menus

> **In short:**
> a menu is a titled grid of up to 54 items over the player's
> view. It is not an inventory: the player cannot take or put items; a click
> only picks one. Every client draws one — a chest on Java, a form of buttons
> on Bedrock — so no version check is needed. The hotbar is the other menu:
> nine items set per player, with slot and click events.


## `player.ui.menu`

```luau
commands.add("kit", function(player)
    local m = player.ui.menu{
        title = "Trains",
        items = {
            { item = "coal", name = "Steam locomotive", lore = { "right click a rail holding it" } },
            { item = "redstone", name = "High-speed electric" },
            "iron_ingot",                 -- a bare name works, as everywhere
        },
        on_pick = function(p, n)          -- n is the item picked, 1 up
            p:give(({ "coal", "redstone", "iron_ingot" })[n])
        end,
        on_close = function(p) end,       -- put away without picking
    }
    -- m:destroy() takes it down again; m:update(items) redraws it in place
end)
```

| Option | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | The menu's title (text — see [UI basics](#ui-ui-basics--text-runs)) |
| `items` | Up to 54 item specs |
| `on_pick` | `function(player, n)` — `n` is the item picked, 1 up |
| `on_close` | `function(player)` — fired when the player puts the menu away without picking |

## Items

An item is an item (see [Inventory](#players-inventory)) with `name`, `lore`,
`color`, `dye`, `glint`, `skin` and `count`. The count shows on the stack, for
a price or a quantity. A bare item name works, as everywhere.

## Every client draws a menu

Java (1.7 to 26.3) shows a chest. Bedrock shows a form with one button per
item, labelled with `name` or the item's name. No `player:supports` check is
needed.

## Picks and closes

- `on_pick` may `task.wait`.
  - On Java the menu stays open. Destroy it in `on_pick` if one pick is enough.
  - A Bedrock form closes on the press. Open it again for another pick.
- [`menu:destroy()`](#ref-Menu-destroy) and a Bedrock pick do not fire `on_close`.
- A new menu replaces the old one.
- Only the pack that opened a menu gets its picks. The menu ends when the
  script ends, the player leaves, or the pack calls `destroy`.

> **Gotcha:**
> a Bedrock form cannot be taken back: it stays until the player
> answers, and the answer then lands nowhere.


## Updating in place

[`menu:update(items)`](#ref-Menu-update) puts new pictures in place, the menu
left open: a bar that fills, a count that changes. `on_pick` still answers by
position.

- `menu:update` returns `false` once the player has put the menu away; a
  Bedrock form keeps what it showed.
- Under a Java menu, the player's inventory shows. Clicks in it change nothing.

## Hotbar menus

The hotbar is a menu of nine items, set per player.

```luau
player:hotbar{                       -- replaces the nine hotbar slots; a missing index is empty
    [1] = { item = "lapis_block", name = "HIT", count = 1 },
    [7] = { item = "gold_nugget", name = "Bet: 50" },
    [8] = { canvas = minimap, name = "Map" },   -- a filled map of a canvas: a live picture in the hand
}
player.slot                          -- the slot in hand, 1..9, live
hit.slot                             -- on every players.on_click, 1..9
```

The events:

- Selecting a slot fires `players.on_slot`.
- A click while holding a slot fires `players.on_click` with `hit.slot` set.
  Any target and either button counts.
- Right clicks never merge into a hold. The halves of one click (block use,
  item use, both hands) are one event.
- In pack mode the rest of the inventory is locked.

A slot is an item, with the same meta. An item name that the game version
lacks is an error.

> **Tip:**
> with `canvas = c`, the map shows the picture on every client from
> 1.8, and it updates as the script draws — a live minimap in the hand (see
> [Canvases and pictures](#ui-canvases)).


## See also

- [Dialogs](#ui-dialogs) — full-screen dialogs for 1.21.6+ clients, with a menu as the fallback.
- [Inventory](#players-inventory) — the item spec: `name`, `lore`, `count`, `glint`, skins.
- [Canvases and pictures](#ui-canvases) — the canvas behind a hotbar map.
- [UI basics](#ui-ui-basics) — the text runs a menu title takes.

<!-- /ui/dialogs/ -->

<a id="ui-dialogs"></a>

## Dialogs

> **In short:**
> a dialog is a screen of boxes, words and pictures over the
> player's view: a server list, a shop, a page of rules. It needs Java 1.21.6
> or newer (`player:supports("dialog")`); on any other client `player.ui.dialog`
> answers `nil`, so give those players a menu or chat instead. Dialogs are
> built from `ui.kit` nodes — plain tables — and a function view makes the
> dialog live: it is drawn again after every click.


## Opening a dialog

```luau
local kit = ui.kit

local function servers(player)
    local tab = 1
    local d = player.ui.dialog(function()           -- a function: drawn again after every click
        return kit.window{
            title = "Servers", size = "screen", button = false,
            kit.tabs{ "Featured", "Popular", selected = tab, on_change = function(p, i) tab = i end },
            kit.grid{ columns = 3,
                kit.card{ image = "https://example.org/carball.png", title = "Carball", text = "by Melvin",
                    badges = { kit.badge{ "LIVE", color = kit.theme.live, dot = true } },
                    on_click = function(p) p:message("Joining Carball") end },
            },
            kit.row{ justify = "end", kit.close() },
        }
    end)
    if not d then player.ui.menu{ title = "Servers", items = { "slime_ball" }, on_pick = function() end } end
end
```

## Declaring dialogs in `citadel.yml`

A pack that opens dialogs says so in its `citadel.yml`, so their fonts are in
the resource pack from the first join:

```yaml
dialogs: true
```

Without it, `player.ui.dialog` is an error that names the line to add.

## The dialog handle

[`player.ui.dialog(view)`](#ref-PlayerUi-dialog) takes a `ui.kit.window{}`, or
a function that returns one. With a function the dialog is live: after every
click it calls the function again and draws what it returns, so a click only
has to change your state. It returns a handle:

| Call or field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `d:refresh()` | Draws a live view again (after a change that was not a click) |
| `d:update(view)` | Puts a new view (a window or a function) in place |
| `d:destroy()` | Closes it |
| `d.open` | `false` once the player closed it |

The view itself is a [`DialogNode`](#ref-DialogNode): a table with a `kind`,
made by `ui.kit` — or written by hand.

## `ui.kit`: the six primitives

`ui.kit` is what a dialog is made of. Six primitives the engine draws, each a
table you can also write by hand:

- `kit.row{ ... }`, `kit.column{ ... }`, `kit.stack{ ... }` (children on top of
  each other): the children are the list part. Keys: `gap`, `pad` (a number,
  `{ y, x }` or `{ top, right, bottom, left }`), `align` and `justify`
  (`"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`, and `"stretch"` or `"between"`), `fill` and
  `fill_to` (a gradient), `border`, `border_width`, `radius`, `shadow` (0 to 8).
- `kit.space{}`: an empty box that takes `width`, `height` or `grow`.
- `kit.text("Hi")` or `kit.text{ "Hi", color = ..., bold = true, shadow = false, align = "center" }`.
- `kit.image{ image = ..., radius = 4, detail = 2 }`: `image` is an `https://`
  URL (fetched once by the engine), a PNG or WebP file in the pack, or a
  `game.texture`; `detail = 2` has four times the pixels. Or
  `kit.image{ glyph = "name" }` for one of the pack's own glyphs. A picture
  still on its way shows a placeholder, and the dialog is drawn again when it
  arrives.

Every node also takes `width`, `height`, `grow`, `on_click` (a
`function(player)`, or `"close"`) and `hover` (words shown under the pointer).

> **Gotcha:**
> how an image is drawn — one `width = 144, height = 80` directly
> in `kit.window`, or first in a `kit.row` directly in it (the row's other
> children sit beside it), is one picture the client renders once, so it is
> cheap. Only the first such image in a window is drawn this way; every other
> image is drawn in glyph cells, which the client draws every frame.


## Composed nodes

Made of the primitives, in plain Luau (copy one to make your own):

| Node | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `kit.window{ title, button, on_close, input, size = "screen", ... }` | The dialog itself. `button` is its button's label, `false` for none; `input = { label, value, width, on_submit = function(player, text) end }` adds a text field; `size = "screen"` is `kit.SCREEN`, a body that fits every screen without a scrollbar |
| `kit.button{ "Play", style = ..., on_click }` | A button; `style` is `"primary"`, `"secondary"`, `"ghost"` or `"danger"` |
| `kit.tabs{ "A", "B", selected, on_change }` | Tabs |
| `kit.close{}` | A close button |
| `kit.badge{ "LIVE", color, dot }` | A badge |
| `kit.dot{}` | A dot |
| `kit.progress{ value = 0.5 }` | A progress bar |
| `kit.divider{}` | A divider |
| `kit.card{ image, title, text, badges, on_click }` | A card |
| `kit.grid{ columns = 3, gap = 6, ... }` | Any nodes, in rows of `columns` |

`kit.theme` holds the colours they use when a call names none: change it once
to restyle them all. `kit.mix(a, b, t)` mixes two `"#rrggbb"` colours.

## The rules

- A new dialog replaces the open one. Escape closes it and calls the window's
  `on_close(player)`.
- Clicks may `task.wait`. Only the pack that opened a dialog gets its clicks.
- A player who turned the resource pack down is sent no dialog: it is drawn in
  the pack's fonts. A pack-declined client answers `false` to
  `player:supports("dialog")` — and an open dialog closes from that moment.

## See also

- [Menus](#ui-menus) — the every-client fallback for a dialog.
- [Screens and layouts](#ui-screens) — layouts, the other pack-drawn surface.
- [UI basics](#ui-ui-basics) — text runs and colour spellings for words in a dialog.
- [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions) — the `dialog` row and pack-declined behaviour.
