<!-- /ui/displays/ -->

<a id="ui-displays"></a>

## Displays and models

> **In short:**
> a display is a floating item, text or block with no physics,
> placed by the pack and live-edited field by field. Clients from 1.19.4 see
> the real display; older ones get a stand-in. A 3D model — boxes in a tree of
> named parts, with materials, textures and named animations — shows through
> `world.display{ kind = "model" }` on Java clients from 1.21.4, with a
> `fallback` for everyone else. Vehicles and riding close the page.


## Kinds and versions

[`world.display{}`](#ref-World-display) places a visual without simulation. The
kinds: `"text"`, `"item"`, `"block"`, `"frame"` (a map picture — see
[Canvases](#ui-canvases)) and `"model"`.

- Clients from 1.19.4 see the real display and tween `animate`. A display
  belongs to its room and ends with the script.
- Older clients see an invisible armor stand holding the `item`, or with the
  `text` as a name tag — and nothing for `block` and `hitbox`. Give them a pad.

```luau
-- every kind takes these
local d = world.display{
    kind = "text",                      -- "item", "text" or "block"
    at = vec3(0.5, 66, 0.5),            -- where it sits
    rotation = { yaw = 0, pitch = 0, roll = 0 },   -- degrees; pitch = 90 lays a text flat on a table
    scale = 1,                          -- or vec3(1, 2, 1); a number is the same on every axis
    billboard = "center",               -- "fixed", "vertical", "horizontal" or "center";
                                        --   text defaults to "center", the rest to "fixed"
    glow = colors.cyan,                 -- outline colour; leave it out, or write false, for none
    -- and a text takes these
    text = "BLACKJACK",                 -- text, see "Text formatting"
    color = colors.white,               -- a colour or a name
    background = color(0, 0, 0),        -- behind the words; leave it out, or write false, for none
    line_width = 200, shadow = false,
}
world.display{ kind = "item", at = vec3(2.5, 66, 0.5),
    item = "paper",                     -- canonical item name; or canvas = c, a world.canvas{}: a filled map of the picture
    context = "frame",                  -- how the item is posed: "frame", "none", "menu", "dropped", "worn", "held", "own_hand"
}
world.display{ kind = "block", at = vec3(4.5, 66, 0.5), block = "lapis_block" }
```

`billboard` is how a display turns toward the viewer: `"fixed"` never turns,
`"vertical"` turns about the up axis, `"horizontal"` tips up and down,
`"center"` does both.

## Live fields and tweening

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `d.id` | Entity id, what `players.on_click` reports in `hit.entity_id` |
| `d.at, d.rotation, d.scale, d.billboard, d.glow` | Live, every kind |
| `d.item, d.canvas, d.context` | Live, item kind (`canvas` reads back as the map id) |
| `d.text, d.color, d.background, d.line_width, d.shadow` | Live, text kind; `background = nil` or `false` for none |
| `d.block` | Live, block kind |
| `d.duration` | Seconds later changes take to play out (1.19.4+); 0 |
| `d.glide` | Advanced: movement smoothing seconds (1.20.2+); default 0.1 |
| `d.lead` | Advanced: `true` enables linear prediction; `false` by default, `nil` restores `false` |

```luau
d:animate{ at = ..., scale = ..., rotation = { ... }, text = ..., duration = 0.5 }   -- one tweened change
d:destroy()
```

`animate` makes one tweened change of place, scale, rotation or text over
`duration` seconds (0.5 by default), played by the client; it sets the position
interpolation time as well as the transform time. Use `animate` for an authored
transition, `tween` for other live fields. `duration`, `glide` and `lead` are
advanced controls, not requirements for moving a model.

## Hitboxes and walls

```luau
local h = world.hitbox{ at = vec3(...), width = 1, height = 1, on_click = function(player, button) end }
h.id; h.at; h:destroy()                 -- button is "left" or "right"
```

A hitbox is an invisible clickable box. Its `on_click` fires through
`players.on_click`; clients below 1.19.4 get no hitbox.

[`world.hitbox{ ..., solid = true }`](#ref-World-hitbox) is also a **wall**: a
player cannot walk through it and can stand on it.

- It works anywhere and moves when you write `at`.
- Its size is `width` (x) by `height` by `depth` (z); `depth` defaults to
  `width`; `at` is its bottom centre.
- It cannot turn. Build a turning thing from several small walls.
- The engine fills it with cubes of its smallest side, 64 at most, and warns
  past 64. Make a thin sheet from blocks.
- Clients from 1.20.5 stop at the exact size; older clients stop at one-block
  cubes.

## Choosing a world object and moving it

| Need | API | Why it exists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reusable appearance and named animations | `models.new` | Defines an asset for visuals or simulated entities. |
| A visual controlled by the pack | `world.display` | Places text, an item, a block or a model without simulation. |
| Physics, gameplay hooks or persistence | `game.entities.define` and `world.spawn` | Gives a body behavior independent of its appearance. |
| A mob appearance moved entirely by the pack | `world.puppet` | Uses a mob body without its AI or gameplay simulation. |
| A player-shaped character with a skin and equipment | `world.npc` | Adds avatar-specific behavior. |
| A player or NPC seated on something | `:ride` | Controls attachment and occupancy. |
| A different viewpoint | `player.camera` | Controls the view; `chase` composes with riding. |
| Authored changes over time | `tween` or `camera.path` | A tween animates fields; a camera path sequences shots. |

Displays, model displays, NPCs, puppets and entity handles share `id`, `alive`,
`at`, `rotation` and `:move(at, rotation?)` — a table of degree angles, where
partial writes preserve omitted angles; `move` changes position and rotation in
one operation, validating both before applying either. `at` and `rotation` read
`nil` when the object is gone; cleanup can be repeated.

Displays and models also share `scale`: reads return a `vec3`, writes accept a
number or vector. Models preserve their proportions and accept only equal,
positive axes; plain displays can stretch individual axes. Displays also accept
`rotation = { forward = direction, up = roof }`; reads always return angles. Use
angle targets for `tween`: partial targets preserve other axes, and angles
interpolate as written, so `roll = 360` can author a full turn. Write current
positions with `at` or `move`; the engine smooths visual movement.

## Vehicles and riding

A vehicle is an entity that looks like a model. Seat 1's keys drive it; the
engine does the driving, gravity, walls and steps. `game.entities.define` with
`physics = "vehicle"` makes one:

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `looks` | A model from `models.new` |
| `physics` | `"vehicle"` — the engine drives it |
| `size` | Its body in blocks: width, height |
| `seats` | In model units; seat 1 drives |
| `speed` | Blocks a second at full throttle (12 if left out) |
| `turn` | Degrees a second at speed (90) |
| `accel` | Seconds from standing to top speed (1) |
| `step` | Blocks it climbs without a jump (1) |
| `scale` | The model's size (1) |
| `fallback` | What a client older than 1.21.4 sees |

```luau
local c = world.spawn(car, vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5))    -- a car defined as above
player:ride(c)                                -- seat 1: W and S throttle, A and D steer
friend:ride(c, { seat = 2, locked = true })   -- locked: sneaking does not get them off
c.driver          -- player supplying seat 1 input; nil for an NPC or empty seat
c.riders[2]       -- actual occupant, including NPCs; nil means empty
c.paint = { paint = colors.blue }   -- this car's colours, by material name
c.scale = 1.5
c:play("drive", { speed = 2 })      -- again with another speed only changes the speed
c:stop("drive")
```

- Every tick, before any hook, the engine writes seat 1's keys into `c.forward`
  (1 ahead, -1 back), `c.strafe` (1 left, -1 right) and `c.jumping`; with seat 1
  empty, the car rolls to a stop.
- In `on_steer`, call `base(e)`, then adjust — or skip `base` and set
  `e.velocity` and `e.rotation` yourself. A CPU driver (or an npc in seat 1)
  writes `e.forward` and `e.strafe`, or the velocity, in this hook:

```luau
on_steer = function(e, base)
    base(e)                                    -- drive as defined
    if e.data.boost then e.velocity = e.velocity * 1.4 end
end
```

- `rotation.yaw` works as for every entity: 0 faces south (+z), 90 west; the
  model's front (-z) faces that way.
- Without `locked`, sneaking gets a rider off and fires `players.on_sneak`;
  `player:dismount()` gets anyone off. A seat holds one rider: `player:ride`
  and `npc:ride` return `false` for a full seat.
- Only `physics = "vehicle"` reads `speed`, `turn`, `accel` and `step`, and it
  needs `looks`. Anything else is an error at `define`.

`player:ride(thing)` also seats a player on a model display, a display, a
hitbox or an npc: anything with an `id` the client sees; the pack moves these
things. The player's feet are 0.6 below the thing's position. A model display's
`seats` work as a vehicle's; with none, seat 1 is the model's origin. A ridden
display glides two ticks between moves (1.20.2+), unless the pack set a `glide`
or `duration`; the rider's chunks follow the ridden thing, at any distance. A
rider stays upright — for a car on a wall, hide the driver (`invisibility`) and
use `camera.fixed`.

## 3D models

A model is a 3D shape a pack writes in code: boxes in a tree of named parts.
The engine shows it as item displays that move together.

> **Gotcha:**
> make models while the pack loads — [`models.new`](#ref-models-new)
> in a callback is an error.


```luau
local car = models.new("car", function(m)
    local paint = m:material("paint", colors.red, { grain = 0.1 })   -- a colour a display may repaint
    local glass = m:material("glass", "dark_aqua", { alpha = 0.45 }) -- what is behind shows through
    local door = m:texture(30, 16, { tint = paint })                 -- drawn in greys, coloured by paint
    local grille = m:texture(8, 4)                  -- pixel art for one face, drawn as it is
    grille:fill(colors.black)
    grille:rect(1, 1, 6, 2, colors.gray)            -- x, y, w, h, colour
    grille:pixel(0, 0, colors.transparent)          -- a see-through pixel

    local body = m:part("body", { pivot = vec3(0, 6, 0) })
    body:box(vec3(0, 4, -20), vec3(8, 12, 20), paint, {
        faces = { north = grille },                 -- one side wears something else
    })
    local screen = body:part("windscreen")
    screen:box(vec3(0, 12, -6), vec3(8, 18, 2), glass, { rotation = vec3(22.5, 0, 0) })
    local wheel = body:part("wheel_front", { pivot = vec3(8, 4, -12) })
    wheel:box(vec3(6, 0, -16), vec3(10, 8, -8), paint)
    wheel:box(vec3(6, 0, -16), vec3(10, 8, -8), paint, { rotation = vec3(45, 0, 0) })
    body:mirror("x")                                -- the left half, from the right one

    m:animation("drive", {
        length = 1, loop = true,
        wheel_front = { rotation = { [0] = vec3(0, 0, 0), [0.25] = vec3(-90, 0, 0), [0.5] = vec3(-180, 0, 0),
            [0.75] = vec3(-270, 0, 0), [1] = vec3(-360, 0, 0) } },   -- quarter turns: see the rules
        wheel_front_mirrored = { rotation = { [0] = vec3(0, 0, 0), [0.25] = vec3(-90, 0, 0), [0.5] = vec3(-180, 0, 0),
            [0.75] = vec3(-270, 0, 0), [1] = vec3(-360, 0, 0) } },
    })
end)
```

### Materials and textures

- A material is flat unless it has a `grain` (`0..1`: how much darker its
  darkest pixel is). `0.1` is a painted panel, `0.4` a tyre. A grained face has
  four tones, one pixel per unit. `alpha` below 1 is glass.
- A texture stretches over its face; for fine detail, draw two pixels per unit.
  Its drawing calls are `fill(color)`, `rect(x, y, w, h, color)` and
  `pixel(x, y, color)`; `colors.transparent` makes a see-through pixel.
- With `tint = material`, draw in greys: white is the material's colour, darker
  is a seam or a shadow.
- `m:texture(w, h, { scroll = "up", speed = 2 })` is a texture that moves when
  a block is drawn from the model.
- A mirrored box shows a side texture from the other end. Draw an asymmetric
  texture once per side, after the `mirror`.

### Parts, boxes and mirrors

- **16 units are one block.** The origin is the model's bottom centre, `+y` is
  up, the front is `-z`. A box reaches `-24 .. 24` on every axis: three blocks.
  For a bigger thing, set the display's `scale`.
- A box turns on **one** axis only, in steps of 22.5 degrees, up to 45 either
  way. Anything else is an error. An octagonal wheel is two boxes, one turned
  45.
- Box corners go in any order and can be fractional. A box's `pivot` defaults
  to its centre.
- Every box is in a part; there is no `m:box`. A part turns around its `pivot`
  (default: the model's origin). `m:part` makes a child of the root, `part:part`
  a child of that part.
- `part:mirror("x")` mirrors what the part has so far, pivots, turns and
  hitboxes too. A child's twin is `<name>_mirrored`. Only `"x"` works in this
  version.
- `part:hitbox(from, to)` is a box a player can hit on a living body that wears
  the model.

### Animations

An animation is keys per part: `{ [seconds] = vec3 }` for `rotation` (degrees
about the pivot) and `position` (an offset in model units).

- Keys can be in any order. An unknown part name is an error that lists the
  model's parts. Parts cannot share a track — write a loop.
- Between two keys, a part turns **the short way round**. Keep each step under
  180 degrees: a wheel is `[0] = 0, [0.1] = -90, [0.2] = -180, ...` — one key
  from 0 to 360 does not turn. A `tween` of `rotation` is not like this: it
  turns as written, so there `roll = 360` is a full turn.
- `speed` is 0.01 to 100; a value outside is taken as the nearest end. A speed
  of 0 does not pause: use `stop`. A new speed applies at once.

## Model displays

```luau
local d = world.display{
    kind = "model", model = car,
    at = vec3(10.5, 65, 4.5), rotation = { yaw = 90 },      -- degrees, as every entity turns: 0 faces south, 90 west
    scale = 3.5,                             -- 1 draws it at 16 units to the block
    paint = { paint = colors.blue },         -- keys are material names
    fallback = "minecart",                   -- what a client that cannot show it sees; nil shows nothing
    seats = { vec3(0, 7, 2) },               -- optional: where riders sit, in model units; see "vehicles"
}
d:move(vec3(12.5, 65, 4.5), { yaw = 180 })   -- place and turn it in one step, every part together
d:move(at, { forward = forward, up = up })   -- pointed: nose along forward, roof toward up (a car on a wall)
d.at, d.rotation                             -- live too; each write is a move of its own
d.scale = 2                                  -- live
d.paint = { paint = colors.red }             -- live
d:play("drive")                              -- from the beginning; an unknown name is an error
d:play("drive", { speed = 2 })               -- twice as fast; on the one already playing, the new speed at once
d:stop("drive")                              -- the parts stay where they are
d:destroy()
```

- `rotation.pitch` and `rotation.roll` tip the whole model about its origin,
  with parts, animations and seats.
- `paint` repaints materials by name, and every texture they tint. An unknown
  material name is an error that lists the model's materials.
- Only Java clients from 1.21.4 see a model; older clients and Bedrock see
  `fallback`. A client that loads the resource pack after it joined gets its
  models again when the pack is in; the pack does nothing for this.
- A client that turns the resource pack down, or cannot load it, sees
  `fallback` from then on, also for the models it already sees.

> **Tip:**
> `citadel model render <pack dir> <name> --out car.png` draws a model
> with no client; add `--animation drive --at 0.25` for mid-move. No name lists
> the models.

<!-- /ui/fx/ -->

<a id="ui-fx"></a>

## Particles and lasers

> **In short:**
> particles at points: a burst, a trail, or a laser drawn as a
> line of dust. One call, [`fx.particle`](#ref-Fx-particle), serves a room — a
> name, a point or a list of points, and an options table. Dust alone takes a
> colour and a size, which is what a beam or laser is made of. Particles fade
> on their own, so a beam that stays is redrawn every other tick.


## The call

Particles live on the `fx` global — Minecraft's particle packet, for a room
(`fx`, or `room.fx` in another room):

```luau
fx.particle(name, pos, { count = 1, spread = 0, velocity = nil, speed = 0, color = nil, size = 1 })
```

| Option | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | 1 | Particles at each point |
| `spread` | 0 | A random box this many blocks out from each point; a number or a vec3 (one size per axis) |
| `velocity` | nil | A vec3: one particle that moves along it |
| `speed` | 0 | With `velocity`, scales it (1); without it, how fast the particles scatter — 0 is still |
| `color` | nil | `dust` only |
| `size` | 1 | `dust` only, 0.5 to 4 |

`name` is the particle: `dust`, `end_rod`, `explosion`, `firework`, `flame`,
`note` or `totem_of_undying`. Any other name sends nothing.

## Points and who sees them

`pos` is a vec3, or a list of vec3s, with the same particle at every point.
Each point is sent only to players in the same room within 64 blocks of its
origin in 3D, including the boundary, before spread or velocity.

## Velocity against count and spread

- `count` particles appear at each point, in a random box `spread` blocks out
  from it.
- `velocity` (a vec3) sends one particle that moves along it. It cannot go with
  `count` above 1 or with `spread`.
- `color` and `size` (0.5 to 4) are for `dust` only. Dust is white and size 1
  unless they say.

> **Gotcha:**
> `color` or `size` on any other particle is an error.


## Version behaviour

- A client whose version lacks a particle does not get it.
- Before 1.13, dust is one particle a point, in its colour, with no count,
  spread or size.
- 1.7 shows dust only.

## Beams

Dust at points along a line, in one call:

```luau
-- a beam: dust at points along a line, in one call
local points = {}
for i = 0, 7 do points[i + 1] = from:lerp(to, i / 7) end
fx.particle("dust", points, { color = colors.red, size = 1.5 })

fx.particle("flame", pos, { velocity = vec3(0, 1, 0), speed = 0.5 })        -- a jet
fx.particle("firework", pos, { count = 40, spread = 2, speed = 0.05 })       -- a burst
fx.particle("totem_of_undying", at + vec3(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), { count = 12, spread = 0.4, speed = 0.3 })   -- a pickup burst
```

Particles fade on their own. A beam that stays is drawn again every other tick:

```luau
local beam = { from = vec3(0.5, 76, 0.5), to = vec3(0.5, 66, 0.5), color = colors.cyan }
local conn = time.on_tick(function(tick)
    if tick % 2 ~= 0 then return end
    local points = {}
    for i = 0, 7 do points[i + 1] = beam.from:lerp(beam.to, i / 7) end
    fx.particle("dust", points, { color = beam.color, size = 2 })
end)
tween(beam, { to = beam.to + vec3(4, 0, 0) }, { duration = 1 })   -- its fields are plain; set or tween them
conn:cancel()                                                     -- and it is gone
```

The beam's fields are plain values: set or tween them (a laser that sweeps),
and `conn:cancel()` takes the beam away.

## See also

- [Sound](#ui-sound) — the other room-wide effect, `sound.play` and streams.
- [UI basics](#ui-ui-basics) — colour spellings for `color`.
- [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions) — what old clients get.
- [Coin rush guide](#guides-guide-coin-rush) — pickup particles in a working pack.

<!-- /ui/sound/ -->

<a id="ui-sound"></a>

## Sound

> **In short:**
> play the game's sounds or the pack's own, for everyone or at a
> point. [`sound.play`](#ref-Sound-play) sends short effects through the
> resource pack — no mod needed. [`sound.stream`](#ref-Sound-stream) plays a
> live stream or a pack's sound file through the players' voice mods, with
> speakers, moving sources and a list of listeners: music, ambience, radios.


## `sound.play`

```luau
sound.play("block.note_block.hat", { at = player.at, pitch = 1.5 })
sound.play(name, { at = spawn, volume = 1, pitch = 1, category = "record" })
```

- Names are `"<pack>.<file>"` for your assets, or vanilla names like
  `"block.note_block.hat"`.
- Volume above 1 carries further (16 blocks per unit); pitch 0.5..2.0 is two
  octaves.
- `category` is `"record"` (the jukebox slider), `"music"` or `"master"`.
- Every call is one packet to every player, sent ahead of particles.

[`player:sound(name, opts)`](#ref-Player-sound) plays a sound by name to this
player only, with the same optional position, volume, pitch and category.

## Stopping

```luau
sound.stop("rave.track")   -- stops that sound for everyone in the room
sound.stop()               -- stops every sound
```

`sound.stop` needs 1.13 and later; older clients play on.

## `sound.stream`

`sound.stream` plays a live stream or a pack's sound file through the players'
voice mods, with no screen. A live stream is MP3, as a radio station sends it,
or the sound of an FLV stream. A file is OGG (Vorbis), MP3 or WAV in the pack;
it is decoded while it plays, never loaded whole.

```luau
-- 3D: from speakers. Each player hears every speaker within `distance`.
local radio = sound.stream{ url = "https://radio.example.org/live.mp3", at = vec3(10, 67, 28), distance = 24 }
local pa = sound.stream{ url = url, at = { vec3(10, 67, 28), vec3(-10, 67, 28), captain }, distance = 16 }
local hum = sound.stream{ file = "assets/music/engine.ogg", at = engine_room, loop = true }

-- No place: the same volume for each listener, no fade, no direction.
sound.stream{ url = url }                         -- everyone in the room
sound.stream{ file = "assets/voice/welcome.mp3", to = player }
sound.stream{ url = url, to = { p1, p2 }, name = "Radio" }

radio.playing            -- false once stopped, or once a file that does not loop ends
pa:move(2, vec3(-12, 67, 30))   -- speakers are numbered from 1
pa:add(npc)                     -- a speaker that follows a player or an entity; gives its number
pa:remove(3)
radio:listen(player)            -- starts to hear it
radio:unlisten(player)          -- stops hearing it
radio:stop()
```

| Option | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `url` or `file` | A live stream URL, or a pack sound file (OGG, MP3, WAV). Give one, never both |
| `at` | A vec3, a player, an entity, or a list of them: the speakers |
| `distance` | 1 to 128 blocks, 48 when not given; needs `at` |
| `to` | A player or a list of players; without it, everyone in the room, players who join later too |
| `loop` | `true` is for a file only: a live stream has no end, and if it drops it is tried again every 2 seconds |
| `name` | 1 to 16 characters, `"Sounds"` when not given: the sound's own volume slider in the mod |

## Speakers

- A speaker that follows a player or entity moves with it, and is silent while
  they are gone. `at = {}` starts with no speakers; `add` gives it some.
- All speakers play the same sound at the same time, as a speaker system does.
  A player hears every speaker in range, each from its own place, and the voice
  mod mixes them. Each one is a packet of its own to that player: three
  speakers in range send three times the sound's data.
- `move`, `add` and `remove` on a sound with no `at` are an error. A sound with
  no place has no distance, and giving one is an error.
- `listen` and `unlisten` change who hears while it plays.

> **Gotcha:**
> on a stopped sound, every call does nothing. The sound stops with
> `stop()`, or when the script stops or reloads.


## The mod

Players hear a stream through Simple Voice Chat: Citadel is a voice server for
it, as a Paper server with the mod's plugin is (UDP port 24454,
`CITADEL_VOICE_PORT`). A player without the mod, or on a client older than
1.13, hears nothing.

A screen can carry the sound itself — an FLV stream's sound, or an MP3 radio
over a pack-drawn picture — with `screen:play{ url = .. }`; see
[Canvases and pictures](#ui-canvases--streams-and-sound).

## `sound.play` or `sound.stream`

|  | `sound.play` | `sound.stream` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How it reaches the player | The game's or the pack's resource pack; the client plays it | Simple Voice Chat, from the server |
| Mod needed | No | Yes |
| Control | Start and stop | Speakers, moving sources, a list of listeners, all players in time |
| Best for | Short effects: a click, a door, an alarm | Music, ambience, long voice lines, radios, speaker systems |

## See also

- [Canvases and pictures](#ui-canvases) — streams and sound through a screen.
- [Particles and lasers](#ui-fx) — the other room-wide effect, sent after sound.
- [Conventions](#concepts-conventions) — the `"<pack>.<file>"` sound-name rule.
- [Coin rush guide](#guides-guide-coin-rush) — `sound.play` in a working pack.

<!-- /systems/commands/ -->

<a id="systems-commands"></a>

## Commands

> **In short:**
> a pack adds slash commands with `commands.add` from a usage
> string that doubles as the grammar: `<name:type>` marks a required argument,
> `[name:type]` an optional one. This page covers the usage grammar, the
> argument types and what `args.name` becomes, the `opts` table (permission,
> aliases, help, suggest), tab-completion with tooltips, several shapes under
> one name, and the rules of who owns a command name in a room.


## Adding a command

```luau
commands.add(usage, function(player, args) end, opts?) -> command
--   opts = { permission = "casino.play", aliases = { "hub" }, help = "Set your bet",
--            suggest = { place = { "roulette", "arcade" }, item = function(player, typed, args) return { ... } end } }
command:suggest(arg, words)   -- a list, a function, or nil or false for nothing: what `arg` offers from now on
command:cancel()              -- takes the command away
```

`commands.add` takes the usage line, the function that runs it, and options;
it returns a [`Command`](#ref-Command) handle. The function receives the
player who typed it and a table holding each argument by name — an optional
argument that was not typed is `nil`.

```luau
commands.add("bet <amount:integer 1..10000> [color:red|black]", function(player, args)
    bank.bet(player, args.amount, args.color or "red")   -- args.amount is a number
end, { permission = "casino.play", help = "Bet on the wheel" })

commands.add("spawn", function(player) player:teleport(SPAWN) end, { aliases = { "hub" } })
commands.add("tekkit give <item:word> [count:integer 1..64]", give, {
    permission = "tekkit.give",
    suggest = { item = function(player, typed) return item_names() end },
})
```

## The usage line

A usage is the name, any fixed words, then the arguments. Fixed words let one
name carry several shapes — see [One name, several shapes](#systems-commands--one-name-several-shapes).

- `<name:type>` is required and `[name:type]` is optional.
- **A required argument never follows an optional one.**
- A range may leave out either end: `integer 1..` or `integer ..64`.
- `text...` and `words...` come last.

## Argument types

What the player types, and what `args.name` is inside the function:

| type | the player types | `args.name` is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `word` | one word | a string |
| `integer`, `integer 1..64` | a whole number, in the range if there is one | a number |
| `number`, `number 0..1` | any number, in the range if there is one | a number |
| `player` | the name of someone in this room | that player |
| `red|black` | one of the listed words | the word, in lower case |
| `text...` | the rest of the line | a string |
| `words...` | the rest of the line | a list of words |

## The function and what it returns

The function runs when a player types the command and the line fits. Two
behaviour rules:

- **The function may `task.wait`.** A command is an input event, outside the
  tick budget but under the 100 ms runaway limit (see
  [Limits](#systems-limits)).
- **A returned string shows to the player in red**, such as
  `return "Finish this match first"`. It is the built-in way to refuse.

## Options

| Option | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `permission` | string | A permission node; without it, a player does not see or run the command. |
| `aliases` | `{ string }` | More names for the same command, such as `{ "hub" }`. |
| `help` | string | The text `/help` shows after the usage. |
| `suggest` | `{ [arg]: list or function }` | Per argument: the words to offer as the player types. |

`/help` is the engine's own: it lists **every command the player may run**, so
a command behind a permission node the player lacks does not appear there.

## Suggestions

`suggest` is per argument name: a list of words, or a function
`(player, typed, args)` that returns one. `args` holds the earlier arguments
that parse. It runs as the player types: **no `task.wait`**.

```luau
-- A tooltip shows beside a suggestion; `args` holds what was typed before.
commands.add("pay <to:player> <amount:integer 1..>", pay, {
    suggest = { amount = function(player, typed, args)
        return { { text = tostring(bank.of(player)), tooltip = "Everything you have" }, "10", "100" }
    end },
})
```

- A word may be `{ text = "arcade", tooltip = "Games" }`; **1.13+ clients show
  the tooltip**.
- Only words that start with the typed text are kept.
- `player` arguments and word lists (`red|black`) suggest themselves.

The handle changes a list while the pack runs — `command:suggest` sends the
new list to every player:

```luau
-- The handle changes a list while the pack runs.
local go = commands.add("go <place:word>", go_to, { suggest = { place = { "lobby" } } })
go:suggest("place", open_places())
```

Pass `nil` or `false` to offer nothing from now on. `command:cancel()` takes
the command away entirely.

<a id="systems-commands--one-name-several-shapes"></a>

## One name, several shapes

Calls with one name, such as `"tekkit"` and
`"tekkit give <item:word>"`, make one command. Each shape has its own
permission. **The first shape the line fits runs.**

## Who owns a name

- **One pack owns a name** in a room. A second pack that adds the name or an
  alias of it gets an error.
- `/help` and `/world` belong to the engine.
- A pack command replaces a game command of the same name.

> **Gotcha:**
> aliases claim the name too — adding `/spawn` with the alias
> `"hub"` blocks every other pack in the room from either name.


## Per room

- [`commands.run(player, line)`](#ref-Commands-run) runs a line for a player
  as if they typed it, so one pack opens what another declared: a compass
  runs `"/servers"`, whichever pack owns it. The player's own permissions
  apply. Only a command a pack declared in the player's room runs; `false`
  means none did, and the engine's and the game's commands are never run
  this way.

`commands` is the main room's, `room.commands` another room's. Destroying a
room removes its commands (see
[Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions)).

## See also

- [Permissions](#players-permissions) — the permission nodes `opts.permission` checks.
- [The event model](#concepts-events) — commands as input events, and what may `task.wait`.
- [Limits](#systems-limits) — the 100 ms runaway limit that covers commands.
- [`commands.add`](#ref-Commands-add) — the reference entry.
- [`Command`](#ref-Command) — the handle: `:suggest` and `:cancel`.

---

<!-- /systems/storage/ -->

<a id="systems-storage"></a>

## Storage

> **In short:**
> `storage` is a pack's own local key–value store, saved as JSON
> in its `storage.json` — values a pack keeps between restarts. This page
> covers the five calls, what a value may be (the JSON shape rules), the
> UTF-8 rule for strings and keys, and `storage.status`/`storage.flush` for
> tracking and forcing the save. For data shared across every server of an
> experience, see [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores).


## The calls

| Call | Returns | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `storage.get(key: string)` | any | The value saved under `key`, or nil when there is none. |
| `storage.set(key: string, value: any)` | — | Saves a value under `key`; nil forgets it. |
| `storage.keys(prefix: string?)` | `{ string }` | Every key, sorted; with a prefix, only those that start with it. |
| `storage.status()` | `{ pending, error }` | Last persistence error and whether there are unsaved changes. |
| `storage.flush()` | — | Yields until saved; raises an error on failure. |

`storage.set` changes memory immediately; unflushed changes can still be lost
if the process crashes. **Only `nil` deletes** — `{}` saves and reads back as
an empty table.

## What a value may be

Storage is JSON-backed, so a value must have a JSON shape. A value it cannot
hold is an error that names it, never a changed copy:

```luau
local t = { 1, 2 }; t.total = 3
storage.set("score", t)
-- error names score and total: mixed lists and records have no JSON shape.

storage.set("tick", function() end)
-- error: storage cannot save tick: a function is not a JSON value...
```

The shape rules:

- Records use string keys; lists must be contiguous from index 1. A table
  cannot mix the two.
- Numbers must be finite, and cyclic tables raise an error **before changing
  stored data**.
- Persistent data views are accepted directly; reads return detached plain
  tables.

## The UTF-8 rule

Strings and record keys in JSON-backed storage must be valid UTF-8; invalid
bytes raise an error instead of being replaced. Use
`stores.open():blob_put` for binary data — see
[Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores--blobs).

> **Note:**
> the UTF-8 rule also applies to persistent entity and block data
> and other JSON-backed APIs.


## Saving, status and flush

`storage.status()` returns `{ pending: boolean, error: string? }`. A write
failure remains visible and is retried.

`storage.flush()` yields until the current values are saved, or raises the
write error. Call it from a callback or `task.spawn`, **after initialization**
— not at the top level of the entry script.

> **Gotcha:**
> a failed flush raises the write error; the values stay pending
> and the failure stays visible in `storage.status().error` until a retry
> succeeds.


On a script reload, local storage is flushed before the replacement loads
(see [Runtime](#concepts-runtime--reload-exactly)).

## When to use storage, and when a shared store

The `storage` API stays a **local per-pack JSON file, even in a published
world**: each server of the experience has its own copy, and nothing is
shared. Use it for per-pack state that one server owns outright — a pack's
own settings, a local cache, a leaderboard the pack computes alone.

Use [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) when several servers — every
instance of an experience, or a development workload and its instances — must
read and write the same facts, or for blobs and leases.

## See also

- [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) — the experience-wide store, with
  versions, conflicts, leases and blobs.
- [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) — the reload rules that flush storage first.
- [Limits](#systems-limits) — the tick budget, and where every numeric limit
  lives.

---

<!-- /systems/shared-stores/ -->

<a id="systems-shared-stores"></a>

## Shared stores

> **In short:**
> `stores.open` returns the one store an experience shares —
> every instance, and the development workload, see the same facts and blobs.
> Writes are versioned (a conflict is a structured error your `pcall` sees),
> leases hand out fencing tokens, and blobs keep per-player binary data. Every
> call yields while the I/O runs, so there are calling rules and a
> 32-pending-requests cap.


## One store per experience

On Minefort, a development workload and all instances of its experience share
one store. **A pack cannot choose another store.** When `CITADEL_STORE` names
a socket, that socket must work or the call fails. The first call logs which
store opened, and where.

```luau
local scores = stores.open()
players.on_join(function(player)
    local visits = scores:increment("visits", 1)
    player:message("Visit number " .. tostring(visits))
end)
```

`stores.open()` returns the experience's store. **Passing an id is an
error.** The `storage` API, by contrast, stays a local per-pack JSON file even
in a published world — see [Storage](#systems-storage).

## The calls

| Call | Returns | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stores.open()` | `DurableStore` | The experience's one store; no id. |
| `handle:get(key)` | `(value, version)` | A fact's value; version zero means absent. |
| `handle:set(key, value, if_version, lease?)` | new version | Writes a fact if its version is still `if_version`. |
| `handle:delete(key, if_version, lease?)` | — | Removes a fact if its version is still `if_version`. |
| `handle:increment(key, by)` | number | Atomically increments a number, starting at zero. |
| `handle:list(prefix?, cursor?, limit?)` | `(keys, next_cursor)` | Fact keys with this prefix, a page at a time. |
| `handle:blob_get(player_uuid, key)` | `(string?, version)` | One player's binary blob, or nil. |
| `handle:blob_put(player_uuid, key, bytes, if_version, lease?)` | new version | Writes one player's binary blob. |
| `handle:blob_delete(player_uuid, key, if_version, lease?)` | — | Deletes one player's blob. |
| `stores.blob_list(player_uuid)` | entries | A player's blobs across all blob stores in this scope. |
| `stores.lease(key, holder, ttl_ms)` | number | Takes a lease; returns a fencing token. |
| `stores.renew(key, token)` | — | Extends the lease that `token` holds. |
| `stores.release(key, token)` | — | Gives up the lease that `token` holds. |
| `stores.request(query, bytes?)` | `(answer, blob_bytes?)` | Sends one raw query; yields until it answers. |

`stores.blob_list` returns entries across all blob stores in this scope, each
with its store, key, version and size. `handle:list` returns the cursor for
the next page, or nil at the end.

**Facts and blobs have separate keys:** a fact `"world"` and a blob `"world"`
are different values.

## Versions and conflicts

`get` returns the value with its version — **version zero means absent**.
`set` and `delete` take `if_version`: the write only lands if the version is
still the one you read. A mismatch is a conflict, not a silent overwrite.

`pcall` preserves the value passed to `error`, including tables, numbers and
booleans; native binding errors remain readable strings. Store errors reach
`pcall` as a table:

| Error table | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `{err = "conflict", version = current_version}` | The version you read is stale — read again and retry. |
| `{err = "held", by = current_holder}` | The fencing token is stale — the lease is held by someone else. |

> **Gotcha:**
> after an I/O timeout, a write may have committed. Retry only
> versioned writes, never an increment.


## Leases

`stores.lease(key, holder, ttl_ms)` returns a **fencing token**; `renew` and
`release` maintain the lease. Leases last up to **one hour**, and there are at
most 100,000 issued lease tokens. A stale fencing token fails with
`{err = "held", by = current_holder}` — the `lease?` argument of `set`,
`delete`, `blob_put` and `blob_delete` ties the write to a token you hold.

<a id="systems-shared-stores--blobs"></a>

## Blobs

Blobs are per-player binary values, keyed by the player's uuid — use them
where JSON cannot hold the data (see the UTF-8 rule in
[Storage](#systems-storage)). At most 32 MiB a blob, and each player may have at
most 1,000 blobs.

> **Note:**
> hosted blobs are not in world archive backups.


<a id="systems-shared-stores--limits"></a>

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Keys | at most 256 bytes |
| Facts | at most 1 MiB |
| Blobs | at most 32 MiB |
| Hosted storage per experience | 512 MiB, and 1 MiB more for every Java player who has ever joined it |
| Number of values | no limit |
| Blobs per player | at most 1,000 |
| Lease tokens | at most 100,000 issued; leases last up to one hour |
| Pending requests per pack | at most 32 |

<a id="systems-shared-stores--where-the-data-lives-without-a-socket"></a>

## Where the data lives without a socket

**Without a socket, data lives in files that survive a restart.** Every local
run works this way.

- Facts are in `data/store/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000.json`.
- A blob is a file under
  `data/store/blobs/<player-uuid>/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/`.
- **Writes are atomic.** A killed server keeps the previous value.
- `store_dir` in `citadel.yml` moves that directory. Two servers on one laptop
  need two directories (see [Server settings](#systems-server-settings)).

<a id="systems-shared-stores--calling-rules"></a>

## Calling rules

Every call yields while the I/O runs; other callbacks continue meanwhile.

- Call from scripts, callbacks or tasks.
- **Do not call from synchronous ask handlers or at module initialization.**
- A pack can have up to **32 pending requests**.

> **Tip:**
> a `task.spawn` around a store call at startup keeps module load
> from blocking on I/O — the pattern [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) describes for
> the initialization exception.


A world release rollback does not rewind shared facts or blobs — treat store
writes as external effects that survive (see [Runtime](#concepts-runtime--reload-exactly)).

## See also

- [Storage](#systems-storage) — the local per-pack JSON store, and when it is
  the better fit.
- [Shop](#systems-shop) — purchase delivery uses the same retry rules.
- [Server settings](#systems-server-settings) — `store_dir` moves the store
  files.
- [`DurableStore`](#ref-DurableStore) — the reference entry for the handle.
- [Limits](#systems-limits) — every numeric limit in one place.

---

<!-- /systems/network/ -->

<a id="systems-network"></a>

## Network

> **In short:**
> `network` is for an experience made of more than one server:
> the pack asks Minefort to start **instances** of the experience's members
> and is told about them. This page covers members and labels, `find` and
> `start`, the instance table and its states, how [`player:connect`](#ref-Player-connect)
> moves players between servers, the failure reasons, and every limit.


## Members, labels, instances

An experience's servers are **instances** of its **members**. An instance has
a **label**. One member can run in several ways, such as `2v2` and `4v4` —
the label says which. Minefort stores the label and filters on it, and does
nothing else with it.

**Any server of the network can call `network`.** The pack names a member and
a label. Minefort decides the network, the instance's id and where the
instance runs. Without a network — every local run — every answer is
`nil, "unavailable"`.

## The default member: sending players there

The default member is a place where players pick how to play. This author
calls an instance of `"bedwars-arena"` an arena:

```luau
-- The default member: a place where players pick how to play.
-- This author calls an instance of "bedwars-arena" an arena.
local waiting = {} -- instance id -> the players who go there when it is online

commands.add("join <label:word>", function(player, args)
    local arena, why = network.find{
        label = args.label,   -- "2v2"
        party = player,       -- room for the player's whole party
        start = { member = "bedwars-arena", slots = 8, data = { map = "castle" } },
    }
    if not arena then return "No arena now: " .. tostring(why) end
    if arena.state == "online" then
        player:connect(arena.id)
    else
        -- It is still starting. Keep the player here until it is online.
        waiting[arena.id] = waiting[arena.id] or {}
        table.insert(waiting[arena.id], player)
    end
end)

network.on_instance_change(function(instance)
    if instance.state ~= "online" then return end
    for _, player in waiting[instance.id] or {} do player:connect(instance.id) end
    waiting[instance.id] = nil
end)

network.on_instance_stop(function(id) waiting[id] = nil end)
```

## The member's side: saying where it is

An instance says how much room it has with `network.status`, and learns its
own `data` — the value the starter passed — with `network.info`:

```luau
-- The member "bedwars-arena": it says how much room it has.
local me = network.info()                 -- `me.id` is nil on a server that is not an instance
local map = me and me.data and me.data.map or "castle"

players.on_join(function()
    if me and me.id then network.status{ open = math.max(0, me.slots - #players.list()), status = "waiting" } end
end)
-- When the round starts: network.status{ open = 0, status = "playing" }
-- When the round ends, each player goes back to the default member:
--   player:connect(me.network)     -- the name of the network
```

## The calls

| Call | Returns | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `network.start{ member, label, slots, data? }` | `{id, state}` | Starts an instance; answers at once with `state = "starting"`. |
| `network.find{ label, players?, party?, start? }` | `{id, state}` or nil | The instance to send `players` players to. |
| `network.instances(label?)` | list | Everything this network runs: its always-on servers, then its games started on demand. |
| `network.online(label?)` | number | How many play on this network; the answer is kept 5 seconds. |
| `network.browse(view, options?)` | rows, total | Finds other networks. **The platform's hub only.** |
| `network.stop(id)` | boolean | Stops an instance of this network; true when accepted. |
| `network.info()` | `{network, id?, ...}` | This server's network, and the instance it runs on. |
| `network.status{ open, status?, meta? }` | — | Says where this instance is. Does not yield. |
| `network.on_instance_start(fn)` | Connection | Calls `fn(instance)` when an instance is first seen. |
| `network.on_instance_change(fn)` | Connection | Calls `fn(instance)` when an instance's `state`, `open`, `status` or `meta` changes. |
| `network.on_instance_stop(fn)` | Connection | Calls `fn(id)` when an instance is gone. |

`network.start` returns `{id, state}` at once, with `state = "starting"`: the
instance comes online later. `slots` is the number of players the instance
takes. `data` is the pack's own value for the instance, read there with
`network.info()`.

`network.info()` returns `{network}` on every server of a network —
`network` is the name of the network. On an instance it returns
`{network, id, member, label, slots, data}`; `id` is nil on a server that is
not an instance.

## `find` in detail

`network.find{ label, players?, party?, start? }` returns `{id, state}` for
the instance to send `players` players to, or nil when no instance has room.

- It picks an `online` instance with that label and that much `open`, **the
  fullest first**.
- The room is held for **10 seconds**, so two calls do not both get the last
  place.
- `players` is 1 unless you set it.
- `party` is a player, or their uuid. When they lead a `/party`, Minefort
  holds room for every member. Connect the leader, and the party follows them
  there. A player who leads no party needs room for one.
- With `start = { member, slots, data? }`, Minefort starts an instance when
  none has room, and holds the room on it. The `state` is then `"starting"`.

> **Tip:**
> use `find` with `start`, not `find` and then `start`. The default
> runs on many servers, and each would start its own instance.


## `instances`, `online` and `browse`

`network.instances(label?)` returns everything this network runs, as this
experience sees it: first its own servers that run all the time, online and
taking players, as `{id, name, state, players, region}` — on the platform's
hub, the hubs — then the network's games started on demand, each the
instance table below. With `label`, only that mode's games:
`network.instances('4v4v4v4')`. `id` is what [`player:connect`](#ref-Player-connect)
takes; never another network's. It returns nil and why when Minefort did not
answer.

`network.online(label?)` returns how many play on this network: on the
platform's hub, everyone on Minefort; on any other network, its members and
their instances. With `label`, only the players in that mode's games, every
region's. An answer is kept for **5 seconds**, so a scoreboard can ask on
every redraw. It returns nil and why when Minefort did not answer.

`network.browse(view, options?)` finds **other networks**, and only the
platform's hub may ask:

- `view` is `"search"` (what matches `query`: names as they are typed, and
  domains), `"for-you"` (more of what `player` plays, busiest first, none of
  their recent ones), `"recent"` (where `player` played last, newest first)
  or `"featured"` (the busiest). A network is one row, however many servers
  it has: `{id, name, category, motd, icon, players, maxPlayers, state}`.
- `options` is `{player?, query?, page?, category?, online?, ids?, sort?,
  also?}`. `page` is from 1; `sort` is `"players"` or `"name"`. It returns
  one page of **6 rows** and how many there are in all:
  `local rows, total = network.browse('featured', { page = 2 })`.
- `also = { recent = true, favorites = ids }` brings a board's sidebar in the
  same round trip, as a third value: `side.recent` and `side.favorites` are
  each `{rows, total}`.
- On a refusal it returns nil and why: `"unsupported"` anywhere but the
  platform's hub, `"not-here"` for a player who is not on this hub,
  `"unavailable"` when Minefort's search is down, or `"timeout"`.

## `status` in detail

`network.status{ open, status?, meta? }` says where this instance is. It
returns nothing and does not yield.

- `open` is the number of players the instance takes now. `0` closes it to
  `find`.
- `status` is the pack's own word, such as `"waiting"` or `"playing"`.
- `meta` is the pack's own value. Other servers of the network read it.
- Minefort takes **one status a second**. The first call goes at once. Of the
  calls in the second after it, only the last goes.

## The instance table

Every instance — from `instances`, the `on_instance_*` events, or a
`find`/`start` answer — is the same shape:

| Field | Set by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Minefort | The instance's name. `player:connect` takes it. |
| `member`, `label` | the pack that started it | Which member, and which label. |
| `state` | Minefort | `"starting"`, then `"online"`, then `"stopping"`. |
| `open` | the instance | The number of players it takes now. |
| `status` | the instance | Its own word, or nil. |
| `players` | Minefort | The number of players on it. |
| `meta` | the instance | Its own value, or nil. |

## Moving players

**`network` does not move players. [`player:connect`](#ref-Player-connect)
does.** The instance's `id` is the server name it takes. The name of the
network, `network.info().network`, sends a player back to the default member.

Do not send a player to an instance that is `"starting"`: keep the player
until the instance is `"online"` — the default-member example above shows the
`waiting` pattern.

## Events, and repairing the list

**Events come to the default member's servers only.** Call
`network.instances()` once at the start, then keep the list from
`on_instance_start`, `on_instance_change` and `on_instance_stop`. An event
can be lost — call `network.instances()` again, **once a minute at most**, to
repair the list.

## Failures

**A failed call returns nil and a reason.** `start`, `find` and `info` return
`nil, reason`; `instances`, `online` and `browse` return `nil, reason` too;
`stop` returns `false, reason`. The reason is Minefort's word, or one of
these:

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `"unavailable"` | There is no network here. Every local run answers this. |
| `"io"` | The request was not sent. |
| `"timeout"` | No answer came in 35 seconds. A `start` may have happened. |

`find` returns `nil` with **no reason** when no instance has room — that is
not a failure.

<a id="systems-network--limits"></a>

## Limits

A value out of these is an error, and nothing is sent:

| Value | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | 1 to 32 characters of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-` |
| `member` | 1 to 40 characters of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-` |
| `slots` | 1 to 200 |
| `players` | 1 to 64 |
| `open` | 0 to 200 |
| `data` | at most 4096 bytes as JSON |
| `meta` | at most 512 bytes as JSON |
| `status` | at most 32 characters |

- An unknown field in a table is an error.
- A network has at most **20 instances in a region**, and **one `start` a
  second**.
- Minefort removes an instance with no players for 60 seconds after its first
  player, or for 5 minutes without one.

## Calling rules

Calls yield, like `stores`, but for `status` and the three events. Call from
scripts, callbacks or tasks — the same rules as
[Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores--calling-rules).

## See also

- [Hub](#systems-hub) — the hub browses networks with `network.browse` and
  lists its hubs with `network.instances`, all travelled with
  `player:connect`.
- [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) — the store every instance of the
  experience shares.
- [`NetworkInstance`](#ref-NetworkInstance) — the reference entry for the
  instance table.
- [Limits](#systems-limits) — every numeric limit in one place.

<!-- /systems/http/ -->

<a id="systems-http"></a>

## HTTP

> **In short:**
> `http.get` fetches a public URL and waits, like `task.wait` —
> events and other callbacks run meanwhile. The answer is an
> [`HttpResponse`](#ref-HttpResponse): read `ok`, `status`, `body`, `headers`,
> or parse it with `:json()` and `:image()`. A `cache` option keeps 200
> answers on disk, and `http.socket` opens a WebSocket the engine keeps
> alive.


## `http.get`

```luau
local res = http.get("https://tile.example.org/15/9649/12315.png", {
    query = { key = "abc" },             -- added to the URL, encoded
    headers = { accept = "image/png" },
    timeout = 15,                        -- seconds, 1 .. 60; 15 is the default
    cache = 86400,                       -- seconds a 200 answer is kept on disk; left out, nothing is kept
})
res.ok        -- true for a 2xx status
res.status    -- 200; 0 when no answer came
res.error     -- why no answer came, or nil
res.body      -- the answer, a string
res.headers   -- { ["content-type"] = "image/png", ... }, names in lower case
res:json()    -- the body as a table; an error when it is not JSON
res:image()   -- a PNG body as { width, height, pixels }; pixels is a buffer, 4 bytes (RGBA) a pixel, row by row
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `query` | Added to the URL, encoded. |
| `headers` | Request headers, such as `{ accept = "image/png" }`. |
| `timeout` | Seconds, 1 .. 60; 15 is the default. Clamped, and must be finite. |
| `cache` | Seconds a 200 answer is kept on disk; left out, nothing is kept. Negative means zero. |

`res:image()` reads PNG with 8 bits a channel, not interlaced.

## Waiting, and where to call it from

The call waits, like `task.wait`. Events, other callbacks and other chunks run
during the wait. **Call it from a script or a callback, not from the top level
of a module.**

- Transport failures return `res.ok = false` — a failed request is not an
  error; read `res.error`.
- Invalid arguments or exhausted request slots raise errors.

<a id="systems-http--limits"></a>

## Limits

- Only `http` and `https`, and only GET. An answer is at most **16 MiB**.
- A pack can have **64 requests without an answer**. Eight are on the wire at
  the same time.
- A server's packs send **600 requests in a minute** at most, all packs
  together. Over that, a request waits for room, and fails when its `timeout`
  ends first. An answer from the cache does not count.
- A host can turn off private and loopback addresses. Such an address is then
  an error in `res.error`, **also after a redirect**.

<a id="systems-http--the-cache"></a>

## The cache

`cache` keeps the body in `<pack>/data/http/`. A cached answer has status 200
and no headers. Use it for data that does not change, such as tiles — the
86400-second tile cache in the example above is one day.

A `range` header gets a part of a file
(`headers = { range = "bytes=0-126" }`). The status is then **206**, and the
cache keeps each range by itself.

> **Note:**
> a gzip body arrives undone, with the server's
> `content-encoding: gzip` or without it. A tile cut out of an archive is
> gzip without the header.


## The host's switches

The host decides whether packs get this, with the environment the server
starts in. **A pack cannot change it, and the server's `citadel.yml` cannot:**

```sh
CITADEL_DISABLE_HTTP=true         # http.get is off for every pack; res.error then says so
CITADEL_DISABLE_HTTP_LOCAL=true   # no private or loopback address: a pack cannot reach the host's own network
```

## A socket

`http.socket` opens a WebSocket and keeps it open. Use it for what a server
says the moment it happens, such as a chat line or a score, where `http.get`
would ask again and again.

```luau
local socket = http.socket("wss://live.example.org/room/7", {
    headers = { authorization = "Bearer abc" },   -- sent with the handshake
    on_message = function(message)
        local event = message:json()               -- or message.text, the message as it came
        if event.kind == "chat" then message(event.author .. ": " .. event.body) end
    end,
})
socket.open          -- true while the connection is up
socket:send("hello") -- queues text; true if queued, false if closed or full
socket.error         -- terminal queue overflow, or nil
socket:cancel()      -- closes it for good
```

- When the connection ends or cannot be made, the engine dials again every 3
  seconds. The log says so once. **The pack gets no event for it: read
  `socket.open`.** Receive-queue overflow is terminal and does not reconnect.
- A socket gives no message twice and none from before it opened. For what
  was said before, ask with `http.get` first.
- `on_message` runs on a tick, with the tick budget of any callback. At most
  32 messages of a socket go to the pack in a tick; the rest wait.
- Each direction queues at most **256 messages or 4 MiB per socket**. If the
  incoming queue fills, the socket closes permanently and `socket.error`
  explains why. Cancel its handle, then create a new socket after handling
  the gap. The outgoing queue returns false when full. **A true send result
  means queued, not delivered.**
- Only `ws` and `wss`. A message is at most 1 MiB; a larger send is an error.
  A binary message arrives as text with invalid UTF-8 replaced.
- A pack can have 8 sockets. A socket ends with the script.
- The host's two switches for `http.get` hold for sockets too.

<a id="systems-http--a-world-from-fetched-data"></a>

## A world from fetched data

`world.on_generate` can wait, so a chunk can come from data that is fetched
when the chunk loads:

```luau
local tiles = {}
local function tile(tx, tz)                        -- one fetch for each 256 by 256 blocks
    local key = tx .. "," .. tz
    local t = tiles[key]
    if not t then
        t = { loading = true }
        tiles[key] = t                              -- before the wait, so the next chunk does not fetch it again
        local res = http.get(`https://tile.example.org/heights/{tx}/{tz}.png`, { cache = 86400 })
        if res.ok then t.image = res:image() end
        t.loading = false
    end
    while t.loading do task.wait(0.05) end          -- another chunk started the fetch
    return t.image
end

world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    local image = tile(chunk.min.x // 256, chunk.min.z // 256)
    for x = chunk.min.x, chunk.max.x do
        for z = chunk.min.z, chunk.max.z do
            local h = if image then buffer.readu8(image.pixels, ((z % 256) * 256 + x % 256) * 4) else 64
            chunk:fill(vec3(x, 0, z), vec3(x, h, z), "stone")
        end
    end
end)
```

- The engine waits 60 s for a chunk. A chunk that is not ready then is air.
- Make the chunk without the data when the fetch fails.

## See also

- [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation) — `world.on_generate` and
  the chunk callbacks this pattern runs inside.
- [Hub](#systems-hub) — reading experience banners with the cache and
  `:image()`.
- [`HttpResponse`](#ref-HttpResponse), [`Socket`](#ref-Socket) — the
  reference entries.
- [Limits](#systems-limits) — every numeric limit in one place.

<!-- /systems/shop/ -->

<a id="systems-shop"></a>

## Shop

> **In short:**
> `shop` sells an experience's products for Minefort Gems. The
> player says yes or no in **Minefort's own dialog** — the pack learns only
> whether a purchase was paid, never the balance, the price or a reason.
> This page covers prompting, checking ownership, the `on_paid` delivery
> contract and its acknowledgement rules, `on_declined`, and the retry rules
> that make delivery exactly once.


## The privacy model

**The player says yes or no in Minefort's own dialog, not in the pack.** The
pack learns only whether a purchase was paid. It never sees the player's
Gems, the price or a reason. A pack's own shop screen can offer and explain,
but the transaction itself is Minefort's.

## Prompting and checking ownership

```luau
players.on_join(function(player)
    if shop.owns(player, "vip") then
        player:message("Welcome back, VIP")
    else
        shop.prompt(player, "vip") -- Minefort shows its dialog
    end
end)
```

| Call | Returns | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shop.prompt(player, product)` | request id, or nil | Minefort shows its dialog; nil when it did not offer it. |
| `shop.owns(player, product)` | boolean | Whether the player owns a pass. |
| `shop.on_paid(fn)` | Connection | Called for each undelivered paid purchase. |
| `shop.on_declined(fn)` | Connection | Called when the player said no or did not answer. |

A player or a uuid string works wherever a player is taken.

## Delivery: `on_paid`

```luau
shop.on_paid(function(purchase)
    -- Hand the item over here. Returning without an error marks it delivered.
    for _, player in players.list() do
        if player.uuid == purchase.player then player:message("Thanks for buying VIP") end
    end
end)
```

`shop.on_paid` calls `fn({request, player, product})` for each undelivered
paid purchase — `player` is the buyer's uuid, `product` the product's key,
`request` the purchase's own id.

The delivery contract:

- It **runs on the server the player is on**: an experience has many servers,
  and each one hands over only to its own players.
- A purchase for a player who is not online **waits until they join one**.
- **At least one active paid handler must complete successfully, and all
  active paid handlers must succeed, before the purchase is acknowledged.**
- With no paid handler, or if one raises an error, it stays pending.
- An `on_declined` listener alone never acknowledges a paid purchase.

## `on_declined`

```luau
shop.on_declined(function(purchase)
    -- The player said no, or did not answer. Close the pack's own shop screen.
end)
```

`shop.on_declined` calls `fn({request, player, product})` when the player
said no or did not answer. It sees the same purchase shape as `on_paid`.

## Retries and idempotence

**Delivery can repeat after a failure or restart: use `purchase.request` as a
durable idempotency key when granting a reward.** Record the request id in
[shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) or [storage](#systems-storage) before
granting, so a repeated delivery does not grant twice.

The same error discipline as stores applies:

- After an error, read again.
- After an I/O timeout, a write may have committed. **Retry only versioned
  writes, never an increment.**
- A world release rollback does not rewind shared facts or blobs.

## Product keys

A product key is **1 to 32 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`**. Another
key is an error.

## Where the shop exists

Calls yield, like `stores` — call them from scripts, callbacks or tasks, not
from synchronous ask handlers or module initialization.

> **Gotcha:**
> only experiences in the Minefort Creator Rewards Program have
> the shop. Elsewhere, and in local runs, `prompt` returns nil and `owns`
> returns false — code written against the shop degrades, it does not error.


## Portals: rent and point

On the experience grounds, `hub.rent(player, slot, product, experience)`
offers a portal for Gems **like `shop.prompt`**: it returns a request id or
nil, and **`shop.on_paid` hands the purchase over**. `hub.point` turns the
player's own live portal for free. See [Hub](#systems-hub--portals-rent-and-point).

## See also

- [Hub](#systems-hub) — `hub.rent` and `hub.point`, the portal calls that flow
  through the shop.
- [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) — versioned writes for idempotent
  delivery.
- [Menus](#ui-menus) — a pack's own shop screen to close on decline.
- [`ShopPurchase`](#ref-ShopPurchase) — the reference entry for the purchase
  table.

<!-- /systems/hub/ -->

<a id="systems-hub"></a>

## Hub

> **In short:**
> `hub` is what Minefort tells its own hub: the experience
> portals of the grounds, player ranks, and the `rent` and `point` calls for
> live portals. The server lists are not the hub's any more — the hub browses
> them with [`network.browse`](#ref-network-browse), its hubs and always-on
> servers with [`network.instances`](#ref-network-instances), and asks the
> player count with [`network.online`](#ref-network-online). The lists refresh
> every minute; the first call of `experiences` waits up to two seconds for
> them, so call it from a task. This page covers the calls with their exact
> fields, ranks, banners and the portal calls `hub.rent` and `hub.point`.


## The calls

```luau
task.spawn(function()
    for _, s in network.browse('featured') or {} do print(s.name, s.players) end
    for _, e in hub.experiences() do print(e.slot, e.experience) end
    for _, h in network.instances() or {} do print(h.name, h.players) end
    print(network.online())
end)
```

| Call | Returns | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hub.experiences()` | list | The portals of the experience grounds. |
| `hub.role(player)` | string | The player's rank on Minefort, or nil. |
| `hub.rent(player, slot, product, experience?)` | request id | Offers a portal of the grounds for Gems. |
| `hub.point(player, slot, experience)` | boolean | Turns the player's own live portal. |
| `network.browse(view, options?)` | rows, total | Finds other networks. Hub only. |
| `network.instances(label?)` | list | The network's always-on servers and hubs. |
| `network.online(label?)` | number | How many play on this network. |

**Anywhere but a hub, the lists are empty and the ranks are nil** — the calls
work, they just have nothing to say.

## `hub.experiences()`

Returns a list of `{slot, experience, title, pitch, icon, banner, players}` —
the portals of the experience grounds:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `slot` | The portal's slot. |
| `experience` | The name `/play` takes. |
| `title`, `pitch` | What the portal shows. |
| `icon`, `banner` | Artwork, or nil. |
| `players` | How many players the experience has. |

A slot that is not in the list has no experience.

## The server lists live on `network`

`hub` no longer lists servers or hubs. The hub reads them through the
`network` calls — all documented on [Network](#systems-network):

- [`network.browse(view, options?)`](#ref-network-browse) finds other
  networks: `"featured"` (the busiest), `"search"`, `"for-you"` and
  `"recent"`. Each row is a network — `{id, name, category, motd, icon,
  players, maxPlayers, state}` — and `id` is what `player:connect` takes.
- [`network.instances()`](#ref-network-instances) returns this network's
  servers that run all the time — on the platform's hub, the hubs — each
  `{id, name, state, players, region}`, then the network's games started on
  demand.
- [`network.online()`](#ref-network-online) returns how many play on this
  network: on the platform's hub, everyone on Minefort.

## Ranks

`hub.role(player)` returns the player's rank on Minefort — `"owner"`,
`"admin"`, `"moderator"` or `"builder"` — and nil for everyone else. It also
takes a uuid, with or without dashes.

Minefort sends the ranks **every minute**, so a new rank reaches the hub
within one. Anywhere but a hub, they are nil.

> **Note:**
> `hub.role` is Minefort-wide — the ranks of the platform, not of
> this server. The server's own all-permissions list is `operators` in
> [server settings](#systems-server-settings).


## Reading a banner

A `banner` is a 1024×512 PNG its creator uploaded and Minefort checked:
**8 by 4 maps**. Read it with the HTTP cache — a new banner has a new URL, so
the cache never shows an old one:

```luau
local image = http.get(banner, { cache = 86400 }):image()
```

See [HTTP](#systems-http--the-cache) for `cache` and `:image()`.

<a id="systems-hub--portals-rent-and-point"></a>

## Portals: rent and point

- `hub.rent(player, slot, product, experience)` offers a portal of the
  grounds for Gems, **like `shop.prompt`**: `product` is one of the hub's
  rentals, such as `portal_24h`, and `experience` the name `/play` takes of
  any published experience, which the portal then leads to. It returns a
  request id, or nil; **`shop.on_paid` hands the purchase over**. Renting
  your own portal again adds time, and may leave `experience` out to keep
  what it shows.
- `hub.point(player, slot, experience)` turns the player's own live portal
  to another published experience, as often as they like. It returns whether
  it did.

**Minefort decides who may rent or point what:** a stand someone else holds,
or a name that is no published experience, is a no. Anywhere but its hub,
every answer is no.

## Calling from a task

Minefort keeps the lists up to date. **The first call of `experiences` waits
at most two seconds for them, so call it from a task** — the opening example
wraps the list calls in `task.spawn`.

## See also

- [Shop](#systems-shop) — `on_paid` delivers what `hub.rent` sells.
- [HTTP](#systems-http) — banners through the cache and `:image()`.
- [Network](#systems-network) — `browse`, `instances`, `online` and the
  instance events; the other kind of server `player:connect` reaches.
- [Permissions](#players-permissions) — the server's own operator and
  permission model.

<!-- /systems/server-settings/ -->

<a id="systems-server-settings"></a>

## Server settings

> **In short:**
> beside the server runs a `citadel.yml` — the server's own
> configuration, separate from a pack's manifest. It picks the mode, where
> the packs and the world live, what to listen on, the operators and how a
> player's identity is checked. Every key is optional; an unknown key stops
> the server. This page is the key table and the two decisions the file
> makes: the mode, and identity.


## The file

```yaml
# citadel.yml
mode: lite              # "full" = Citadel plays the game, "lite" = the packs are the game
packs: packs            # where the packs are, relative to this folder
bind:                   # what to listen on; each line left out is this default
  java: 0.0.0.0:25565
  packs: 0.0.0.0:25566  # resource packs over HTTP; give a second server on one machine its own
  bedrock: 0.0.0.0:19132    # Bedrock over RakNet (UDP); "" turns it off
  nethernet: 0.0.0.0:19132  # Bedrock over NetherNet (TCP signaling, the same number as RakNet on UDP); "" turns it off
game: a0.1.0            # the game version, "1.8.9" (the default) or "a0.1.0"
world_dir: worlds/a0    # the world folder; a world keeps the game it was written by
operators:              # players with every permission, by uuid (Minefort writes the owner here)
  - 069a79f4-44e9-4726-a5be-fca90e38aaf5
online_mode: true       # check each player with Mojang, as vanilla does; this is the default
nethernet_tls:          # the certificate for Bedrock clients that dial HTTPS; not used behind a proxy with a forwarding secret
  cert: fullchain.pem
  key: privkey.pem
store_dir: data/store   # where `stores` keeps its files when no platform store was named; this is the default
```

## The keys

| Key | Default in the block above | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | — | `"full"` = Citadel plays the game, `"lite"` = the packs are the game. |
| `packs` | `packs` | Where the packs are, relative to this folder. |
| `bind.java` | `0.0.0.0:25565` | The Java listeners' address and port. |
| `bind.packs` | `0.0.0.0:25566` | Resource packs over HTTP. |
| `bind.bedrock` | `0.0.0.0:19132` | Bedrock over RakNet (UDP); `""` turns it off. |
| `bind.nethernet` | `0.0.0.0:19132` | Bedrock over NetherNet (TCP signaling, the same number as RakNet on UDP); `""` turns it off. |
| `game` | `1.8.9` | The game version: `"1.8.9"` (the default) or `"a0.1.0"`. |
| `world_dir` | — | The world folder; a world keeps the game it was written by. |
| `operators` | — | Players with every permission, by uuid; Minefort writes the owner here. |
| `online_mode` | `true` | Check each player with Mojang, as vanilla does. |
| `nethernet_tls.cert` / `.key` | — | The certificate for Bedrock clients that dial HTTPS. |
| `store_dir` | `data/store` | Where `stores` keeps its files when no platform store was named. |
| `min_client` | — | Refuses old clients (see [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions)). |

Every key is optional, and so is the file. With no `packs` key, a `packs`
folder beside the world is used when one exists. **An unknown key or mode
stops the server.**

> **Gotcha:**
> `bind.packs` is its own listener. Give a second server on one
> machine its own `bind.packs` port — two servers cannot serve resource packs
> on the same address.


A pack has its own `citadel.yml` manifest — `entry`, `world`, `spawn_point`
and the rest — documented in [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy); the world
keys are covered in [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation).

## The mode decision order

The mode is decided in this order:

1. A `--full` or `--lite` flag.
2. This file.
3. What the packs agree on in their own manifests.
4. Survival, when there are no packs.

A flag or the server file overrules a pack that names the other mode.

## A player's identity

A player's identity comes from one of three places:

| Where | Who vouches for the name |
| --- | --- |
| Behind a proxy with `MODERN_FORWARDING_SECRET` | The proxy signs it. |
| No proxy, `online_mode: true` | Citadel checks with Mojang. |
| `online_mode: false` | Nobody is checked. |

> **Gotcha:**
> with `online_mode: false`, **anyone can join with any name, an
> operator's too** — and the log warns at start.


## Where the store lives

`store_dir` names where `stores` keeps its files when no platform store was
named — `data/store` by default. Two servers on one laptop need two
directories. See [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores--where-the-data-lives-without-a-socket).

## Old clients

Features differ by client: guard a version-gated call with
`player:supports(...)` and offer something else when it answers false — the
full feature table is in [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions). Or set
`min_client` in citadel.yml to refuse old clients.

## See also

- [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy) — the pack's own `citadel.yml` manifest
  and the load limits.
- [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) — what `store_dir` moves.
- [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions) — `player:supports` and the
  full feature table.
- [What is Citadel](#getting-started-what-is-citadel) — lite, full and plugin modes.
