<!-- /systems/limits/ -->

<a id="systems-limits"></a>

## Limits

> **In short:**
> a pack's tick and event callbacks share a slice of every
> tick — `budget_ms` in the pack's `citadel.yml`, **2 ms by default**. When
> it runs out nothing is killed: events are retained, ticks coalesce, socket
> messages queue. This page covers the budget, `citadel.budget()` and
> `citadel.on_slow`, the 4096-event queue, the asks, and a pointer table to
> every other limit. Reload semantics live in [Runtime](#concepts-runtime--reload-exactly).


## The tick budget

A pack's tick and event callbacks share part of each tick. Set it with
`budget_ms` in the pack's `citadel.yml`. The default is **2 ms**.

| Covered by the budget | Not covered |
| --- | --- |
| `time.on_tick`, `time.every`, the survival events (`world.on_block_break` and the rest) | `players.on_join`, input events (`on_click`, `on_chat`, commands), task threads — these keep the **100 ms runaway limit** |
| | Chunk callbacks keep their separate **2 s** limit |

**It counts work, not time spent waiting** — a callback that yields on I/O
does not spend budget while it waits.

## When the budget runs out

When the budget runs out mid-batch:

- **Ordinary events retain** their original arguments and remaining listeners
  until the next budget window. Canceling a subscription also removes its
  pending delivery. The bounded event queue still applies.
- **`time.on_tick` coalesces** missed ticks: remaining listeners resume with
  the latest tick number. It does not replay every elapsed tick.
- **Socket messages stay queued** until their callback can run.
- **A `time.every` timer that does not fit retains its place** among due
  timers.
- **Nothing is killed.** A started callback always finishes.

Going over is not an error. Do less per tick, or raise `budget_ms`.

## Reading the numbers

```luau
local b = citadel.budget()
print(b.of)        -- 2, the ms this pack gets per tick
print(b.used)      -- what the last tick spent
print(b.peak)      -- the most any tick has spent
print(b.skipped)   -- callbacks not run for want of budget, since the script started
print(b.dropped)   -- events this pack never saw; see below
print(b.slowest)   -- { hook = "on_tick", ms = 4.1 }, or nil
print(b.asks)      -- what the engine's questions cost this pack; see below

citadel.on_slow(function(slow)
    print(slow.hook, slow.used, slow.of, slow.skipped)   -- "on_tick" 2.4 2 3
end)
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `b.of` | The ms this pack gets per tick — `budget_ms` in citadel.yml; 2 by default. |
| `b.used` | What the last tick spent. |
| `b.peak` | The most any tick has spent. |
| `b.skipped` | Callbacks not run for want of budget, since the script started. |
| `b.dropped` | Events this pack never saw — overflow of the event queue. |
| `b.slowest` | `{ hook = "on_tick", ms = 4.1 }`, or nil. |
| `b.asks` | What the engine's questions cost this pack; see below. |

Hook names are short: `"on_tick"`, `"every"`, or the event's name
(`"block_break"`, `"pickup"`).

> **Note:**
> `on_slow` runs **at most once a second**. The server log shows
> the pack, hook and time, **at most once every five seconds**.


## The event queue

**`b.dropped` counts lost ordinary events.** Each pack retains at most
**4096 ordinary events**; overflow drops the oldest ordinary event and logs
the pack.

Joins, leaves, deaths and respawns are retained in order and **never evicted
by ordinary traffic or skipped because the tick budget was spent**. They carry
the original player session, so a delayed leave still has its `player.data`
after a reconnect. This is in-process delivery, not a durable journal across a
server crash — keep lifecycle callbacks short so their retained backlog drains
(see [Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle)).

## The asks

**`b.asks` counts the engine's questions.** An **ask** is a cancellable
event, such as "may this player break this block". The engine waits a few
milliseconds for the answer. Three exist:

| Ask | Kind |
| --- | --- |
| `players.on_break` | `"break"` |
| `players.on_place` | `"place"` |
| `players.on_damage` | `"damage"` |

With no answer in time, the engine **denies the protected action**. With no
protection listener registered, the action follows the normal game rules. A
listener that completes and returns nil still allows the action; an error or
missing answer does not.

Counters are totals; watch them per kind:

```luau
time.every(60, function()
    for kind, count in citadel.budget().asks.kinds do
        if count.missed > count.answered then
            citadel.log(`slow at {kind}: {count.missed} of {count.asks} missed`)
        end
    end
end)
```

The log names a kind you keep missing. **Miss it too often and the engine
stops asking you that kind.** It then takes the default, logs this once, and
sets `disabled`.

Ask handler rules:

- Answer at once. Never call `task.wait` in one.
- Answering costs tick budget, under the hook name `"ask"`.
- A spent budget does not stop an ask from being answered.

The full ask model — vetoes, deadline behaviour, observe-after-veto — is in
[The event model](#concepts-events--asks-the-cancellable-events).

## Other limits, and where they live

| Limit | Where it is documented |
| --- | --- |
| Load: 5 s of work between waits, 30 s in all for the entry script | [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy) |
| Reload entry: 30 s including `task.wait` and read requests | [Runtime](#concepts-runtime--reload-exactly) |
| Chunk callbacks: 2 s; the engine waits 60 s for a chunk | [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation), [HTTP](#systems-http--a-world-from-fetched-data) |
| Store limits: keys 256 B, facts 1 MiB, blobs 32 MiB, hosted 512 MiB + 1 MiB a player, 1,000 blobs a player, 100,000 lease tokens, 32 pending requests | [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores--limits) |
| HTTP: 16 MiB an answer, 64 pending and 8 on the wire a pack, 600 requests a minute a server, 8 sockets, 1 MiB a message, 256 messages or 4 MiB a queue | [HTTP](#systems-http--limits) |
| Network: label 1–32, member 1–40, slots 1–200, players 1–64, `open` 0–200, `data` 4096 B, `meta` 512 B, `status` 32 chars, 20 instances a region, one `start` a second | [Network](#systems-network--limits) |
| Command arguments: ranges and the 100 ms runaway limit | [Commands](#systems-commands), this page |

The one-table view of every number in the corpus is
[the limits table](#appendix-limits-table).

## See also

- [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) — the scheduler around the budget, and the reload
  rules.
- [The event model](#concepts-events) — asks, vetoes and queue semantics.
- [The limits table](#appendix-limits-table) — every numeric limit in one
  table.
- [`Budget`](#ref-Budget) — the reference entry for the numbers.

<!-- /guides/guide-build-a-cottage/ -->

<a id="guides-guide-build-a-cottage"></a>

## Build a cottage

> **In short:**
> this tutorial builds a whole cottage in code — footing, walls,
> windows, roof and garden — as one `world.build` with named parts, pastes it
> into generated terrain, and holds the sky at sunset. It is the guide for
> building well.


## What you build
- A cottage of 9 by 7 blocks on a cobblestone plinth, with oak posts and
  white walls.
- Windows set back into the wall, with a sill under each.
- A gable roof of stairs that overhangs the walls, and a brick chimney.
- A garden: a path, a fence, flowers, a tree and a barrel.

## Before you start

Read [Quick start](#getting-started-quick-start) first. This guide is about building
well, and the code is simple.

## 1. Plan before code

A good build starts as a plan, not as blocks. Write it at the top of
`main.luau`:

```luau
-- main.luau
-- Plan: a small cottage, known at a glance by its steep roof and chimney.
--   footing   a cobblestone plinth, one block wider than the walls
--   body      9 by 7, white walls between oak posts, three blocks tall
--   openings  windows set back, with a sill under each; the door faces south
--   roof      a gable of stairs along x, overhanging by one; a chimney
--   setting   a path to the door, a fenced garden, a tree, a barrel
-- The middle of the door is x = 0, so the cottage is symmetric in x.
```

The plan answers four questions: what makes the build recognisable, its
parts in the order you build them, where it stands, and where the detail
goes. Keep the middle of the door at x = 0: then the house is symmetric,
and every number on the left has a partner on the right.

## 2. One build, in parts

[`world.build`](#ref-World-build) makes a build in code: a schematic with no
file. It gets a builder, `b`, with three calls: `b:block` sets one block,
`b:box` fills a box between two corners, and `b:line` draws a line.

```luau
-- main.luau
-- One build from two parts; `b:part` names each stage inside them.
local cottage = world.build(function(b)
    house(b)
    garden(b)
end)
```

The house and the garden are two modules, each a function that takes the
builder. Inside them, `b:part("walls", ...)` names what it writes. The
names show up when you check and render the build, below.

## 3. The footing

A plinth one block wider than the walls makes the house stand on something:

```luau
-- house.luau
b:part("plinth", function()
    for x = -5, 5 do
        for z = -4, 4 do
            b:block(vec3(x, 0, z), if mix(x, 0, z) < 0.3 then "mossy_cobblestone" else "cobblestone")
        end
    end
    b:box(vec3(-3, 0, -2), vec3(3, 0, 2), "spruce_planks") -- the floor inside
end)
```

A plain cobblestone floor looks flat, so one block in three is mossy. `mix`
decides which:

```luau
-- mix.luau
--!strict
-- 0..1, the same every time for the same block. A wall mixed from two
-- blocks by it builds the same way after every restart.

local function mix(x: number, y: number, z: number): number
    local v = math.sin(x * 12.9898 + y * 4.1414 + z * 78.233) * 43758.5453
    return v - math.floor(v)
end

return mix
```

`math.random` would give a new pattern on every restart. `mix` gives the
same number for the same block every time, so the wall never changes.

## Try it

Render the build at this stage (the commands are in step 9): the plinth is
one block wider than the walls, and about one block in three is mossy —
the same ones after every restart.

## 4. The walls

The walls go up in two `b:box` calls:

```luau
-- house.luau
b:part("walls", function()
    b:box(vec3(-4, 1, -3), vec3(4, 3, 3), "white_terracotta")
    b:box(vec3(-3, 1, -2), vec3(3, 3, 2), "air") -- hollow inside
    for _, x in { -4, 0, 4 } do -- oak posts at the corners and the middle
        for _, z in { -3, 3 } do
            b:box(vec3(x, 1, z), vec3(x, 3, z), "oak_log")
        end
    end
    -- The beam the roof sits on: a ring on the walls, so the room inside
    -- is open up to the roof.
    b:box(vec3(-4, 4, -3), vec3(4, 4, 3), "spruce_planks")
    b:box(vec3(-3, 4, -2), vec3(3, 4, 2), "air")
end)
```

- Fill the whole box, then hollow it out: two lines instead of four walls.
- Oak posts at the corners and in the middle of the long walls stand in
  front of the white wall. That is the timber frame.
- The beam on top is a ring, so the room inside is open up to the roof.

## 5. Windows and the door

A window is not a pane in a flat wall. It is a hole with the glass set
back, and a sill under it:

```luau
-- house.luau
b:part("openings", function()
    for _, x in { -2, 2 } do -- two windows in each long wall, a sill under each
        for _, z in { -3, 3 } do
            local out = if z < 0 then -1 else 1
            b:block(vec3(x, 2, z), "air")
            b:block(vec3(x, 2, z - out), "glass_pane") -- set back into the wall
            b:block(vec3(x, 1, z + out), `spruce_trapdoor[half=top,facing={if out > 0 then "south" else "north"}]`)
        end
    end
    for _, x in { -4, 4 } do -- one in each end wall
        local out = if x < 0 then -1 else 1
        b:block(vec3(x, 2, 0), "air")
        b:block(vec3(x - out, 2, 0), "glass_pane")
    end
    b:block(vec3(0, 1, 3), "spruce_door[facing=south,half=lower]")
    b:block(vec3(0, 2, 3), "spruce_door[facing=south,half=upper]")
    b:block(vec3(0, 3, 4), "lantern[hanging=true]") -- under the eaves
end)
```

- `out` is which way the wall faces: the glass goes one block in, the sill
  one block out.
- A block name can carry its state: `spruce_trapdoor[half=top,facing=north]`
  is a trapdoor on the top half of its block, which reads as a sill.
- The lantern hangs under the eaves, over the door.

## Try it

For every window at x = -2 there is one at x = 2, and the door sits at
x = 0: the build is symmetric in x.

## 6. The roof

The gable steps in and up from both sides, to the ridge:

```luau
-- house.luau
b:part("roof", function()
    -- Four rows of stairs a side, each one block in and one block up.
    for k = 0, 3 do
        b:box(vec3(-5, 4 + k, -4 + k), vec3(5, 4 + k, -4 + k), "spruce_stairs[facing=south]")
        b:box(vec3(-5, 4 + k, 4 - k), vec3(5, 4 + k, 4 - k), "spruce_stairs[facing=north]")
        -- The gable ends, filled under the roof.
        if k < 3 then
            for _, x in { -4, 4 } do
                b:box(vec3(x, 5 + k, -2 + k), vec3(x, 5 + k, 2 - k), "spruce_planks")
            end
        end
    end
    b:box(vec3(-5, 8, 0), vec3(5, 8, 0), "spruce_slab") -- the ridge
    b:box(vec3(3, 1, -2), vec3(3, 9, -2), "bricks") -- the chimney, through the roof
end)
```

Each row of stairs is one block in and one block up from the one below,
from both sides, until they meet at the ridge. The stairs face the middle.
The rows start one block outside the walls: the overhang throws a shadow,
and the house stops looking like a box. The chimney goes up through the
roof from the floor inside.

## 7. The garden

A build with bare grass round it floats. The garden sets the house in a
place:

```luau
-- garden.luau
b:box(vec3(0, 0, 5), vec3(0, 0, 11), "dirt_path")
for _, x in { -6, 6 } do
    b:box(vec3(x, 1, 5), vec3(x, 1, 9), "oak_fence")
end
b:box(vec3(-6, 1, 9), vec3(-2, 1, 9), "oak_fence") -- a gap for the path
b:box(vec3(2, 1, 9), vec3(6, 1, 9), "oak_fence")
```

Fences join their neighbours on their own. The gap in the front fence is
where the path goes through.

```luau
-- garden.luau
for x = -5, 5 do
    for z = 5, 8 do
        if x ~= 0 and mix(x, 1, z) < 0.35 then
            b:block(vec3(x, 1, z), if mix(z, 1, x) < 0.5 then "poppy" else "dandelion")
        end
    end
end
```

```luau
-- garden.luau
-- A tree beside the house, and a barrel by the wall.
b:box(vec3(-8, 1, -1), vec3(-8, 4, -1), "oak_log")
b:box(vec3(-10, 4, -3), vec3(-6, 5, 1), "oak_leaves")
b:box(vec3(-9, 6, -2), vec3(-7, 6, 0), "oak_leaves")
b:block(vec3(5, 1, 2), "barrel[facing=up]")
```

## 8. Into the world

The build exists; now put it in the world:

```luau
-- main.luau
world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 63, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 63, chunk.max.z), "dirt")
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z), "grass_block")
    -- A paste puts the build's lowest corner at the origin; adding
    -- `cottage.min` puts the build's own (0, 0, 0) at (0, 64, 0).
    chunk:paste(cottage, vec3(0, 64, 0) + cottage.min) -- only the part in this chunk
end)
```

[`chunk:paste`](#ref-Chunk-paste) puts the part of the cottage that falls in
each chunk as the chunk is made. A paste puts the build's lowest corner at
the origin; adding `cottage.min` puts the build's own `(0, 0, 0)` at
`(0, 64, 0)` instead.

```luau
-- main.luau
world.time("sunset")

players.on_join(function(player)
    player.ui.title{ title = "Home", subtitle = "a cottage built in code", color = "gold" }
end)
```

`world.time("sunset")` holds the sky at sunset: low light makes the roof
and the walls stand out.

## Try it

Run the pack and join: the middle of the door lands at `(0, 64, 0)`, the
sky stays at sunset, and the title Home shows.

## 9. Look, then fix

Build it in stages, and look at each stage before the next. On your own
machine, `citadel render` draws the build to a picture, and `citadel check`
measures it:

```sh
citadel render ./cottage --view approach,sides --out cottage.png
citadel check ./cottage --enclosed --storeys 1
```

`check` names what to fix: a room nobody can walk to, a flat wall, a
window with no depth, bare ground round the build. The first version of
this cottage had a closed ceiling that made a sealed second floor, and no
window in its end walls; the check found both.

## The whole pack

```luau
-- main.luau
--!strict
-- A cottage by a path: built in code, pasted into the ground, lit by sunset.

-- Plan: a small cottage, known at a glance by its steep roof and chimney.
--   footing   a cobblestone plinth, one block wider than the walls
--   body      9 by 7, white walls between oak posts, three blocks tall
--   openings  windows set back, with a sill under each; the door faces south
--   roof      a gable of stairs along x, overhanging by one; a chimney
--   setting   a path to the door, a fenced garden, a tree, a barrel
-- The middle of the door is x = 0, so the cottage is symmetric in x.

local house = require("house")
local garden = require("garden")

-- One build from two parts; `b:part` names each stage inside them.
local cottage = world.build(function(b)
    house(b)
    garden(b)
end)

world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 63, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 63, chunk.max.z), "dirt")
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z), "grass_block")
    -- A paste puts the build's lowest corner at the origin; adding
    -- `cottage.min` puts the build's own (0, 0, 0) at (0, 64, 0).
    chunk:paste(cottage, vec3(0, 64, 0) + cottage.min) -- only the part in this chunk
end)

world.time("sunset")

players.on_join(function(player)
    player.ui.title{ title = "Home", subtitle = "a cottage built in code", color = "gold" }
end)
```

```luau
-- house.luau
--!strict
-- The house: plinth, walls, openings and roof, written round (0, 0, 0),
-- the middle of the door's wall line. See main.luau for the plan.

local mix = require("mix")

return function(b)
    b:part("plinth", function()
        for x = -5, 5 do
            for z = -4, 4 do
                b:block(vec3(x, 0, z), if mix(x, 0, z) < 0.3 then "mossy_cobblestone" else "cobblestone")
            end
        end
        b:box(vec3(-3, 0, -2), vec3(3, 0, 2), "spruce_planks") -- the floor inside
    end)

    b:part("walls", function()
        b:box(vec3(-4, 1, -3), vec3(4, 3, 3), "white_terracotta")
        b:box(vec3(-3, 1, -2), vec3(3, 3, 2), "air") -- hollow inside
        for _, x in { -4, 0, 4 } do -- oak posts at the corners and the middle
            for _, z in { -3, 3 } do
                b:box(vec3(x, 1, z), vec3(x, 3, z), "oak_log")
            end
        end
        -- The beam the roof sits on: a ring on the walls, so the room inside
        -- is open up to the roof.
        b:box(vec3(-4, 4, -3), vec3(4, 4, 3), "spruce_planks")
        b:box(vec3(-3, 4, -2), vec3(3, 4, 2), "air")
    end)

    b:part("openings", function()
        for _, x in { -2, 2 } do -- two windows in each long wall, a sill under each
            for _, z in { -3, 3 } do
                local out = if z < 0 then -1 else 1
                b:block(vec3(x, 2, z), "air")
                b:block(vec3(x, 2, z - out), "glass_pane") -- set back into the wall
                b:block(vec3(x, 1, z + out), `spruce_trapdoor[half=top,facing={if out > 0 then "south" else "north"}]`)
            end
        end
        for _, x in { -4, 4 } do -- one in each end wall
            local out = if x < 0 then -1 else 1
            b:block(vec3(x, 2, 0), "air")
            b:block(vec3(x - out, 2, 0), "glass_pane")
        end
        b:block(vec3(0, 1, 3), "spruce_door[facing=south,half=lower]")
        b:block(vec3(0, 2, 3), "spruce_door[facing=south,half=upper]")
        b:block(vec3(0, 3, 4), "lantern[hanging=true]") -- under the eaves
    end)

    b:part("roof", function()
        -- Four rows of stairs a side, each one block in and one block up.
        for k = 0, 3 do
            b:box(vec3(-5, 4 + k, -4 + k), vec3(5, 4 + k, -4 + k), "spruce_stairs[facing=south]")
            b:box(vec3(-5, 4 + k, 4 - k), vec3(5, 4 + k, 4 - k), "spruce_stairs[facing=north]")
            -- The gable ends, filled under the roof.
            if k < 3 then
                for _, x in { -4, 4 } do
                    b:box(vec3(x, 5 + k, -2 + k), vec3(x, 5 + k, 2 - k), "spruce_planks")
                end
            end
        end
        b:box(vec3(-5, 8, 0), vec3(5, 8, 0), "spruce_slab") -- the ridge
        b:box(vec3(3, 1, -2), vec3(3, 9, -2), "bricks") -- the chimney, through the roof
    end)
end
```

```luau
-- garden.luau
--!strict
-- The setting: a path to the door, a fenced garden with flowers, a tree
-- and a barrel. It is what makes the house sit in a place.

local mix = require("mix")

return function(b)
    b:part("garden", function()
        b:box(vec3(0, 0, 5), vec3(0, 0, 11), "dirt_path")
        for _, x in { -6, 6 } do
            b:box(vec3(x, 1, 5), vec3(x, 1, 9), "oak_fence")
        end
        b:box(vec3(-6, 1, 9), vec3(-2, 1, 9), "oak_fence") -- a gap for the path
        b:box(vec3(2, 1, 9), vec3(6, 1, 9), "oak_fence")

        for x = -5, 5 do
            for z = 5, 8 do
                if x ~= 0 and mix(x, 1, z) < 0.35 then
                    b:block(vec3(x, 1, z), if mix(z, 1, x) < 0.5 then "poppy" else "dandelion")
                end
            end
        end

        -- A tree beside the house, and a barrel by the wall.
        b:box(vec3(-8, 1, -1), vec3(-8, 4, -1), "oak_log")
        b:box(vec3(-10, 4, -3), vec3(-6, 5, 1), "oak_leaves")
        b:box(vec3(-9, 6, -2), vec3(-7, 6, 0), "oak_leaves")
        b:block(vec3(5, 1, 2), "barrel[facing=up]")
    end)
end
```

  walk to each.

<!-- /guides/guide-coin-rush/ -->

<a id="guides-guide-coin-rush"></a>

## Coin rush

> **In short:**
> this tutorial builds a whole game in one pack: a round arena,
> five gold pressure plates that vanish when a player walks onto them, a
> boss bar counting down the round, a sidebar of live scores, and a winner
> with fireworks at the end. It exercises zones, `player.data`, `storage`,
> tasks and the UI bars together.


## What you build
- A round grass arena with a fence on its rim.
- Five gold pressure plates, the coins, at random places on the floor.
  Walk onto one to take it; a new one appears somewhere else.
- A boss bar that counts down the round, and a sidebar with every
  player's score.
- At the end: the winner's name on screen, fireworks, and a message to
  each player who beat their best.

## Before you start

Read [Quick start](#getting-started-quick-start) first: this guide uses what it
explains.

## 1. The pack

Three Luau files this time. `main.luau` runs the game, and it loads two
modules: `arena.luau` for the ground, `coins.luau` for the coins.

```yaml
# citadel.yml
name: coins
entry: main.luau
motd: Coin rush
spawn_point: [0.5, 65.0, 0.5]
gamemode: 2
mode: lite
world: script
```

## 2. The arena

A module is a file that returns a table. `require("arena")` runs
`arena.luau` once and hands back what it returned, so every file that
requires it shares one arena (see [Runtime](#concepts-runtime)).

```luau
-- arena.luau
world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    for x = chunk.min.x, chunk.max.x do
        for z = chunk.min.z, chunk.max.z do
            local d = math.sqrt(x * x + z * z)
            if d <= arena.RADIUS then
                chunk:set(vec3(x, 64, z), "grass_block")
            elseif d <= arena.RADIUS + 1.5 then
                chunk:set(vec3(x, 64, z), "stone_bricks")
                chunk:set(vec3(x, 65, z), "oak_fence")
            end
        end
    end
end)
```

`math.sqrt(x * x + z * z)` is the distance from the middle. Inside the
radius is grass; a ring just outside it gets a stone floor and a fence.
Fences join their neighbours on their own: write `"oak_fence"`, and the
ring closes.

The coins need random places on the floor, away from the fence:

```luau
-- arena.luau
-- A random block on the floor, two blocks in from the fence.
function arena.spot(): vector
    local r = arena.RADIUS - 2
    while true do
        local x, z = math.random(-r, r), math.random(-r, r)
        if x * x + z * z <= r * r then
            return vec3(x, 65, z)
        end
    end
end
```

It picks a random square around the middle, and tries again until the
spot is inside the circle.

## Try it

Run the pack and walk out from the middle: grass inside the radius, then
a stone ring with a fence on it — and the ring closes on its own, because
fences join their neighbours.

## 3. The coins

A coin is two things: a gold pressure plate that players see, and a
**zone** that notices a player walking onto it.

```luau
-- coins.luau
function coins.place(on_take: (player: any) -> ())
    -- Pick again when that spot already holds a coin.
    local at = arena.spot()
    while world.get_block(at) ~= "air" do
        at = arena.spot()
    end
    world.set_block(at, "light_weighted_pressure_plate")
    local coin = { at = at }
    -- A zone notices the player who walks onto the plate.
    coin.zone = world.zone{
        from = at,
        to = at,
        on_enter = function(player)
            coins.remove(coin)
            fx.particle("totem_of_undying", at + vec3(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), { count = 12, spread = 0.4, speed = 0.3 })
            sound.play("entity.experience_orb.pickup", { at = at, pitch = 1.2 })
            on_take(player)
        end,
    }
    table.insert(placed, coin)
end
```

- A spot that already has a coin is not `"air"`, so `place` picks again.
- [`world.zone`](#ref-World-zone) is a box of blocks. Here it is one
  block, and `on_enter` runs when a player's feet enter it.
- Taking a coin removes it, plays a sound and a burst of particles at
  it, and calls `on_take`: the game decides what a coin is worth, not the
  coin.

Removing a coin puts the floor back and forgets the zone:

```luau
-- coins.luau
function coins.remove(coin)
    coin.zone:destroy()
    world.set_block(coin.at, "air")
    table.remove(placed, table.find(placed, coin) :: number)
end

function coins.clear()
    while #placed > 0 do
        coins.remove(placed[1])
    end
end
```

## 4. Scores

Each player carries their own score in `player.data`, a table that lives
as long as the player is connected (see
[Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle)). The sidebar shows everyone's:

```luau
-- main.luau
-- The sidebar lists every player, most coins first.
local function show_scores()
    local list = players.list()
    table.sort(list, function(a, b)
        return a.data.coins > b.data.coins
    end)
    local lines = {}
    for _, p in list do
        table.insert(lines, `{p.name}  {p.data.coins}`)
    end
    ui.sidebar{ title = "COIN RUSH", lines = lines }
end

-- One coin taken: count it, and put a new one down.
local function take(player)
    player.data.coins += 1
    show_scores()
    coins.place(take)
end
```

`take` counts the coin and places a new one, so there are always five on
the floor. It passes itself to `coins.place`: the new coin calls `take`
again when someone walks onto it.

When a player joins, their score starts at 0, and `storage` tells them
their best:

```luau
-- main.luau
players.on_join(function(player)
    player.data.coins = 0
    local best = storage.get("best." .. player.uuid) or 0
    player:message(`Walk onto the gold plates! Your best is {best}.`, "gold")
    show_scores()
end)
```

[Storage](#systems-storage) keeps values across restarts. The key uses
`player.uuid`, not the name: a player can change their name, never their
id.

## Try it

Join with the pack running: your score starts at 0, chat tells you your
best, and the sidebar lists every player, most coins first. Rounds — which
put the coins on the floor — come next.

## 5. A round

One round sends everyone to the middle, puts five coins down, and counts
down sixty seconds on a boss bar:

```luau
-- main.luau
local bar = ui.bossbar{ title = "Coin rush", color = "yellow", progress = 1 }

local function round()
    for _, p in players.list() do
        p.data.coins = 0
        p:teleport(arena.CENTER)
    end
    show_scores()
    for _ = 1, ON_FIELD do
        coins.place(take)
    end
    ui.title{ title = "GO!", color = "gold", stay = 1 }

    for left = ROUND, 1, -1 do
        bar.title = `Coin rush · {left} s`
        bar.progress = left / ROUND
        task.wait(1)
    end
    coins.clear()
    local function coins_text(n: number): string
        return if n == 1 then "1 coin" else `{n} coins`
    end
    local winner, most = nil, -1
    for _, p in players.list() do
        local key = "best." .. p.uuid
        if p.data.coins > (storage.get(key) or 0) then
            storage.set(key, p.data.coins)
            p:message(`New best: {coins_text(p.data.coins)}!`, "gold")
        end
        if p.data.coins > most then
            winner, most = p, p.data.coins
        end
    end
    if winner then
        ui.title{ title = `{winner.name} wins`, subtitle = coins_text(most), color = "gold" }
        fx.particle("firework", arena.CENTER + vec3(0, 2, 0), { count = 60, spread = 2, speed = 0.1 })
    end
end
```

`task.wait(1)` inside the loop pauses the round, not the server: coins
are taken, sounds play and other players join while it waits. At the end
the round finds the winner and saves each best score:

```luau
-- main.luau
local function coins_text(n: number): string
    return if n == 1 then "1 coin" else `{n} coins`
end
local winner, most = nil, -1
for _, p in players.list() do
    local key = "best." .. p.uuid
    if p.data.coins > (storage.get(key) or 0) then
        storage.set(key, p.data.coins)
        p:message(`New best: {coins_text(p.data.coins)}!`, "gold")
    end
    if p.data.coins > most then
        winner, most = p, p.data.coins
    end
end
if winner then
    ui.title{ title = `{winner.name} wins`, subtitle = coins_text(most), color = "gold" }
    fx.particle("firework", arena.CENTER + vec3(0, 2, 0), { count = 60, spread = 2, speed = 0.1 })
end
```

## Try it

Let a round run out: the boss bar drains a second at a time, the coins
clear, each player who beat their best is told so, and the winner's name
goes on screen with fireworks.

## 6. Rounds forever

One round is not a game — run them forever:

```luau
-- main.luau
-- Rounds run forever: a round, a five-second break, the next round.
task.spawn(function()
    while true do
        if players.count() == 0 then
            task.wait(1)
        else
            round()
            task.wait(5)
        end
    end
end)
```

`task.spawn` runs the loop as its own script, so `main.luau` finishes
loading while the rounds go on. With nobody online it waits; otherwise
it plays a round, rests five seconds, and plays the next.

## Try it

Be the last one online, then leave: the loop waits, one second at a
time, until someone joins again — and a round starts straight away.

## The whole pack

```luau
-- main.luau
--!strict
-- Coin rush: sixty seconds to pick up as many coins as you can.

local arena = require("arena")
local coins = require("coins")

local ROUND = 60 -- seconds
local ON_FIELD = 5 -- coins on the floor at once

-- The sidebar lists every player, most coins first.
local function show_scores()
    local list = players.list()
    table.sort(list, function(a, b)
        return a.data.coins > b.data.coins
    end)
    local lines = {}
    for _, p in list do
        table.insert(lines, `{p.name}  {p.data.coins}`)
    end
    ui.sidebar{ title = "COIN RUSH", lines = lines }
end

-- One coin taken: count it, and put a new one down.
local function take(player)
    player.data.coins += 1
    show_scores()
    coins.place(take)
end

players.on_join(function(player)
    player.data.coins = 0
    local best = storage.get("best." .. player.uuid) or 0
    player:message(`Walk onto the gold plates! Your best is {best}.`, "gold")
    show_scores()
end)

local bar = ui.bossbar{ title = "Coin rush", color = "yellow", progress = 1 }

local function round()
    for _, p in players.list() do
        p.data.coins = 0
        p:teleport(arena.CENTER)
    end
    show_scores()
    for _ = 1, ON_FIELD do
        coins.place(take)
    end
    ui.title{ title = "GO!", color = "gold", stay = 1 }

    for left = ROUND, 1, -1 do
        bar.title = `Coin rush · {left} s`
        bar.progress = left / ROUND
        task.wait(1)
    end
    coins.clear()
    local function coins_text(n: number): string
        return if n == 1 then "1 coin" else `{n} coins`
    end
    local winner, most = nil, -1
    for _, p in players.list() do
        local key = "best." .. p.uuid
        if p.data.coins > (storage.get(key) or 0) then
            storage.set(key, p.data.coins)
            p:message(`New best: {coins_text(p.data.coins)}!`, "gold")
        end
        if p.data.coins > most then
            winner, most = p, p.data.coins
        end
    end
    if winner then
        ui.title{ title = `{winner.name} wins`, subtitle = coins_text(most), color = "gold" }
        fx.particle("firework", arena.CENTER + vec3(0, 2, 0), { count = 60, spread = 2, speed = 0.1 })
    end
end

-- Rounds run forever: a round, a five-second break, the next round.
task.spawn(function()
    while true do
        if players.count() == 0 then
            task.wait(1)
        else
            round()
            task.wait(5)
        end
    end
end)
```

```luau
-- coins.luau
--!strict
-- Coins: gold pressure plates on the floor. Walk onto one to take it.

local arena = require("arena")

local coins = {}
local placed: { any } = {}

function coins.place(on_take: (player: any) -> ())
    -- Pick again when that spot already holds a coin.
    local at = arena.spot()
    while world.get_block(at) ~= "air" do
        at = arena.spot()
    end
    world.set_block(at, "light_weighted_pressure_plate")
    local coin = { at = at }
    -- A zone notices the player who walks onto the plate.
    coin.zone = world.zone{
        from = at,
        to = at,
        on_enter = function(player)
            coins.remove(coin)
            fx.particle("totem_of_undying", at + vec3(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), { count = 12, spread = 0.4, speed = 0.3 })
            sound.play("entity.experience_orb.pickup", { at = at, pitch = 1.2 })
            on_take(player)
        end,
    }
    table.insert(placed, coin)
end

function coins.remove(coin)
    coin.zone:destroy()
    world.set_block(coin.at, "air")
    table.remove(placed, table.find(placed, coin) :: number)
end

function coins.clear()
    while #placed > 0 do
        coins.remove(placed[1])
    end
end

return coins
```

```luau
-- arena.luau
--!strict
-- The arena: a round grass floor with a fence on its rim.

local arena = {}
arena.RADIUS = 12
arena.CENTER = vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5)

world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    for x = chunk.min.x, chunk.max.x do
        for z = chunk.min.z, chunk.max.z do
            local d = math.sqrt(x * x + z * z)
            if d <= arena.RADIUS then
                chunk:set(vec3(x, 64, z), "grass_block")
            elseif d <= arena.RADIUS + 1.5 then
                chunk:set(vec3(x, 64, z), "stone_bricks")
                chunk:set(vec3(x, 65, z), "oak_fence")
            end
        end
    end
end)

-- A random block on the floor, two blocks in from the fence.
function arena.spot(): vector
    local r = arena.RADIUS - 2
    while true do
        local x, z = math.random(-r, r), math.random(-r, r)
        if x * x + z * z <= r * r then
            return vec3(x, 65, z)
        end
    end
end

return arena
```

## Where to go next

  in `coins.place`, and pass the value to `on_take`.

  scores, with `storage.keys("best.")`.
- Give the winner a golden title in chat for the next round with
  `player.data`.

player a world of their own.

  lifetime.

<!-- /guides/guide-parkour-a-room-each/ -->

<a id="guides-guide-parkour-a-room-each"></a>

## Parkour, a room each

> **In short:**
> this tutorial gives every player a private parkour world.
> `/play` creates a room with a random twelve-jump course, a timer on the
> action bar, gold checkpoints that move the respawn point, and an emerald
> finish that saves the best time. It is the guide for rooms: one world per
> player, made at runtime.


## What you build
- A lobby: a small platform, and a title that says to type `/play`.
- `/play` makes a room with a random course of twelve jumps. Every fourth
  jump is a gold checkpoint; the last one is an emerald.
- A timer above the hotbar, from the start to the emerald.
- Fall, and you are back at the last checkpoint.
- `/leave` goes back to the lobby; finishing does too, after the time
  shows.

## Before you start

This guide builds on [Coin rush](#guides-guide-coin-rush): modules,
`player.data`, zones and `storage`.

## 1. The pack and the lobby

The manifest, then the lobby every player joins first:

```yaml
# citadel.yml
name: parkour
entry: main.luau
motd: Parkour, a room each
spawn_point: [0.5, 65.0, 0.5]
gamemode: 2
mode: lite
world: script
```

The lobby is the main room, the one every player joins first:

```luau
-- main.luau
world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(vec3(-3, 64, -3), vec3(3, 64, 3), "quartz_block") -- clipped to the chunk
end)

players.on_join(function(player)
    player.ui.title{ title = "Parkour", subtitle = "Type /play", color = "green" }
    local best = storage.get("best." .. player.uuid)
    if best then
        player:message(`Your best time is {string.format("%.1f s", best)}.`, "green")
    end
end)
```

`chunk:fill` with corners outside the chunk is clipped to it, so one line
makes a 7 by 7 platform whichever chunk asks.

## Try it

Run the pack and join: a 7 by 7 quartz platform, a title that says
"Type /play", and — if you have a time saved — your best time in chat.

## 2. A course

A course is two lists: every block to place, and the pads a player lands
on, in order.

```luau
-- course.luau
function course.make(jumps: number)
    local blocks = {} -- every block of the course: { at, block }
    local pads = {} -- where a player lands, in order: { at, kind }

    for x = -1, 1 do
        for z = -1, 1 do
            table.insert(blocks, { at = vec3(x, 64, z), block = "quartz_block" })
        end
    end

    local at = vec3(0, 64, 0)
    for i = 1, jumps do
        -- Up one block is a short jump; level or down is a longer one.
        local up = math.random(-1, 1)
        local forward = if up == 1 then 2 else 3
        at = vec3(at.x + math.random(-1, 1), math.clamp(at.y + up, 62, 70), at.z + forward)
        local kind = if i == jumps then "finish" elseif i % 4 == 0 then "checkpoint" else "jump"
        local block = if kind == "finish" then "emerald_block" elseif kind == "checkpoint" then "gold_block" else "stone_bricks"
        table.insert(blocks, { at = at, block = block })
        table.insert(pads, { at = at, kind = kind })
    end
    return { blocks = blocks, pads = pads, finish = at }
end
```

- A jump one block up is two blocks forward; a level jump or a drop is
  three. A running jump makes every one of them.
- `math.clamp` keeps the course between y = 62 and y = 70.
- The pad's kind decides its block: stone bricks, a gold checkpoint, or the
  emerald finish.

The course is random, but it is made **once**, before the room exists.
That matters for the next step.

## 3. A room of its own

`rooms.create` makes a world with its own chunks, players and effects
(see [Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions)):

```luau
-- run.luau
local c = course.make(12)
local room = rooms.create{
    spawn_point = vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5),
    -- The same blocks every time: the course was made once, above.
    generate = function(chunk)
        for _, b in c.blocks do
            chunk:set(b.at, b.block) -- a block outside this chunk is ignored
        end
    end,
}
```

A room's `generate` works like `world.on_generate`: it must make the same
blocks every time a chunk loads. It does, because it only reads the course
that was made above. `chunk:set` ignores a block outside the chunk, so the
function can hand every chunk the whole course.

## 4. The timer

The run's time, live on the action bar:

```luau
-- run.luau
local started = time.now()
local respawn = vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5)
local timer = time.every(0.1, function()
    player.ui.actionbar(seconds(time.now() - started), "yellow")
end)
```

`time.now()` is seconds since the pack started; the difference is the
run's time. Ten times a second the action bar shows it. `time.every` gives
back a connection: `timer:cancel()` stops it later.

## 5. Checkpoints and falls

Checkpoints move the respawn; the air under the course sends a faller
back:

```luau
-- run.luau
-- A zone checks a player's feet, one point. One block wider than the
-- pad each way, so a landing on its edge counts too.
local function above(at: vector): (vector, vector)
    return at + vec3(-1, 1, -1), at + vec3(1, 2, 1)
end

for _, pad in c.pads do
    if pad.kind == "checkpoint" then
        local from, to = above(pad.at)
        room.world.zone{ from = from, to = to, on_enter = function(p)
            if respawn ~= pad.at + vec3(0.5, 1, 0.5) then
                respawn = pad.at + vec3(0.5, 1, 0.5)
                p:message("Checkpoint!", "gold")
                room.sound.play("block.note_block.bell", { at = pad.at })
            end
        end }
    end
end

-- Everything under the course is a zone: fall into it, and go back.
room.world.zone{ from = vec3(-40, 30, -10), to = vec3(40, 58, c.finish.z + 10), on_enter = function(p)
    p:teleport(respawn)
end }
```

- Each checkpoint is a zone just above its gold block. Walking in moves
  `respawn` there, once.
- A zone checks a player's feet, which is one point. `above` makes each
  zone one block wider than its pad, so a player who lands on the edge
  still counts.
- One big zone fills the air under the whole course. Falling into it
  teleports the player back to `respawn`: no fall damage, no death
  screen.

## Try it

With the run wired up (step 7 adds `/play`), fall off the course: you are
teleported back to the last checkpoint you crossed — or the start, if you
crossed none — with no fall damage and no death screen.

## 6. The finish

The emerald ends the run:

```luau
-- run.luau
local done = false
local from, to = above(c.finish)
room.world.zone{ from = from, to = to, on_enter = function(p)
    if done then return end
    done = true
    timer:cancel()
    local t = time.now() - started
    local key = "best." .. p.uuid
    local best = storage.get(key)
    if best == nil or t < best then
        storage.set(key, t)
        p:message(`New best time: {seconds(t)}!`, "green")
    end
    p.ui.title{ title = seconds(t), subtitle = "Finished!", color = "green" }
    room.fx.particle("firework", c.finish + vec3(0.5, 2, 0.5), { count = 50, spread = 1.5, speed = 0.1 })
    task.wait(3)
    p:move_to(rooms.main)
end }
```

`done` makes the finish count once. The time is compared with the
player's best in `storage`: a lower time is better, and `nil` means no
time yet. After three seconds of fireworks, the player goes back to the
lobby: `rooms.main` is the room everyone starts in.

## Try it

Reach the emerald: the timer stops, a lower time than your best is saved
as the new best, the title shows the time, and after three seconds of
fireworks you are back in the lobby.

## 7. Leaving, and cleaning up

Every way out of the room goes through the lobby, and the last player out
cleans up:

```luau
-- run.luau
room.commands.add("leave", function(p)
    p:move_to(rooms.main)
end, { help = "Back to the lobby" })

room.players.on_join(function(p)
    p.ui.title{ title = "GO!", subtitle = "Reach the emerald", color = "green", stay = 1 }
end)
room.players.on_leave(function()
    timer:cancel()
    if room.players.count() == 0 then
        room:destroy()
    end
end)
player:move_to(room)
```

- `room.commands` adds a command that works only in this room: `/leave`.
- A room's own `on_join` runs when a player moves in. Add it **before**
  `move_to`, or it misses the player it was written for.
- When the last player leaves, the timer stops and `room:destroy()` frees
  the world.

And the command that starts it all:

```luau
-- main.luau
commands.add("play", function(player)
    run.start(player)
end, { help = "Run a new course" })
```

## Try it

Type `/play`: a new room, a new course, the GO! title. Type `/leave`
mid-run: back to the lobby. Leave as the last player and the room is
destroyed — a fresh `/play` makes a fresh course.

## The whole pack

```luau
-- run.luau
--!strict
-- One run: a room of its own with a new course, a timer, checkpoints, a
-- floor of air that sends a faller back, and a finish.

local course = require("course")

local run = {}

local function seconds(t: number): string
    return string.format("%.1f s", t)
end

function run.start(player)
    local c = course.make(12)
    local room = rooms.create{
        spawn_point = vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5),
        -- The same blocks every time: the course was made once, above.
        generate = function(chunk)
            for _, b in c.blocks do
                chunk:set(b.at, b.block) -- a block outside this chunk is ignored
            end
        end,
    }

    local started = time.now()
    local respawn = vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5)
    local timer = time.every(0.1, function()
        player.ui.actionbar(seconds(time.now() - started), "yellow")
    end)

    -- A zone checks a player's feet, one point. One block wider than the
    -- pad each way, so a landing on its edge counts too.
    local function above(at: vector): (vector, vector)
        return at + vec3(-1, 1, -1), at + vec3(1, 2, 1)
    end

    for _, pad in c.pads do
        if pad.kind == "checkpoint" then
            local from, to = above(pad.at)
            room.world.zone{ from = from, to = to, on_enter = function(p)
                if respawn ~= pad.at + vec3(0.5, 1, 0.5) then
                    respawn = pad.at + vec3(0.5, 1, 0.5)
                    p:message("Checkpoint!", "gold")
                    room.sound.play("block.note_block.bell", { at = pad.at })
                end
            end }
        end
    end

    -- Everything under the course is a zone: fall into it, and go back.
    room.world.zone{ from = vec3(-40, 30, -10), to = vec3(40, 58, c.finish.z + 10), on_enter = function(p)
        p:teleport(respawn)
    end }

    local done = false
    local from, to = above(c.finish)
    room.world.zone{ from = from, to = to, on_enter = function(p)
        if done then return end
        done = true
        timer:cancel()
        local t = time.now() - started
        local key = "best." .. p.uuid
        local best = storage.get(key)
        if best == nil or t < best then
            storage.set(key, t)
            p:message(`New best time: {seconds(t)}!`, "green")
        end
        p.ui.title{ title = seconds(t), subtitle = "Finished!", color = "green" }
        room.fx.particle("firework", c.finish + vec3(0.5, 2, 0.5), { count = 50, spread = 1.5, speed = 0.1 })
        task.wait(3)
        p:move_to(rooms.main)
    end }

    room.commands.add("leave", function(p)
        p:move_to(rooms.main)
    end, { help = "Back to the lobby" })

    room.players.on_join(function(p)
        p.ui.title{ title = "GO!", subtitle = "Reach the emerald", color = "green", stay = 1 }
    end)
    room.players.on_leave(function()
        timer:cancel()
        if room.players.count() == 0 then
            room:destroy()
        end
    end)
    player:move_to(room)
end

return run
```

```luau
-- course.luau
--!strict
-- A course: a start pad, then a line of jumps, every fourth one a
-- checkpoint, the last one the finish. Made once per run.

local course = {}

function course.make(jumps: number)
    local blocks = {} -- every block of the course: { at, block }
    local pads = {} -- where a player lands, in order: { at, kind }

    for x = -1, 1 do
        for z = -1, 1 do
            table.insert(blocks, { at = vec3(x, 64, z), block = "quartz_block" })
        end
    end

    local at = vec3(0, 64, 0)
    for i = 1, jumps do
        -- Up one block is a short jump; level or down is a longer one.
        local up = math.random(-1, 1)
        local forward = if up == 1 then 2 else 3
        at = vec3(at.x + math.random(-1, 1), math.clamp(at.y + up, 62, 70), at.z + forward)
        local kind = if i == jumps then "finish" elseif i % 4 == 0 then "checkpoint" else "jump"
        local block = if kind == "finish" then "emerald_block" elseif kind == "checkpoint" then "gold_block" else "stone_bricks"
        table.insert(blocks, { at = at, block = block })
        table.insert(pads, { at = at, kind = kind })
    end
    return { blocks = blocks, pads = pads, finish = at }
end

return course
```

```luau
-- main.luau
--!strict
-- Parkour, a room each: the lobby, and the command that starts a run.

local run = require("run")

world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(vec3(-3, 64, -3), vec3(3, 64, 3), "quartz_block") -- clipped to the chunk
end)

players.on_join(function(player)
    player.ui.title{ title = "Parkour", subtitle = "Type /play", color = "green" }
    local best = storage.get("best." .. player.uuid)
    if best then
        player:message(`Your best time is {string.format("%.1f s", best)}.`, "green")
    end
end)

commands.add("play", function(player)
    run.start(player)
end, { help = "Run a new course" })
```

## Where to go next

- Show the lobby a leaderboard of best times in the sidebar, with
  `storage.keys("best.")`.
- Let two friends race: `/race <name>` moves both players into one room,
  and the first to the emerald wins.
- Make the course harder as it goes: longer jumps after each checkpoint.

Next, [Build a cottage](#guides-guide-build-a-cottage) shows how to build
something that looks handmade.

Then go deeper:

- [Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions) — rooms, per-room
  tables, spawn points.

  loop pattern on its own.

<!-- /guides/guide-a-dungeon-dimension/ -->

<a id="guides-guide-a-dungeon-dimension"></a>

## A dungeon dimension

> **In short:**
> this tutorial adds a second world to a pack: `dungeon`,
> declared in `citadel.yml` and generated in code, with bedrock at both
> ends and two crossing corridors a client draws with the Nether's dark
> sky. Stepping on a square of carpet routes a player in; `/leave` brings
> them back. It is the guide for dimensions and routes.


## What you build
- A castle yard of stone bricks with a square of blue carpet in it.
- `dungeon`, a second world: bedrock at both ends, mossy walls, two
  crossing corridors. A client draws it with the Nether's dark sky.
- Step on the carpet and you arrive in the dungeon. `/leave` brings you
  back.

## Before you start

This guide builds on [Quick start](#getting-started-quick-start): `world.on_generate`
and `commands.add`. The concept page behind this tutorial is
[Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions).

## 1. Declare the dimension

A pack adds a world in `citadel.yml`, under `dimensions:`. The name is its
id inside the pack, so this one is `castle:dungeon`:

```yaml
# citadel.yml
name: castle
entry: main.luau
motd: A castle with a dungeon under it
spawn_point: [0.5, 65.0, 0.5]
gamemode: 2
mode: lite
world: script
dimensions:
  dungeon:
    type: { has_skylight: false, has_ceiling: true, weather: false }
    world: script
```

- `type` says how the world behaves. Every field is optional and starts
  from the main world's: `has_skylight`, `has_ceiling`, `weather`,
  `ultrawarm`, `bed_works`, `respawn_anchor_works`, `coordinate_scale`,
  `fixed_time` and `effects`.
- A world with a roof looks like the Nether to a client, one with no sky
  and no roof like the End. `effects` chooses one of the three yourself.
- `world: script` means the pack makes its chunks. `void` leaves them
  empty.

The dungeon is a world of the server's group: it ticks after the main world
and, on a server that keeps its world, saves to `world_dungeon` beside it.

> **Note:**
> the manifest is read once at boot — add the dimension before
> the server starts, and restart after any edit to `citadel.yml`
> (see [Quick start](#getting-started-quick-start)).


## 2. The yard

The main world, as in the first guide:

```luau
-- main.luau
-- The castle yard: a stone floor, and a square of blue carpet in the middle.
world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z), "stone_bricks")
    chunk:fill(vec3(4, 65, 4), vec3(5, 65, 5), "light_blue_carpet")
end)
```

## 3. The dungeon's terrain

`world.dimension(name)` is that world's own `world` table. Its
`on_generate` fills the dungeon's chunks:

```luau
-- main.luau
-- The dungeon: bedrock below and above, dark corridors in between.
local dungeon = world.dimension("dungeon")
dungeon.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 63, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 63, chunk.max.z), "bedrock")
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 68, chunk.max.z), "mossy_cobblestone")
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z + 6), vec3(chunk.max.x, 66, chunk.min.z + 9), "air")
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x + 6, 64, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.min.x + 9, 66, chunk.max.z), "air")
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 69, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 69, chunk.max.z), "bedrock")
end)
```

## 4. The gate

A route is how a player gets from one world to another. This one starts in
the overworld, and the trigger is standing in a block:

```luau
-- main.luau
-- Step on the carpet and you are in the dungeon.
routes.add{
    from = "overworld",
    to = "dungeon",
    trigger = { block = "light_blue_carpet" },
    placement = { x = 7.5, y = 64, z = 7.5 },
}
```

- `trigger = { block = "light_blue_carpet" }` fires on the first tick a
  player stands in carpet. `ticks = 80` would make them wait, as a Nether
  portal does.
- `placement` is where they arrive. Leave it out and they arrive at the
  dungeon's spawn.

> **Gotcha:**
> after a trip a player must step out of the trigger block for
> half a second before it can fire again.


## 5. The way back

`player:travel(dimension, pos)` sends a player to any world of the group, at
`pos` or, without it, at its spawn:

```luau
-- main.luau
-- `/leave` goes back up, to the yard's spawn.
commands.add("leave", function(player)
    player:travel("overworld")
end)
```

## Try it

Run the pack, step on the carpet, look up at the roof, and type `/leave`.

## Where to go next

- [Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions) — dimensions, routes
  and `travel` in depth, and rooms, the runtime way to another world.
- [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy) — the manifest's `dimensions` key and
  every other key.
- [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation) — `on_generate` and the
  chunk API.
- [Commands](#systems-commands) — typed arguments, help text.
- [Cookbook: teleport pads](#cookbook-cookbook-teleport-pads) — the
  trigger-block route pattern, alone.

  per player, made at runtime.

<!-- /guides/guide-scoreboard-with-a-button/ -->

<a id="guides-guide-scoreboard-with-a-button"></a>

## Scoreboard with a button

> **In short:**
> a one-file pack that counts clicks. A screen hangs in the
> air over a stone floor, every player gets a "Tap me" block in hotbar
> slot 1, and each right-click plays a sound and adds one to that player's
> count on the board. The counts live in `storage`, so they survive a
> restart.


## What you build
- A stone floor, and a 4 by 2 screen in the air, facing south.
- Every player who joins gets a lapis block, "Tap me", in hotbar slot 1.
- Right-clicking the block in hand counts a tap: a hat sound plays, and
  the count is kept in `storage` under `"taps.<name>"`.
- The board lists every player's name and taps, redrawn on every join,
  leave and click.

## Before you start

Built on [Quick start](#getting-started-quick-start): `world.on_generate`,
`players.on_join` and one `main.luau`.

## 1. The ground

Flat stone, one fill per chunk:

```luau
-- main.luau
world.on_generate(function(chunk)
    chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z), "stone")
end)
```

## 2. The board

The board itself — a screen at `(-2, 68, -10)`, four blocks wide, two
tall, facing south:

```luau
local board = world.screen{ at = vec3(-2, 68, -10), facing = "south", width = 4, height = 2 }
```

`world.screen` is the call for a picture in the air; the full set of
drawing calls and options is in [Screens](#ui-screens).

## 3. Redraw the scores

One function draws the whole board, so every change goes through it:

```luau
local function redraw()
    board:clear(colors.black)
    board:text(16, 12, "TAPS", colors.yellow, 40)
    local y = 64
    for _, p in players.list() do
        local score = storage.get("taps." .. p.name) or 0
        board:text(16, y, p.name, colors.white, 28)
        board:text(board.width - 16 - board:measure(tostring(score), 28), y, tostring(score), colors.cyan, 28)
        y += 34
    end
end
```

The board clears to black, writes the `TAPS` header in yellow at size 40,
then a row per connected player: the name in white from x = 16, the count
in cyan right-aligned — its x is `board.width - 16 - board:measure(..)`,
the board's width less a 16-pixel margin less the text's measured width.
`storage.get("taps." .. p.name) or 0` reads a player with no taps yet as
0.

## 4. Players in and out

Joining hands out the button; leaving redraws the list:

```luau
players.on_join(function(player)
    player:hotbar{ [1] = { item = "lapis_block", name = "Tap me" } }
    player:message("Right click the block in your hand.", colors.cyan)
    redraw()
end)

players.on_leave(function()
    redraw()
end)
```

`player:hotbar` puts a lapis block named "Tap me" in slot 1 (see
[Menus](#ui-menus) for the hotbar and its click events), and both events
call `redraw` so the board stays current.

## 5. The click

The click is the game — count it, sound it, redraw:

```luau
players.on_click(function(player, hit)
    if hit.slot ~= 1 or hit.button ~= "right" then
        return
    end
    local key = "taps." .. player.name
    storage.set(key, (storage.get(key) or 0) + 1)
    sound.play("block.note_block.hat", { at = player.at, pitch = 1.5 })
    redraw()
end)
```

Only a right-click while holding slot 1 counts: any other slot or button
returns early. The count is `storage.get(key) or 0`, plus one, written
back under the same key; a hat note plays at the player, pitched at 1.5;
and the board redraws.

## Try it

Run the pack and join: a lapis block named "Tap me" in slot 1, and a cyan
message telling you to right-click it. Right-click — a hat sound plays
where you stand and your count on the board goes up by one. Join with a
second player and the board lists both; leave, and the list redraws
without you.

## Where to go next

- [Screens](#ui-screens) — `world.screen`, every drawing call,
  per-player views.
- [Menus](#ui-menus) — hotbar menus, `on_click`, `on_slot`.
- [Storage](#systems-storage) — keys, values, what storage can hold.
- [Sound](#ui-sound) — playback options and positions.

## See also

- [Coin rush](#guides-guide-coin-rush) — the same scores on a sidebar, in a
  full game.
- [Cookbook: leaderboards](#cookbook-cookbook-leaderboards) — the list-and-
  storage pattern on its own.

<!-- /cookbook/cookbook-cooldowns/ -->

<a id="cookbook-cookbook-cooldowns"></a>

## Cooldowns

> **In short:**
> a cooldown is a per-player timestamp plus a check. Store the
> last use in `player.data` and compare against `time.now()` — seconds since
> the pack started. `player.data` lives as long as the player is connected,
> which is exactly the lifetime a cooldown wants.


## The pattern

```luau
--!strict
local COOLDOWN = 5  -- seconds

commands.add("kit", function(player)
    local last = player.data.kit_at
    if last and time.now() - last < COOLDOWN then
        local wait_for = math.ceil(COOLDOWN - (time.now() - last))
        player:message(`Wait {wait_for}s for your kit.`, "red")
        return
    end
    player.data.kit_at = time.now()
    player:give({ item = "iron_sword", count = 1 })
    player:message("Kit delivered.", "green")
end)
```

Why each piece is what it is:

- **`player.data`** is a table that lives as long as the player is connected.
  It resets when they reconnect, which is the right scope for gameplay
  cooldowns — no cleanup needed on leave, no persistence needed.
- **`time.now()`** returns seconds since the pack started, as a number —
  arithmetic on it is plain subtraction.
- **A returned string** from a command shows to the player in red; here we
  send the message ourselves instead because it is informational, not an
  error.

> **Gotcha:**
> a script reload restarts the clock — `time.now()` counts from
> the pack's start — but `player.data` is also reset per session, so the two
> stay consistent. For cooldowns that must survive restarts, store the
> timestamp in [storage](#systems-storage) with `storage.set("cooldown." ..
> player.uuid, time.now())` instead.


## Cooldown on an action, not a command

The same guard works inside any event. This one rate-limits a button drawn on
a screen, using the click event's player:

```luau
players.on_click(function(player, hit)
    if hit.button ~= "right" then return end
    local last = player.data.press_at
    if last and time.now() - last < 0.2 then return end   -- 200 ms like the client's own
    player.data.press_at = time.now()
    sound.play("block.note_block.hat", { at = player.at, pitch = 1.5 })
end)
```

The client itself fires one click per 200 ms — a script-side guard tighter
than that only breaks legitimate use.

## A repeating timer with a shared budget

For "every player may use this once per round", keep the round's start time
once instead of per-player timestamps:

```luau
local round_start = time.now()

commands.add("daily", function(player)
    if player.data.daily_round == round_start then
        player:message("Already claimed this round.", "red")
        return
    end
    player.data.daily_round = round_start
    player:give("diamond")
end)
```

Marking the round by identity (a copied timestamp) rather than comparing
times means no drift, no off-by-one, and no arithmetic.

## See also

- [Commands](#systems-commands) — the command options (`permission`,
  `suggest`) that pair with cooldowns.
- [Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle) — what `player.data` survives.
- [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) — `time.now`, `time.every` and tick timing.

<!-- /cookbook/cookbook-leaderboards/ -->

<a id="cookbook-cookbook-leaderboards"></a>

## Leaderboards

> **In short:**
> a leaderboard needs a score, a sort, and a place to draw.
> Scores live in `player.data` for the session, `storage` for the pack, or
> `stores` for the whole experience; the drawing side is `ui.sidebar` for a
> running game or a `world.screen` board in the world. This page shows the
> three patterns from the working guides.


## Pattern 1: the live sidebar

The sidebar lists every player, most coins first — this is the Coin rush
pattern verbatim:

```luau
local function show_scores()
    local list = players.list()
    table.sort(list, function(a, b)
        return a.data.coins > b.data.coins
    end)
    local lines = {}
    for _, p in list do
        table.insert(lines, `{p.name}  {p.data.coins}`)
    end
    ui.sidebar{ title = "COIN RUSH", lines = lines }
end
```

- Scores are `player.data.coins` — session state, right for a round.
- `players.list()` returns everyone in the main room; `table.sort` with a
  comparator does the ranking.
- Call `show_scores()` after every score change; the sidebar is a replace,
  not an append.

## Pattern 2: the screen board that persists

A `world.screen` board in the world, backed by `storage` so scores survive a
restart — the "Scoreboard with a button" pattern:

```luau
local board = world.screen{ at = vec3(-2, 68, -10), facing = "south", width = 4, height = 2 }

local function redraw()
    board:clear(colors.black)
    board:text(16, 12, "TAPS", colors.yellow, 40)
    local y = 64
    for _, p in players.list() do
        local score = storage.get("taps." .. p.name) or 0
        board:text(16, y, p.name, colors.white, 28)
        board:text(board.width - 16 - board:measure(tostring(score), 28), y,
                   tostring(score), colors.cyan, 28)
        y += 34
    end
end

players.on_leave(function() redraw() end)
```

- `storage.get(key) or 0` — absent is `nil`, never zero.
- `board:measure(text, size)` right-aligns the score column.
- Redraw on the events that change the board (score, join, leave), not on a
  tick; a screen keeps its pixels until you redraw.
- The full working example, including the click that increments, is
  [Scoreboard with a button](#guides-guide-scoreboard-with-a-button).

## Pattern 3: the experience-wide best

For a best score that spans every server of an experience, use
`stores:increment` — it is atomic, so two servers can raise the same key at
once:

```luau
local scores = stores.open()

local function finish(player: Player, coins: number)
    local best = scores:increment(`best.{player.uuid}`, 0)   -- read-start at 0
    if coins > best then
        scores:set(`best.{player.uuid}`, coins)
        player:message(`New best: {coins}!`, "gold")
    end
end
```

- Every store call yields while the I/O runs — call from a callback or
  `task.spawn`, never from a synchronous ask handler or module top level.
- Keys are strings; facts are at most 1 MiB. A number is a long way from that.
- The conflict rules (`if_version`, fencing tokens) are in
  [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores).

## Sorting helper

Every pattern above sorts the same way; one helper serves all of them:

```luau
local function ranked(get: (p: Player) -> number): { Player }
    local list = players.list()
    table.sort(list, function(a, b) return get(a) > get(b) end)
    return list
end
```

## See also

- [Guide: Coin rush](#guides-guide-coin-rush) — the full game these patterns
  come from.
- [UI basics](#ui-ui-basics) — `ui.sidebar` and text runs.
- [Screens and layouts](#ui-screens) — the screen drawing API.
- [Storage](#systems-storage) and [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores).

<!-- /cookbook/cookbook-teleport-pads/ -->

<a id="cookbook-cookbook-teleport-pads"></a>

## Teleport pads

> **In short:**
> inside one room, a pad is a `world.zone` with `on_enter`.
> Between dimensions, a `routes.add` trigger moves the player when they stand
> in a block. And `/spawn`-style commands move players explicitly. All three
> patterns come straight from the docs' own examples.


## Pattern 1: a zone pad in a room

```luau
local goal = world.zone{
    from = vec3(10, 64, 10), to = vec3(14, 66, 14),
    on_enter = function(player)
        message(player.name .. " scored", colors.lime)
    end,
    on_leave = function(player) end,
}
```

The rules that make a zone a good pad:

- `from` and `to` are block positions, in either order, both corners inside.
- A player is inside when their **feet** are.
- Disconnecting inside a zone runs `on_leave`.
- A zone ends with the script — re-create it on reload.
- `goal:contains(player)` and `goal:players()` answer "is someone in it now".

To teleport on entry rather than just score:

```luau
world.zone{
    from = vec3(-2, 64, -2), to = vec3(2, 66, 2),
    on_enter = function(player)
        player:teleport(world.spawn_point)
    end,
}
```

`player:teleport(pos)` keeps the way the player faces when you leave the
rotation out.

## Pattern 2: a route between dimensions

The dungeon guide's gate — step on the carpet, arrive in the dungeon:

```luau
routes.add{
    from = "overworld",
    to = "dungeon",
    trigger = { block = "light_blue_carpet" },
    placement = { x = 7.5, y = 64, z = 7.5 },
}
```

- `trigger = { block = "light_blue_carpet" }` fires on the first tick a
  player stands in the block; `ticks = 80` makes them wait, as a Nether
  portal does.
- `placement` is where they arrive; leave it out for the dimension's spawn.
- After a trip a player must step out of the trigger block for half a second
  before it can fire again.

The way back is a command with `player:travel`:

```luau
commands.add("leave", function(player)
    player:travel("overworld")
end)
```

The full walkthrough is [A dungeon dimension](#guides-guide-a-dungeon-dimension).

## Pattern 3: proximity pads

For "everyone within N blocks", skip the zone and use `players.near` on a
tick or timer:

```luau
local conn = time.every(0.5, function()
    for _, p in players.near(vec3(0, 65, 0), 4) do
        p:teleport(vec3(0.5, 80, 0.5))
    end
end)
```

- `players.near(pos, 8)` — every player within eight blocks of a point.
- `players.within(from, to)` — every player inside a box of blocks, corners
  included.
- Cancel with `conn:cancel()` when the pad closes.

## Choosing the pattern

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Move within the room, by area | `world.zone` with `on_enter` |
| Move between the group's worlds, by standing | `routes.add` with a trigger |
| Move between the group's worlds, on demand | `player:travel(dim, pos)` |
| Move within the room, by command | `player:teleport(pos)` |
| Effect on everyone near a point | `players.near` on a timer |

## See also

- [Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions) — zones' neighbours:
  spawn points, rooms, travel.
- [Zones and raycasts](#world-world-state) — the full zone API in context.
- [Movement](#players-movement) — teleport, rotation, `move_to`.

<!-- /cookbook/cookbook-kits/ -->

<a id="cookbook-cookbook-kits"></a>

## Kits

> **In short:**
> a kit is a loop of `player:give` calls. Understanding the
> three merge rules — hotbar first, stacks merge, overflow drops — makes the
> rest of the pattern obvious. This page covers plain kits, kits that cost
> something, and the hotbar-button form.


## A plain kit

```luau
local KIT = {
    { item = "iron_sword" },
    { item = "cooked_beef", count = 8 },
    { item = "oak_planks", count = 32 },
}

commands.add("kit", function(player)
    for _, stack in KIT do
        player:give(stack)
    end
    player:message("Kit delivered.", "green")
end, { help = "Claim your starter kit" })
```

What `player:give` does with each stack:

- A given stack **merges into existing stacks, hotbar first**.
- What does not fit is **dropped from the give, not duplicated** — count what
  you need before sending a full inventory.
- One item is a bare string (`"stone"`), several are `{ item = "arrow",
  count = 16 }`. A pack's own item carries its `id`.

## A kit that costs something

`player:take(item, count)` removes up to `count` of what matches, the hand
first, and **answers how many it took** — that return value is the whole
trick:

```luau
commands.add("kit stone", function(player)
    local took = player:take("cobblestone", 16)
    if took < 16 then
        player:give({ item = "cobblestone", count = took })   -- give the change back
        player:message("You need 16 cobblestone.", "red")
        return
    end
    player:give({ item = "stone_sword" })
    player:give({ item = "stone_pickaxe" })
end, { help = "Trade 16 cobblestone for stone tools" })
```

`player:count(item)` asks without taking — use it to grey out a menu entry or
skip a prompt entirely.

## Replacing the whole loadout

`player:set_held(item)` replaces the stack in hand (`nil` or `false` empties
it), and `player:inventory()` lists one `{ item, count }` row per filled
slot. To clear everything and hand out a fresh kit:

```luau
commands.add("reset", function(player)
    for _, slot in player:inventory() do
        player:take(slot.item, slot.count)
    end
    for _, stack in KIT do
        player:give(stack)
    end
end)
```

## The one-click kit: a hotbar button

The smallest useful kit is a named item in the hotbar that acts when used —
this is the "Scoreboard with a button" form:

```luau
players.on_join(function(player)
    player:hotbar{ [1] = { item = "lapis_block", name = "Kit" } }
end)

players.on_click(function(player, hit)
    if hit.slot ~= 1 or hit.button ~= "right" then return end
    for _, stack in KIT do
        player:give(stack)
    end
end)
```

- `hit.slot` is the hotbar slot number; `hit.button` is `"left"` or
  `"right"`.
- The click event fires for the item in hand wherever the player aims it, so
  the button works anywhere in the world.
- Pair it with the [cooldown](#cookbook-cookbook-cooldowns) pattern so it cannot
  be spammed.

## Kits in menus

`player.ui.menu{}` is the many-item version of the hotbar button —
`on_pick` receives the index chosen:

```luau
commands.add("kits", function(player)
    player.ui.menu{
        title = "Choose a kit",
        items = {
            { item = "iron_sword", name = "Warrior", lore = { "sword + beef" } },
            { item = "bow", name = "Archer", lore = { "bow + arrows" } },
        },
        on_pick = function(p, n)
            if n == 1 then p:give("iron_sword"); p:give({ item = "cooked_beef", count = 4 })
            elseif n == 2 then p:give("bow"); p:give({ item = "arrow", count = 16 })
            end
        end,
    }
end)
```

## See also

- [Inventory and items](#players-inventory) — every inventory call and the
  ItemSpec forms.
- [Menus](#ui-menus) — the full menu options.
- [Cooldowns](#cookbook-cookbook-cooldowns) — rate-limiting kit claims.

<!-- /cookbook/cookbook-teams/ -->

<a id="cookbook-cookbook-teams"></a>

## Teams

> **In short:**
> a team is a field on the player — `player.data.team` — plus
> two rules: apply visibility when the team is set, and re-apply it when
> anyone joins. The visibility calls are `viewer:hide(player)` and
> `viewer:show(player)`.


## Assigning teams

```luau
local TEAMS = { "red", "blue" }

commands.add("team <name:red|blue>", function(player, args)
    player.data.team = args.name
    player:message(`You are on team {args.name}.`, args.name)
end, { help = "Pick a team" })
```

`player.data` is a table that lives as long as the player is connected, and
players compare by identity (`a == b`), so it is the natural home for team
membership during a match. The enum argument type (`red|blue`) makes the
command validate itself — the parser only accepts the listed words.

## Applying team visibility

The docs' own teams pattern — each side sees only its own:

```luau
local function apply_teams()
    for _, a in players.list() do
        for _, b in players.list() do
            if a.data.team ~= b.data.team then a:hide(b) else a:show(b) end
        end
    end
end
```

The rules that shape it:

- `viewer:hide(player)` removes the player **from this viewer only**;
  `viewer:show(player)` undoes it. `viewer:can_see(player)` reads what the
  two settings add up to.
- A hidden player is gone from that client: no body, name, armour or hitbox.
  The `invisibility` effect differs — it shows armour and the held item.
- The tab list still shows hidden players.
- `hide` is **by account**, so it lasts when the other player rejoins.
- A new session resets both: nothing hidden, and `visible` is true.

## Keeping teams alive

Re-apply when someone joins — and remember the global `players.on_join` fires
in the main room, a room's own fires on each move in:

```luau
players.on_join(function(player)
    if not player.data.team then
        player.data.team = TEAMS[math.random(#TEAMS)]     -- or a balancing pick
    end
    apply_teams()
end)
```

> **Gotcha:**
> `player.data` resets when the player reconnects, and a script
> reload runs `players.on_join` again for every online player. Make
> `apply_teams` safe to run twice — it is, because `hide`/`show` are
> idempotent writes. For teams that outlive the session, store the team in
> [storage](#systems-storage) keyed by `player.uuid` and restore it in
> `on_join`.


## Team scoring

Scoreboards and bars follow the same shape — the Coin rush sidebar, split by
team:

```luau
local function show_scores()
    local sum = {}
    for _, p in players.list() do
        local t = p.data.team or "?"
        sum[t] = (sum[t] or 0) + p.data.coins
    end
    local lines = {}
    for _, t in TEAMS do
        table.insert(lines, `{t}:  {sum[t] or 0}`)
    end
    ui.sidebar{ title = "TEAM SCORES", lines = lines }
end
```

## Friendly fire

The cancellable damage ask is where teams meet combat — return `false` to
veto a hit between team-mates:

```luau
players.on_damage(function(player, hit)
    if hit.by and hit.by.data.team == player.data.team then return false end
end)
```

`hit.by` is the player who hit, or who shot the arrow; `nil` for anything
else. Answer at once — the engine waits two milliseconds (see
[The event model](#concepts-events)).

## See also

- [Visibility](#players-visibility) — the full hide/show/visible rules.
- [The event model](#concepts-events) — the damage ask and its deadline.
- [Leaderboards](#cookbook-cookbook-leaderboards) — the sidebar patterns.
- [Permissions](#players-permissions) — when teams should be groups instead.
