<!-- /cookbook/cookbook-minigame-loop/ -->

<a id="cookbook-cookbook-minigame-loop"></a>

## A minigame loop

> **In short:**
> a round-based game is a room, a timer, a scoreboard and a
> cleanup. Make a room with `rooms.create`, count the round down with
> `time.every` and `ui.bossbar`, keep scores in `player.data`, and destroy
> the room when the last player leaves. This skeleton is distilled from the
> Coin rush and Parkour guides.


## The skeleton

Two functions and a command. `finish` comes first, because `start_round`'s
countdown calls it:

```luau
--!strict
local ROUND_SECONDS = 60

local function finish(room)
    local winner: Player? = nil
    for _, p in room.players.list() do
        if not winner or p.data.coins > winner.data.coins then winner = p end
    end
    if winner then
        room.ui.title{ title = winner.name .. " wins", color = "gold" }
    end
    for _, p in room.players.list() do
        p:move_to(rooms.main())     -- back to the lobby
    end
    room:destroy()
end

local function start_round(who: { Player })
    local room = rooms.create{
        spawn_point = vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5),
        generate = function(chunk)
            chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z),
                       vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z), "grass_block")
        end,
    }

    for _, p in who do
        p:move_to(room)          -- the client swaps worlds in place
    end

    local left = ROUND_SECONDS
    room.ui.bossbar{ title = "Round", progress = 1 }
    local timer = time.every(1, function()
        left -= 1
        room.ui.bossbar{ title = "Round", progress = left / ROUND_SECONDS }
        if left <= 0 then
            timer:cancel()
            finish(room)
        end
    end)

    room.players.on_leave(function()
        if room.players.count() == 0 then room:destroy() end   -- the last one out closes it
    end)
end

commands.add("play", function(player)
    start_round({ player })
end)
```

## Why each piece is what it is

- **`rooms.create` per round.** A room made this way runs no survival rules
  and no natural spawning by default, and its `generate` function is its own
  little `on_generate` — a fresh arena per round, and the old room's world is
  discarded with it.
- **`player:move_to(room)`** swaps the client's world in place. A room's own
  `room.players.on_join` fires on each move in, so put the round's welcome
  there.
- **`time.every(1, fn)`** is precise to 1 ms and never drifting; a
  `time.every` timer can cancel itself inside its own callback, which is how
  the countdown ends. For tick-exact work there is `time.on_tick`.
- **`room.ui.*`** addresses everyone in the room — the boss bar counts the
  round down, the title announces the winner. `ui.bossbar` needs clients
  1.9+; on older clients it is simply not sent.
- **`player.data.coins`** scores the round. It resets on reconnect, which is
  the right lifetime for a round score — cross-round bests go to
  [storage](#systems-storage) or [stores](#systems-shared-stores).
- **The `on_leave` guard** destroys the room when the last player leaves, so
  an abandoned round cannot leak rooms. Players still in it keep the world
  until they go.

## The lobby, and going back

The main room is `rooms.main()` — the lobby players start in. Moving a player
back there ends their round. The global `players.on_join` fires on connect in
the main room; a room's own fires on each move in; `players.on_leave`
matches. Keep the lobby's welcome in the global, the round's welcome in the
room's own:

```luau
players.on_join(function(player)
    player.ui.title{ title = "Lobby", subtitle = "type /play", color = colors.cyan }
end)
```

## Rounds on a schedule

To run rounds back-to-back without a command, chain them with `task.delay` —
and remember tasks spawned at load start only after initialization commits
(see [Runtime](#concepts-runtime)):

```luau
task.spawn(function()
    while true do
        start_round(players.list())           -- everyone in the lobby; it ends itself
        task.wait(ROUND_SECONDS + 10)         -- play + winner screen
        task.wait(5)                          -- breather between rounds
    end
end)
```

Each `start_round` owns its own countdown timer and destroys its own room when
it ends (or when the last player leaves), so the loop only paces the rounds.
`task.wait` uses elapsed real time, not ticks — a 60-second round is 60 real
seconds, however loaded the server is. `rooms.main()` is the lobby itself;
`room:destroy()` does nothing to it.

## Spawning things to collect

Coins on the floor are a loop of ground items or a custom block with an
`on_step` hook — the Coin rush guide does it with an item pickup that counts
itself and places a new one, keeping five on the floor at all times. Read
[Guide: Coin rush](#guides-guide-coin-rush) for that half of the game, and
[Custom entities](#entities-custom-entities) for mobs that think.

## See also

- [Guide: Coin rush](#guides-guide-coin-rush) — the complete game this
  skeleton comes from.
- [Guide: Parkour, a room each](#guides-guide-parkour-a-room-each) — one room
  per player instead of per round.
- [Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions) — the room API.
- [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) — `time.every`, `task.wait`, and reload rules.

<!-- /cookbook/cookbook-save-load/ -->

<a id="cookbook-cookbook-save-load"></a>

## Save and load

> **In short:**
> Citadel has exactly three persistence layers, and each has a
> clear job: `player.data` for the session, `storage` for per-pack values
> (a local JSON file, atomic writes), and `stores` for the whole experience
> (versioned keys, leases, blobs). This page is the decision table and the
> two working patterns.


## Choosing the layer

| Need | Use | Lifetime | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Score mid-round, cooldown stamp, team | `player.data` | the player's connection | in-memory |
| Best score, settings, per-pack state | `storage.get/set` | the pack, across restarts | local JSON file, per-pack |
| Cross-server values, purchases, player blobs | `stores:*` | the experience | facts 1 MiB, blobs 32 MiB, 512 MiB hosted |

`player.data` is a plain table — no calls, no yields, gone on reconnect.
`storage` is per-pack even on a published world. `stores` is shared by a
development workload and all instances of its experience, and a pack cannot
choose another store.

## The per-pack layer: `storage`

```luau
-- A best score that survives a restart
players.on_leave(function(player)
    local key = "best." .. player.uuid
    local best = storage.get(key) or 0
    if (player.data.coins or 0) > best then
        storage.set(key, player.data.coins)
    end
end)
```

- `storage.set` changes memory immediately; `storage.get` reads the current
  value. Strings and record keys must be valid UTF-8 — invalid bytes raise an
  error instead of being replaced.
- Writes are atomic; a killed server keeps the previous value. Unflushed
  changes can still be lost if the process crashes.
- `storage.status()` returns `{ pending: boolean, error: string? }` — a write
  failure stays visible and is retried.
- `storage.flush()` yields until the current values are saved, or raises the
  write error. Call it from a callback or `task.spawn`, after initialization.

> **Gotcha:**
> on a script reload, local storage is flushed **before** the
> replacement loads — so writing from the old script's last breath is safe,
> but writes that belong in the new script must happen in its callbacks.


## The experience layer: `stores`

```luau
local scores = stores.open()

players.on_join(function(player)
    local visits, version = scores:increment("visits." .. player.uuid, 1)
    player:message("Visit number " .. tostring(visits))
end)
```

- Every call **yields** while the I/O runs; other callbacks continue. Call
  from scripts, callbacks or tasks — never from synchronous ask handlers or
  at module initialization.
- `handle:get(key)` returns `(value, version)`; version zero means absent.
- `handle:set(key, value, if_version)` is a compare-and-set — a stale version
  reaches `pcall` as `{ err = "conflict", version = current }`.
- `handle:increment(key, by)` is atomic; a number is the common case.
- A pack can have up to **32 pending requests** — batch your writes in a task
  rather than firing hundreds from one event.

The version check, for read-modify-write that must not race:

```luau
task.spawn(function()
    local coins, version = scores:get("pot")
    local ok, err = pcall(function()
        scores:set("pot", coins + 10, version)   -- fails if another server moved it
    end)
    if not ok and err.err == "conflict" then
        -- re-read and retry
    end
end)
```

## Saving on the clock

Persistence that must not lose more than a minute of play:

```luau
local DIRTY = {}

local function mark(player: Player)
    table.insert(DIRTY, player)
end

time.every(60, function()
    if #DIRTY == 0 then return end
    task.spawn(function()
        for _, p in DIRTY do
            scores:set(`coins.{p.uuid}`, p.data.coins or 0)
        end
    end)
    table.clear(DIRTY)
end)
```

`time.every` never drifts, and moving the writes into `task.spawn` keeps the
timer's callback out of the tick budget's way.

## Binary data: blobs

Player-owned binary (a skin, a screenshot) goes in blob calls, which have
their own keyspace — a fact `"world"` and a blob `"world"` are different
values:

```luau
local bytes = http.get(url):image()          -- binary as a string
scores:blob_put(player.uuid, "banner", bytes)
local saved, version = scores:blob_get(player.uuid, "banner")
```

Each player may have at most 1,000 blobs; hosted blobs are not in world
archive backups.

## See also

- [Storage](#systems-storage) — the per-pack API in full.
- [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) — every call, lease and limit.
- [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) — the reload flush rule and task rules.
- [Leaderboards](#cookbook-cookbook-leaderboards) — scoring on top of these
  layers.

<!-- /appendix/event-catalog/ -->

<a id="appendix-event-catalog"></a>

## Event catalog

> **In short:**
> every `on_*` subscription in the API, one row each.
> Subscribe with the call, keep the connection, cancel to stop. The
> model itself — deadlines, asks, ordering — is in
> [The event model](#concepts-events).


65 events across 13 types.

## `BlockAmendSpec`

| Event | Signature | Fires when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`on_added`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_added) | `blockAmendSpec.on_added((block: BlockAt, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | It has just been stored, whatever stored it. |
| [`on_break`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_break) | `blockAmendSpec.on_break((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, by: Breaker, base: (... any) -> any) -> Drops ?) → ?` | Something broke it; `by` says what. Answers "none", "table" or a drops list. |
| [`on_neighbour`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_neighbour) | `blockAmendSpec.on_neighbour((block: BlockAt, from: Vec3, announced: string, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | A neighbour at `from` changed; `announced` is the block the notifier announced itself as. |
| [`on_place`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_place) | `blockAmendSpec.on_place((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | A player put it down. |
| [`on_power`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_power) | `blockAmendSpec.on_power((block: BlockAt, powered: boolean, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | A redstone signal started (`powered` is true) or stopped reaching it. Called once for each, not for every change beside it. |
| [`on_random_tick`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_random_tick) | `blockAmendSpec.on_random_tick((block: BlockAt, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | The random pass landed on it. |
| [`on_removed`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_removed) | `blockAmendSpec.on_removed((block: BlockAt, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | It has just gone. |
| [`on_step`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_step) | `blockAmendSpec.on_step((block: BlockAt, body: Body, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | A body (a player, mob, item or other) is standing on it. |
| [`on_tick`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_tick) | `blockAmendSpec.on_tick((block: BlockAt, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | A scheduled tick this block asked for came due. |
| [`on_trigger`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_trigger) | `blockAmendSpec.on_trigger((block: BlockAt, cause: Trigger, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | It was lit, blasted or burnt; `cause` is "ignite", "explosion" or "fire". |
| [`on_use`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_use) | `blockAmendSpec.on_use((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, held: string ?, base: (... any) -> any) -> Used ?) → ?` | Somebody right-clicked it; `held` is the item in hand. Answers "used" or "pass"; a missed deadline passes the click through. |

## `BlockSpec`

| Event | Signature | Fires when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`on_added`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_added) | `blockSpec.on_added((block: BlockAt, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | It has just been stored, whatever stored it. |
| [`on_break`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_break) | `blockSpec.on_break((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, by: Breaker, base: (... any) -> any) -> Drops ?) → ?` | Something broke it. Answers "none", "table" or a drops list; fails closed to the definition's `drops`. |
| [`on_neighbour`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_neighbour) | `blockSpec.on_neighbour((block: BlockAt, from: Vec3, announced: string, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | A neighbour changed; `from` is its position and `announced` the block name the notifier announced itself as. |
| [`on_place`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_place) | `blockSpec.on_place((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | A player put it down; `block.data` is empty then, ready to be filled. |
| [`on_power`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_power) | `blockSpec.on_power((block: BlockAt, powered: boolean, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | A redstone signal started (`powered` is true) or stopped reaching it. Called once for each, not for every change beside it. |
| [`on_random_tick`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_random_tick) | `blockSpec.on_random_tick((block: BlockAt, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | The random pass landed on it. Not the same thing as `on_tick`, which is why it has the longer name. |
| [`on_removed`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_removed) | `blockSpec.on_removed((block: BlockAt, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | It has just gone from the world. |
| [`on_step`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_step) | `blockSpec.on_step((block: BlockAt, body: Body, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | A body is standing on it; `body` is `{ id, kind }`. |
| [`on_tick`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_tick) | `blockSpec.on_tick((block: BlockAt, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | A scheduled tick this block asked for came due. |
| [`on_trigger`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_trigger) | `blockSpec.on_trigger((block: BlockAt, cause: Trigger, base: (... any) -> any) -> ()) → ?` | It was lit, blasted or burnt; `cause` is "ignite", "explosion" or "fire". |
| [`on_use`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_use) | `blockSpec.on_use((block: BlockAt, player: Player ?, held: string ?, base: (... any) -> any) -> Used ?) → ?` | The hooks. Writing one is what asks for it — there is no flag beside `on_random_tick` saying the random pass may land here. |

## `EntitySpec`

| Event | Signature | Fires when |

| [`on_tick`](#ref-EntitySpec-on_tick) | `entitySpec.on_tick((e: EntityHandle, base: () -> ()) -> ()) → ?` | Runs after the physics each tick to react to where it ended up; call `base(e)` to extend. |

## `Players`

| Event | Signature | Fires when |
| --- | --- | --- |

| [`on_chat`](#ref-Players-on_chat) | `players.on_chat(fn: (player: Player, text: string) -> boolean ?) → Connection` | Return false and the line is not said. |
| [`on_click`](#ref-Players-on_click) | `players.on_click(fn: (player: Player, hit: Hit) -> ()) → Connection` | Calls `fn` on a left or right click; `hit` holds the button and the entity, player, block and face it met. |
| [`on_damage`](#ref-Players-on_damage) | `players.on_damage(fn: (player: Player ?, hit: DamageHit) -> boolean ?) → Connection` | Asks `fn` before damage lands on a player; return false to refuse it. A missed deadline denies it. A pack's own `player:damage` is not asked about. |
| [`on_death`](#ref-Players-on_death) | `players.on_death(fn: (player: Player ?, cause: string, message: string, by: Player ?) -> ()) → Connection` | Calls `fn` when a player dies, with the cause (fall, drown, void, lava, ...) and the line broadcast; `player` is nil once they have left. |
| [`on_drop`](#ref-Players-on_drop) | `players.on_drop(fn: (player: Player ?, item: string, count: number) -> ()) → Connection` | Calls `fn` when a stack lands on the ground; `player` is nil where the world dropped it or they have left. |
| [`on_join`](#ref-Players-on_join) | `players.on_join(fn: (player: Player) -> ()) → Connection` | Calls `fn` when a player arrives: on the globals when a client connects, on a room's table each time a player moves into it. |
| [`on_leave`](#ref-Players-on_leave) | `players.on_leave(fn: (player: Player) -> ()) → Connection` | The same player value on_join had; it can no longer be sent to. |
| [`on_pickup`](#ref-Players-on_pickup) | `players.on_pickup(fn: (player: Player ?, item: string, count: number) -> ()) → Connection` | A stack taken off the ground, and one that landed on it. `player` is nil where the world dropped it, or where they have already left. |
| [`on_place`](#ref-Players-on_place) | `players.on_place(fn: (player: Player ?, pos: Vec3, block: string) -> boolean ?) → Connection` | Asks `fn` before a player puts a block down; return false to cancel it. A missed deadline denies the place. |
| [`on_respawn`](#ref-Players-on_respawn) | `players.on_respawn(fn: (player: Player ?) -> ()) → Connection` | Calls `fn` when a player respawns; `player` is nil once they have left. |
| [`on_slot`](#ref-Players-on_slot) | `players.on_slot(fn: (player: Player, slot: number) -> ()) → Connection` | Calls `fn` when a player picks a hotbar slot, 1..9. |
| [`on_sneak`](#ref-Players-on_sneak) | `players.on_sneak(fn: (player: Player, down: boolean) -> ()) → Connection` | Calls `fn` once per sneak press and release; `down` is true on the press. |

<!-- /appendix/client-versions/ -->

<a id="appendix-client-versions"></a>

## Client versions

> **In short:**
> the script never sees a client version. It asks
> `player:supports(feature)` and gets a boolean — the same pack then serves
> 1.8 and 26.x clients at once. Unguarded calls are safe: a client that
> cannot show a feature is not sent it; guard only to show something else.


## The feature matrix

| Feature | What needs it | From |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bossbar` | `ui.bossbar`, `player.ui.bossbar` | 1.9 |
| `potion_color` | an item's `color` | 1.11 |
| `floor_frame` | a screen or frame with `facing = "up"` | 1.13 |
| `light` | `world.light` | 1.14 |
| `hex_color` | a colour outside Minecraft's sixteen names | 1.16 |
| `glow_frame` | `glow = true` on a screen | 1.17 |
| `display` | `world.display`, any kind | 1.19.4 |
| `hitbox` | `world.hitbox` | 1.19.4 |
| `model` | `world.display{ kind = "model" }` | 1.21.4 |
| `layout` | `player.ui.show` | 1.21.4 |
| `dialog` | `player.ui.dialog` | 1.21.6 |
| `overlay` | `player.ui.overlay` | 26.3 only |
| `resource_pack` | the pack's textures, models and sounds | a client that did not turn the pack down |

- A name not in this table is an error.
- A Bedrock client answers `false` to every feature in the table (except where noted in the topic pages).

## The fallback pattern

```luau
if player:supports("display") then
    world.display{ kind = "text", text = "Bet 50", at = pad }
else
    board:text(8, 8, "Bet 50", colors.white, 24)   -- a screen works from 1.8
end
```

## Resource-pack refusals

A client that turns the resource pack down answers `false` to
`resource_pack`, `model`, `layout`, `dialog` and `overlay`, from the moment
it answers. It is sent no layout and no dialog: they are drawn in the pack's
fonts. An open dialog closes.

A pack that needs the textures says so with `min_client` in `citadel.yml`,
which refuses old clients outright instead of degrading feature by feature.

## Version-related behaviours elsewhere

- Particles: a client whose version lacks a particle does not get it. Before
  1.13, dust is one particle a point, in its colour, with no count, spread or
  size. 1.7 shows dust only. See [FX](#ui-fx).
- Sound: a client older than 1.13 hears nothing of streams; Simple Voice
  Chat is required. See [Sound](#ui-sound).
- Player heads: clients from 1.7 see the face; Bedrock clients see no face.
- Input: `player.input` reads keys on foot from 1.21.2; before that a client
  reports keys only while it rides. See [Movement](#players-movement).
- Cameras: from 1.20.2 the client glides between moves. See
  [Movement](#players-movement).
- Textures of your own: on Java 1.21.4 and later. See
  [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy).

## See also

- [Conventions](#concepts-conventions) — what a version lacks is absent, not zero.
- [Pack anatomy](#concepts-pack-anatomy) — `min_client` in the manifest.
- [Server settings](#systems-server-settings) — the server's own file.

---

<!-- /appendix/faq/ -->

<a id="appendix-faq"></a>

## FAQ and troubleshooting

> **In short:**
> almost every Citadel surprise is one of these: a budget was
> exceeded, a reload changed more than expected, a version lacked a feature,
> or an options field was misspelt. Work down this page with the server log
> open — Citadel's errors name the field, the file and the nearest valid
> spelling.


## The pack will not load

**The log says the load failed.** The entry script has **5 seconds** of work
between two waits and **30 seconds** in all. Build big scenery once at load
and paste it per chunk — do not loop over every block of every level at load.
If the entry script fails, its drafts are discarded and the previous script
resumes (see [Runtime](#concepts-runtime)).

**The server stops on an unknown key.** Manifest keys — in both the pack's
and the server's `citadel.yml` — are checked at boot; an unknown key or mode
stops the server with the field named. `rooms.create` options are checked the
same way at runtime.

**Packs name different modes.** Packs that name different modes in their
manifests, or that all name none, stop the server. The message says how to
set one: a `--lite`/`--full` flag, or `mode` in the server file.

## I edited the script and nothing changed

Saving any `.luau` file restarts the pack's script — but:

- **Existing chunks are kept.** Edits to `world.on_generate`, `seed` or
  `terrain` apply only to chunks generated from here on. For a fresh map,
  stop the server and delete the world folder; the log names it the first
  time a script world reloads.
- **`citadel.yml` is read at boot only.** Manifest changes need a restart.
- **`players.on_join` runs again for every online player.** Make it safe to
  run twice (see [Runtime](#concepts-runtime)).
- **A spawn/drops/attacks value the new script does not set is removed** —
  set it again in the new run (see [Game data](#world-game-data)).

## My calls error with "no option"

Options tables are strict: **an unknown field is an error** that names the
nearest valid one — `colour` suggests `color`; a field of the wrong type is
also an error. Check the signature in the [API reference](#ref) and remember
the API spells it `color` (and `colors.gray`), `at` for positions, `from`/`to`
for box corners. See [Conventions](#concepts-conventions).

## Mobs do not spawn

On a `mode: lite` world — and in every room made by `rooms.create` — **no mob
spawns by itself**. Switch a kind on with `game.entities.<kind>.spawn = true`
(make sure the world has biomes; a script world spawns nothing on 1.8.9), or
spawn directly with `world.spawn(name, pos)`:

- `spawn = false` stops natural spawning only — spawners, `/summon`,
  `world.spawn` and breeding still work.
- A zombie from `world.spawn` does not hurt players until `spawn = true`,
  `attacks = true`, or the room has the `damage` rule.
- a0.1.0 to a0.1.3 have no natural spawning at all: every write is an error.
- The full tri-state rules are in [Game data](#world-game-data) and
  [Mobs](#entities-mobs).

## Blocks do not drop / players take no damage

- Block drops by the world (a torch whose wall is gone, decay, explosions)
  are **off by default on lite worlds**; write the block's `drops = true`
  field, or switch survival on with `world.rules{ survival = true }`. A
  player's dig is a different thing — see the next item.
- A dig reaches no block without `survival`, or in the `gamemode: 2`
  (adventure) the quick start uses.
- Anything that is not a rule is the pack's job: `player:damage` for a hit,
  `player.health` to heal, `players.on_death` and `players.on_respawn` for
  what happens next (see [Health](#players-health)).
- A refused action you did not veto yourself is usually an **ask deadline**:
  a handler that errors or runs over two milliseconds counts as a missed
  deadline, and protection fails closed. Never `task.wait` in an ask; miss a
  kind too often and the engine stops asking (see
  [The event model](#concepts-events)).

## The command exists but nobody sees it

- **`permission`:** without the node, a player neither sees nor runs the
  command — and `/help` lists only what the player may run.
- **One pack owns a name** in a room: a second pack that adds the name or an
  alias is the conflict the log names.
- A required argument never follows an optional one; check the usage grammar
  in [Commands](#systems-commands).

## Store calls error or hang

- Every `stores` call **yields** — call from a callback or `task.spawn`,
  never from a synchronous ask handler or at module initialization.
- At most **32 pending requests** per pack: batch writes in a task.
- A version conflict reaches `pcall` as `{ err = "conflict", version = ... }`;
  a stale fencing token as `{ err = "held", by = ... }`. Re-read and retry —
  see [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores).
- `storage.flush()` may only run from a callback or `task.spawn`, after
  initialization.

## `nil` where a number should be

What a game version lacks is **absent, not zero**: `player.food` is `nil` on
Alpha, `game.block(name)` returns `nil` for a block the game lacks, an
unknown particle name sends nothing. Check for `nil` before arithmetic —
[Conventions](#concepts-conventions--what-a-version-lacks-is-absent).

## Performance: the budget

`citadel.budget()` tells you where the time went (`used`, `peak`, `skipped`,
`dropped`, `slowest`), `citadel.on_slow` names the hook at most once a
second, and the server log reports a slow pack at most once every five
seconds. Going over is not an error — do less per tick or raise `budget_ms`.
The full diagnosis guide is [Limits](#systems-limits).

## Where the log is

`citadel.log(...)` writes under the pack's name. Callback errors are logged
with file and line automatically. The first store call logs which store
opened and where; the first script-world reload logs the world folder's path.

## See also

- [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) — load and reload semantics in full.
- [Limits](#systems-limits) — every budget and queue.
- [The event model](#concepts-events) — ask deadlines and disabled kinds.
- [API reference](#ref) — signatures for every call.

---

<!-- /appendix/limits-table/ -->

<a id="appendix-limits-table"></a>

## Limits

> **In short:**
> every number the engine enforces, in one place. Each row
> links to the page that explains what happens at the edge.


| Limit | Value | What it bounds | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tick budget | 2 ms default (`budget_ms`) | A pack's tick and event callbacks per tick | [Limits](#systems-limits) |
| Runaway limit | 100 ms | Joins, input events, commands, task threads | [Limits](#systems-limits) |
| Chunk callback | 2 s | `on_generate` / `on_populate` per chunk | [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation) |
| Chunk wait | 60 s | The engine's wait for a chunk to be made; then it is air | [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation) |
| Entry script | 5 s between waits, 30 s total | Pack load; past it the load fails | [Runtime](#concepts-runtime) |
| Event queue | 4096 ordinary events per pack | Overflow drops the oldest and logs | [Limits](#systems-limits) |
| Ask deadline | 2 ms | `on_break` / `on_place` / `on_damage` answers; miss and the action is denied | [The event model](#concepts-events) |
| `on_slow` | at most once a second | Budget warnings to the script | [Limits](#systems-limits) |
| Slow-pack log | at most once every 5 s | Server log lines about budget | [Limits](#systems-limits) |
| Zone re-trigger | 0.5 s | A route trigger block, after a trip | [Rooms and dimensions](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions) |
| Store facts | 1 MiB each, keys 256 B | `stores` values | [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) |
| Store blobs | 32 MiB each, 1,000 per player | `stores` blobs | [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) |
| Hosted storage | 512 MiB + 1 MiB per Java player ever joined | Per experience | [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) |
| Pending store requests | 32 per pack | Concurrent yielding store calls | [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) |
| Lease tokens | 100,000 issued; leases last up to 1 hour | `stores.lease` | [Shared stores](#systems-shared-stores) |
| Build size | 4,096 16-block cubes (32 MB) in a 256-million-block box | One `world.build` | [Building](#world-building) |
| `max_health` | 1 to 1024 | `player.max_health` writes | [Health](#players-health) |
| Player name to `player:connect` | 1 to 128 chars | Server addresses | [Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle) |
| Camera moves | 20 per second | Camera positioning | [Movement](#players-movement) |
| Client versions | 1.8 to 26.x join every server | Java clients | [Client versions](#appendix-client-versions) |

## See also

- [Limits](#systems-limits) — the budget system in depth.
- [FAQ](#appendix-faq) — when a limit is why.

<!-- /ref/ -->

<a id="ref"></a>

## API reference

Every global, type and call in Citadel, one page each: the signature,
the parameters, the returns, and the guides that use it. Pick a domain,
or browse the types.

## World & game

| Global | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`world`](#ref-World) | A room's blocks, entities, displays, screens and time — the `world` global, or `room.world`. Start here for terrain, block writes, entities in the world, and world rules. |
| [`game`](#ref-Game) | The game version's own facts — blocks, items, entity kinds, terrain — and the pack's definitions of its own blocks and entities. |
| [`models`](#ref-models) | The models this pack makes, for `world.display{ kind = "model" }`. |
| [`parts`](#ref-parts) | Named parts of a stored world and the generators that build them. |
| [`routes`](#ref-routes) | How players get between the worlds of the group. |
| [`noise`](#ref-noise) | Smooth random numbers for a generator, made by the engine. |
| [`fields`](#ref-fields) | Recipes for numbers over the world, for `world.generate`. |
| [`data`](#ref-data) | Helpers for persistent data views — `data.copy`, `data.insert`, `data.remove`. |

## Players

| Global | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`players`](#ref-Players) | Everyone in the room: joins and leaves, clicks and chat, inventory, visibility and health — the `players` global, or `room.players`. |
| [`camera`](#ref-camera) | Camera paths and modes per player. |

## Interface & media

| Global | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`ui`](#ref-Ui) | What the players see: titles, chat lines, sidebars, boss bars, screens, menus and dialogs — the `ui` global, or `room.ui`. |
| [`fx`](#ref-Fx) | Particles: `fx.particle` with count, spread, velocity and dust colour. |
| [`sound`](#ref-Sound) | Sound by name from the resource pack, or streamed through Simple Voice Chat. |
| [`message`](#ref-message) | A chat line to everyone in the main room. |
| [`tween`](#ref-tween) | Any live field eased over time — numbers, vec3 and color values. |
| [`color`](#ref-color) | Colour helpers: hsv, gradients and nearest-map-colour. |
| [`colors`](#ref-colors) | The named colour table: Minecraft's sixteen and more. |

## Systems

| Global | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`commands`](#ref-Commands) | `commands.add` with typed arguments, tab-completion, permissions and aliases. |
| [`time`](#ref-time) | Clocks for a pack: a callback every tick, one every few seconds, and the seconds since the pack started. |
| [`task`](#ref-task) | The scheduler: `spawn`, `delay`, `defer`, `wait` and `cancel`. |
| [`rooms`](#ref-rooms) | Making and destroying rooms — isolated worlds with their own tables. |
| [`storage`](#ref-storage) | A per-pack JSON file that survives a restart. |
| [`stores`](#ref-stores) | The experience's shared store: versioned facts, blobs and leases across every server. |
| [`http`](#ref-http) | HTTP requests from the pack, with caching. |
| [`network`](#ref-network) | WebSockets out and listening sockets, for multiplayer-scale IO. |
| [`shop`](#ref-shop) | Minefort's Gem shop: prompts, ownership and paid delivery. |
| [`hub`](#ref-hub) | The Minefort hub: servers, experiences and portals. |

## Engine

| Global | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`citadel`](#ref-citadel) | The engine itself: the log, versions, environment and the tick budget. |
| [`vec3`](#ref-vec3) | Positions and directions with `x`, `y`, `z` — plus `lerp`, `distance` and friends. |

<!-- /ref/World/ -->

<a id="ref-World"></a>

## world global · type World

A room's blocks, entities, displays, screens and time: the `world` global, or `room.world`.

Part of the [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`on_generate`](#ref-World-on_generate) | Called for a chunk each time it comes into memory, in a script world; it must make the same blocks every time. |
| [`on_populate`](#ref-World-on_populate) | Each chunk the overworld terrain made, once, after it made it. |
| [`dimension`](#ref-World-dimension) | Another world of the server's group, by dimension id or its last part ("dungeon", "minecraft:the_nether"): that world's own `world` table. |
| [`drop`](#ref-World-drop) | A stack on the ground at a block, as a broken block leaves one. |
| [`container`](#ref-World-container) | A chest's stacks, or nil where the block keeps none. |
| [`rules`](#ref-World-rules) | `world.rules{ fall = true }` switches one on, false off; a rule left out or nil keeps its value, and a number or a string is an error. `world.rules()` reads them. |
| [`raycast`](#ref-World-raycast) | The first block a ray from `from` along `direction` meets within `max` blocks, and the face it came in through; nil for none. |
| [`sees`](#ref-World-sees) | True when no block stops the line from `from` to `to`: a block with a collision box does (glass, leaves), water and grass do not. |
| [`raycasts`](#ref-World-raycasts) | `n` lines at once. `rays` holds six f64 a line (from x, y, z, to x, y, z); `out` gets one f64 a line: how far along it the first block is that stops it, or -1 for a clear line. |
| [`light_at`](#ref-World-light_at) | Block light and sky light, 0 to 15, and whether nothing above holds off the sky. |
| [`path`](#ref-World-path) | The points a body walks from `from` to the block at `to`, or nil. The game's own search: a step up of one block, falls of `fall` (3). `size` is { width, height } (0.6, 1.8); `swim` goes through water; `range` (the distance + 16) and `budget` (2000 nodes) stop a long search, which then gives the part that came closest. |
| [`zone`](#ref-World-zone) | Makes a box of blocks, both corners included, that knows who is in it; checked once a tick by feet position. Ends with the script. |
| [`set_block`](#ref-World-set_block) | `skin` is for "player_head" and "player_wall_head" only: an account's name, or the raw `textures` property. |
| [`set_blocks`](#ref-World-set_blocks) | Sets many blocks at once, live, stored and sent; the cheapest way. A row takes `skin` too, for a player head. |
| [`fill`](#ref-World-fill) | Fills a box of blocks between two corners, live, stored and sent to everyone. |
| [`schematic`](#ref-World-schematic) | A file inside the pack; a path that leaves it, or one that is not there, is an error naming the file. |
| [`build`](#ref-World-build) | The same value, written in code instead of read from a file. `{ detail = 2 }`: coordinates are half blocks, fitted to slabs and stairs. |
| [`paste`](#ref-World-paste) | Live, stored and sent; air is skipped unless `air` is true. |
| [`get_block`](#ref-World-get_block) | `nil` where that chunk is not in memory: a read never generates. |
| [`block`](#ref-World-block) | The block there as the handle a hook gets: reads are live, and what it does lands on the next tick. `state` and `data` are for this pack's own blocks. `nil` where that chunk is not in memory. |
| [`get_biome`](#ref-World-get_biome) | Returns the biome name of the column at `pos`; `nil` where that chunk is not in memory. |
| [`generate`](#ref-World-generate) | Declares this world: the engine makes each chunk from the rules, on every core, and no script runs for a chunk. |
| [`get_blocks`](#ref-World-get_blocks) | A box, in x, then z, then y order. |
| [`items`](#ref-World-items) | The stacks on the ground: `{ id, item, count, at }` rows. |
| [`spawn`](#ref-World-spawn) | Puts an entity at a point and returns its handle. A mob kind of the game by name (`world.spawn("cow", pos)`) is the game's own entity, and takes no `data`. A pack's own kind takes the data it starts life holding. `nil` for a kind nothing defined and this game does not have. |
| [`entities`](#ref-World-entities) | Live and queued entities, in ascending id. Optional near/radius select a sphere; kind filters by canonical name. near and radius go together. `mob = true` gives the mobs only, `mob = false` the rest. |
| [`explode`](#ref-World-explode) | A blast at a point. The power is clamped by this game's own column and the tick's explosion budget decides when it goes off, never whether. |
| [`on_block_break`](#ref-World-on_block_break) | What the survival tick did. Observe-only: the world has already changed, and what the callback returns is not read. |
| [`on_block_place`](#ref-World-on_block_place) | Tells after a block was placed, with its canonical name. Observe-only; `player` is nil when nobody placed it or they left. |
| [`on_entity_spawn`](#ref-World-on_entity_spawn) | Tells after a mob appeared, with its handle and name; a natural spawn fires it on every game version that has one, and a pack's own `world.spawn("cow", pos)` fires it too. Mob kinds only. |
| [`on_entity_death`](#ref-World-on_entity_death) | Tells after a mob died; it is gone, so its id and name is all there is. Mob kinds only. |
| [`time`](#ref-World-time) | Holds the sky at a time (ticks, or "sunrise", "day", "noon", "sunset", "night", "midnight"), or asks a function each tick, `s` seconds after the call. With no argument: the time of day now, 0 to 23999. |
| [`light`](#ref-World-light) | Sends players light no block makes, 1 to 15 a source; each call replaces the last, `{}` ends it. 1.14 and later. |
| [`screen`](#ref-World-screen) | Puts a wall of map frames, `width` by `height` frames (128 pixels each), in front of a wall; `at` is the top-left frame. Returns a Screen. |
| [`canvas`](#ref-World-canvas) | Makes a picture of `width` by `height` maps (1 by 1 by default, 16 at most a side) with no frame of its own, for a frame, a hand or a screen. |
| [`display`](#ref-World-display) | A model stands in the world through the same call as everything else, and is the one kind that hands back something other than a Display. |
| [`hitbox`](#ref-World-hitbox) | Makes an invisible box a player can click; `solid` also makes it a wall. `depth` is the width unless given. 1.19.4 and later. |
| [`npc`](#ref-World-npc) | Places a player-shaped entity every client from 1.8 sees; removed when the script ends or reloads. |
| [`puppet`](#ref-World-puppet) | Places a mob's body with no mind of its own that the script moves; its name tag always shows. An error when this game has no such mob kind. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`world.spawn_point: Vec3`](#ref-World-spawn_point) | Where players arrive in this room; writable. The same value as the room's `spawn_point`. |

## world.block

Part of [`world`](#ref-World).

```luau
world.block(pos: Vec3) → BlockAt ?
```

The block there as the handle a hook gets: reads are live, and what it does lands on the next tick. `state` and `data` are for this pack's own blocks. `nil` where that chunk is not in memory.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pos` | [`Vec3`](#ref-Vec3) | yes |

## Returns

- [`BlockAt`](#ref-BlockAt)

## Used in

> "world.block(pos)                          -- the block there as a handle: its state, its data, whether it is powered; see "power"" — [Blocks and terrain](#world-terrain-generation)
> "it from anywhere with `world.block(pos)`:" — [Custom blocks](#world-custom-blocks)
> "local door = world.block(vec3(10, 65, 10))   -- the block there, or nil where the chunk is not loaded" — [Custom blocks](#world-custom-blocks)

## world.display

Part of [`world`](#ref-World).

```luau
world.display((opts: { kind: "model", model: Model, at: Vec3 ?, rotation: Orientation ?, scale: (number | Vec3)?, -- models require equal positive axes paint: { [string]: Ink }?, fallback: string ?, seats: { Vec3 }?, lead: boolean ?, }) -> ModelDisplay) → & ((opts: { kind: "item" | "text" | "block" | "frame", at: Vec3 ?, rotation: Orientation ?, scale: (Vec3 | number)?, billboard: Billboard ?, glow: (Ink | false)?, item: ItemSpec ?, canvas: Canvas ?, context: Context ?, text: Text ?, color: Ink ?, background: (Ink | false)?, line_width: number ?, shadow: boolean ?, block: string ?, facing: ScreenFacing ?, invisible: boolean ?, glide: number ?, lead: boolean ?, }) -> Display)
```

A model stands in the world through the same call as everything else, and is the one kind that hands back something other than a Display.

| --- | --- | --- |

## Returns

- `& ((opts: { kind: "item" | "text" | "block" | "frame" , at: Vec3 ?, rotation: Orientation ?, scale: ( Vec3 | number )?, billboard: Billboard ?, glow: ( Ink | false )?, item: ItemSpec ?, canvas: Canvas ?, context: Context ?, text: Text ?, color: Ink ?, background: ( Ink | false )?, line_width: number ?, shadow: boolean ?, block: string ?, facing: ScreenFacing ?, invisible: boolean ?, glide: number ?, lead: boolean ?, }) -> Display )`

<a id="ref-World-drop"></a>

## world.drop

Live and queued entities, in ascending id. Optional near/radius select a sphere; kind filters by canonical name. near and radius go together. `mob = true` gives the mobs only, `mob = false` the rest.

> "world.entities { mob = true }    -- every mob in this room, as handles" — [Mobs and drops](#entities-mobs)

<!-- /ref/World/path/ -->

<a id="ref-World-path"></a>

## world.path

Part of [`world`](#ref-World).

```luau
world.path(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, opts: { size: (number | { number })?, swim: boolean ?, fall: number ?, range: number ?, budget: number ? }?) → { Vec3 }?
```

The points a body walks from `from` to the block at `to`, or nil. The game's own search: a step up of one block, falls of `fall` (3). `size` is { width, height } (0.6, 1.8); `swim` goes through water; `range` (the distance + 16) and `budget` (2000 nodes) stop a long search, which then gives the part that came closest.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | [`Vec3`](#ref-Vec3) | yes |
| `to` | [`Vec3`](#ref-Vec3) | yes |
| `opts` | `{ size: ( number \| { number })?, swim: boolean ?, fall: number ?, range: number ?, budget: number ? }` | no |

## Returns

- `{ Vec3 }?`

## Used in

> "need. It turns smoothly, follows the points of `world.path`, jumps when a" — [Custom entities](#entities-custom-entities)
> "-- Body i of `b` walks the route { points = world.path(...), at = 1 }." — [Custom entities](#entities-custom-entities)
> "world.path(from, to, { size = { 0.6, 1.95 } })  -- the points a body walks, a list of vec3, or nil" — [Zones and raycasts](#world-spatial-queries)
> "- `world.path(from, to, opts)` is the game's own search for a mob: four ways" — [Zones and raycasts](#world-spatial-queries)

---

## world.screen

Part of [`world`](#ref-World).

```luau
world.screen(opts: { at: Vec3, facing: Facing | "up", up: Facing ?, width: number ?, height: number ?, glow: boolean ?, on_click: ((player: Player, x: number, y: number, button: "left" | "right") -> ())?, }) → Screen
```

Puts a wall of map frames, `width` by `height` frames (128 pixels each), in front of a wall; `at` is the top-left frame. Returns a Screen.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opts` | `{ at: Vec3 , facing: Facing \| "up" , up: Facing ?, width: number ?, height: number ?, glow: boolean ?, on_click: ((player: Player , x: number , y: number , button: "left" \| "right" ) -> ())?, }` | yes |

## Returns

- [`Screen`](#ref-Screen)

## Used in

> "local board = world.screen{ at = vec3(-2, 68, -10), facing = "south", width = 4, height = 2 }" — [Scoreboard with a button](#guides-guide-scoreboard-with-a-button)
> "local board = world.screen{ at = vec3(-2, 68, -10), facing = "south", width = 4, height = 2 }" — [Screens](#ui-screens)
> "Set `on_click` (in `world.screen{}` or later) to get the pixel a player" — [Screens](#ui-screens)

<!-- /ref/World/spawn/ -->

<a id="ref-World-spawn"></a>

## world.spawn

Part of [`world`](#ref-World).

```luau
world.spawn(def: EntityDef | string, pos: Vec3, data: { [string]: any }?) → EntityHandle ?
```

Puts an entity at a point and returns its handle. A mob kind of the game by name (`world.spawn("cow", pos)`) is the game's own entity, and takes no `data`. A pack's own kind takes the data it starts life holding. `nil` for a kind nothing defined and this game does not have.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `def` | `EntityDef \| string` | yes |
| `pos` | [`Vec3`](#ref-Vec3) | yes |
| `data` | `{ [ string ]: any }` | no |

## Returns

- [`EntityHandle`](#ref-EntityHandle)

## Used in

> "assigning the whole record again. This works on handles from `world.spawn` and" — [Custom blocks](#world-custom-blocks)
> "`mob = false`. Pass it to `world.spawn` just like the handle from `define`." — [Game data](#world-game-data)
> "- `false` stops natural spawning only. A spawner block, `world.spawn`," — [Game data](#world-game-data)
> "\| Physics, gameplay hooks or persistence \| `game.entities.define` and `world.spawn` \| Gives a body behavior independent of its appearance. \|" — [Displays](#ui-displays)
> "local c = world.spawn(car, vec3(0.5, 65, 0.5))" — [Displays](#ui-displays)
> "its normal drops. `world.spawn` with the name of a mob kind spawns one and" — [Mobs and drops](#entities-mobs)

## world.time

Part of [`world`](#ref-World).

```luau
world.time((at: number | TimeName | (s: number) -> number | TimeName) -> ()) → & (() -> number)
```

Holds the sky at a time (ticks, or "sunrise", "day", "noon", "sunset", "night", "midnight"), or asks a function each tick, `s` seconds after the call. With no argument: the time of day now, 0 to 23999.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(at` | `number \| TimeName \| (s: number ) -> number \| TimeName ) -> ()` | yes |

## Returns

- `& (() -> number )`

## Used in

> "world.time("sunset")" — [Guide: Build a cottage](#guides-guide-build-a-cottage)
> "`world.time("sunset")` holds the sky at sunset: low light makes the roof" — [Guide: Build a cottage](#guides-guide-build-a-cottage)
> "world.time("day")                         -- the sky stays there; see "the time of day"" — [Blocks and terrain](#world-terrain-generation)
> "world.time(function(s) return s * 20 end) -- asked each tick; s is seconds since this call" — [Blocks and terrain](#world-terrain-generation)

<!-- /ref/Game/ -->

<a id="ref-Game"></a>

## game global · type Game

The game version a room runs, its entity kinds, blocks and items, and the pack's own blocks, items and recipes: the `game` global, or `room.game`.

Part of the [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`block`](#ref-Game-block) | Returns one block in this version's numbers, or nil for a name this game has no word for. |
| [`item`](#ref-Game-item) | Returns an item this game has, or nil for a name it does not; never an error. |
| [`texture`](#ref-Game-texture) | Returns a new texture of width by height pixels, see-through until drawn on, for a pack's block or item. A texture to draw on (512 at most a side), or a PNG file in the pack (4096 at most a side). |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`game.version: string`](#ref-Game-version) | This game's version, such as "a0.1.0". |
| [`game.world_height: number`](#ref-Game-world_height) | How tall the world is in blocks: 128, or 256 for a 1.8.9 world. |
| [`game.sea_level: number`](#ref-Game-sea_level) | The y of this world's sea level. |
| [`game.entities: Entities & { [string]: (EntityKind \| EntityDef)? }`](#ref-Game-entities) | The kinds of entity: `define` a pack's own, `amend` the game's own, and read a kind of the game: a mob kind by either spelling (`game.entities.cow`, `game.entities.Cow`), a kind that is not a mob by its name (`game.entities.arrow`); nil where the game has none. It iterates every kind, including pack definitions: `for name, kind in game.entities do`. |
| [`game.blocks: Blocks`](#ref-Game-blocks) | The one table that *adds* to a version rather than reading it. |
| [`game.biomes: Biomes`](#ref-Game-biomes) | Biomes of the pack's own: a vanilla biome with other colours and weather. |
| [`game.recipes: Recipes`](#ref-Game-recipes) | What a crafting grid and a furnace make of a pack's items; recipes are added while the pack loads. |
| [`game.items: Items`](#ref-Game-items) | Defines items of the pack's own, with a texture for clients from 1.21.4. |
| [`game.terrain: { snow: boolean ?, steps: { TerrainStep }? }?`](#ref-Game-terrain) | What this world's overworld is made of: `snow` and `steps`, as citadel.yml writes them; read-only, nil when there is no list. |

---

<!-- /ref/Game/entities/ -->

<a id="ref-Game-entities"></a>

## game.entities

Part of [`game`](#ref-Game).

```luau
game.entities: Entities & { [string]: (EntityKind | EntityDef)? }
```

The kinds of entity: `define` a pack's own, `amend` the game's own, and read a kind of the game: a mob kind by either spelling (`game.entities.cow`, `game.entities.Cow`), a kind that is not a mob by its name (`game.entities.arrow`); nil where the game has none. It iterates every kind, including pack definitions: `for name, kind in game.entities do`.

## Used in

> "game.entities.names { mob = true }   -- {"pig", "sheep", "cow", ...}" — [Game data](#world-game-data)
> "entity here: players are in `players`, never in `world.entities`. `game.entities.<kind>`" — [Game data](#world-game-data)
> "\| Physics, gameplay hooks or persistence \| `game.entities.define` and `world.spawn` \| Gives a body behavior independent of its appearance. \|" — [Displays](#ui-displays)
> "local car = game.entities.define {" — [Displays](#ui-displays)
> "`game.entities.<kind>`." — [Custom entities](#entities-custom-entities)
> "game.entities.amend("pig", {" — [Custom entities](#entities-custom-entities)

## noise global

Part of the [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`new`](#ref-noise-new) | Returns a noise. `scale` is the size of a hill in blocks (64), and each of the `octaves` (1) adds detail `lacunarity` (2) times finer and `gain` (0.5) times as strong. |

<!-- /ref/noise/new/ -->

<a id="ref-noise-new"></a>

## noise.new

Part of [`noise`](#ref-noise).

```luau
noise.new(opts: { seed: number ?, scale: number ?, octaves: number ?, gain: number ?, lacunarity: number ? }?) → Noise
```

Returns a noise. `scale` is the size of a hill in blocks (64), and each of the `octaves` (1) adds detail `lacunarity` (2) times finer and `gain` (0.5) times as strong.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opts` | `{ seed: number ?, scale: number ?, octaves: number ?, gain: number ?, lacunarity: number ? }` | no |

- [`Noise`](#ref-Noise)

## Used in

> "local hills = noise.new { seed = 7, scale = 96, octaves = 4 }" — [Blocks and terrain](#world-terrain-generation)
> "local hills = noise.new { seed = 7, scale = 96, octaves = 4 }" — [Blocks and terrain](#world-terrain-generation)

<!-- /ref/fields/ -->

<a id="ref-fields"></a>

## fields global

Recipes for numbers over the world, for `world.generate`.

Part of the [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`noise`](#ref-fields-noise) | Smooth noise, about -1..1. `solid = true` changes with y too. |
| [`mix`](#ref-fields-mix) | `a` where `t` is 0, `b` where it is 1. |
| [`hash`](#ref-fields-hash) | One number 0..1 for each square of `cell` blocks (1). |
| [`cells`](#ref-fields-cells) | A scattered grid, one point per `size` blocks: the distance to the nearest point, and that point's own number 0..1. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`fields.x: Field`](#ref-fields-x) |  |
| [`fields.y: Field`](#ref-fields-y) |  |
| [`fields.z: Field`](#ref-fields-z) |  |
| [`fields.height: Field`](#ref-fields-height) | The y of the surface of a column, as a block. |
| [`fields.slope: Field`](#ref-fields-slope) | The step to the steepest of the four columns beside this one. |
| [`fields.water: Field`](#ref-fields-water) | How deep the water is over the surface; 0 and below on land. |
| [`fields.shore: Field`](#ref-fields-shore) | 1 on a column at the water's edge with water beside it. |
| [`fields.depth: Field`](#ref-fields-depth) | Blocks under the surface: `fields.height - fields.y`. |
| [`fields.room: Field`](#ref-fields-room) | The height of the open space a block is in: 0 in rock, 64 at most (and in the open sky). `density` cannot use it. |

---

<!-- /ref/fields/cells/ -->

<a id="ref-fields-cells"></a>

## fields.cells

Part of [`fields`](#ref-fields).

```luau
fields.cells(size: number, seed: number ?) → { distance: Field, random: Field }
```

A scattered grid, one point per `size` blocks: the distance to the nearest point, and that point's own number 0..1.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `number` | yes |
| `seed` | `number` | no |

## Returns

- `{ distance: Field , random: Field }`

## Used in

> "fields.cells(size, seed)                    -- { distance = field, random = field }: the nearest point of a scattered grid" — [Blocks and terrain](#world-terrain-generation)

## fields.noise

```luau
fields.noise(opts: { seed: number ?, scale: number ?, octaves: number ?, gain: number ?, lacunarity: number ?, solid: boolean ? }?) → Field
```

| --- | --- | --- |
| `opts` | `{ seed: number ?, scale: number ?, octaves: number ?, gain: number ?, lacunarity: number ?, solid: boolean ? }` | no |

## Used in

## data global

Helpers for persistent data views — `data.copy`, `data.insert`, `data.remove`.

Part of the [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`copy`](#ref-data-copy) | A detached JSON snapshot as ordinary Lua values/tables. |
| [`insert`](#ref-data-insert) | Insert into a nested data list; omitted index appends. |
| [`remove`](#ref-data-remove) | Remove and return a detached value; omitted index removes the last element. |

## data.insert

<!-- /ref/Players/ -->

<a id="ref-Players"></a>

## players global · type Players

A room's players and their events: the `players` global, or `room.players`.

Part of the [Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`on_join`](#ref-Players-on_join) | Calls `fn` when a player arrives: on the globals when a client connects, on a room's table each time a player moves into it. |
| [`on_leave`](#ref-Players-on_leave) | The same player value on_join had; it can no longer be sent to. |
| [`list`](#ref-Players-list) | Returns every player in the room. |
| [`get`](#ref-Players-get) | Returns the player with this name, or nil. |
| [`count`](#ref-Players-count) | Returns how many players are in the room. |
| [`near`](#ref-Players-near) | Who is within a radius of a point, and who is inside a box of blocks. |
| [`within`](#ref-Players-within) | Returns every player inside a box of blocks, corners included. |
| [`on_click`](#ref-Players-on_click) | Calls `fn` on a left or right click; `hit` holds the button and the entity, player, block and face it met. |
| [`on_sneak`](#ref-Players-on_sneak) | Calls `fn` once per sneak press and release; `down` is true on the press. |
| [`on_slot`](#ref-Players-on_slot) | Calls `fn` when a player picks a hotbar slot, 1..9. |
| [`on_chat`](#ref-Players-on_chat) | Return false and the line is not said. |
| [`on_pickup`](#ref-Players-on_pickup) | A stack taken off the ground, and one that landed on it. `player` is nil where the world dropped it, or where they have already left. |
| [`on_drop`](#ref-Players-on_drop) | Calls `fn` when a stack lands on the ground; `player` is nil where the world dropped it or they have left. |
| [`on_death`](#ref-Players-on_death) | Calls `fn` when a player dies, with the cause (fall, drown, void, lava, ...) and the line broadcast; `player` is nil once they have left. |
| [`on_respawn`](#ref-Players-on_respawn) | Calls `fn` when a player respawns; `player` is nil once they have left. |
| [`on_break`](#ref-Players-on_break) | Cancellable. Return `false` to stop it; return nothing to let it through. These are asked *before* the world changes and the engine waits milliseconds for the answer, so they must be quick and must never `task.wait`.  Timeout, error, overflow and disabled handlers deny the action. Across packs any `false` wins. See docs/luau-api.md, "saying no". |
| [`on_place`](#ref-Players-on_place) | Asks `fn` before a player puts a block down; return false to cancel it. A missed deadline denies the place. |
| [`on_damage`](#ref-Players-on_damage) | Asks `fn` before damage lands on a player; return false to refuse it. A missed deadline denies it. A pack's own `player:damage` is not asked about. |

---

<!-- /ref/Players/on_break/ -->

<a id="ref-Players-on_break"></a>

## players.on_break

Part of [`players`](#ref-Players).

```luau
players.on_break(fn: (player: Player ?, pos: Vec3, block: string) -> boolean ?) → Connection
```

Cancellable. Return `false` to stop it; return nothing to let it through. These are asked *before* the world changes and the engine waits milliseconds for the answer, so they must be quick and must never `task.wait`. Timeout, error, overflow and disabled handlers deny the action. Across packs any `false` wins. See docs/luau-api.md, "saying no".

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fn` | `(player: Player ?, pos: Vec3 , block: string ) -> boolean` | no |

## Returns

- [`Connection`](#ref-Connection)

## Used in

> "`players.on_break` and `players.on_place` run **before** the world changes. A" — [Cancelling events](#concepts-events)
> "players.on_break(function(player, pos, block) return false end) -> connection" — [Cancelling events](#concepts-events)
> "waits a few milliseconds for the answer. Three exist: `players.on_break`" — [Limits and reload](#systems-limits)

---

<!-- /ref/Ui/ -->

<a id="ref-Ui"></a>

## ui global · type Ui

Titles, chat, the action bar, boss bars, the sidebar and the tab list: for everyone in a room (the `ui` global, or `room.ui`), or for one player (`player.ui`, the same calls). "Everyone" below is one player on `player.ui`.

Part of the [UI basics](#ui-ui-basics) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`title`](#ref-Ui-title) | Shows a title and subtitle to everyone in the room; fades and stay are in seconds. |
| [`actionbar`](#ref-Ui-actionbar) | Shows a line above the hotbar to everyone in the room. |
| [`bossbar`](#ref-Ui-bossbar) | Shows a boss bar to everyone in the room and returns its handle; progress 0..1. 1.8 reads the title on its action bar. |
| [`sidebar`](#ref-Ui-sidebar) | Sets the sidebar for everyone in the room; lines run top to bottom and only changed lines are sent. nil or false removes the sidebar. |
| [`tab`](#ref-Ui-tab) | Sets the player list's header and footer for everyone in the room. |
| [`box`](#ref-Ui-box) | The pieces of a layout (see "Layouts"). Sizes are pixels of the game's own HUD; a box is 1 to 256 a side. An item with an `id` is live. |
| [`image`](#ref-Ui-image) |  |
| [`label`](#ref-Ui-label) | Words in the client's own letters, space to `~`. Give a label whose words change a `width`. |
| [`row`](#ref-Ui-row) | The children are the list part: `ui.row{ gap = 4, a, b }`. |
| [`column`](#ref-Ui-column) |  |
| [`stack`](#ref-Ui-stack) |  |
| [`define`](#ref-Ui-define) | A layout of one child, centred over the hotbar with its bottom edge `margin` pixels above the screen's (40, or 25 when `hide_hud` takes the hearts and the food away). While the pack loads only. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`ui.kit: { [string]: any }`](#ref-Ui-kit) | What a dialog is made of (see "Dialogs"): row, column, stack, space, text, image, and window, button, tabs, close, badge, dot, progress, divider, card, grid, theme, mix and SCREEN. |

---

<!-- /ref/Fx/ -->

<a id="ref-Fx"></a>

## fx global · type Fx

Particles for a room: Minecraft's particle packet; the `fx` global, or `room.fx`.

Part of the [Sound](#ui-sound) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`particle`](#ref-Fx-particle) | Shows particle `name` ("dust", "end_rod", "explosion", "firework", "flame", "note", "totem_of_undying") at `pos`, or at every point of a list. Each point reaches players in the room within 64 blocks of its origin in 3D, including the boundary, before spread or velocity. `count` (1) at each point in a box `spread` (0) out; or with `velocity`, one particle moving along it (`speed` 1 then, else 0). `color` and `size` are for dust only. |

---

<!-- /ref/Fx/particle/ -->

<a id="ref-Fx-particle"></a>

## fx.particle

Part of [`fx`](#ref-Fx).

```luau
fx.particle(name: string, pos: Vec3 | { Vec3 }, opts: { count: number ?, spread: (number | Vec3)?, velocity: Vec3 ?, speed: number ?, color: Ink ?, size: number ?, }?)
```

Shows particle `name` ("dust", "end_rod", "explosion", "firework", "flame", "note", "totem_of_undying") at `pos`, or at every point of a list. Each point reaches players in the room within 64 blocks of its origin in 3D, including the boundary, before spread or velocity. `count` (1) at each point in a box `spread` (0) out; or with `velocity`, one particle moving along it (`speed` 1 then, else 0). `color` and `size` are for dust only.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes |
| `pos` | `Vec3 \| { Vec3 }` | yes |
| `opts` | `{ count: number ?, spread: ( number \| Vec3 )?, velocity: Vec3 ?, speed: number ?, color: Ink ?, size: number ?, }` | no |

## Used in

> "fx.particle("totem_of_undying", at + vec3(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), { count = 12, spread = 0.4, speed = 0.3 })" — [Guide: Coin rush](#guides-guide-coin-rush)
> "fx.particle("firework", arena.CENTER + vec3(0, 2, 0), { count = 60, spread = 2, speed = 0.1 })" — [Guide: Coin rush](#guides-guide-coin-rush)
> "room.fx.particle("firework", c.finish + vec3(0.5, 2, 0.5), { count = 50, spread = 1.5, speed = 0.1 })" — [Guide: Parkour, a room each](#guides-guide-parkour-a-room-each)
> "room.fx.particle("firework", c.finish + vec3(0.5, 2, 0.5), { count = 50, spread = 1.5, speed = 0.1 })" — [Guide: Parkour, a room each](#guides-guide-parkour-a-room-each)
> "fx.particle(name, pos, { count = 1, spread = 0, velocity = nil, speed = 0, color = nil, size = 1 })" — [Particles and lasers](#ui-fx)
> "fx.particle("dust", points, { color = colors.red, size = 1.5 })" — [Particles and lasers](#ui-fx)

<!-- /ref/Sound/ -->

<a id="ref-Sound"></a>

## sound global · type Sound

Plays and stops sounds for everyone in a room: the `sound` global, or `room.sound`.

Part of the [Sound](#ui-sound) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`play`](#ref-Sound-play) | Plays a sound by name to everyone in the room; volume above 1 carries further, pitch 0.5..2.0. |
| [`stop`](#ref-Sound-stop) | One sound by name, or every sound, for everyone in the room; 1.13+. |
| [`stream`](#ref-Sound-stream) | A live stream (MP3, or an FLV's sound) or a pack's sound file (OGG, MP3, WAV), heard through the mod a screen's stream uses. With `at`, from speakers: each player hears every speaker within `distance`. Without, from no place, at one volume. `to`: only these players. `loop`: files only. |

---

<!-- /ref/Sound/stream/ -->

<a id="ref-Sound-stream"></a>

## sound.stream

Part of [`sound`](#ref-Sound).

```luau
sound.stream(opts: { url: string ?, file: string ?, at: (SoundSpeaker | { SoundSpeaker })?, to: (Player | { Player })?, distance: number ?, loop: boolean ?, name: string ?, }) → SoundStream
```

A live stream (MP3, or an FLV's sound) or a pack's sound file (OGG, MP3, WAV), heard through the mod a screen's stream uses. With `at`, from speakers: each player hears every speaker within `distance`. Without, from no place, at one volume. `to`: only these players. `loop`: files only.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opts` | `{ url: string ?, file: string ?, at: ( SoundSpeaker \| { SoundSpeaker })?, to: ( Player \| { Player })?, distance: number ?, loop: boolean ?, name: string ?, }` | yes |

## Returns

- [`SoundStream`](#ref-SoundStream)

## Used in

> "[`sound.stream`](#sound)." — [Canvases](#ui-canvases)
> "## sound.stream" — [Sound](#ui-sound)
> "`sound.stream` plays a live stream or a pack's sound file through the" — [Sound](#ui-sound)

| [`nearest`](#ref-color-nearest) | The colour a picture really shows, since it snaps to the map palette. |
| [`gradient`](#ref-color-gradient) | The colour `u` (0 to 1) of the way along the list; with `loop`, `u` wraps and the last colour runs back into the first. |

## color.gradient

```luau
color.gradient(list: { Ink }, u: number, loop: boolean ?) → Color
```

| `loop` | `boolean` | no |

<!-- /ref/Commands/ -->

<a id="ref-Commands"></a>

## commands global · type Commands

Adds a room's slash commands from a usage line: the `commands` global, or `room.commands`.

Part of the [Player lifecycle](#players-player-lifecycle) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`add`](#ref-Commands-add) | usage: "bet <amount:integer 1..10000> [color:red\|black]". Types: word, integer, number (with an optional min..max), player, a\|b\|c, text... (the rest of the line as a string), words... (as a list). args holds each argument by name; an optional one not typed is nil. Return a string and the player reads it in red. |
| [`run`](#ref-Commands-run) | Runs a pack's command for player as if they typed it ("/servers"), with their permissions. false when no pack in their room declared it. |

---

<!-- /ref/Commands/add/ -->

<a id="ref-Commands-add"></a>

## commands.add

Part of [`commands`](#ref-Commands).

```luau
commands.add(usage: string, fn: (player: Player, args: { [string]: any }) -> string ?, opts: CommandOpts ?) → Command
```

usage: "bet <amount:integer 1..10000> [color:red|black]". Types: word, integer, number (with an optional min..max), player, a|b|c, text... (the rest of the line as a string), words... (as a list). args holds each argument by name; an optional one not typed is nil. Return a string and the player reads it in red.

<!-- /ref/time/ -->

<a id="ref-time"></a>

## time global

Clocks for a pack: a callback every tick, one every few seconds, and the seconds since the pack started.

Part of the [Terrain generation](#world-terrain-generation) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`on_tick`](#ref-time-on_tick) | Calls `fn` every tick, 20 times a second, with the tick number; keep it short. |
| [`every`](#ref-time-every) | Calls `fn` every `seconds`, precise to 1 ms and never drifting; use it for music. |
| [`now`](#ref-time-now) | Seconds since the pack started. |

---

<!-- /ref/rooms/create/ -->

<a id="ref-rooms-create"></a>

## rooms.create

Part of [`rooms`](#ref-rooms).

```luau
rooms.create(opts: { spawn_point: Vec3 ?, generate: ((chunk: Chunk) -> ())? }) → Room
```

Creates an isolated room with its own chunks, players and effects; `spawn_point` defaults to (0.5, 65, 0.5), `generate` fills each chunk.

- [`Room`](#ref-Room)

## storage global

A per-pack JSON file that survives a restart.

Part of the [Storage](#systems-storage) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`status`](#ref-storage-status) | Last persistence error and whether there are unsaved changes. |
| [`flush`](#ref-storage-flush) | Yields until saved; raises an error on failure. After initialization only. |
| [`get`](#ref-storage-get) | Returns the value saved under `key`, or nil when there is none. |
| [`set`](#ref-storage-set) | Saves a value under `key` in this pack's storage.json; nil forgets it. |
| [`keys`](#ref-storage-keys) | Every key, sorted; with a prefix, only those that start with it. |

<!-- /ref/stores/ -->

<a id="ref-stores"></a>

## stores global

The experience's shared store: versioned facts, blobs and leases across every server.

Part of the [Storage](#systems-storage) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`open`](#ref-stores-open) | Returns the experience's one store. It takes no id; passing one is an error. |
| [`request`](#ref-stores-request) | Sends one raw query to the store and yields until it answers; returns the answer table and any blob bytes. |
| [`lease`](#ref-stores-lease) | Takes a lease on `key` for `holder`, lasting `ttl_ms` milliseconds (up to one hour); returns a fencing token. |
| [`renew`](#ref-stores-renew) | Extends the lease on `key` that `token` holds. |
| [`release`](#ref-stores-release) | Gives up the lease on `key` that `token` holds. |
| [`blob_list`](#ref-stores-blob_list) | Lists a player's blobs across all blob stores in this scope, each with its store, key, version and size. |

---

<!-- /ref/http/ -->

<a id="ref-http"></a>

## http global

HTTP requests from the pack, with caching.

Part of the [Storage](#systems-storage) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`get`](#ref-http-get) | GET a URL. `cache` is the seconds a 200 answer is kept on disk; `timeout` is 1 to 60 seconds, 15 by default. |
| [`socket`](#ref-http-socket) | Opens a WebSocket (`ws` or `wss`) and keeps it open: when the connection ends, the engine dials again. `on_message` gets each message on a tick. |

---

<a id="ref-http-get"></a>

GET a URL. `cache` is the seconds a 200 answer is kept on disk; `timeout` is 1 to 60 seconds, 15 by default.

## Used in

> "- A `banner` is a 1024×512 PNG its creator uploaded and Minefort checked: 8 by 4 maps. Read it with `http.get(banner, { cache = 86400 }):image()`; a new banner has a new URL, so the cache never shows an old one." — [Hub](#systems-hub)
> "`http.get` fetches a URL: map tiles, a leaderboard, any public API." — [HTTP](#systems-http)
> "local res = http.get("https://tile.example.org/15/9649/12315.png", {" — [HTTP](#systems-http)

<!-- /ref/network/ -->

<a id="ref-network"></a>

## network global

WebSockets out and listening sockets, for multiplayer-scale IO.

Part of the [Storage](#systems-storage) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`start`](#ref-network-start) | Starts an instance of `member`. Answers at once; it is online later. |
| [`find`](#ref-network-find) | The instance to send `players` players to (1 unless set), or nil when none has room. With `start`, one is started when none has room. |
| [`stop`](#ref-network-stop) | Stops an instance of this network. |
| [`info`](#ref-network-info) | This server's network, by name, and the instance this pack runs on: `id` and the fields after it are nil on a server that is not one. |
| [`status`](#ref-network-status) | Says where this instance is. At most one a second is sent: the first at once, then the last of those that came after. |
| [`on_instance_start`](#ref-network-on_instance_start) | Called when an instance is first seen: started, or already running. |
| [`on_instance_change`](#ref-network-on_instance_change) | Called when an instance's state, open, status or meta changes. |
| [`on_instance_stop`](#ref-network-on_instance_stop) | Called with the id of an instance that is gone. |
| [`online`](#ref-network-online) | How many play on this network (everyone on Minefort on the platform's hub), or in one mode's games. An answer is kept for 5 seconds. |
| [`browse`](#ref-network-browse) | The platform's hub finding every network, in the order to show them. nil and why on a refusal, and anywhere but that hub. One page of 6 rows (page from 1), and how many there are in all; nil and why on a refusal. |
| [`instances`](#ref-network-instances) | Everything this network runs: this experience's own always-on servers (on the platform's hub, the hubs), then its games started on demand. With `label`, only that mode's games. |

---

<!-- /ref/network/browse/ -->

<a id="ref-network-browse"></a>

## network.browse

Part of [`network`](#ref-network).

```luau
network.browse(view: "search" | "for-you" | "recent" | "featured", options: {player: (Player | string)?, query: string ?, page: number ?, category: string ?, online: boolean ?, ids: {string}?, sort: ("players" | "name")?, also: {recent: boolean ?, favorites: {string}?}?}?) → ({BrowseEntry}?, (number | string)?, {recent: {rows: {BrowseEntry}, total: number} | false | nil, favorites: {rows: {BrowseEntry}, total: number} | false | nil}?)
```

The platform's hub finding every network, in the order to show them. nil and why on a refusal, and anywhere but that hub. One page of 6 rows (page from 1), and how many there are in all; nil and why on a refusal.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `view` | `"search" \| "for-you" \| "recent" \| "featured"` | yes |
| `options` | `{player: (Player \| string)?, query: string ?, page: number ?, category: string ?, online: boolean ?, ids: {string}?, sort: ("players" \| "name")?, also: {recent: boolean ?, favorites: {string}?}?}` | no |

## Returns

- `({BrowseEntry}?, (number | string)?, {recent: {rows: {BrowseEntry}, total: number} | false | nil, favorites: {rows: {BrowseEntry}, total: number} | false | nil}?)`

## Used in

> "- `network.browse(view, options?)` finds other networks, and only the platform's hub may ask:" — [Network](#systems-network)
> "- `view` is `"search"` (what matches `query`: names as they are typed, and domains), `"for-you"` (more of what `player` plays, busiest first, none of their recent ones), `"recent"` (where `player` played last, newest first) or `"featured"` (the busiest). Each row is a network: `{id, name, category, motd, icon, players, maxPlayers, state}`, and `id` is what `player:connect` takes. A network is one row, however many servers it has. It returns one page of 6 rows and how many there are in all: `local rows, total = network.browse('featured', { page = 2 })`." — [Network](#systems-network)
> "with `network.browse`, and its hubs with `network.instances`, and asks the" — [Hub](#systems-hub)
> "for _, s in network.browse('featured') or {} do print(s.name, s.players) end" — [Hub](#systems-hub)

---

<!-- /ref/network/instances/ -->

<a id="ref-network-instances"></a>

## network.instances

Part of [`network`](#ref-network).

```luau
network.instances(label: string ?) → ({BrowseEntry | NetworkInstance}?, string ?)
```

Everything this network runs: this experience's own always-on servers (on the platform's hub, the hubs), then its games started on demand. With `label`, only that mode's games.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | no |

## Returns

- `({BrowseEntry | NetworkInstance}?, string ?)`

## Used in

> "- `network.instances(label?)` returns everything this network runs, as this experience sees it: first its own servers that run all the time, online and taking players, as `{id, name, state, players, region}` (on the platform's hub, the hubs), then the network's games started on demand, each the instance table below. With `label`, only that mode's games: `network.instances('4v4v4v4')`. `id` is what `player:connect` takes. Never another network's. It returns nil and why when Minefort did not answer." — [Network](#systems-network)
> "**Events come to the default member's servers only.** Call `network.instances()` once at the start, then keep the list from `on_instance_start`, `on_instance_change` and `on_instance_stop`. An event can be lost. Call `network.instances()` again, once a minute at most, to repair the list." — [Network](#systems-network)
> "with `network.browse`, and its hubs with `network.instances`, and asks the" — [Hub](#systems-hub)
> "for _, h in network.instances() or {} do print(h.name, h.players) end" — [Hub](#systems-hub)

## Used in

> "- `network.start{ member, label, slots, data? }` starts an instance of `member`. It returns `{id, state}` at once, with `state = "starting"`: the instance comes online later. `slots` is the number of players the instance takes. `data` is the pack's own value for the instance, read there with `network.info()`." — [Network](#systems-network)

---

<!-- /ref/network/status/ -->

<a id="ref-network-status"></a>

## network.status

Part of [`network`](#ref-network).

```luau
network.status(options: {open: number, status: string ?, meta: any })
```

Says where this instance is. At most one a second is sent: the first at once, then the last of those that came after.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{open: number , status: string ?, meta: any }` | yes |

## Used in

> "if me and me.id then network.status{ open = math.max(0, me.slots - #players.list()), status = "waiting" } end" — [Network](#systems-network)
> "-- When the round starts: network.status{ open = 0, status = "playing" }" — [Network](#systems-network)

## shop global

Minefort's Gem shop: prompts, ownership and paid delivery.

Part of the [Storage](#systems-storage) article.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`prompt`](#ref-shop-prompt) | Asks Minefort to offer `product` to the player. Returns the request id, or nil when it was not offered. |
| [`owns`](#ref-shop-owns) | Whether the player owns this pass. |
| [`on_paid`](#ref-shop-on_paid) | Called once per paid purchase; returning without an error hands it over. An error leaves it waiting, to be called again later. |
| [`on_declined`](#ref-shop-on_declined) | Called when the player said no or did not answer. |
