---

<!-- /ref/shop/on_paid/ -->

<a id="ref-shop-on_paid"></a>

## shop.on_paid

Part of [`shop`](#ref-shop).

```luau
shop.on_paid(handler: (purchase: ShopPurchase) -> ()) → Connection
```

Called once per paid purchase; returning without an error hands it over. An error leaves it waiting, to be called again later.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handler` | `(purchase: ShopPurchase ) -> ()` | yes |

## Returns

- [`Connection`](#ref-Connection)

## Used in

> "shop.on_paid(function(purchase)" — [Shop](#systems-shop)
> "- `shop.on_paid(fn)` calls `fn({request, player, product})` for each undelivered paid purchase. It runs on the server the player is on: an experience has many servers, and each one hands over only to its own players. A purchase for a player who is not online waits until they join one. At least one active paid handler must complete successfully, and all active paid handlers must succeed, before the purchase is acknowledged. With no paid handler, or if one raises an error, it stays pending. An `on_declined` listener alone never acknowledges a paid purchase. Delivery can repeat after a failure or restart; use `purchase.request` as a durable idempotency key when granting a reward." — [Shop](#systems-shop)
> "- `hub.rent(player, slot, product, experience)` offers a portal of the grounds for Gems, like `shop.prompt`: `product` is one of the hub's rentals, such as `portal_24h`, and `experience` the name `/play` takes of any published experience, which the portal then leads to. It returns a request id, or nil; `shop.on_paid` hands the purchase over. Renting your own portal again adds time, and may leave `experience` out to keep what it shows." — [Hub](#systems-hub)

---

<!-- /ref/AskCount/ -->

<a id="ref-AskCount"></a>

## AskCount type

What one kind of ask has cost this pack, and what every kind has together. An ask is a question the engine puts to a pack with a deadline on it; an answer that does not arrive in time is not used.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`askCount.asks: number`](#ref-AskCount-asks) | Questions the engine put to this pack. |
| [`askCount.answered: number`](#ref-AskCount-answered) | Answers that arrived in time. |
| [`askCount.missed: number`](#ref-AskCount-missed) | Deadlines that passed with no answer. |
| [`askCount.late: number`](#ref-AskCount-late) | Answers that arrived after the engine had acted, and were dropped. |
| [`askCount.skipped: number`](#ref-AskCount-skipped) | Asks never sent, because this kind is switched off for this pack. |
| [`askCount.disabled: boolean`](#ref-AskCount-disabled) | True once the engine has stopped asking this pack this kind at all. |

---

<!-- /ref/BarColor/ -->

<a id="ref-BarColor"></a>

## BarColor type

A boss bar's colour is its own closed set — six the client draws, and anything else is white. It is not an `Ink`: the bar has no hex form.

`"pink"` | `"blue"` | `"red"` | `"green"` | `"yellow"` | `"purple"` | `"white"`

---

<!-- /ref/Billboard/ -->

<a id="ref-Billboard"></a>

## Billboard type

How a display turns toward the viewer: "fixed" never turns, "vertical" turns about the up axis, "horizontal" tips up and down, "center" does both.

`"fixed"` | `"vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | `"center"`

---

## biomeDefinition.like

Part of [`biomeDefinition`](#ref-BiomeDefinition).

The vanilla biome to copy; "plains" when left out.

<!-- /ref/Block/ -->

<a id="ref-Block"></a>

## Block type

One block the game version has, in its own numbers, from `game.block(name)`: hardness, light, fire and material.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`block.name: string`](#ref-Block-name) | The block's canonical name. |
| [`block.behaviour: string ?`](#ref-Block-behaviour) | The rule Citadel runs for it, such as "grass", "flowing", "torch" or "falling"; nil for a block that does nothing on its own. |
| [`block.hardness: number`](#ref-Block-hardness) | Seconds-scale hardness in this version's numbers; below zero is unbreakable. |
| [`block.random_ticks: boolean`](#ref-Block-random_ticks) | Whether the random-tick pass acts on it. |
| [`block.opaque: boolean`](#ref-Block-opaque) | Whether it is an opaque full cube, which is not the material's question. |
| [`block.light: number`](#ref-Block-light) | What it gives off, 0..15, and what a step through it takes away. |
| [`block.light_filter: number`](#ref-Block-light_filter) | What a step through it takes off the light, 0 to 15. |
| [`block.resistance: number ?`](#ref-Block-resistance) | The three the block-update tables own: nil in a game that has none. |
| [`block.flammability: { catches: number, burns_away: number }?`](#ref-Block-flammability) | Fire's two numbers: how readily it catches and how fast it burns away. Nil in a game with no block-update tables. |
| [`block.material: Material ?`](#ref-Block-material) | The jar's Material as five questions; nil in a game with no block-update tables. |
| [`block.drops: boolean ?`](#ref-Block-drops) | The one field a pack writes. Whether a block of this kind that the world breaks by itself leaves its item: true leaves it on a lite world too, false never, nil is the world's default. Reads what this pack set. |

---

<!-- /ref/BlockAmendSpec/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockAmendSpec"></a>

## BlockAmendSpec type

What `game.blocks.amend` takes: **hooks only**.  Every tnt in every world already looks like tnt and is as hard as tnt, so a data column here is refused by name. For a block of your own with different numbers, `game.blocks.define { extends = "tnt" }`.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`on_use`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_use) | Somebody right-clicked it; `held` is the item in hand. Answers "used" or "pass"; a missed deadline passes the click through. |
| [`on_break`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_break) | Something broke it; `by` says what. Answers "none", "table" or a drops list. |
| [`on_step`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_step) | A body (a player, mob, item or other) is standing on it. |
| [`on_tick`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_tick) | A scheduled tick this block asked for came due. |
| [`on_random_tick`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_random_tick) | The random pass landed on it. |
| [`on_place`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_place) | A player put it down. |
| [`on_neighbour`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_neighbour) | A neighbour at `from` changed; `announced` is the block the notifier announced itself as. |
| [`on_trigger`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_trigger) | It was lit, blasted or burnt; `cause` is "ignite", "explosion" or "fire". |
| [`on_power`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_power) | A redstone signal started (`powered` is true) or stopped reaching it. Called once for each, not for every change beside it. |
| [`on_added`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_added) | It has just been stored, whatever stored it. |
| [`on_removed`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_removed) | It has just gone. |

---

<!-- /ref/BlockAmendSpec/on_added/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockAmendSpec-on_added"></a>

<!-- /ref/BlockAt/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockAt"></a>

## BlockAt type

The block a hook was called about.  Reads are fields and acts are methods. The reads are **live** — the world as it is right now — and everything that changes the world is carried out by the engine the moment the hook returns, in the order it was asked for.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`get`](#ref-BlockAt-get) | The block one face away, by name; nil where that chunk is not in memory. |
| [`set`](#ref-BlockAt-set) | Puts another block at this position. |
| [`destroy`](#ref-BlockAt-destroy) | Takes it out, leaving nothing. |
| [`become`](#ref-BlockAt-become) | **The door**: this block stops being a block, and that entity appears. |
| [`drop`](#ref-BlockAt-drop) | A name, or an item table: a pack item keeps its id. |
| [`schedule`](#ref-BlockAt-schedule) | Asks for this block's `on_tick`, `tick_every` seconds from now. |
| [`notify`](#ref-BlockAt-notify) | Tells the six neighbours this block changed. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`blockAt.data: DataView`](#ref-BlockAt-data) | What this block remembers beyond its state; kept with the position, saved with the chunk, and gone when the block goes. Nested writes are tracked; whole-record assignment is supported. Copy before keeping it beyond the hook. |
| [`blockAt.at: Vec3`](#ref-BlockAt-at) | The block's position; a live read. |
| [`blockAt.name: string`](#ref-BlockAt-name) | The block's name with its namespace, such as "rave:crate"; a live read. |
| [`blockAt.room: number`](#ref-BlockAt-room) | Which room the block is in. |
| [`blockAt.state: number`](#ref-BlockAt-state) | Which of this definition's states it is in, counting from 1. Writable, and bounds-checked against the definition's own `looks` list: it *is* the block state, so a crop's stages cost nothing. |
| [`blockAt.facing: Facing ?`](#ref-BlockAt-facing) | A facing block's front: "north", "south", "west", "east"; nil otherwise. Writable. |
| [`blockAt.powered: boolean ?`](#ref-BlockAt-powered) | Whether a redstone signal reaches it: what a lamp asks. A live read; nil where the chunk is not loaded. |

---

<!-- /ref/BlockAt/at/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockAt-at"></a>

Part of [`blockAt`](#ref-BlockAt).

```luau

```

```luau
blockAt.data: DataView
```

What this block remembers beyond its state; kept with the position, saved with the chunk, and gone when the block goes. Nested writes are tracked; whole-record assignment is supported. Copy before keeping it beyond the hook.

## blockAt.state

Part of [`blockAt`](#ref-BlockAt).

```luau
blockAt.state: number
```

Which of this definition's states it is in, counting from 1. Writable, and bounds-checked against the definition's own `looks` list: it *is* the block state, so a crop's stages cost nothing.

<!-- /ref/BlockDef/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockDef"></a>

## BlockDef type

The handle `define` hands back. Equality is identity — two handles are the same block when they name the same block.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`blockDef.name: string`](#ref-BlockDef-name) | Canonical, with the pack's namespace already on it: "rave:crate". |
| [`blockDef.states: number`](#ref-BlockDef-states) | How many states it has; `block.state` counts 1 to this. |
| [`blockDef.item: ItemTable ?`](#ref-BlockDef-item) | The block as an item, when the definition gave it one: `player:give(def.item)`. |

---

<!-- /ref/Blocks/ -->

<a id="ref-Blocks"></a>

## Blocks type

`game.blocks`: defines a pack's own blocks and amends the game's own, at load time.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`define`](#ref-Blocks-define) | Load-time only: a world may already be holding blocks of a definition, so one that arrived later would change the rules under the players standing on it. Define at the top of `main.luau`. |
| [`amend`](#ref-Blocks-amend) | Only the game's own blocks, never another pack's. |

---

<!-- /ref/Blocks/amend/ -->

<a id="ref-Blocks-amend"></a>

## blocks.amend

Part of [`blocks`](#ref-Blocks).

```luau
blocks.amend(block: string, hooks: BlockAmendSpec)
```

Only the game's own blocks, never another pack's.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `block` | `string` | yes |
| `hooks` | [`BlockAmendSpec`](#ref-BlockAmendSpec) | yes |

## Used in

> "game.blocks.amend("tnt", {" — [Custom blocks](#world-custom-blocks)
> "For a block of the game (`game.blocks.amend`) it is kept in memory: after" — [Custom blocks](#world-custom-blocks)

<!-- /ref/Blocks/define/ -->

<a id="ref-Blocks-define"></a>

## blocks.define

Part of [`blocks`](#ref-Blocks).

```luau
blocks.define(spec: BlockSpec) → BlockDef
```

Load-time only: a world may already be holding blocks of a definition, so one that arrived later would change the rules under the players standing on it. Define at the top of `main.luau`.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec` | [`BlockSpec`](#ref-BlockSpec) | yes |

## Returns

- [`BlockDef`](#ref-BlockDef)

## Used in

> "Set `texture` in `game.items.define` and `game.blocks.define` (below). The" — [Packs](#concepts-pack-anatomy)
> "`game.blocks.define` gives a pack its own block:" — [Custom blocks](#world-custom-blocks)
> "local crate = game.blocks.define {" — [Custom blocks](#world-custom-blocks)
> "- Use it for the game's blocks. A block from `game.blocks.define` leaves the" — [Game data](#world-game-data)

---

<!-- /ref/BlockSpec/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockSpec"></a>

## BlockSpec type

What a definition says a block *is*.  Every hook takes `base` as its **last** argument: call it and you extended what is under you, leave it out and you replaced it. `base` is a decision rather than a reentrant call — its effects land when your hook returns, and calling it twice happens once.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`on_use`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_use) | The hooks. Writing one is what asks for it — there is no flag beside `on_random_tick` saying the random pass may land here. |
| [`on_break`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_break) | Something broke it. Answers "none", "table" or a drops list; fails closed to the definition's `drops`. |
| [`on_step`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_step) | A body is standing on it; `body` is `{ id, kind }`. |
| [`on_tick`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_tick) | A scheduled tick this block asked for came due. |
| [`on_random_tick`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_random_tick) | The random pass landed on it. Not the same thing as `on_tick`, which is why it has the longer name. |
| [`on_place`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_place) | A player put it down; `block.data` is empty then, ready to be filled. |
| [`on_neighbour`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_neighbour) | A neighbour changed; `from` is its position and `announced` the block name the notifier announced itself as. |
| [`on_trigger`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_trigger) | It was lit, blasted or burnt; `cause` is "ignite", "explosion" or "fire". |
| [`on_power`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_power) | A redstone signal started (`powered` is true) or stopped reaching it. Called once for each, not for every change beside it. |
| [`on_added`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_added) | It has just been stored, whatever stored it. |
| [`on_removed`](#ref-BlockSpec-on_removed) | It has just gone from the world. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`blockSpec.name: string`](#ref-BlockSpec-name) | Without a namespace. The pack's own is put in front of it, and a colon here is refused: a pack cannot write another pack's name. |
| [`blockSpec.looks: (string \| { string })?`](#ref-BlockSpec-looks) | A block state the client already draws, because a client has never heard of this pack. One name, or one per state in state order. `\|` takes the first this version has: "crimson_planks\|nether_brick". |
| [`blockSpec.hardness: number ?`](#ref-BlockSpec-hardness) | Seconds-scale, as vanilla's hardness is; below zero is unbreakable. |
| [`blockSpec.resistance: number ?`](#ref-BlockSpec-resistance) | What an explosion has to chew through. |
| [`blockSpec.material: { solid: boolean ?, covers: boolean ?, firm: boolean ?, liquid: boolean ?, burns: boolean ?, }?`](#ref-BlockSpec-material) | The jar's Material as five questions: solid, covers (grass under it dies), firm (snow and ice need it), liquid, burns. |
| [`blockSpec.opacity: number ?`](#ref-BlockSpec-opacity) | What a step through it takes off the light; 15 is an opaque cube. |
| [`blockSpec.light: number ?`](#ref-BlockSpec-light) | What it gives off, 0 to 15. |
| [`blockSpec.tick_every: number ?`](#ref-BlockSpec-tick_every) | Seconds between `block:schedule()` and `on_tick`; 0.5 unless you say. |
| [`blockSpec.drops: (Drops \| false)?`](#ref-BlockSpec-drops) | What a break leaves — and, because `on_break` fails closed, what it leaves when this pack is too slow to answer. Never the looks block's. false is nothing, as "none" is. |
| [`blockSpec.item: (ItemTable \| false)?`](#ref-BlockSpec-item) | The block in a hand. Its `id` is set to the block's name, so placing it puts this block down, and a break leaves it unless `drops` says. false is no item, also for a block with a texture. |
| [`blockSpec.texture: (Faces \| { Faces })?`](#ref-BlockSpec-texture) | Its own picture on 1.21.4+: one for every state, or one per state. |
| [`blockSpec.model: (Model \| { Model })?`](#ref-BlockSpec-model) | Its own shape on 1.21.4+, in place of `texture`: a model that stays inside the block, one for every state or one per state. The block collides as its `looks` block does: "rail" is walked through. |
| [`blockSpec.facing: boolean ?`](#ref-BlockSpec-facing) | Turns its front to whoever places it; `block.facing` reads and turns it. |
| [`blockSpec.power: (number \| { [string]: number } \| { number \| { [string]: number } })?`](#ref-BlockSpec-power) | What it gives a redstone circuit, 0 or 15: one number for every face, a table keyed by face (the names `texture` takes), or a list of either with one entry per state. It is the power a block of redstone gives. |
| [`blockSpec.label: Text ?`](#ref-BlockSpec-label) | The name of the item a textured block comes with. |
| [`blockSpec.extends: (BlockRef \| { [string]: any } \| { any })?`](#ref-BlockSpec-extends) | A handle, a game block's name, a plain table of fields and hooks, or a list of those **innermost first**. There is no class and no metatable: fields merge and hooks wrap. |

---

<!-- /ref/BlockSpec/drops/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockSpec-drops"></a>

## blockSpec.drops

Part of [`blockSpec`](#ref-BlockSpec).

```luau
blockSpec.drops: (Drops | false)?
```

What a break leaves — and, because `on_break` fails closed, what it leaves when this pack is too slow to answer. Never the looks block's. false is nothing, as "none" is.

---

<!-- /ref/BlockSpec/extends/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockSpec-extends"></a>

## blockSpec.extends

Part of [`blockSpec`](#ref-BlockSpec).

```luau
blockSpec.extends: (BlockRef | { [string]: any } | { any })?
```

A handle, a game block's name, a plain table of fields and hooks, or a list of those **innermost first**. There is no class and no metatable: fields merge and hooks wrap.

---

<!-- /ref/BlockSpec/facing/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockSpec-facing"></a>

## blockSpec.facing

Part of [`blockSpec`](#ref-BlockSpec).

```luau
blockSpec.facing: boolean ?
```

Turns its front to whoever places it; `block.facing` reads and turns it.

<!-- /ref/BlockSpec/hardness/ -->

## blockSpec.hardness

Part of [`blockSpec`](#ref-BlockSpec).

```luau
blockSpec.hardness: number ?
```

Seconds-scale, as vanilla's hardness is; below zero is unbreakable.

---

<!-- /ref/BlockSpec/item/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockSpec-item"></a>

## blockSpec.item

Part of [`blockSpec`](#ref-BlockSpec).

```luau
blockSpec.item: (ItemTable | false)?
```

The block in a hand. Its `id` is set to the block's name, so placing it puts this block down, and a break leaves it unless `drops` says. false is no item, also for a block with a texture.

---

The name of the item a textured block comes with.

What it gives off, 0 to 15.

<!-- /ref/BlockSpec/looks/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockSpec-looks"></a>

## blockSpec.looks

Part of [`blockSpec`](#ref-BlockSpec).

```luau
blockSpec.looks: (string | { string })?
```

A block state the client already draws, because a client has never heard of this pack. One name, or one per state in state order. `|` takes the first this version has: "crimson_planks|nether_brick".

---

<!-- /ref/BlockSpec/material/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockSpec-material"></a>

## blockSpec.material

Part of [`blockSpec`](#ref-BlockSpec).

```luau
blockSpec.material: { solid: boolean ?, covers: boolean ?, firm: boolean ?, liquid: boolean ?, burns: boolean ?, }?
```

The jar's Material as five questions: solid, covers (grass under it dies), firm (snow and ice need it), liquid, burns.

---

<!-- /ref/BlockSpec/model/ -->

<a id="ref-BlockSpec-model"></a>

## blockSpec.model

Part of [`blockSpec`](#ref-BlockSpec).

```luau
blockSpec.model: (Model | { Model })?
```

Its own shape on 1.21.4+, in place of `texture`: a model that stays inside the block, one for every state or one per state. The block collides as its `looks` block does: "rail" is walked through.

---

Without a namespace. The pack's own is put in front of it, and a colon here is refused: a pack cannot write another pack's name.

<!-- /ref/Body/ -->

<a id="ref-Body"></a>

## Body type

Whatever is standing on one. `kind` is `"mob"` for a cow or a zombie.

`{ id: number, kind: "player"` | `"mob"` | `"item"` | `"other" }`

---

<!-- /ref/BodyRotation/ -->

<a id="ref-BodyRotation"></a>

## BodyRotation type

Degrees: 0 yaw faces south, 90 west; positive pitch tips down. Constructors default missing angles to zero; later writes preserve them.

`{ read yaw: number?, read pitch: number? }`

---

<!-- /ref/Breaker/ -->

<a id="ref-Breaker"></a>

## Breaker type

What took a block out, and with what.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`breaker.cause: "player" \| "fire" \| "explosion" \| "water" \| "support"`](#ref-Breaker-cause) | What took the block out: a player, fire, an explosion, flowing water, or the loss of what held it up ("support"). |
| [`breaker.tool: string ?`](#ref-Breaker-tool) | The item in hand, or nil for a bare hand and for the four causes that have none. |
| [`breaker.creative: boolean`](#ref-Breaker-creative) | Whether a creative player broke it; creative takes the block and leaves nothing. False for the four causes with no player. |

---

<!-- /ref/BrowseEntry/ -->

<a id="ref-BrowseEntry"></a>

## BrowseEntry type

A row of network.browse: a network on the platform's hub, or one of this experience's own servers. `id` is what `player:connect` takes.

`{id: string, name: string?, category: string?, motd: string?, icon: string?, players: number?, maxPlayers: number?, state: string?, region: string?}`

---

<!-- /ref/Budget/ -->

<a id="ref-Budget"></a>

## Budget type

What a pack's tick and event callbacks are allowed per tick, together, and what it did with it. Milliseconds throughout.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`budget.of: number`](#ref-Budget-of) | `budget_ms` in citadel.yml; 2 by default. |
| [`budget.used: number`](#ref-Budget-used) | What the last tick spent. |
| [`budget.peak: number`](#ref-Budget-peak) | The most any tick has spent. |
| [`budget.skipped: number`](#ref-Budget-skipped) | Callbacks not run for want of budget, since the script started. |
| [`budget.dropped: number`](#ref-Budget-dropped) | Ordinary events lost to queue overflow. Joins, leaves, deaths and respawns are retained with their original player sessions. |
| [`budget.slowest: { hook: string, ms: number }?`](#ref-Budget-slowest) | The slowest single callback so far, by short hook name. |
| [`budget.asks: Asks`](#ref-Budget-asks) | The engine's questions to this pack, and what it did with those. |

---

<!-- /ref/Builder/ -->

<a id="ref-Builder"></a>

## Builder type

What `world.build` hands the function it is given. Coordinates are whole blocks of the build's own and may be negative; later writes win.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`block`](#ref-Builder-block) | Sets one block of the build; later writes win. |
| [`box`](#ref-Builder-box) | Inclusive corners, in any order, like `chunk:fill`. |
| [`line`](#ref-Builder-line) | Every block the straight line between the ends passes through. |
| [`part`](#ref-Builder-part) | What `fn` writes is a named part, found by `citadel render --part` and `citadel check` once pasted. Nested calls name "tower/roof". |

---

<a id="ref-Builder-block"></a>


Sets one block of the build; later writes win.

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pos` | [`Vec3`](#ref-Vec3) | yes |
| `block` | `string` | yes |

<!-- /ref/Builder/part/ -->

<a id="ref-Builder-part"></a>

## builder:part

Part of [`Builder`](#ref-Builder).

```luau
builder:part(name: string, fn: () -> ())
```

What `fn` writes is a named part, found by `citadel render --part` and `citadel check` once pasted. Nested calls name "tower/roof".

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes |
| `fn` | `() -> ()` | yes |

## Canvas type

A picture of one or more maps with no frame of its own, from `world.canvas`, for a frame display, a hand or a screen.

[`Picture`](#ref-Picture)

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`view`](#ref-Canvas-view) | The map id of its top-left map, for a `filled_map`. Returns that player's own layer over the canvas, drawn with the same calls; only they see it. |
| [`destroy`](#ref-Canvas-destroy) | Removes the canvas; clients that saw it keep its last picture, and its id is never reused. |

<!-- /ref/Chunk/ -->

<a id="ref-Chunk"></a>

## Chunk type

A 16 by 16 column of blocks, handed to `world.on_generate`, `world.on_populate` and a room's `generate` to fill.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`get`](#ref-Chunk-get) | Chunk X coordinate (16 blocks each). Chunk Z coordinate (16 blocks each). The chunk's lowest corner, inclusive; y runs 0..255 or the game version's height. The chunk's highest corner, inclusive. Returns the block there now, by name; air outside the chunk. |
| [`set`](#ref-Chunk-set) | Sets one block; positions outside the chunk are ignored. |
| [`fill`](#ref-Chunk-fill) | Fills a box of blocks, clipped to the chunk. |
| [`paste`](#ref-Chunk-paste) | Clipped to this chunk; air is skipped unless `air` is true. `part` names the paste for `citadel render --part` and `citadel check`; the build's own `b:part`s are then inside it ("house/roof"). |
| [`get_biome`](#ref-Chunk-get_biome) | Returns the biome of the column at `pos`, by name; `nil` outside the chunk. A biome belongs to a column, so `pos.y` is not read. |
| [`set_biome`](#ref-Chunk-set_biome) | Sets the biome of one column: a vanilla name ("desert") or the name `game.biomes.define` returned. |
| [`fill_biome`](#ref-Chunk-fill_biome) | Sets the biome of every column in a box, clipped to the chunk. |

---

<!-- /ref/Chunk/fill/ -->

<a id="ref-Chunk-fill"></a>

## chunk:fill

Part of [`Chunk`](#ref-Chunk).

```luau
chunk:fill(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, block: string)
```

Fills a box of blocks, clipped to the chunk.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | [`Vec3`](#ref-Vec3) | yes |
| `to` | [`Vec3`](#ref-Vec3) | yes |
| `block` | `string` | yes |

## Used in

> "chunk:fill(" — [Guide: Your first pack](#getting-started-quick-start)
> "`chunk:fill` fills the box between two corners, including both corners." — [Guide: Your first pack](#getting-started-quick-start)
> "chunk:fill(vec3(-3, 64, -3), vec3(3, 64, 3), "quartz_block") -- clipped to the chunk" — [Guide: Parkour, a room each](#guides-guide-parkour-a-room-each)
> "`chunk:fill` with corners outside the chunk is clipped to it, so one line" — [Guide: Parkour, a room each](#guides-guide-parkour-a-room-each)
> "chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 63, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 63, chunk.max.z), "dirt")" — [Guide: Build a cottage](#guides-guide-build-a-cottage)
> "chunk:fill(vec3(chunk.min.x, 64, chunk.min.z), vec3(chunk.max.x, 64, chunk.max.z), "grass_block")" — [Guide: Build a cottage](#guides-guide-build-a-cottage)

<!-- /ref/ColorName/ -->

<a id="ref-ColorName"></a>

## ColorName type

Every colour's name: Minecraft's sixteen, which every client has had since 1.7, six more, and "transparent". `colors` holds the same names.

`"black"` | `"dark_blue"` | `"dark_green"` | `"dark_aqua"` | `"dark_red"` | `"dark_purple"` | `"gold"` | `"gray"` | `"dark_gray"` | `"blue"` | `"green"` | `"aqua"` | `"red"` | `"light_purple"` | `"yellow"` | `"white"` | `"orange"` | `"lime"` | `"cyan"` | `"purple"` | `"magenta"` | `"pink"` | `"transparent"`

| [`commandOpts.help: string ?`](#ref-CommandOpts-help) | The line /help shows after the usage. |
| [`commandOpts.suggest: { [string]: { Suggestion } \| Suggester }?`](#ref-CommandOpts-suggest) | Per argument name: the words to offer, or a function that returns them. |

## Container type

A chest's stacks: `world.container(pos)`. A chest a player has open is theirs until it closes — `take` takes nothing, `put` puts nothing.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`items`](#ref-Container-items) | The filled slots, in order. |
| [`take`](#ref-Container-take) | Up to `count` (1 unless you say) of what matches; how many it took. |
| [`put`](#ref-Container-put) | How many did not fit; 0 when all of it went in. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`container.size: number`](#ref-Container-size) | How many slots the chest has, e.g. 27; 0 once it has gone. |
| [`container.at: Vec3`](#ref-Container-at) | The chest's block position. |

<!-- /ref/DataView/ -->

<a id="ref-DataView"></a>

## DataView type

An attached JSON record/list, with tracked nested writes and generalized iteration. Runtime userdata: use data.copy for ordinary table operations. Roots use string keys; nested lists use contiguous indices starting at 1. Assignment validates the entire value. Hook views expire after their callback batch finishes.

`{ [any]: any }`

<!-- /ref/Display/ -->

<a id="ref-Display"></a>

## Display type

An item, text, block or frame shown in the world, from `world.display`; its place, rotation, scale and look are live.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`animate`](#ref-Display-animate) | Makes one tweened change of place, scale, rotation or text over `duration` seconds (0.5 by default), played by the client. |
| [`move`](#ref-Display-move) | Removes the display. Sets position and optional rotation together. |
| [`destroy`](#ref-Display-destroy) |  |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`display.id: number`](#ref-Display-id) | The raw entity id. `hit.entity` hands back this handle itself, so a pack rarely needs the number. |
| [`display.billboard: Billboard`](#ref-Display-billboard) | Whether it is still present. Read-only. Where it sits; live, every kind. Its yaw, pitch and roll in degrees; live. Pitch 90 lays a text flat on a table. Reads a vec3; write a number for every axis at once. How it turns toward the viewer; text defaults to "center", the other kinds to "fixed". |
| [`display.glow: (Color \| false)?`](#ref-Display-glow) | Its outline colour; nil or false for none. |
| [`display.duration: number`](#ref-Display-duration) | Seconds later changes take to play out on the client (1.19.4 and later); 0 by default. |
| [`display.glide: number`](#ref-Display-glide) | Advanced movement smoothing in seconds (1.20.2+); default 0.1, 0 follows duration. |
| [`display.lead: boolean ?`](#ref-Display-lead) | Advanced: true enables linear prediction. Default false; nil restores it. Normally submit current positions and leave this alone. |
| [`display.item: string ?`](#ref-Display-item) | item kind |
| [`display.canvas: number ?`](#ref-Display-canvas) | Item kind: the canvas shown as a filled map; written as a canvas, read back as its map id. |
| [`display.context: Context ?`](#ref-Display-context) | Item kind: how the item is posed, as in a frame, a hand or on the ground. |
| [`display.text: string ?`](#ref-Display-text) | text kind Reads back the words; takes any text. |
| [`display.color: Color ?`](#ref-Display-color) | The colour of the words that did not pick one. |
| [`display.background: (Color \| false)?`](#ref-Display-background) | Text kind: the colour behind the words; nil or false for none. |
| [`display.line_width: number ?`](#ref-Display-line_width) | Text kind: the width its lines wrap at; 200 by default. |
| [`display.shadow: boolean ?`](#ref-Display-shadow) | Text kind: whether the words have a shadow; false by default. |
| [`display.block: string ?`](#ref-Display-block) | block kind |

---

<!-- /ref/Display/animate/ -->

<a id="ref-Display-animate"></a>

## display:animate

Part of [`Display`](#ref-Display).

```luau
display:animate(opts: { at: Vec3 ?, scale: (Vec3 | number)?, rotation: Orientation ?, text: Text ?, color: Ink ?, background: (Ink | false)?, line_width: number ?, shadow: boolean ?, duration: number ?, })
```

Makes one tweened change of place, scale, rotation or text over `duration` seconds (0.5 by default), played by the client.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opts` | `{ at: Vec3 ?, scale: ( Vec3 \| number )?, rotation: Orientation ?, text: Text ?, color: Ink ?, background: ( Ink \| false )?, line_width: number ?, shadow: boolean ?, duration: number ?, }` | yes |

## Used in

> "Use `display:animate{..., duration = seconds}` for an authored display transition," — [Displays](#ui-displays)

<!-- /ref/Display/background/ -->

<a id="ref-Display-background"></a>

## display.background


Text kind: the colour behind the words; nil or false for none.

<!-- /ref/Display/billboard/ -->

<a id="ref-Display-billboard"></a>

## display.billboard

Part of [`display`](#ref-Display).

```luau
display.billboard: Billboard
```

Whether it is still present. Read-only. Where it sits; live, every kind. Its yaw, pitch and roll in degrees; live. Pitch 90 lays a text flat on a table. Reads a vec3; write a number for every axis at once. How it turns toward the viewer; text defaults to "center", the other kinds to "fixed".

<!-- /ref/Drops/ -->

<a id="ref-Drops"></a>

## Drops type

What a broken block leaves. "table" is whatever the site that broke it would have left — the version's drop table for a player's hands, a roll for a blast, nothing at all for a fire — and "none" is nothing, which is what a pack block leaves unless it says otherwise.

`"none"` | `"table"` | `{ ItemTable }`

---

<!-- /ref/DurableStore/ -->

<a id="ref-DurableStore"></a>

## DurableStore type

Shared durable stores. Calls yield; pcall catches structured errors such as {err = "conflict", version = 3}. One store per experience.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`get`](#ref-DurableStore-get) | Returns a fact's value and its version; version 0 means absent. |
| [`set`](#ref-DurableStore-set) | Writes a fact if its version is still `if_version`, and returns the new version. A mismatch errors with {err = "conflict"}. |
| [`delete`](#ref-DurableStore-delete) | Removes a fact if its version is still `if_version`. |
| [`increment`](#ref-DurableStore-increment) | Adds `by` to a number atomically, starting at zero, and returns the result. Never retry it blindly after a timeout. |
| [`list`](#ref-DurableStore-list) | Returns fact keys with this prefix and the cursor for the next page, or nil at the end. |
| [`blob_get`](#ref-DurableStore-blob_get) | Returns one player's binary blob, or nil, and its version; `owner` is the player's uuid. |
| [`blob_put`](#ref-DurableStore-blob_put) | Writes a player's binary blob if its version is still `if_version`, and returns the new version. At most 32 MiB. |
| [`blob_delete`](#ref-DurableStore-blob_delete) | Deletes a player's blob if its version is still `if_version`. |

---

<!-- /ref/DurableStore/blob_delete/ -->

<a id="ref-DurableStore-blob_delete"></a>


| --- | --- | --- |

<!-- /ref/Easing/ -->

<a id="ref-Easing"></a>

## Easing type

How a tween moves over its duration: "linear" (the default) at one speed, "in" starts slow, "out" ends slow, "in_out" both, "bounce" bounces at the end.

`"linear"` | `"in"` | `"out"` | `"in_out"` | `"bounce"`

---

<!-- /ref/Effect/ -->

<a id="ref-Effect"></a>

## Effect type

A function called for every letter each frame a text shows, handing back how that letter looks; `i` of `n` is the letter's place, `t` is `time.now()`.

`(letter: string, i: number, n: number, t: number) -> LetterStyle?`

---

<!-- /ref/Entities/ -->

<a id="ref-Entities"></a>

## Entities type

`game.entities`: the three verbs over one shape.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`define`](#ref-Entities-define) | Load time only. A definition is a fact about the world. |
| [`amend`](#ref-Entities-amend) | The game's own content only — never another pack's. |
| [`names`](#ref-Entities-names) | Every kind by name: the pack's own and the game's, mob or not. `mob = true` gives the mob kinds only, `mob = false` the rest. |

---

> "game.entities.amend("pig", {" — [Custom entities](#entities-custom-entities)
> "- Profiles run no callbacks. To change gameplay, use `game.entities.amend(name, hooks)` and `game.entities.define(spec)`." — [Custom entities](#entities-custom-entities)

<!-- /ref/EntityAmendOptions/ -->

<a id="ref-EntityAmendOptions"></a>

## EntityAmendOptions type

A pack's hooks on one of the game's own entities. Hooks only: every pig already looks like a pig, so the data columns are refused by name.

`{ priority: number?, replace: boolean? }`

---

<!-- /ref/EntityAmendSpec/ -->

<a id="ref-EntityAmendSpec"></a>

## EntityAmendSpec type

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`on_spawn`](#ref-EntityAmendSpec-on_spawn) | Called when a new entity of this kind spawns; told, never waited on. |
| [`on_load`](#ref-EntityAmendSpec-on_load) | Called for an entity that already existed: a saved chunk loaded it, or a reload rebound it. |
| [`on_steer`](#ref-EntityAmendSpec-on_steer) | Wrapped behavior runs first unless options.replace = true. |
| [`on_tick`](#ref-EntityAmendSpec-on_tick) | Wrapped behavior runs first unless options.replace = true. |
| [`on_damage`](#ref-EntityAmendSpec-on_damage) | Asked when it takes damage; return "ignore" to cancel it. Silence or a missed deadline is "take". |
| [`on_remove`](#ref-EntityAmendSpec-on_remove) | Called when it leaves the world; `why` is "removed", "settled", "killed" or "unloaded". Not called when the pack goes away. |

---

<!-- /ref/EntityDef/ -->

<a id="ref-EntityDef"></a>

## EntityDef type

What `define{}` hands back. Usable anywhere the name is, so an author rarely types the namespace at all.

`{ read name: string, read mob: false }`

---

<!-- /ref/EntityHandle/ -->

<a id="ref-EntityHandle"></a>

## EntityHandle type

A body the world moves: a pack's own entity, a mob, a stack on the ground.  Every read is a fresh look at the world, so a handle to something that has died reads `nil`. Inside a hook the same handle reads the entity as it was at the top of the tick, and its writes land at that hook's own slot.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`play`](#ref-EntityHandle-play) | Model size: reads vec3; write a positive number or equal-axis vec3. Nil without a model. Plays a model entity's animation from the start; on the one already playing, `speed` only changes its speed. |
| [`stop`](#ref-EntityHandle-stop) | Stops a model entity's animation; the parts stay where they are. |
| [`move`](#ref-EntityHandle-move) | Gone on the next tick. Sets position and optional rotation together. |
| [`destroy`](#ref-EntityHandle-destroy) |  |
| [`push`](#ref-EntityHandle-push) | A shove, in blocks a tick, added to what it is already doing. |
| [`settle`](#ref-EntityHandle-settle) | It stops being an entity and is a block again where it stands. No argument: the entity remembers what it was. |
| [`nearby`](#ref-EntityHandle-nearby) | What else is around it, by horizontal distance. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`entityHandle.id: number`](#ref-EntityHandle-id) | Its entity id, the one players.on_click reports in `hit.entity_id`. |
| [`entityHandle.name: string ?`](#ref-EntityHandle-name) | The kind's name: "cow", "rave:rocket". Nil once it is gone. |
| [`entityHandle.alive: boolean`](#ref-EntityHandle-alive) | Whether it is still in the world. A hook only runs for one that is. |
| [`entityHandle.age: number ?`](#ref-EntityHandle-age) | Ticks lived. |
| [`entityHandle.velocity: Vec3 ?`](#ref-EntityHandle-velocity) | Where it is, live; writing it is a teleport. Nil once it is gone. Partial writes preserve other angles; nil after removal. Bodies have no roll. How it is moving, live; writing it is steering by hand. Nil once it is gone. writing it is steering by hand |
| [`entityHandle.on_ground: boolean ?`](#ref-EntityHandle-on_ground) | Whether it stands on something. Nil once it is gone. |
| [`entityHandle.health: number ?`](#ref-EntityHandle-health) | Its health now. Nil once it is gone. |
| [`entityHandle.max_health: number ?`](#ref-EntityHandle-max_health) | The most health its kind gives it. Nil for an entity that is not a mob and once it is gone. Read-only. |
| [`entityHandle.hostile: boolean ?`](#ref-EntityHandle-hostile) | Whether its kind is hostile. Nil once it is gone. |
| [`entityHandle.physics: Physics ?`](#ref-EntityHandle-physics) | Which order of operations moves it: "vehicle", "living", "falling", "item" or "none". |
| [`entityHandle.origin: string ?`](#ref-EntityHandle-origin) | The block it used to be, for anything that arrived through a transition; nil for anything that was never a block. |
| [`entityHandle.data: DataView`](#ref-EntityHandle-data) | A pack-defined entity's attached record. Nested edits write through. Saved with persist = "save". Built-in entities raise an error on access. on_steer/on_tick views expire after the callback batch; copy to keep a snapshot. |
| [`entityHandle.forward: number`](#ref-EntityHandle-forward) | The intent fields: what a body *wants* to do, which is what steering is. Writing one outside `on_steer` lasts until the next decision. |
| [`entityHandle.strafe: number`](#ref-EntityHandle-strafe) | Intent: 1 left, -1 right. A vehicle's seat 1 writes it from the keys every tick. |
| [`entityHandle.jumping: boolean`](#ref-EntityHandle-jumping) | Intent: whether it wants to jump. A vehicle's seat 1 writes it from the keys every tick. |
| [`entityHandle.flying: boolean`](#ref-EntityHandle-flying) | Intent, a living body with can_fly only: true flies (no gravity; forward moves it along its look, pitch included), false falls and walks. Setting it true on another body is an error. |
| [`entityHandle.driver: Player ?`](#ref-EntityHandle-driver) | Whether it is in water now. False for an entity that is not alive. The player supplying driving input from seat 1; nil for an NPC or empty seat. |
| [`entityHandle.paint: { [string]: Ink }`](#ref-EntityHandle-paint) | Every occupant by seat number, including NPCs; nil means empty. Material name to colour; write-only. |

---

Whether it is in water now. False for an entity that is not alive. The player supplying driving input from seat 1; nil for an NPC or empty seat.

---

<!-- /ref/EntityHandle/flying/ -->

<a id="ref-EntityHandle-flying"></a>

## entityHandle.flying

Part of [`entityHandle`](#ref-EntityHandle).

```luau
entityHandle.flying: boolean
```

Intent, a living body with can_fly only: true flies (no gravity; forward moves it along its look, pitch included), false falls and walks. Setting it true on another body is an error.

---

<!-- /ref/EntityHandle/forward/ -->

<a id="ref-EntityHandle-forward"></a>

## entityHandle.forward

Part of [`entityHandle`](#ref-EntityHandle).

```luau
entityHandle.forward: number
```

The intent fields: what a body *wants* to do, which is what steering is. Writing one outside `on_steer` lasts until the next decision.

---

## entityHandle.velocity

Part of [`entityHandle`](#ref-EntityHandle).

```luau
entityHandle.velocity: Vec3 ?
```

Where it is, live; writing it is a teleport. Nil once it is gone. Partial writes preserve other angles; nil after removal. Bodies have no roll. How it is moving, live; writing it is steering by hand. Nil once it is gone. writing it is steering by hand

<!-- /ref/EntityKind/ -->

<a id="ref-EntityKind"></a>

## EntityKind type

One kind the game version has, in its own numbers, from `game.entities.<kind>`: name, size, max_health, speed and drop. A kind that is not a mob (an arrow, a boat, primed TNT; `mob == false`) has `name`, `mob`, `width`, `height` and `physics` only: every other fact is nil for it, and a write to `spawn`, `attacks` or `interact` and a call of `amend` are errors.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`amend`](#ref-EntityKind-amend) | The same as `game.entities.amend(name, hooks)`. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`entityKind.name: string`](#ref-EntityKind-name) | Its modern registry name: "cow". |
| [`entityKind.mob: boolean`](#ref-EntityKind-mob) | Whether the kind is a mob: true for a cow, false for an arrow. |
| [`entityKind.physics: string ?`](#ref-EntityKind-physics) | For a kind that is not a mob, which order of operations moves it: "item", "falling", "vehicle" or "none". Nil for a mob kind. |
| [`entityKind.behaviour: string`](#ref-EntityKind-behaviour) | The name of the behaviour the engine runs for this kind, such as "sheep" or "living". |
| [`entityKind.profile: { [string]: string \| number \| boolean }?`](#ref-EntityKind-profile) | Read-only copy; nil for a specialized behavior without a shared profile. |
| [`entityKind.registry_name: string`](#ref-EntityKind-registry_name) | This version's own registry spelling: "Cow". A dungeon spawner stores this one. |
| [`entityKind.width: number`](#ref-EntityKind-width) | Its width in blocks, in this version's numbers. |
| [`entityKind.height: number`](#ref-EntityKind-height) | Its height in blocks, in this version's numbers. |
| [`entityKind.max_health: number`](#ref-EntityKind-max_health) | The most health one of this kind has, in this version's numbers. `health` on a kind is an error: health is what one entity has now. |
| [`entityKind.speed: number`](#ref-EntityKind-speed) | Blocks a tick at a full walk. |
| [`entityKind.hostile: boolean`](#ref-EntityKind-hostile) | Whether it is hostile. |
| [`entityKind.drop: string ?`](#ref-EntityKind-drop) | The item its death leaves behind, such as "leather"; nil for none. |
| [`entityKind.spawn: boolean ?`](#ref-EntityKind-spawn) | The one writable field. `true`: the kind is in this world as the game defines it: it spawns by the game's own rule, also on a `mode: lite` world, and `attacks` and `interact` are on for it unless a pack sets them; an error on a 1.8.9 world with no biomes, where nothing would spawn it. `false`: the kind never spawns by itself in this world; spawner blocks, `world.spawn`, `/summon` and breeding still make it. `nil`: the pack says nothing and the world's default applies: no natural spawning on a `mode: lite` world and in a room from `rooms.create`, the game's own rule on a `mode: full` world and after `world.rules{ survival = true }`. A table is an error today. Reads what this pack set (`true`, `false` or nil), not the game's own rule. The value is this room's (`room.game.entities.cow.spawn`) and this pack's: a `false` of any pack wins. Every write is an error on a game with no natural spawning (a0.1.0 to a0.1.3). |
| [`entityKind.attacks: boolean ?`](#ref-EntityKind-attacks) | Whether its hits hurt players. `nil`: on for a kind with `spawn = true`, else the room's `damage` rule. The kind's own setting is stronger than the room's rule. It covers the kind's own hit, its arrow (also after the shooter died) and a creeper's blast. `false` stops the damage to players only: a blast still breaks blocks. |
| [`entityKind.interact: boolean ?`](#ref-EntityKind-interact) | Whether a player's right click on it has the game's effect (milk, a saddle). `nil`: on for a kind with `spawn = true`, else the room's `survival`. `true` is an error on 1.8.9, which has no right click on a mob. |

---


The same as `game.entities.amend(name, hooks)`.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `hooks` | [`EntityAmendSpec`](#ref-EntityAmendSpec) | yes |
| `options` | [`EntityAmendOptions`](#ref-EntityAmendOptions) | no |

---

<!-- /ref/EntityKind/attacks/ -->

<a id="ref-EntityKind-attacks"></a>

## entityKind.attacks

Part of [`entityKind`](#ref-EntityKind).

```luau
entityKind.attacks: boolean ?
```

Whether its hits hurt players. `nil`: on for a kind with `spawn = true`, else the room's `damage` rule. The kind's own setting is stronger than the room's rule. It covers the kind's own hit, its arrow (also after the shooter died) and a creeper's blast. `false` stops the damage to players only: a blast still breaks blocks.

---

<!-- /ref/EntityKind/spawn/ -->

<a id="ref-EntityKind-spawn"></a>

## entityKind.spawn

Part of [`entityKind`](#ref-EntityKind).

```luau
entityKind.spawn: boolean ?
```

The one writable field. `true`: the kind is in this world as the game defines it: it spawns by the game's own rule, also on a `mode: lite` world, and `attacks` and `interact` are on for it unless a pack sets them; an error on a 1.8.9 world with no biomes, where nothing would spawn it. `false`: the kind never spawns by itself in this world; spawner blocks, `world.spawn`, `/summon` and breeding still make it. `nil`: the pack says nothing and the world's default applies: no natural spawning on a `mode: lite` world and in a room from `rooms.create`, the game's own rule on a `mode: full` world and after `world.rules{ survival = true }`. A table is an error today. Reads what this pack set (`true`, `false` or nil), not the game's own rule. The value is this room's (`room.game.entities.cow.spawn`) and this pack's: a `false` of any pack wins. Every write is an error on a game with no natural spawning (a0.1.0 to a0.1.3).

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec"></a>

## EntitySpec type

A kind of entity a pack makes up. `base` is the last argument of every hook: call it and you extended, don't and you replaced.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`on_spawn`](#ref-EntitySpec-on_spawn) | Told when one of this kind is spawned; nothing waits on it and its answer is not read. |
| [`on_load`](#ref-EntitySpec-on_load) | Told when one that already existed comes back: a saved chunk loaded it or a reload rebound it. |
| [`on_steer`](#ref-EntitySpec-on_steer) | Runs before the physics each tick to decide where it goes; call `base(e)` to extend, leave it out to replace. |
| [`on_tick`](#ref-EntitySpec-on_tick) | Runs after the physics each tick to react to where it ended up; call `base(e)` to extend. |
| [`on_think`](#ref-EntitySpec-on_think) | define only. The brain: one call for all due bodies of the kind, with their numbers in columns. The engine never waits for it; the answer lands on the next tick it is there, and is never dropped. |
| [`on_damage`](#ref-EntitySpec-on_damage) | Asked when a player hits it: answer "take" or "ignore". Nil or a missed deadline is "take". `by` is the player who hit. |
| [`on_remove`](#ref-EntitySpec-on_remove) | Told when it goes; `why` is "removed", "settled", "killed" or "unloaded". Not called when the pack goes away. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`entitySpec.name: string`](#ref-EntitySpec-name) | Your own word for the kind, lower case, digits and underscores; the pack's namespace is added for you ("rocket" is "rave:rocket"). |
| [`entitySpec.looks: Looks \| Model`](#ref-EntitySpec-looks) | A shape the client draws, or a model from models.new. |
| [`entitySpec.physics: Physics ?`](#ref-EntitySpec-physics) | Which order of operations moves it: "living", "falling", "item", "none", or "vehicle" to drive by seat 1's keys. |
| [`entitySpec.size: (number \| { number })?`](#ref-EntitySpec-size) | One number, or { width, height }. An entity is as deep as it is wide. |
| [`entitySpec.persist: Persist ?`](#ref-EntitySpec-persist) | "save" brings it back with its chunk, `data` and all; "despawn", the default, is gone when the chunk goes. |
| [`entitySpec.seats: { Vec3 }?`](#ref-EntitySpec-seats) | A model's: where riders sit (model units, seat 1 drives), its size, and what a client older than 1.21.4 sees. |
| [`entitySpec.scale: number ?`](#ref-EntitySpec-scale) | A model's size; 1 by default. |
| [`entitySpec.fallback: string ?`](#ref-EntitySpec-fallback) | What a client older than 1.21.4 sees in place of the model, such as "minecart". |
| [`entitySpec.speed: number ?`](#ref-EntitySpec-speed) | How fast it goes, in blocks a second. A vehicle's top speed; a living body's walk at forward = 1, the game's own mob walk by default. |
| [`entitySpec.max_health: number ?`](#ref-EntitySpec-max_health) | physics = "living" only: the most health it has, and what it starts with. 1 to 1024; 20 by default. |
| [`entitySpec.drops: ({ { [string]: any } } \| false)?`](#ref-EntitySpec-drops) | physics = "living" only: what it leaves when it dies. Each row is { item = "stick", count = 2 }, count = { least, most } for a random count, chance = 0.05 for a row that comes from one death in twenty, or a pack item. false or nil: nothing. |
| [`entitySpec.sounds: ({ hurt: string ?, death: string ?, ambient: string ? } \| false)?`](#ref-EntitySpec-sounds) | physics = "living" only: sound names for its hurt, its death and its idle sound, vanilla or "<pack>.<file>". false or nil: silent. |
| [`entitySpec.can_fly: boolean ?`](#ref-EntitySpec-can_fly) | physics = "living" only: it may fly when its pack sets e.flying = true, and it takes no fall damage. |
| [`entitySpec.turn: number ?`](#ref-EntitySpec-turn) | physics = "vehicle" only: degrees a second it turns at speed; 90 by default. |
| [`entitySpec.accel: number ?`](#ref-EntitySpec-accel) | physics = "vehicle" only: seconds from standing to top speed; 1 by default. |
| [`entitySpec.step: number ?`](#ref-EntitySpec-step) | physics = "vehicle" only: blocks it climbs without a jump; 1 by default. |
| [`entitySpec.think_every: number ?`](#ref-EntitySpec-think_every) | define only. Seconds between two thinks of one body; one tick (0.05) by default, at most 60. The engine spreads the bodies over the ticks. |

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/accel/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-accel"></a>

physics = "vehicle" only: seconds from standing to top speed; 1 by default.

## entitySpec.can_fly

physics = "living" only: it may fly when its pack sets e.flying = true, and it takes no fall damage.

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/drops/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-drops"></a>

## entitySpec.drops

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.drops: ({ { [string]: any } } | false)?
```

physics = "living" only: what it leaves when it dies. Each row is { item = "stick", count = 2 }, count = { least, most } for a random count, chance = 0.05 for a row that comes from one death in twenty, or a pack item. false or nil: nothing.

- `?`

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/on_steer/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-on_steer"></a>

## entitySpec.on_steer

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.on_steer((e: EntityHandle, base: () -> ()) -> ()) → ?
```

Runs before the physics each tick to decide where it goes; call `base(e)` to extend, leave it out to replace.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(e` | `EntityHandle , base: () -> ()) -> ()` | yes |

## Returns

- `?`

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/on_think/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-on_think"></a>

## entitySpec.on_think

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.on_think((b: Think) -> ()) → ?
```

define only. The brain: one call for all due bodies of the kind, with their numbers in columns. The engine never waits for it; the answer lands on the next tick it is there, and is never dropped.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(b` | `Think ) -> ()` | yes |

## Returns

- `?`

---

```luau
entitySpec.on_tick((e: EntityHandle, base: () -> ()) -> ()) → ?
```

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/persist/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-persist"></a>

## entitySpec.persist

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.persist: Persist ?
```

"save" brings it back with its chunk, `data` and all; "despawn", the default, is gone when the chunk goes.

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/physics/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-physics"></a>

## entitySpec.physics

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.physics: Physics ?
```

Which order of operations moves it: "living", "falling", "item", "none", or "vehicle" to drive by seat 1's keys.

---

## entitySpec.scale

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.scale: number ?
```

A model's size; 1 by default.

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/seats/ -->

## entitySpec.seats

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.seats: { Vec3 }?
```

A model's: where riders sit (model units, seat 1 drives), its size, and what a client older than 1.21.4 sees.

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/size/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-size"></a>

## entitySpec.size

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.size: (number | { number })?
```

One number, or { width, height }. An entity is as deep as it is wide.

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/sounds/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-sounds"></a>

## entitySpec.sounds

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.sounds: ({ hurt: string ?, death: string ?, ambient: string ? } | false)?
```

physics = "living" only: sound names for its hurt, its death and its idle sound, vanilla or "<pack>.<file>". false or nil: silent.

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/speed/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-speed"></a>

## entitySpec.speed

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.speed: number ?
```

How fast it goes, in blocks a second. A vehicle's top speed; a living body's walk at forward = 1, the game's own mob walk by default.

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/step/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-step"></a>

## entitySpec.step

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.step: number ?
```

physics = "vehicle" only: blocks it climbs without a jump; 1 by default.

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/think_every/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-think_every"></a>

## entitySpec.think_every

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.think_every: number ?
```

define only. Seconds between two thinks of one body; one tick (0.05) by default, at most 60. The engine spreads the bodies over the ticks.

---

<!-- /ref/EntitySpec/turn/ -->

<a id="ref-EntitySpec-turn"></a>

## entitySpec.turn

Part of [`entitySpec`](#ref-EntitySpec).

```luau
entitySpec.turn: number ?
```

physics = "vehicle" only: degrees a second it turns at speed; 90 by default.

---

<!-- /ref/Face/ -->

<a id="ref-Face"></a>

## Face type

One of a block's six faces: up, down, north, south, west or east, as `hit.face` and `world.raycast` report it.

`"up"` | `"down"` | `"north"` | `"south"` | `"west"` | `"east"`

---

<!-- /ref/Faces/ -->

<a id="ref-Faces"></a>

## Faces type

A block's faces: one picture, or `all`, `side`, `top`, `bottom`, `front`, `back`, or a face by name.

[`TextureRef`](#ref-TextureRef) | ``

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`faces.all: TextureRef ?, side: TextureRef ?, top: TextureRef ?, bottom: TextureRef ?`](#ref-Faces-all) | `all` is one picture for all six faces, `side` for the four sides (`all` if left out), `top` and `bottom` the ends. |
| [`faces.front: TextureRef ?, back: TextureRef ?`](#ref-Faces-front) | `front` is the side a facing block faces and `back` the other; a face left out is `side`. |
| [`faces.down: TextureRef ?, up: TextureRef ?, north: TextureRef ?, south: TextureRef ?, west: TextureRef ?, east: TextureRef ?`](#ref-Faces-down) | One face by its name; a face left out is `side`. |

---

<!-- /ref/Faces/all/ -->

<a id="ref-Faces-all"></a>

## faces.all

Part of [`faces`](#ref-Faces).

```luau
faces.all: TextureRef ?, side: TextureRef ?, top: TextureRef ?, bottom: TextureRef ?
```

`all` is one picture for all six faces, `side` for the four sides (`all` if left out), `top` and `bottom` the ends.

---

<!-- /ref/Faces/down/ -->

<a id="ref-Faces-down"></a>

## faces.down

One face by its name; a face left out is `side`.

<!-- /ref/Faces/front/ -->

Part of [`faces`](#ref-Faces).

```luau
faces.front: TextureRef ?, back: TextureRef ?
```

`front` is the side a facing block faces and `back` the other; a face left out is `side`.

---

<!-- /ref/Facing/ -->

<a id="ref-Facing"></a>

## Facing type

One of the four sides: north, south, west or east; a facing block's front, or the side a screen faces.

`"north"` | `"south"` | `"west"` | `"east"`

---

<!-- /ref/Feature/ -->

<a id="ref-Feature"></a>

## Feature type

What a client is able to show. Ask this instead of comparing versions: a script never sees a version number.

`"bossbar"` | `"potion_color"` | `"floor_frame"` | `"light"` | `"hex_color"` | `"glow_frame"` | `"display"` | `"hitbox"` | `"model"` | `"layout"` | `"dialog"` | `"overlay"` | `"resource_pack"`

---

<!-- /ref/Field/ -->

<a id="ref-Field"></a>

## Field type

A number at every block, as a recipe the engine works out. Sums (`+ - * / ^` and unary minus) and the methods make new fields; a plain number is a field too. A field above 0.5 is "true" where a rule asks a question.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`abs`](#ref-Field-abs) |  |
| [`floor`](#ref-Field-floor) |  |
| [`sqrt`](#ref-Field-sqrt) |  |
| [`min`](#ref-Field-min) |  |
| [`max`](#ref-Field-max) |  |
| [`gt`](#ref-Field-gt) | 1 where this is the larger, else 0. |
| [`lt`](#ref-Field-lt) | 1 where this is the smaller, else 0. |
| [`clamp`](#ref-Field-clamp) |  |
| [`smooth`](#ref-Field-smooth) | 0 at `from`, 1 at `to`, smooth between. `from` may be the larger. |
| [`curve`](#ref-Field-curve) | Straight lines through `{ { input, output }, ... }`, inputs rising. |
| [`at`](#ref-Field-at) | This field read `dx, dy, dz` blocks away: `fields.water:at(1, 0, 0)` is the water east of here. |

---

<!-- /ref/FixedCamera/ -->

<a id="ref-FixedCamera"></a>

## FixedCamera type

Camera modes expose only the fields they use. Values shared across players update all their views. A removed target reads nil and ends the active view.

---

<!-- /ref/FluidRule/ -->

<a id="ref-FluidRule"></a>

## FluidRule type

The carved air under `below` becomes `block` (a lake, lava): the first rule that holds at each block. Never the open sky over the land.

`{ block: string, below: number, biome: string?, when: (Field` | `number)? }`

<!-- /ref/GeneratorRules/ -->

<a id="ref-GeneratorRules"></a>

## GeneratorRules type

What `world.generate` takes. Without `height` and `density`, the rules add to the land the game's own terrain made.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`generatorRules.height: (Field \| number)?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-height) | The y of the surface. |
| [`generatorRules.density: Field ?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-density) | Solid where this is above 0, for caves, overhangs and land in the air. |
| [`generatorRules.sea: number ?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-sea) | Water fills the open air up to this y. |
| [`generatorRules.fluid: string ?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-fluid) |  |
| [`generatorRules.floor: string ?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-floor) | The block at y 0; "bedrock" for a land of its own. |
| [`generatorRules.biomes: { { [number]: string, when: (Field \| number)? } }?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-biomes) | `{ "desert", when = field }`: the first that holds names the column's biome; one with no `when` is for the rest. |
| [`generatorRules.rock: { GroundRule }?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-rock) | The body of the land, under the ground rules. |
| [`generatorRules.surface: { GroundRule }?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-surface) |  |
| [`generatorRules.plants: { PlantRule }?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-plants) |  |
| [`generatorRules.things: { ThingGrid }?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-things) |  |
| [`generatorRules.fluids: { FluidRule }?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-fluids) | What fills the caves: needs `density` or `carvers`. |
| [`generatorRules.carvers: { "caves" \| "ravines" }?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-carvers) | The game version's own carvers, with the world seed, after the land and before the cave rules: "caves" (every version), "ravines" (b1.8 and later). Needs `height` or `density`. |
| [`generatorRules.structures: { "mineshaft" \| "dungeon" }?`](#ref-GeneratorRules-structures) | The game version's own structures, with spawners and loot: "mineshaft", "dungeon" (1.7 to 1.12). Needs `height` or `density`. |

---

<!-- /ref/GroundRule/ -->

## GroundRule type

A layer of ground: `block` for the top `depth` blocks (1) of a surface. The first rule that holds wins.

`{ block: BlockPick, biome: string?, when: (Field` | `number)?, depth: number? }`

<!-- /ref/Hit/ -->

<a id="ref-Hit"></a>

## Hit type

What `players.on_click` hands its callback: the button, the slot, and the player, entity, block and face the click met.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`hit.button: "left" \| "right"`](#ref-Hit-button) | "left" is an attack or swing, "right" is an interact or use. |
| [`hit.slot: number`](#ref-Hit-slot) | The hotbar slot in hand, 1..9. |
| [`hit.player: Player ?`](#ref-Hit-player) | Another player, when that is what was clicked. |
| [`hit.entity: (Display \| Hitbox \| Npc \| Puppet)?`](#ref-Hit-entity) | The thing clicked, as the handle the script holds for it. |
| [`hit.entity_id: number ?`](#ref-Hit-entity_id) | Its raw entity id, which is all there is for something the engine made itself, such as one of a screen's own frames. |
| [`hit.block: Vec3 ?`](#ref-Hit-block) | The block, when the click hit one. |
| [`hit.face: Face ?`](#ref-Hit-face) | The face of the block that was clicked. |

---

<a id="ref-Hit-block"></a>

## hit.block

Part of [`hit`](#ref-Hit).

```luau
hit.block: Vec3 ?
```

The block, when the click hit one.

> "--   hit.block  = vec3?                 the block, when the click hit one" — [Input](#players-movement)

<!-- /ref/Hit/button/ -->

<a id="ref-Hit-button"></a>

## hit.button

Part of [`hit`](#ref-Hit).

```luau
hit.button: "left" | "right"
```

"left" is an attack or swing, "right" is an interact or use.

## Used in

> "if hit.slot ~= 1 or hit.button ~= "right" then" — [Scoreboard with a button](#guides-guide-scoreboard-with-a-button)
> "--   hit.button = "left" \| "right"      left is attack / swing, right is interact / use" — [Input](#players-movement)
> "if hit.button == "left" and hit.player then" — [Room rules](#world-world-state)

<!-- /ref/Hit/player/ -->

<a id="ref-Hit-player"></a>

## hit.player

Part of [`hit`](#ref-Hit).

```luau
hit.player: Player ?
```

Another player, when that is what was clicked.

## Used in

> "--   hit.player = player?               another player, when that is what was clicked: a hit in a game" — [Input](#players-movement)
> "happens next, and `hit.player` in `players.on_click` for one player hitting" — [Room rules](#world-world-state)
> "if hit.button == "left" and hit.player then" — [Room rules](#world-world-state)

---

<!-- /ref/Hit/slot/ -->

<a id="ref-Hit-slot"></a>

## hit.slot

Part of [`hit`](#ref-Hit).

```luau
hit.slot: number
```

The hotbar slot in hand, 1..9.

## Used in

> "if hit.slot ~= 1 or hit.button ~= "right" then" — [Scoreboard with a button](#guides-guide-scoreboard-with-a-button)
> "- A click while holding a slot fires `players.on_click` with `hit.slot`" — [Hotbar menus](#ui-menus)
> "hit.slot                             -- on every players.on_click, 1..9" — [Hotbar menus](#ui-menus)

## Hitbox type

An invisible box a player can click, and a wall when solid, from `world.hitbox` (1.19.4 and later).

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`destroy`](#ref-Hitbox-destroy) | Removes the hitbox, and its wall when solid. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`hitbox.id: number`](#ref-Hitbox-id) | Its entity id, what `players.on_click` reports in `hit.entity_id`. |
| [`hitbox.at: Vec3`](#ref-Hitbox-at) | Its bottom centre; write it to move the hitbox, and its wall when solid. |

<!-- /ref/HttpResponse/ -->

<a id="ref-HttpResponse"></a>

## HttpResponse type

What `http.get` returns. A failed request is not an error: read `ok`.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`json`](#ref-HttpResponse-json) | The body as a table; an error when it is not JSON. |
| [`image`](#ref-HttpResponse-image) | A PNG body: `pixels` is 4 bytes (RGBA) a pixel, row by row from the top. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`httpResponse.ok: boolean`](#ref-HttpResponse-ok) | True for a 2xx status. |
| [`httpResponse.status: number`](#ref-HttpResponse-status) | The HTTP status; 0 when no answer came. |
| [`httpResponse.error: string ?`](#ref-HttpResponse-error) | Why no answer came, or nil. |
| [`httpResponse.body: string`](#ref-HttpResponse-body) | The answer as bytes. |
| [`httpResponse.headers: {[string]: string}`](#ref-HttpResponse-headers) | The answer's headers, names in lower case. |

---

<!-- /ref/HttpResponse/body/ -->

<a id="ref-HttpResponse-body"></a>

## httpResponse.body

Part of [`httpResponse`](#ref-HttpResponse).

```luau
httpResponse.body: string
```

The answer as bytes.

---

<!-- /ref/HttpResponse/error/ -->

<a id="ref-HttpResponse-error"></a>

## httpResponse.error

Part of [`httpResponse`](#ref-HttpResponse).

```luau
httpResponse.error: string ?
```

Why no answer came, or nil.

---

<!-- /ref/HttpResponse/headers/ -->

<a id="ref-HttpResponse-headers"></a>

## httpResponse.headers

Part of [`httpResponse`](#ref-HttpResponse).

```luau
httpResponse.headers: {[string]: string }
```

The answer's headers, names in lower case.

---

<!-- /ref/HttpResponse/image/ -->

<a id="ref-HttpResponse-image"></a>

## httpResponse:image

Part of [`HttpResponse`](#ref-HttpResponse).

```luau
httpResponse:image() → {width: number, height: number, pixels: buffer}
```

A PNG body: `pixels` is 4 bytes (RGBA) a pixel, row by row from the top.

## Returns

- `{width: number , height: number , pixels: buffer}`

---

<!-- /ref/HttpResponse/json/ -->

<a id="ref-HttpResponse-json"></a>

## httpResponse:json

Part of [`HttpResponse`](#ref-HttpResponse).

```luau
httpResponse:json() → any
```

The body as a table; an error when it is not JSON.

## Returns

- `any`

---

<a id="ref-HttpResponse-ok"></a>

## httpResponse.ok

Part of [`httpResponse`](#ref-HttpResponse).

```luau
httpResponse.ok: boolean
```

True for a 2xx status.

```luau
httpResponse.status: number
```

The HTTP status; 0 when no answer came.

<!-- /ref/Hud/ -->

<a id="ref-Hud"></a>

## Hud type

A layout on one player's screen, from `player.ui.show`. `hud.<id>` is the item with that id.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`set`](#ref-Hud-set) | A value per id: a number is a fill, a string a label's words, true or false whether it shows. An unknown id is an error that lists the ids. |
| [`destroy`](#ref-Hud-destroy) | Takes it off the player's screen. |
| [`on_hover`](#ref-Hud-on_hover) |  |
| [`on_click`](#ref-Hud-on_click) |  |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`hud.hover: string ?`](#ref-Hud-hover) | With `cursor = true`: the id under the pointer, and what fires when it changes and on a click. |
| [`hud.cursor: { x: number, y: number }?`](#ref-Hud-cursor) | Where the pointer is, in the layout's pixels from its top left. |

---

<!-- /ref/Ink/ -->

<a id="ref-Ink"></a>

## Ink type

Anywhere a colour is asked for, every spelling works: a `color` value, a name, or hex ("#ff8800"). A name nobody has is an error that says the nearest. A client from 1.16 gets the exact tone in text and an older one the nearest name it has.

[`Color`](#ref-Color) | [`ColorName`](#ref-ColorName) | `string`

---

<!-- /ref/InventorySlot/ -->

<a id="ref-InventorySlot"></a>

## InventorySlot type

A stack as a script reads it. `id` is there for a pack item, `damage` for a worn tool.

`{ item: string, count: number, id: string?, damage: number? }`

---

<!-- /ref/Item/ -->

<a id="ref-Item"></a>

## Item type

An item the game version has, from `game.item(name)`: its name and stack size.

`{ name: string, stack_size: number }`

---

<!-- /ref/ItemMatch/ -->

<a id="ref-ItemMatch"></a>

## ItemMatch type

An item to find — `take`, `count`, a recipe's ingredient. A name is the plain item and never a pack item made of it; a table matches the fields it names.

`string` | `{ id: string?, item: string? }`

---

<!-- /ref/ItemMeta/ -->

<a id="ref-ItemMeta"></a>

## ItemMeta type

The extras an item table may carry: count, name, lore, colours, glint, a canvas map, a pack item id, wear, a 1.21.4+ model and a head's skin.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`itemMeta.count: number ?`](#ref-ItemMeta-count) | How many in the stack; 1 by default. |
| [`itemMeta.name: Text ?`](#ref-ItemMeta-name) | Never italic unless it says so. |
| [`itemMeta.lore: ({ Text } \| Text)?`](#ref-ItemMeta-lore) | One line or a list of lines, grey unless they say otherwise. |
| [`itemMeta.color: Color ?`](#ref-ItemMeta-color) | A potion's liquid colour; 1.11 and later. |
| [`itemMeta.dye: Color ?`](#ref-ItemMeta-dye) | Leather armour's colour. |
| [`itemMeta.glint: boolean ?`](#ref-ItemMeta-glint) | The enchanted shine, with no enchantment. |
| [`itemMeta.canvas: Canvas ?`](#ref-ItemMeta-canvas) | A filled map of that canvas: what the item *is*, so `item` may be left out. Everywhere an item is taken — a hand, a hotbar slot, a display. |
| [`itemMeta.id: string ?`](#ref-ItemMeta-id) | A pack's own item: a brick with `id = "copper_ingot"` is a copper ingot, kept under the pack's name and known by it everywhere it goes. |
| [`itemMeta.damage: number ?`](#ref-ItemMeta-damage) | The wear a tool has taken; 0 is new. |
| [`itemMeta.model: string ?`](#ref-ItemMeta-model) | The item model a 1.21.4+ client draws: `assets/<pack>/items/<model>.json`. |
| [`itemMeta.skin: (string \| { value: string, signature: string ? })?`](#ref-ItemMeta-skin) | The face a "player_head" item shows: a player's name, or the raw `textures` property. On any other item it is an error. |

---

<!-- /ref/ItemMeta/canvas/ -->

<a id="ref-ItemMeta-canvas"></a>

Part of [`itemMeta`](#ref-ItemMeta).

```luau
itemMeta.canvas: Canvas ?
```

A filled map of that canvas: what the item *is*, so `item` may be left out. Everywhere an item is taken — a hand, a hotbar slot, a display.

## items.define

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |

## LayoutNode type

A piece of a layout's tree: what `ui.box`, `ui.image`, `ui.label`, `ui.row`, `ui.column` and `ui.stack` hand back. See "Layouts".

`{ read _layout_node: true }`

## LetterStyle type

What an effect hands back for one letter; `text` shows something else in its place ("" hides it).

`{ color: Ink?, bold: boolean?, italic: boolean?, underline: boolean?, strike: boolean?, text: string? }`

<!-- /ref/LightSource/ -->

## LightSource type

One spot of light no block makes, for `world.light`: a position and a level from 1 to 15.

`{ at: Vec3, level: number? }`

---

<!-- /ref/Looks/ -->

<a id="ref-Looks"></a>

## Looks type

What a client is told a pack's entity is: a shape it already draws. The two table forms carry a payload — the block a falling block shows, the stack an item shows.

`string` | `{ entity: string, block: string }` | `{ entity: string, item: string }`

## Material type

A block's material as five yes-or-no questions, from `block.material`: solid, covers, firm, liquid and burns.

## Fields

| --- | --- |
| [`material.solid: boolean`](#ref-Material-solid) | Whether the jar's Material counts as solid. |
| [`material.covers: boolean`](#ref-Material-covers) | Grass under it dies. |
| [`material.firm: boolean`](#ref-Material-firm) | Snow and ice need it beneath them. |
| [`material.liquid: boolean`](#ref-Material-liquid) | Whether the jar's Material is a liquid. |
| [`material.burns: boolean`](#ref-Material-burns) | Whether the jar's Material burns. |

<!-- /ref/Menu/ -->

<a id="ref-Menu"></a>

## Menu type

An open menu, from `player.ui.menu`.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`destroy`](#ref-Menu-destroy) | Takes it down and forgets its callbacks. A Bedrock form cannot be taken back: it stays until the player answers, and the answer then lands nowhere. |
| [`update`](#ref-Menu-update) | New pictures in place, the menu left open: a bar that fills, a count that changes. `on_pick` still answers by position. `false` once the player has put it away; a Bedrock form keeps what it showed. |

---

<!-- /ref/Menu/destroy/ -->

<a id="ref-Menu-destroy"></a>

## menu:destroy

Part of [`Menu`](#ref-Menu).

```luau
menu:destroy()
```

Takes it down and forgets its callbacks. A Bedrock form cannot be taken back: it stays until the player answers, and the answer then lands nowhere.

## Used in

> "- `menu:destroy()` and a Bedrock pick do not fire `on_close`." — [Menus](#ui-menus)

---

<!-- /ref/Menu/update/ -->

<a id="ref-Menu-update"></a>

## menu:update

Part of [`Menu`](#ref-Menu).

```luau
menu:update(items: { ItemSpec }) → boolean
```

New pictures in place, the menu left open: a bar that fills, a count that changes. `on_pick` still answers by position. `false` once the player has put it away; a Bedrock form keeps what it showed.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `{ ItemSpec }` | yes |

## Returns

- `boolean`

## Used in

> "- `menu:update` returns `false` after the player closes the menu. Picks still answer by position. A Bedrock form keeps its first items." — [Menus](#ui-menus)
