<!-- /ref/ModelBuild/ -->

<a id="ref-ModelBuild"></a>

## ModelBuild type

What `models.new` hands its build function: makes the model's materials, textures, parts and animations.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`material`](#ref-ModelBuild-material) | Makes a named colour a display may repaint; `grain` (0 to 1) darkens pixels into four tones, `alpha` below 1 is glass. |
| [`texture`](#ref-ModelBuild-texture) | Makes a pixel picture for one face; with `tint`, drawn in greys and coloured by that material. With `scroll`, it moves by itself on a block drawn from the model, `speed` texels a tick (1, 2, 3, or 0.5, 0.25). |
| [`part`](#ref-ModelBuild-part) | Makes a named child part of the root that turns around its `pivot`, the model's origin unless given. |
| [`animation`](#ref-ModelBuild-animation) | `{ length = seconds, loop = false, <part name> = { rotation = { [t] = is both named fields and part names, so this one is open. |

---

<!-- /ref/ModelBuild/animation/ -->

<a id="ref-ModelBuild-animation"></a>

## modelBuild:animation

Part of [`ModelBuild`](#ref-ModelBuild).

```luau
modelBuild:animation(name: string, opts: { [string]: any })
```

`{ length = seconds, loop = false, <part name> = { rotation = { [t] = is both named fields and part names, so this one is open.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes |
| `opts` | `{ [ string ]: any }` | yes |

---

<!-- /ref/ModelBuild/material/ -->

<a id="ref-ModelBuild-material"></a>

## modelBuild:material

Part of [`ModelBuild`](#ref-ModelBuild).

```luau
modelBuild:material(name: string, color: Ink, opts: { grain: number ?, alpha: number ? }?) → ModelMaterial
```

Makes a named colour a display may repaint; `grain` (0 to 1) darkens pixels into four tones, `alpha` below 1 is glass.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes |
| `color` | [`Ink`](#ref-Ink) | yes |
| `opts` | `{ grain: number ?, alpha: number ? }` | no |

## Returns

- [`ModelMaterial`](#ref-ModelMaterial)

---

<!-- /ref/ModelBuild/part/ -->

<a id="ref-ModelBuild-part"></a>

## modelBuild:part

Part of [`ModelBuild`](#ref-ModelBuild).

```luau
modelBuild:part(name: string, opts: { pivot: Vec3 ? }?) → ModelPart
```

Makes a named child part of the root that turns around its `pivot`, the model's origin unless given.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes |
| `opts` | `{ pivot: Vec3 ? }` | no |

## Returns

- [`ModelPart`](#ref-ModelPart)

---

<!-- /ref/ModelBuild/texture/ -->

<a id="ref-ModelBuild-texture"></a>

## modelBuild:texture

Part of [`ModelBuild`](#ref-ModelBuild).

```luau
modelBuild:texture(width: number, height: number, opts: { tint: ModelMaterial ?, scroll: ("up" | "down" | "left" | "right")?, speed: number ? }?) → ModelTexture
```

Makes a pixel picture for one face; with `tint`, drawn in greys and coloured by that material. With `scroll`, it moves by itself on a block drawn from the model, `speed` texels a tick (1, 2, 3, or 0.5, 0.25).

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | `number` | yes |
| `height` | `number` | yes |
| `opts` | `{ tint: ModelMaterial ?, scroll: ( "up" \| "down" \| "left" \| "right" )?, speed: number ? }` | no |

## Returns

- [`ModelTexture`](#ref-ModelTexture)

---

<!-- /ref/ModelDisplay/ -->

<a id="ref-ModelDisplay"></a>

## ModelDisplay type

A model visual in a room. Shares at, rotation, scale, alive and move with other visuals; adds named animations and model materials.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`move`](#ref-ModelDisplay-move) | Place and turn it in one step, every part and seat together. |
| [`play`](#ref-ModelDisplay-play) | Starts an animation; replaying the current one changes speed without restarting. |
| [`stop`](#ref-ModelDisplay-stop) | Where it is; the parts stay as they are. |
| [`destroy`](#ref-ModelDisplay-destroy) | Removes the model from the room. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`modelDisplay.id: number`](#ref-ModelDisplay-id) | What `player:ride(model)` is handed; the seat is picked from `seats`. |
| [`modelDisplay.paint: { [string]: Ink }`](#ref-ModelDisplay-paint) | Whether it is still present. Read-only. Where it stands; live, and each write is a move of its own. Partial writes preserve other angles; nil after removal. Reads vec3; write a number or equal-axis vec3 for uniform size. Nil when gone. Material name to colour; write-only. |

---

<!-- /ref/ModelDisplay/destroy/ -->

Removes the model from the room.

<!-- /ref/ModelPart/ -->

<a id="ref-ModelPart"></a>

## ModelPart type

A named group of boxes that turns around its pivot. Units are 16 to the block, the origin is the model's bottom centre, and a box reaches -24..24.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`part`](#ref-ModelPart-part) | Makes a child part of this one; it turns around `pivot`, the model's origin unless you give one. |
| [`box`](#ref-ModelPart-box) | Corners in any order; a box turns on one axis, in steps of 22.5 up to 45, and `pivot` is the box's own centre unless you give one. |
| [`hitbox`](#ref-ModelPart-hitbox) | A box a player can hit on a living body that wears the model (clients from 1.19.4). Not drawn; corners in any order, in model units. Square from above (its longer side), so split a long part. Animations do not move it. A model with none is hit on one box of the body's `size`. |
| [`mirror`](#ref-ModelPart-mirror) | A mirrored copy of every box and hitbox this part has, and a mirrored twin named `<name>_mirrored` of every child. Only "x" in this version. |

---

<!-- /ref/ModelPart/box/ -->

<a id="ref-ModelPart-box"></a>

## modelPart:box

Part of [`ModelPart`](#ref-ModelPart).

```luau
modelPart:box(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, skin: ModelSkin, opts: { rotation: Vec3 ?, pivot: Vec3 ?, faces: { [Face]: ModelSkin }?, }?)
```

Corners in any order; a box turns on one axis, in steps of 22.5 up to 45, and `pivot` is the box's own centre unless you give one.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | [`Vec3`](#ref-Vec3) | yes |
| `to` | [`Vec3`](#ref-Vec3) | yes |
| `skin` | [`ModelSkin`](#ref-ModelSkin) | yes |
| `opts` | `{ rotation: Vec3 ?, pivot: Vec3 ?, faces: { [ Face ]: ModelSkin }?, }` | no |

---

<!-- /ref/ModelPart/hitbox/ -->

<a id="ref-ModelPart-hitbox"></a>

## modelPart:hitbox

Part of [`ModelPart`](#ref-ModelPart).

```luau
modelPart:hitbox(from: Vec3, to: Vec3)
```

A box a player can hit on a living body that wears the model (clients from 1.19.4). Not drawn; corners in any order, in model units. Square from above (its longer side), so split a long part. Animations do not move it. A model with none is hit on one box of the body's `size`.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | [`Vec3`](#ref-Vec3) | yes |
| `to` | [`Vec3`](#ref-Vec3) | yes |

---

<a id="ref-ModelPart-mirror"></a>

## modelPart:mirror

Part of [`ModelPart`](#ref-ModelPart).

```luau
modelPart:mirror(axis: "x")
```

A mirrored copy of every box and hitbox this part has, and a mirrored twin named `<name>_mirrored` of every child. Only "x" in this version.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` | `"x"` | yes |

<!-- /ref/ModelTexture/ -->

<a id="ref-ModelTexture"></a>

## ModelTexture type

Pixel art for one face of a box: plain RGBA, and never repainted.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`fill`](#ref-ModelTexture-fill) | Paints every pixel one colour. |
| [`pixel`](#ref-ModelTexture-pixel) | Paints the pixel at x, y; `colors.transparent` makes it see-through. |
| [`rect`](#ref-ModelTexture-rect) | Paints a rectangle `w` by `h` pixels from x, y. |
| [`draw`](#ref-ModelTexture-draw) | A game.texture over this one, its top left at x, y; see-through pixels skipped, what falls outside cut. |

---

| `y` | `number` | no |

<!-- /ref/Noise/ -->

<a id="ref-Noise"></a>

## Noise type

Smooth random numbers from `noise.new`: the same seed gives the same numbers every time.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`get`](#ref-Noise-get) | Returns about -1..1 at a point: `get(x, z)` for a height map, `get(x, y, z)` for caves and overhangs. |
| [`grid`](#ref-Noise-grid) | Returns `width * depth` heights in one call, row by row: the number for `(x + dx, z + dz)` is at `[dz * width + dx + 1]`. |

---

<!-- /ref/Noise/get/ -->

<a id="ref-Noise-get"></a>

## noise:get

Part of [`Noise`](#ref-Noise).

```luau
noise:get(x: number, y_or_z: number, z: number ?) → number
```

Returns about -1..1 at a point: `get(x, z)` for a height map, `get(x, y, z)` for caves and overhangs.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | `number` | yes |
| `y_or_z` | `number` | yes |
| `z` | `number` | no |

## Returns

- `number`

---

<!-- /ref/Noise/grid/ -->

<a id="ref-Noise-grid"></a>

## noise:grid

Part of [`Noise`](#ref-Noise).

```luau
noise:grid(x: number, z: number, width: number, depth: number) → { number }
```

Returns `width * depth` heights in one call, row by row: the number for `(x + dx, z + dz)` is at `[dz * width + dx + 1]`.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | `number` | yes |
| `z` | `number` | yes |
| `width` | `number` | yes |
| `depth` | `number` | yes |

## Returns

- `{ number }`

<!-- /ref/Npc/ -->

<a id="ref-Npc"></a>

## Npc type

A player-shaped entity every client from 1.8 sees, from `world.npc`; it can walk, talk, hold items, wear armour and ride.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`look_at`](#ref-Npc-look_at) | Where it stands; live, so setting it moves the NPC. A riding NPC reads the seat's position. Partial writes preserve other angles; nil after removal. Bodies have no roll. Turns head and body toward a point. |
| [`swing`](#ref-Npc-swing) | Plays the arm swing animation. |
| [`hold`](#ref-Npc-hold) | Puts an item in the main hand; nil or false empties it. An error on an unknown item. |
| [`say`](#ref-Npc-say) | Sends a chat line "<name> ..." to the room, or just the words for an NPC with no name. |
| [`walk`](#ref-Npc-walk) | Walks the points by itself, facing where it goes; nil stops it. |
| [`wear`](#ref-Npc-wear) | Puts armour on it, head first; each piece is an item. |
| [`ride`](#ref-Npc-ride) | Sits in a seat as `player:ride` does, and never drives; `false` when somebody sits there. |
| [`dismount`](#ref-Npc-dismount) | Gets off where it sits; set `at` after it to put it somewhere else. |
| [`move`](#ref-Npc-move) | Removes the NPC. Sets position and optional rotation together. |
| [`destroy`](#ref-Npc-destroy) |  |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`npc.id: number`](#ref-Npc-id) | The entity id, what `players.on_click` reports in `hit.entity_id`. |
| [`npc.name: string`](#ref-Npc-name) | Whether it is still present. Read-only. "" for one made with no name, which has no name tag. |
| [`npc.walking: boolean`](#ref-Npc-walking) | True while it walks a path, until the last point; never false with `loop`. |
| [`npc.pose: NpcPose`](#ref-Npc-pose) | How the body is held; live. |
| [`npc.riding: boolean`](#ref-Npc-riding) | Whether it sits in a seat; live. |

---

<a id="ref-Npc-say"></a>

## npc:say

Part of [`Npc`](#ref-Npc).

```luau
npc:say(text: Text, color: Ink ?)
```

Sends a chat line "<name> ..." to the room, or just the words for an NPC with no name.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | [`Text`](#ref-Text) | yes |
| `color` | [`Ink`](#ref-Ink) | no |

## Used in

> "color)`, a title's `color`, a text display's `color`, `npc:say(text," — [Text formatting](#ui-ui-basics)

<!-- /ref/Overlay/ -->

<a id="ref-Overlay"></a>

## Overlay type

A canvas on one player's screen, from `player.ui.overlay`: 128 by 128, drawn like a canvas. Row 0 is the engine's and never shows; draw in rows 1 to 127. Colour `colors.transparent` shows the game through it.

[`Picture`](#ref-Picture)

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`destroy`](#ref-Overlay-destroy) | Takes it off the player's screen. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`overlay.open: boolean`](#ref-Overlay-open) | True until `destroy` or the player leaves. |

<!-- /ref/PartDefinition/ -->

<a id="ref-PartDefinition"></a>

## PartDefinition type

A named part of a stored world (`world: <folder>`) and the generator that writes it. Declared, not run: `citadel generate <pack> --part <name>`, or `/part generate <name>` in build mode, runs it; a changed file runs it again while nobody has edited the part. See "parts" in docs/luau-api.md.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`build`](#ref-PartDefinition-build) | Exactly a world.build function. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`partDefinition.name: string`](#ref-PartDefinition-name) | Unique; a path, "downtown/tower-3", nests. |
| [`partDefinition.at: Vec3`](#ref-PartDefinition-at) | Where the build's block (0, 0, 0) lands. |
| [`partDefinition.detail: number ?`](#ref-PartDefinition-detail) | 1 (whole blocks, the default) or 2 (half blocks), as world.build. |

---

<!-- /ref/Persist/ -->

## Persist type

Whether a kind survives a save. "save" puts it in the chunk record, `data` and all; "despawn" is gone when the chunk goes.

`"save"` | `"despawn"`

<!-- /ref/Physics/ -->

<a id="ref-Physics"></a>

## Physics type

Which order of operations moves a body. Not a table of floats: the floats are the game version's, and this says which set of them applies.

`"vehicle"` | `"living"` | `"falling"` | `"item"` | `"none"`

<!-- /ref/Picture/ -->

<a id="ref-Picture"></a>

## Picture type

The calls a screen, a canvas and a view all share.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`clear`](#ref-Picture-clear) | Its width in pixels: 128 for each map across. Its height in pixels: 128 for each map down. Paints every pixel one colour; black by default. On a view, the default clears it to see-through. |
| [`set`](#ref-Picture-set) | Paints one pixel; (0, 0) is the top-left. |
| [`fill`](#ref-Picture-fill) | Fills a w by h box of pixels with one colour, its top-left at (x, y). |
| [`rect`](#ref-Picture-rect) | Fills a box like `fill`, with smoothed rounded corners of `radius` pixels when given. |
| [`circle`](#ref-Picture-circle) | Fills a circle of radius `r` pixels around (x, y). |
| [`text`](#ref-Picture-text) | Draws text in DejaVu Sans Bold, `size` pixels tall (16 by default), smoothed; returns its width in pixels. |
| [`measure`](#ref-Picture-measure) | The width in pixels that `text` would draw, without drawing it; for centring. |
| [`line`](#ref-Picture-line) | Draws a smoothed line with round ends, `width` pixels wide (1 by default); positions may be fractions. |
| [`ring`](#ref-Picture-ring) | Draws a circle's outline, `width` pixels wide (1 by default), smoothed. |
| [`polygon`](#ref-Picture-polygon) | Fills a smoothed shape with any number of corners; a point is `{x, y}` or `{ x = .., y = .. }`. |
| [`gradient`](#ref-Picture-gradient) | Fills a box that fades from `from` to `to`, top to bottom; `"across"` runs it left to right. |
| [`sprite`](#ref-Picture-sprite) | Draws pixel art: each string a row, each character a dot `scale` pixels square (1 by default); a character with no ink is skipped. |
| [`pixels`](#ref-Picture-pixels) | Writes raw RGB bytes (a buffer or a string), three a pixel, row by row, into a w by h box. |
| [`draw`](#ref-Picture-draw) | Draws another screen, canvas or view with its top-left at (x, y), skipping its transparent pixels. |
| [`part`](#ref-Picture-part) | One map of the picture, `{ id = .. }`, by column and row from (0, 0) top- left; for a hand or a single frame. |
| [`play`](#ref-Picture-play) | Plays a raw RGB video file from the pack at `fps` 0.5 to 20, the engine drawing each frame; returns the Video. |

---

<!-- /ref/PlantRule/ -->

<a id="ref-PlantRule"></a>

## PlantRule type

A plant on a column. Each column takes at most one: a rule that holds is tried with its `chance` (1), in the order of the list.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`plantRule.block: BlockPick ?`](#ref-PlantRule-block) |  |
| [`plantRule.blocks: { BlockPick }?`](#ref-PlantRule-blocks) | The blocks from the foot up, in place of `block`: a two-block flower. |
| [`plantRule.tip: BlockPick ?`](#ref-PlantRule-tip) | With `height`, the block on top of a plant that grows. |
| [`plantRule.height: (Field \| number)?`](#ref-PlantRule-height) | How many blocks a plant that grows is tall: `block` repeats. |
| [`plantRule.chance: (Field \| number)?`](#ref-PlantRule-chance) |  |
| [`plantRule.biome: string ?`](#ref-PlantRule-biome) |  |
| [`plantRule.when: (Field \| number)?`](#ref-PlantRule-when) |  |
| [`plantRule.afloat: boolean ?`](#ref-PlantRule-afloat) | On the water over a column, not on its ground. |
| [`plantRule.sink: number ?`](#ref-PlantRule-sink) | Blocks to stand lower: 1 is in the ground, or in the top of the water. |
| [`plantRule.clear: number ?`](#ref-PlantRule-clear) | Blocks of water to keep clear over a plant that grows in it. |
| [`plantRule.place: ("top" \| "floor" \| "ceiling" \| "wall")?`](#ref-PlantRule-place) | Where it goes: "top" (the default), or in the caves `density` or `carvers` dig: "floor", "ceiling" (it hangs down: `tip` is lowest) or "wall" (one block; `{wall}` in its name is the side the rock is on, `{facing}` the side away). One plant on each floor and each ceiling of a cave, and in each wall block. `when` and `chance` are read at the air block it starts in. |
| [`plantRule.y: { number }?`](#ref-PlantRule-y) | `{ low, high }`: the y it may start at. |

---

<a id="ref-PlantRule-afloat"></a>

## plantRule.place

Part of [`plantRule`](#ref-PlantRule).

```luau
plantRule.place: ("top" | "floor" | "ceiling" | "wall")?
```

Where it goes: "top" (the default), or in the caves `density` or `carvers` dig: "floor", "ceiling" (it hangs down: `tip` is lowest) or "wall" (one block; `{wall}` in its name is the side the rock is on, `{facing}` the side away). One plant on each floor and each ceiling of a cave, and in each wall block. `when` and `chance` are read at the air block it starts in.

<!-- /ref/Player/ -->

<a id="ref-Player"></a>

## Player type

A player in the room: what `players.on_join` and every player event hand you.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`ride`](#ref-Player-ride) | The player's name. The account's own id: the one name for a player a rename does not change. Where they stand now. Your own table, kept on the player for as long as they are connected. A player is one value while connected: `a == b` and `t[player]` work. The Room the player is in; nil while they move between rooms. Degrees: `yaw` sideways, `pitch` up or down; live, read only. True while the player sneaks; live. `attack` is the left button held on a block in reach (see player.reach); a client says nothing about a button held on air. True while the player sits on something; live. Seat 1 drives a vehicle; `locked` keeps a sneak from getting them off. `false` when somebody sits in that seat; keeps the current ride on failure. Works immediately after creating the target. Repeating the same ride keeps the seat; no delay or extra movement is needed. |
| [`dismount`](#ref-Player-dismount) | Gets the player off what they ride; sneaking does the same, as off a horse. |
| [`message`](#ref-Player-message) | What shows on this player's screen: the calls `ui` has, for them alone, plus their own menu and overlay. Sends a chat line to this player alone; `color` is for the words that did not pick one. Chat is not part of the screen, so it is not in `ui`. |
| [`sound`](#ref-Player-sound) | Plays a sound by name to this player only, with an optional position, volume, pitch and category. |
| [`teleport`](#ref-Player-teleport) | Yaw and pitch left out keep the way they face. |
| [`move_to`](#ref-Player-move_to) | Moves the player to another room; the client swaps worlds in place. |
| [`travel`](#ref-Player-travel) | Sends the player to another world of the group, at `pos` or its spawn. |
| [`give`](#ref-Player-give) | One item: "stone", or { item = "arrow", count = 16 }. |
| [`held`](#ref-Player-held) | Returns the stack in hand ({ item, count }, plus `id` for a pack item and `damage` for a worn tool), or nil. |
| [`inventory`](#ref-Player-inventory) | Returns one { item, count } row per filled slot. |
| [`take`](#ref-Player-take) | Up to `count` (1 unless you say) of what matches, the hand first; answers how many it took. |
| [`set_held`](#ref-Player-set_held) | The stack in hand, replaced; nil or false empties the hand. |
| [`hotbar`](#ref-Player-hotbar) | Replaces the nine hotbar slots; a missing index is empty. |
| [`wear`](#ref-Player-wear) | The four armour slots; a piece left out is bare. |
| [`kill`](#ref-Player-kill) | 0..20, or nil where the game version has no food bar. The food saturation, or nil where the game version has no food bar. True while the player is on the death screen. Kills the player; returns false on a version with no damage rules. |
| [`hide`](#ref-Player-hide) | This player stops seeing `other`, or sees them again. |
| [`show`](#ref-Player-show) | This player sees `other` again after a `hide`. |
| [`can_see`](#ref-Player-can_see) | True unless `other` is not visible or is hidden from this player. |
| [`effect`](#ref-Player-effect) | A potion effect by its modern name; `duration` in seconds, math.huge for ever. |
| [`clear_effect`](#ref-Player-clear_effect) | Takes a potion effect off the player, by its modern name. |
| [`push`](#ref-Player-push) | A shove in blocks per tick, on top of what they are doing. |
| [`damage`](#ref-Player-damage) | A hit in half-hearts: the flash, the sound, the resistance window. `false` on a version with no damage rules. |
| [`look_at`](#ref-Player-look_at) | Turns the player's head to a point, where they stand. |
| [`stop_sound`](#ref-Player-stop_sound) | Where their view is from: the camera they look out of, or their eyes. One sound by name, or every sound; 1.13 and later. |
| [`kick`](#ref-Player-kick) | Disconnects the player, with that text on their screen. |
| [`connect`](#ref-Player-connect) | Asks Minefort to move the player to another server by name: an instance's `id`, the network's name (its default member) or "hub". Minefort decides and does not answer; a player still here was not moved. |
| [`count`](#ref-Player-count) | Returns how many of an item the player carries, across every slot. |
| [`has`](#ref-Player-has) | True if the player's groups give them this permission node; operators have every node. |
| [`groups`](#ref-Player-groups) | Returns the player's groups; `default` is not listed. |
| [`add_group`](#ref-Player-add_group) | Puts the player in a group until they leave; errors on a group citadel.yml does not define. |
| [`remove_group`](#ref-Player-remove_group) | Takes the player out of a group. |
| [`supports`](#ref-Player-supports) | True if this player's client can show the feature. |
| [`look`](#ref-Player-look) | Returns the unit vector the player faces. |
| [`set_slot`](#ref-Player-set_slot) | Selects hotbar slot 1..9. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`player.gamemode: number`](#ref-Player-gamemode) | The hotbar slot in hand, 1..9; live. 0 survival, 1 creative, 2 adventure, 3 spectator; writable. |
| [`player.spawn_point: Vec3 ?`](#ref-Player-spawn_point) | The player's own respawn point (the block of the position), or nil for the room's. Writable; a point a pack sets needs no bed. nil clears it, a bed's point too. |
| [`player.max_health: number ?`](#ref-Player-max_health) | Their health now, 0 to `max_health`; nil where the game version has no damage rules. Writable: set outright, no flash; 0 is a death; a number above `max_health` stops there. The most health they can have: 20 unless a pack set it; nil where the game version has no damage rules. Writable, 1 to 1024; nil gives the game's own back. A lower maximum takes `health` down to it. It lasts for the session. Every Java client draws its hearts; Bedrock draws none. |
| [`player.speed: number`](#ref-Player-speed) | The body: what a pack sets on a player. See docs/luau-api.md, "Body and movement". Walk speed as a multiple of normal; 0 pins them. |
| [`player.can_fly: boolean`](#ref-Player-can_fly) | May fly in a mode that cannot. |
| [`player.visible: boolean ?`](#ref-Player-visible) | false: no other player is sent this body. The tab line stays. true or nil shows the body again. |
| [`player.scale: number`](#ref-Player-scale) | 1/16 to 16; 1.20.5 and later, older clients stay as they are. |
| [`player.reach: number`](#ref-Player-reach) | How far a block can be clicked or dug, 0 to 64 blocks (4.5 by default); 1.20.5 and later. Measured from the camera when there is one. |
| [`player.level: number`](#ref-Player-level) | The experience bar: the number over it, and how full it is (0..1). |
| [`player.xp: number`](#ref-Player-xp) | How full the experience bar is, 0..1. |
| [`player.camera: (Camera \| false)?`](#ref-Player-camera) | What they look out of: a camera from camera.fixed/free/orbit/chase, or nil or false for their own eyes. No delay is needed after creating its target. Ends when the target is destroyed or the player leaves the room. |
| [`player.time: (number \| TimeName \| false)?`](#ref-Player-time) | This player's sky alone, held at a time of day; nil or false gives them the room's again, as does moving rooms. Reads back in ticks. |


<!-- /ref/Player/connect/ -->

<a id="ref-Player-connect"></a>

## player:connect

Part of [`Player`](#ref-Player).

```luau
player:connect(server: string)
```

Asks Minefort to move the player to another server by name: an instance's `id`, the network's name (its default member) or "hub". Minefort decides and does not answer; a player still here was not moved.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `server` | `string` | yes |

## Used in

> "player:connect("hub")          -- ask Minefort to move them to another server, by its name" — [Body and movement](#players-movement)
> "- `player:connect(server)` asks Minefort's proxy to move the player: a BungeeCord `Connect` for a Java player, a `Transfer` to that name for a Bedrock player. It returns nothing and does not yield." — [Body and movement](#players-movement)
> "player:connect(arena.id)" — [Network](#systems-network)
> "for _, player in waiting[instance.id] or {} do player:connect(instance.id) end" — [Network](#systems-network)
> "- `hub.servers()` returns a list of `{id, name, category, motd, icon, banner, players, maxPlayers}`. `id` is what `player:connect` takes. A field Minefort does not know is nil. An entry with `category = "experience"` is a published experience: its `id` is the name `/play` takes, `motd` its pitch, and `banner` the URL of its banner, or nil." — [Hub](#systems-hub)
> "- `hub.hubs()` returns a list of `{id, name, players, region}`, one per hub that is online, this one included. `player:connect(id)` sends a player to that hub." — [Hub](#systems-hub)

<!-- /ref/Player/max_health/ -->

<a id="ref-Player-max_health"></a>

## player.max_health

Part of [`player`](#ref-Player).

```luau
player.max_health: number ?
```

Their health now, 0 to `max_health`; nil where the game version has no damage rules. Writable: set outright, no flash; 0 is a death; a number above `max_health` stops there. The most health they can have: 20 unless a pack set it; nil where the game version has no damage rules. Writable, 1 to 1024; nil gives the game's own back. A lower maximum takes `health` down to it. It lasts for the session. Every Java client draws its hearts; Bedrock draws none.

## Used in

> "player.health          -- their health now, 0 to player.max_health; nil where the version has no damage rules" — [Players](#players-player-lifecycle)
> "player.max_health      -- the most health they can have: 20 unless a pack set it; nil for the same reason" — [Players](#players-player-lifecycle)
> "player.health = 20             -- set outright, no flash; 0 is a death; above player.max_health it stops there" — [Body and movement](#players-movement)

<a id="ref-Player-message"></a>

## player:message

Part of [`Player`](#ref-Player).

```luau
player:message(text: Text, color: Ink ?)
```

What shows on this player's screen: the calls `ui` has, for them alone, plus their own menu and overlay. Sends a chat line to this player alone; `color` is for the words that did not pick one. Chat is not part of the screen, so it is not in `ui`.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | [`Text`](#ref-Text) | yes |
| `color` | [`Ink`](#ref-Ink) | no |

## Used in

> "player:message("Walk around, then type /spawn to return to the gold block.", "aqua")" — [Guide: Your first pack](#getting-started-quick-start)
> "reads their name; `player.ui.title` shows them a title; `player:message`" — [Guide: Your first pack](#getting-started-quick-start)
> "player:message(`Walk onto the gold plates! Your best is {best}.`, "gold")" — [Guide: Coin rush](#guides-guide-coin-rush)
> "player:message(`Walk onto the gold plates! Your best is {best}.`, "gold")" — [Guide: Coin rush](#guides-guide-coin-rush)
> "player:message(`Your best time is {string.format("%.1f s", best)}.`, "green")" — [Guide: Parkour, a room each](#guides-guide-parkour-a-room-each)
> "player:message(`Your best time is {string.format("%.1f s", best)}.`, "green")" — [Guide: Parkour, a room each](#guides-guide-parkour-a-room-each)

## Used in

> "- `player:push` and a movement effect (`speed`, `jump_boost`, `levitation`, `slow_falling`, `dolphins_grace`) exempt the player while they last. `player:teleport` is always allowed." — [Room rules](#world-world-state)
> "hit.player:push(player:look() * 0.5 + vec3(0, 0.3, 0))" — [Room rules](#world-world-state)

<!-- /ref/Player/ride/ -->

<a id="ref-Player-ride"></a>

## player:ride

Part of [`Player`](#ref-Player).

```luau
player:ride(thing: MountTarget, opts: { seat: number ?, locked: boolean ? }?) → boolean
```

The player's name. The account's own id: the one name for a player a rename does not change. Where they stand now. Your own table, kept on the player for as long as they are connected. A player is one value while connected: `a == b` and `t[player]` work. The Room the player is in; nil while they move between rooms. Degrees: `yaw` sideways, `pitch` up or down; live, read only. True while the player sneaks; live. `attack` is the left button held on a block in reach (see player.reach); a client says nothing about a button held on air. True while the player sits on something; live. Seat 1 drives a vehicle; `locked` keeps a sneak from getting them off. `false` when somebody sits in that seat; keeps the current ride on failure. Works immediately after creating the target. Repeating the same ride keeps the seat; no delay or extra movement is needed.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `thing` | [`MountTarget`](#ref-MountTarget) | yes |
| `opts` | `{ seat: number ?, locked: boolean ? }` | no |

## Returns

- `boolean`

## Used in

> "Likewise, `player:ride` while a free/orbit camera is active is an error;" — [Cameras](#players-movement)
> "- For the driver's own eyes, seat them: `player:ride(car, { locked = true })`" — [Cameras](#players-movement)
> "player:ride(thing) -> boolean   -- sit on a display, a model, a hitbox or an npc, and go where it goes;" — [Input](#players-movement)
> "player:ride(c)                                -- seat 1: W and S throttle, A and D steer" — [Displays](#ui-displays)
> "- A seat holds one rider. `player:ride` and `npc:ride` return `false` for a" — [Displays](#ui-displays)
> "n:ride(car, { seat = 2 }) -> boolean   -- sits as player:ride does; false when that seat is taken" — [NPCs](#entities-npcs)

<!-- /ref/PlayerUi/ -->

<a id="ref-PlayerUi"></a>

## PlayerUi type

`player.ui`: the calls `ui` has, for one player alone, plus what only one player's screen holds.

[`Ui`](#ref-Ui)

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`menu`](#ref-PlayerUi-menu) | A titled grid of up to 54 items over the player's view; each pick is answered by `on_pick(player, n)`. Nothing goes in or out of it: the items are pictures, not stacks. A chest on Java, a form of buttons on Bedrock. `on_close` fires when the player puts it away without picking. A new menu replaces the open one. |
| [`overlay`](#ref-PlayerUi-overlay) | Puts a canvas in a corner of this player's screen, `size` screen pixels square at GUI scale 1 (96 by default, 16 to 511), `margin` from the edges (4 by default); nil where `player:supports("overlay")` is false. |
| [`show`](#ref-PlayerUi-show) | Puts a layout on this player's screen. A client older than 1.21.4 (`player:supports("layout")`) gets a handle that shows nothing. |
| [`dialog`](#ref-PlayerUi-dialog) | A screen of boxes, words and pictures (see "Dialogs"): a `ui.kit.window{}`, or a function that returns one and is drawn again after every click. nil where `player:supports("dialog")` is false. |

---


A titled grid of up to 54 items over the player's view; each pick is answered by `on_pick(player, n)`. Nothing goes in or out of it: the items are pictures, not stacks. A chest on Java, a form of buttons on Bedrock. `on_close` fires when the player puts it away without picking. A new menu replaces the open one.

| --- | --- | --- |

<!-- /ref/Recipes/ -->

<a id="ref-Recipes"></a>

## Recipes type

`game.recipes`: what a crafting grid and a furnace make of a pack's items. Load-time only, like a block definition. The game's own recipes are asked first, so a pack adds and never takes away.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`shaped`](#ref-Recipes-shaped) | 1 to 3 rows of 1 to 3 letters; a space is an empty cell. |
| [`shapeless`](#ref-Recipes-shapeless) | Adds a crafting recipe whose ingredients may go anywhere in the grid. |
| [`smelt`](#ref-Recipes-smelt) | Adds a furnace recipe; a furnace smelts a pack item only by one of these. |

---

<!-- /ref/Room/ -->

<a id="ref-Room"></a>

## Room type

An isolated world with its own players and tables, from `rooms.create` or `rooms.main`.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`message`](#ref-Room-message) | This room's `world` table: its blocks, entities and displays. This room's `players` table; its `on_join` fires each time a player moves in. This room's `sound` table. This room's `fx` table. This room's `ui` table. This room's `game` table: the game version it runs, its entity kinds and blocks. This room's `commands` table. Sends a chat line to everyone in this room. |
| [`destroy`](#ref-Room-destroy) | Takes the room away; players still in it keep the world. Does nothing to `rooms.main`. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`room.spawn_point: Vec3`](#ref-Room-spawn_point) | The room's number. Rooms also compare by identity with `==`. Where players arrive in this room; writable. A write is not stored and does not move the chunks that stay loaded. |

<!-- /ref/Room/message/ -->

<a id="ref-Room-message"></a>

## room:message

Part of [`Room`](#ref-Room).

```luau
room:message(text: Text, color: Ink ?)
```

This room's `world` table: its blocks, entities and displays. This room's `players` table; its `on_join` fires each time a player moves in. This room's `sound` table. This room's `fx` table. This room's `ui` table. This room's `game` table: the game version it runs, its entity kinds and blocks. This room's `commands` table. Sends a chat line to everyone in this room.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | [`Text`](#ref-Text) | yes |
| `color` | [`Ink`](#ref-Ink) | no |

## Used in

> "room:message("A new round starts")   -- a chat line to everyone in this room" — [Rooms](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions)

---

<!-- /ref/Room/spawn_point/ -->

<a id="ref-Room-spawn_point"></a>

## room.spawn_point

Part of [`room`](#ref-Room).

```luau
room.spawn_point: Vec3
```

The room's number. Rooms also compare by identity with `==`. Where players arrive in this room; writable. A write is not stored and does not move the chunks that stay loaded.

## Used in

> "room.spawn_point = vec3(0.5, 80, 0.5)     -- the same field of a different room" — [Rooms](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions)
> "- A write to `world.spawn_point` or `room.spawn_point` changes where a player" — [Rooms](#concepts-rooms-and-dimensions)

---

<!-- /ref/Rotation/ -->

<a id="ref-Rotation"></a>

## Rotation type

`BodyRotation & { read roll: number? }`

---

<!-- /ref/Rules/ -->

<a id="ref-Rules"></a>

## Rules type

Which parts of the player simulation this room runs. All on for a `mode: full` server, all off on a pack server until the pack says. `survival` is the whole game: digging and its drops, placing, the inventory and crafting, respawning — and it turns fall, damage, hunger and day_cycle on. `anticheat` is on everywhere until a pack turns it off, and so is `redstone`: off, no signal moves in the room.

`{ survival: boolean, fall: boolean, damage: boolean, hunger: boolean, anticheat: boolean, day_cycle: boolean, redstone: boolean }`

---

<!-- /ref/Schematic/ -->

<a id="ref-Schematic"></a>

## Schematic type

A box of blocks: a `.schem` file from the pack, read once by `world.schematic`, or one a script wrote with `world.build`. `min` is the build's own lowest corner, which is the corner `origin` puts down; a file has no coordinates of its own, so its `min` is zero.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`rotate`](#ref-Schematic-rotate) | The build's width, height and length in blocks. The build's own lowest corner, which `origin` puts down; zero for a file. A new build turned clockwise seen from above (90, 180 or 270), states and all. |
| [`mirror`](#ref-Schematic-mirror) | A new build flipped: "x" swaps east and west, "z" north and south. |

---

<!-- /ref/Schematic/mirror/ -->

<a id="ref-Schematic-mirror"></a>

## schematic:mirror

Part of [`Schematic`](#ref-Schematic).

```luau
schematic:mirror(axis: "x" | "z") → Schematic
```

A new build flipped: "x" swaps east and west, "z" north and south.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` | `"x" \| "z"` | yes |

## Returns

- [`Schematic`](#ref-Schematic)

---

<!-- /ref/Schematic/rotate/ -->

<a id="ref-Schematic-rotate"></a>

## schematic:rotate

Part of [`Schematic`](#ref-Schematic).

```luau
schematic:rotate(degrees: number) → Schematic
```

The build's width, height and length in blocks. The build's own lowest corner, which `origin` puts down; zero for a file. A new build turned clockwise seen from above (90, 180 or 270), states and all.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `degrees` | `number` | yes |

## Returns

- [`Schematic`](#ref-Schematic)

<!-- /ref/Screen/ -->

<a id="ref-Screen"></a>

## Screen type

A wall or floor of map frames showing a picture, from `world.screen`; it draws like a canvas and can answer clicks by pixel.

[`Picture`](#ref-Picture)

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`on_click`](#ref-Screen-on_click) | Called with the pixel the player points at and the button, when a player clicks the screen. nil or false takes the hook off. |
| [`view`](#ref-Screen-view) | Returns this player's own layer over the screen; only they see it, and the shared picture shows where it is see-through. |
| [`destroy`](#ref-Screen-destroy) | Removes the screen. |

---

<!-- /ref/Screen/destroy/ -->

<a id="ref-Screen-destroy"></a>

## screen:destroy

Part of [`Screen`](#ref-Screen).

```luau
screen:destroy()
```

Removes the screen.

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `((player` | `Player , x: number , y: number , button: "left" \| "right" ) -> ()) \| false` | yes |

<!-- /ref/Slow/ -->

<a id="ref-Slow"></a>

## Slow type

One overrun, as `citadel.on_slow` is handed it.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`slow.hook: string`](#ref-Slow-hook) | The short name of the hook that ran out: "on_tick", "every", or the event's own. |
| [`slow.of: number`](#ref-Slow-of) | The pack's budget per tick, in milliseconds: `budget_ms` in citadel.yml. |
| [`slow.used: number`](#ref-Slow-used) | Milliseconds the pack spent in the tick that ran out. |
| [`slow.skipped: number`](#ref-Slow-skipped) | Callbacks not run for want of budget, since the script started. |

<!-- /ref/Socket/ -->

<a id="ref-Socket"></a>

## Socket type

A WebSocket a pack opened with `http.socket`.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`send`](#ref-Socket-send) | True while the connection is up. Terminal receive-queue overflow; nil otherwise. Queues text; false when closed or full. Messages over 1 MiB are errors. |
| [`cancel`](#ref-Socket-cancel) | Closes the socket for good. |

---

<!-- /ref/Socket/cancel/ -->

<a id="ref-Socket-cancel"></a>

## socket:cancel

Part of [`Socket`](#ref-Socket).

```luau
socket:cancel()
```

Closes the socket for good.

## Used in

> "socket:cancel()      -- closes it for good" — [HTTP](#systems-http)

---

<!-- /ref/Socket/send/ -->

<a id="ref-Socket-send"></a>

## socket:send

Part of [`Socket`](#ref-Socket).

```luau
socket:send(text: string) → boolean
```

True while the connection is up. Terminal receive-queue overflow; nil otherwise. Queues text; false when closed or full. Messages over 1 MiB are errors.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | yes |

## Returns

- `boolean`

## Used in

> "socket:send("hello") -- queues text; true if queued, false if closed or full" — [HTTP](#systems-http)

<!-- /ref/Suggester/ -->

<a id="ref-Suggester"></a>

## Suggester type

Called as the player types; must answer at once (no task.wait). `args` holds the arguments typed before this one, by name.

`(player: Player, typed: string, args: { [string]: any }) -> { Suggestion }`

---

<!-- /ref/Suggestion/ -->

<a id="ref-Suggestion"></a>

## Suggestion type

One word offered as a player types a command argument: a string, or a text with a tooltip.

`string` | `{ text: string, tooltip: string? }`

---

<!-- /ref/TerrainStep/ -->

<a id="ref-TerrainStep"></a>

## TerrainStep type

One populate step of the overworld, as citadel.yml writes it, read from `game.terrain.steps`.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`terrainStep.step: string`](#ref-TerrainStep-step) | Which populate step: "dungeons", "clay", "ore", "trees", "patch", "reeds", "cactus", "springs" or "snow". |
| [`terrainStep.block: string ?`](#ref-TerrainStep-block) | The block a clay, ore or patch step places. |
| [`terrainStep.fluid: string ?`](#ref-TerrainStep-fluid) | The fluid a springs step places: "water" or "lava". |
| [`terrainStep.count: number ?`](#ref-TerrainStep-count) | How many tries, veins, blobs, clumps or springs the step makes in a chunk. |
| [`terrainStep.size: number ?`](#ref-TerrainStep-size) | How long each clay blob or ore vein is. |
| [`terrainStep.below: number ?`](#ref-TerrainStep-below) | An ore step places its veins below this y. |
| [`terrainStep.bonus: number ?`](#ref-TerrainStep-bonus) | Trees: one chunk in this many gets one more tree. |
| [`terrainStep.big: number ?`](#ref-TerrainStep-big) | Trees: one chunk in this many grows big trees instead of small ones. |
| [`terrainStep.chance: number ?`](#ref-TerrainStep-chance) | Patch: made one time in this many, in place of `count` times. |
| [`terrainStep.bound: number ?`](#ref-TerrainStep-bound) | Springs: the y is picked below this bound before `nesting` pushes it deeper. |
| [`terrainStep.nesting: number ?`](#ref-TerrainStep-nesting) | Springs: how many times the y is picked again below itself; lava's 2 keeps it deeper than water's 1. |

---

<!-- /ref/TerrainStep/below/ -->

<!-- /ref/Text/ -->

<a id="ref-Text"></a>

## Text type

A string, a table of runs, or a function of the time (`time.now()`) handing back a text, worked out again every frame it is on screen.

`string` | [`TextRuns`](#ref-TextRuns) | `((t: number) -> any)`

---

<!-- /ref/TextRuns/ -->

<a id="ref-TextRuns"></a>

## TextRuns type

Words wherever the API shows them: a string, or a table of runs. A table's entries are its runs in order (each a string or another table), and its named fields are the style of all of them; a run that names its own style keeps it. See "text" in docs/luau-api.md.

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`textRuns.color: Ink ?`](#ref-TextRuns-color) | The colour of every run that does not pick its own: a colour value, a name or hex. |
| [`textRuns.bold: boolean ?`](#ref-TextRuns-bold) | Bold for every run that does not say otherwise. |
| [`textRuns.italic: boolean ?`](#ref-TextRuns-italic) | Italic for every run that does not say otherwise. |
| [`textRuns.underline: boolean ?`](#ref-TextRuns-underline) | Underlined for every run that does not say otherwise. |
| [`textRuns.strike: boolean ?`](#ref-TextRuns-strike) | Struck through for every run that does not say otherwise. |
| [`textRuns.effect: Effect ?`](#ref-TextRuns-effect) | Called for every letter, every frame the text is on screen: hands back how that letter looks, or nil to leave it. |

---

<!-- /ref/TextRuns/bold/ -->

<a id="ref-TextRuns-bold"></a>

## textRuns.bold

Part of [`textRuns`](#ref-TextRuns).

```luau
textRuns.bold: boolean ?
```

Bold for every run that does not say otherwise.

---

<!-- /ref/Texture/ -->

<a id="ref-Texture"></a>

## Texture type

A picture drawn in code: `game.texture(w, h)`. Where a texture is taken, a string is a PNG file in the pack instead.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`fill`](#ref-Texture-fill) | Paints every pixel one colour. |
| [`pixel`](#ref-Texture-pixel) | Sets one pixel; (0, 0) is the top left. |
| [`rect`](#ref-Texture-rect) | Fills a rectangle of pixels. |
| [`frame`](#ref-Texture-frame) | Draws a box's outline, one pixel wide. |
| [`noise`](#ref-Texture-noise) | Paints each pixel in the area one of the colours at random, as for stone, bark or grain. |
| [`sprite`](#ref-Texture-sprite) | Draws pixel art from rows of characters, each character painted with its ink, as on a screen. |
| [`draw`](#ref-Texture-draw) | Draws another texture over this one; its see-through pixels are skipped. |
| [`copy`](#ref-Texture-copy) | Returns a copy to draw on. |

## Fields

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`texture.width: number`](#ref-Texture-width) | Width in pixels. |
| [`texture.height: number`](#ref-Texture-height) | Height in pixels. |

---

<!-- /ref/Texture/copy/ -->

<a id="ref-Texture-copy"></a>

## texture:copy

Part of [`Texture`](#ref-Texture).

```luau
texture:copy() → Texture
```

Returns a copy to draw on.

## Returns

- [`Texture`](#ref-Texture)

---

<!-- /ref/Texture/draw/ -->

<a id="ref-Texture-draw"></a>

## texture:draw

Part of [`Texture`](#ref-Texture).

```luau
texture:draw(other: Texture, x: number ?, y: number ?)
```

Draws another texture over this one; its see-through pixels are skipped.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `other` | [`Texture`](#ref-Texture) | yes |
| `x` | `number` | no |
| `y` | `number` | no |

---

| `color` | [`Ink`](#ref-Ink) | yes |

## texture:noise

Part of [`Texture`](#ref-Texture).

```luau
texture:noise(x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, colors: { Ink }, seed: number ?)
```

| `w` | `number` | yes |
| `h` | `number` | yes |

| `seed` | `number` | no |

<!-- /ref/TextureRef/ -->

<a id="ref-TextureRef"></a>

## TextureRef type

A block or item picture: a `Texture` drawn in code with `game.texture`, or the name of a PNG file in the pack.

[`Texture`](#ref-Texture) | `string`

---

<!-- /ref/ThingGrid/ -->

<a id="ref-ThingGrid"></a>

## ThingGrid type

Things that share one grid of `cell` blocks (8): a cell holds at most one, at a place that is the cell's own, so a thing over a chunk border is whole.

`{ [number]: ThingRule, cell: number?, seed: number? }`

---

<!-- /ref/ThingRule/ -->

<a id="ref-ThingRule"></a>

## ThingRule type

A thing that stands on a grid cell: one of `shapes`, its `(0, 0, 0)` on the block above the ground. `afloat` stands it on the water where the ground is under water; without it, nothing stands there. `place = "floor"` puts its `(0, 0, 0)` on the air block over a cave floor, `"ceiling"` on the air block under a ceiling (build it down from there).

`{ shapes: { Schematic }, chance: (Field` | `number)?, biome: string?, when: (Field` | `number)?, afloat: boolean?, place: ("top"` | `"floor"` | `"ceiling")?, y: { number }? }`

---

<!-- /ref/Think/ -->

<a id="ref-Think"></a>

## Think type

What `on_think` gets: `n` bodies, and one buffer for each column with one f64 per body (entry i at byte i * 8). A yes or no is 1 or 0, an id of nothing is 0. Write the last nine to change them; a value left as it was changes nothing.

---

<!-- /ref/TimeName/ -->

<a id="ref-TimeName"></a>

## TimeName type

A named time of day that `world.time` holds the sky at: sunrise, day, noon, sunset, night or midnight.

`"sunrise"` | `"day"` | `"noon"` | `"sunset"` | `"night"` | `"midnight" x: number, y: number, z: number, magnitude: (self: Vec3) -> number, unit: (self: Vec3) -> Vec3, dot: (self: Vec3, other: Vec3) -> number, cross: (self: Vec3, other: Vec3) -> Vec3, distance: (self: Vec3, other: Vec3) -> number, lerp: (self: Vec3, other: Vec3, t: number) -> Vec3, floor: (self: Vec3) -> Vec3, with: (self: Vec3, fields: { x: number?, y: number?, z: number? }) -> Vec3,`

---

<!-- /ref/Trigger/ -->

<a id="ref-Trigger"></a>

## Trigger type

Something that happened *to* a block.

`"ignite"` | `"explosion"` | `"fire"`

---

<!-- /ref/Tween/ -->

<a id="ref-Tween"></a>

## Tween type

A field easing over time, from tween or camera.path.

---

<!-- /ref/Used/ -->

<a id="ref-Used"></a>

## Used type

What `on_use` answers. Never true or false.

`"used"` | `"pass"`

---

<!-- /ref/Vec3/ -->

<a id="ref-Vec3"></a>

## Vec3 type

`typeof(setmetatable({} :: Vec3Fields, {} :: r: number, g: number, b: number, lerp: (self: Color, other: Color, t: number) -> Color,`

---

<!-- /ref/Video/ -->

<a id="ref-Video"></a>

## Video type

A raw RGB video playing on a picture, from `picture:play`; read `playing` or call `stop`.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`stop`](#ref-Video-stop) | False once it ends (and does not loop) or is stopped. Stops the video. |

---

```luau
video:stop()
```

False once it ends (and does not loop) or is stopped. Stops the video.

<!-- /ref/View/ -->

<a id="ref-View"></a>

## View type

One player's own layer over a screen or canvas, from `screen:view(player)`; only they see it, drawn with the same calls.

[`Picture`](#ref-Picture)

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`destroy`](#ref-View-destroy) | Removes this player's view; they see the shared picture again. |

---


Removes this player's view; they see the shared picture again.

<!-- /ref/Zone/ -->

<a id="ref-Zone"></a>

## Zone type

A box of blocks that knows who is in it, checked once a tick.

## Functions

| Call | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`contains`](#ref-Zone-contains) | Returns true when the player is in the zone. |
| [`players`](#ref-Zone-players) | Returns who is in the zone now. |
| [`destroy`](#ref-Zone-destroy) | Removes the zone. |
